			},
			Networks: map[string]Object{"shared": {Keys: cpKeys("external", "ipam", "name"), Name: "my-shared-net", External: true}},
			Volumes: map[string]Object{
				"ext":   {Keys: cpKeys("external", "name"), Name: "ext", External: true},
				"other": {Keys: cpKeys("external", "name"), Name: "real-other", External: true},
				"plain": {Keys: cpKeys("name"), Name: "external_plain"},
			},
			Configs: map[string]Object{"cfg": {Keys: cpKeys("content", "labels", "name"), Name: "external_cfg",
				Labels: map[string]string{"k": "v"}}},
			Secrets: map[string]Object{"sec": {Keys: cpKeys("environment", "name"), Name: "external_sec"}},
		}},
		{"include", Config{
			Name:    "include",
			TopKeys: cpKeys("name", "networks", "services"),
			Services: map[string]Service{
				"included": {Keys: cpKeys("command", "entrypoint", "image", "networks"), Image: "busybox:1.36", Networks: cpKeys("default")},
				"main":     {Keys: cpKeys("command", "entrypoint", "image", "networks"), Image: "nginx:1.27", Networks: cpKeys("default")},
			},
			Networks: map[string]Object{"default": {Keys: cpKeys("ipam", "name"), Name: "include_default"}},
		}},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got, err := Parse(cpLoad(t, tc.name))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tc.want) {
				t.Errorf("got  %+v\nwant %+v", got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestCPParseRecordsUnknownKeys: members Parse does not read are recorded by
// name only, whatever their value.
func TestCPParseRecordsUnknownKeys(t *testing.T) {
	in := `{"name":"p","x-ext":1,"include":[{"path":"x"}],` +
		`"services":{"a":{"image":"i","zzz":{"deep":[1,2]},"extends":{"service":"b"}}},` +
		`"volumes":{"v":{"driver":"local","driver_opts":{"o":"1"}}}}`
	got, err := Parse([]byte(in))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if want := cpKeys("include", "name", "services", "volumes", "x-ext"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got.TopKeys, want) {
		t.Errorf("TopKeys %v, want %v", got.TopKeys, want)
	}
	if want := cpKeys("extends", "image", "zzz"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Services["a"].Keys, want) {
		t.Errorf("service Keys %v, want %v", got.Services["a"].Keys, want)
	}
	if want := cpKeys("driver", "driver_opts"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Volumes["v"].Keys, want) {
		t.Errorf("volume Keys %v, want %v", got.Volumes["v"].Keys, want)
	}
}

// TestCPParseNamedVolumes: only mounts of type volume with a source count,
// once each.
func TestCPParseNamedVolumes(t *testing.T) {
	in := `{"services":{"a":{"volumes":[` +
		`{"type":"volume","source":"zed","target":"/z"},{"type":"volume","source":"alpha","target":"/a"},` +
		`{"type":"volume","source":"zed","target":"/z2"},{"type":"volume","target":"/anon"},` +
		`{"type":"bind","source":"/srv","target":"/s"},{"type":"tmpfs","target":"/t"},{"target":"/none"}]}}}`
	got, err := Parse([]byte(in))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if want := cpKeys("alpha", "zed"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Services["a"].Volumes, want) {
		t.Errorf("Volumes %v, want %v", got.Services["a"].Volumes, want)
	}
}

// TestCPParseMemberPresence: build and provider count as present whatever
// their value, so a service cannot hide one behind an odd value.
func TestCPParseMemberPresence(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := Parse([]byte(`{"services":{"a":{"build":".","provider":{"type":"x"}},"b":{"build":null},"c":{"provider":null},"d":{}}}`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := map[string][2]bool{"a": {true, true}, "b": {true, false}, "c": {false, true}, "d": {false, false}}
	for name, w := range want {
		if s := got.Services[name]; s.Build != w[0] || s.Provider != w[1] {
			t.Errorf("service %s: Build %v Provider %v, want %v %v", name, s.Build, s.Provider, w[0], w[1])
		}
	}
}

func TestCPParseRejects(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct{ name, in string }{
		{"empty input", ``},
		{"an array", `[]`},
		{"a string", `"x"`},
		{"two objects", `{"name":"a"} {"name":"b"}`},
		{"trailing garbage", `{"name":"a"}x`},
		{"truncated", `{"name":"a"`},
		{"duplicate top-level key", `{"name":"a","name":"b"}`},
		{"duplicate service", `{"services":{"a":{"image":"x"},"a":{"image":"y"}}}`},
		{"duplicate service key", `{"services":{"a":{"image":"x","image":"y"}}}`},
		{"name is a number", `{"name":3}`},
		{"name is null", `{"name":null}`},
		{"services is an array", `{"services":[]}`},
		{"a service is an array", `{"services":{"a":[]}}`},
		{"image is a number", `{"services":{"a":{"image":1}}}`},
		{"image is null", `{"services":{"a":{"image":null}}}`},
		{"container_name is a bool", `{"services":{"a":{"container_name":true}}}`},
		{"service networks is an array", `{"services":{"a":{"networks":["x"]}}}`},
		{"service labels value is a number", `{"services":{"a":{"labels":{"k":1}}}}`},
		{"service labels is an array", `{"services":{"a":{"labels":["k=v"]}}}`},
		{"service volumes is an object", `{"services":{"a":{"volumes":{}}}}`},
		{"a service volume is a string", `{"services":{"a":{"volumes":["/a:/b"]}}}`},
		{"a service volume type is a number", `{"services":{"a":{"volumes":[{"type":1}]}}}`},
		{"a service volume source is an object", `{"services":{"a":{"volumes":[{"type":"volume","source":{}}]}}}`},
		{"networks is an array", `{"networks":[]}`},
		{"a secret is a number", `{"secrets":{"s":1}}`},
		{"external is a string", `{"volumes":{"v":{"external":"yes"}}}`},
		{"external is an object", `{"volumes":{"v":{"external":{"name":"x"}}}}`},
		{"object name is a number", `{"volumes":{"v":{"name":1}}}`},
		{"object labels is an array", `{"networks":{"n":{"labels":[]}}}`},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got, err := Parse([]byte(tc.in)); err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "compose:") {
				t.Errorf("Parse(%s) = %+v, %v; want an error starting with \"compose:\"", tc.in, got, err)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCPParseSizeLimit(t *testing.T) {
	doc := []byte(`{"name":"x"}`)
	at := make([]byte, MaxConfigBytes)
	copy(at, doc)
	for i := len(doc); i < len(at); i++ {
		at[i] = ' '
	}
	if c, err := Parse(at); err != nil || c.Name != "x" {
		t.Errorf("a configuration of exactly MaxConfigBytes: %+v, %v", c, err)
	}
	if _, err := Parse(append(at, ' ')); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "exceeds") {
		t.Errorf("a configuration of MaxConfigBytes+1: error %v, want one saying it exceeds the limit", err)
	}
}

func TestCPImageName(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		project, service string
		s                Service
		want             string
	}{
		{"web", "app", Service{Image: "nginx:1.27"}, "nginx:1.27"},
		{"web", "app", Service{Image: "example/tagged:1", Build: true}, "example/tagged:1"},
		{"web", "app", Service{Build: true}, "web-app"},
		{"my-proj", "db", Service{}, "my-proj-db"},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		if got := ImageName(tc.project, tc.service, tc.s); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("ImageName(%q, %q, %+v) = %q, want %q", tc.project, tc.service, tc.s, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

Run: `export TMPDIR=/root/.cache/w3-tmp/4 GOTOOLCHAIN=local && timeout 300 go test -count=1 ./internal/modules/docker/compose/`
Expected: FAIL with a build error naming the undefined `Config`, `Service`, `Object`, `Parse`, `ImageName` and `MaxConfigBytes`.

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement**

Create `internal/modules/docker/compose/config.go`, package `compose`, with a package doc comment (a Compose configuration reader and its refusals, spec 3 "Compose"), importing only the standard library. Declare `MaxConfigBytes`, `Config`, `Service`, `Object` exactly as in Contracts "compose parser" (a doc comment on each, and on each field the contract annotates), `Parse` and `ImageName`.

`ImageName(project, service, s)` returns `s.Image` when it is not empty and otherwise `project + "-" + service`.

`Parse(data)` is strict, and every error it returns starts with `compose:`:

1. More than `MaxConfigBytes` bytes is an error that says the configuration exceeds the limit; exactly `MaxConfigBytes` is accepted.
2. Read `data` with a `json.Decoder`, token by token, as one JSON object. Empty input, a value that is not an object, a truncated document, and anything after the object other than whitespace (a second value, stray characters) are errors.
3. A duplicate key in any object `Parse` reads itself (the top level, `services`, each service, each top-level network, volume, config and secret, a service's `networks` and `labels`, and each element of a service's `volumes`) is an error naming the key. Members `Parse` does not read are only collected as raw JSON, so what lies beneath them is not checked for duplicates.
4. Top level: `name` must be a string; `services` an object of objects; `networks`, `volumes`, `configs` and `secrets` each an object of objects. `Config.TopKeys` lists every top-level key (`x-` extensions included), sorted. Any other member is recorded in `TopKeys` and otherwise ignored.
5. Service members read: `image` (string), `container_name` (string), `labels` (object whose values are all strings), `networks` (an object: `Service.Networks` is its keys, sorted; its values are ignored, they are usually `null`), `volumes` (an array of objects: for each element whose `type` is the string `volume` and whose `source` is a non-empty string, add the source to `Service.Volumes`, once, sorted; elements of other types, and elements without `type` or `source`, add nothing; `type` and `source` must be strings when present), and the presence of `build` and `provider`: `Service.Build` and `Service.Provider` are true when the key is present, whatever its value, even `null`. `Service.Keys` lists every key of the service, sorted.
6. Top-level object members read: `name` (string), `external` (a boolean; an object is an error), `labels` (as for a service). `Object.Keys` lists every key, sorted.
7. A member that is read and has the wrong JSON type, including `null` for `name`, `image`, `container_name` and the other members above, is an error that names the member (for example `services.web.image`).
8. Empty results are nil, not empty: a missing or empty `services`, `labels`, `networks` or `volumes` leaves the field nil, so `reflect.DeepEqual` against a literal that omits it holds.

			Profiles: []string{}, Containers: []string{}, FirstSeen: created},

		{"pull event", PullEvent{Status: "Downloading", ID: "l1", Current: 5, Total: 10}, `{"status":"Downloading","id":"l1","current":5,"total":10}`},
		{"stats event", StatsEvent{Read: "t", CPUPercent: 2, MemUsage: 3, MemLimit: 4, NetRx: 5, NetTx: 6, Pids: 7},

	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			b, err := json.Marshal(tc.v)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if string(b) != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("got  %s\nwant %s", b, tc.want)
			}
			back := reflect.New(reflect.TypeOf(tc.v))
			if err := json.Unmarshal(b, back.Interface()); err != nil {

	}

var errDKBoom = errors.New("boom")

func dkAPIStatus(t *testing.T, err error, want int) {
	t.Helper()
	var e *dockerapi.APIError
	if !errors.As(err, &e) || e.StatusCode != want {
		t.Fatalf("error %v, want a daemon answer %d", err, want)
	}

func TestDKBuilders(t *testing.T) {
	if id := dkID("a"); len(id) != 64 || id != dkID("a") || id == dkID("b") || strings.Trim(id, "0123456789abcdef") != "" {
		t.Errorf("dkID(a) = %q", id)
	}
	c := dkContainer("web")
	if c.ID != dkID("web") || c.Name != "/web" || c.Created != "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z" || c.State.Running {
		t.Errorf("dkContainer(web) = %+v", c)
	}
	r := dkContainer("web", dkRunning, dkLabels(map[string]string{"a": "b"}), dkPorts("8080:80/tcp", "127.0.0.1:9090:90/udp"), dkOnNetwork("n1"))
	if !r.State.Running || r.State.Status != "running" || r.Config.Labels["a"] != "b" {
		t.Errorf("options not applied: %+v", r)
	}
	if got := r.HostConfig.PortBindings["80/tcp"]; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []dockerapi.PortBinding{{HostIP: "0.0.0.0", HostPort: "8080"}}) {
		t.Errorf("80/tcp binding %v", got)
	}
	if got := r.NetworkSettings.Ports["90/udp"]; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []dockerapi.PortBinding{{HostIP: "127.0.0.1", HostPort: "9090"}}) {
		t.Errorf("90/udp binding %v", got)
	}
	if ep := r.NetworkSettings.Networks["n1"]; ep == nil || ep.NetworkID != "n1" || ep.EndpointID == "" {
		t.Errorf("endpoint %+v", ep)
	}
	n := dkNetwork("net")
	if n.ID != dkID("network:net") || n.Name != "net" || n.Driver != "bridge" {
		t.Errorf("dkNetwork = %+v", n)
	}
	v := dkVolume("data", map[string]string{"k": "v"})
	if v.Name != "data" || v.Driver != "local" || v.Labels["k"] != "v" {
		t.Errorf("dkVolume = %+v", v)
	}
	i := dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100)
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(i.RepoTags, []string{"nginx:1.27"}) || i.Size != 100 || i.ID == "" {
		t.Errorf("dkImage = %+v", i)
	}
	d1, d2 := dkImage("<none>:a", 1), dkImage("<none>:b", 1)
	if len(d1.RepoTags) != 0 || d1.ID == d2.ID {
		t.Errorf("dangling images %+v %+v", d1, d2)
	}
}

func TestDKFakeContainerLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	f, ctx := h.docker, context.Background()
	f.put(dkContainer("web"))

	started, err := f.StartContainer(ctx, "web")
	if err != nil || !started {
		t.Fatalf("start by name = %v, %v", started, err)
	}
	c, _ := f.container(dkID("web"))
	if !c.State.Running || c.State.StartedAt != "2026-10-30T12:00:00Z" {
		t.Errorf("after start: %+v", c.State)
	}
	if again, err := f.StartContainer(ctx, dkID("web")); err != nil || again {
		t.Errorf("start of a running container = %v, %v; want false", again, err)
	}
	h.clock.Advance(time.Minute)
	if stopped, err := f.StopContainer(ctx, "web", stopTimeout); err != nil || !stopped {
		t.Fatalf("stop = %v, %v", stopped, err)
	}
	c, _ = f.container("web")
	if c.State.Running || c.State.FinishedAt != "2026-10-30T12:01:00Z" {
		t.Errorf("after stop: %+v", c.State)
	}
	if again, err := f.StopContainer(ctx, "web", stopTimeout); err != nil || again {
		t.Errorf("stop of a stopped container = %v, %v; want false", again, err)
	}
	h.clock.Advance(time.Minute)
	if err := f.RestartContainer(ctx, "web", stopTimeout); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	c, _ = f.container("web")
	if !c.State.Running || c.State.StartedAt != "2026-10-30T12:02:00Z" {
		t.Errorf("after restart: %+v", c.State)
	}
	if err := f.RemoveContainer(ctx, "web", dockerapi.RemoveContainerOptions{}); err == nil {
		t.Error("removed a running container without force")
	} else {
		dkAPIStatus(t, err, 409)
	}
	if err := f.RemoveContainer(ctx, "web", dockerapi.RemoveContainerOptions{Force: true}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, ok := f.container("web"); ok {
		t.Error("container still present after removal")
	}
	_, err = f.InspectContainer(ctx, "web")
	dkAPIStatus(t, err, 404)
	if !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Error("IsNotFound false for the fake's 404")
	}
	want := []string{"StartContainer", "StartContainer", "StopContainer", "StopContainer", "RestartContainer",
		"RemoveContainer", "RemoveContainer", "InspectContainer"}
	if got := f.calls(); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("calls %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestDKFakeListContainers(t *testing.T) {
	f, ctx := newDKHost(t).docker, context.Background()
	f.put(dkContainer("a", dkRunning, dkLabels(map[string]string{"com.docker.compose.project": "p"}), dkPorts("8080:80/tcp")))
	f.put(dkContainer("b", dkLabels(map[string]string{"com.docker.compose.project": "p", "x": "y"})))
	f.put(dkContainer("c", dkRunning))

	names := func(o dockerapi.ListContainersOptions) []string {
		cs, err := f.ListContainers(ctx, o)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		var out []string
		for _, c := range cs {
			out = append(out, c.Names[0])
		}
		return out
	}
	if got := names(dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{}); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"/a", "/c"}) {
		t.Errorf("running only: %v", got)
	}
	if got := names(dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{All: true}); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"/a", "/b", "/c"}) {
		t.Errorf("all: %v", got)
	}
	label := dockerapi.Filters{"label": {"com.docker.compose.project=p"}}
	if got := names(dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{All: true, Filters: label}); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"/a", "/b"}) {
		t.Errorf("label filter: %v", got)
	}
	two := dockerapi.Filters{"label": {"com.docker.compose.project", "x=y"}}
	if got := names(dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{All: true, Filters: two}); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"/b"}) {
		t.Errorf("two label filters: %v", got)
	}
	if _, err := f.ListContainers(ctx, dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{Filters: dockerapi.Filters{"status": {"exited"}}}); err == nil {
		t.Error("an unsupported filter was ignored")
	}
	cs, _ := f.ListContainers(ctx, dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{})
	if cs[0].ID != dkID("a") || cs[0].ImageID == "" || cs[0].Labels["com.docker.compose.project"] != "p" ||
		len(cs[0].Ports) != 1 || cs[0].Ports[0].PublicPort != 8080 || cs[0].Ports[0].PrivatePort != 80 || cs[0].Ports[0].Type != "tcp" {
		t.Errorf("summary %+v", cs[0])
	}
}

func TestDKFakeNetworks(t *testing.T) {
	f, ctx := newDKHost(t).docker, context.Background()
	f.put(dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
	id, err := f.CreateNetwork(ctx, dockerapi.NetworkCreate{Name: "front", Labels: map[string]string{"k": "v"}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := f.CreateNetwork(ctx, dockerapi.NetworkCreate{Name: "front"}); err == nil {
		t.Error("created a network twice")
	} else {
		dkAPIStatus(t, err, 409)
	}
	if err := f.ConnectNetwork(ctx, "front", "web", &dockerapi.EndpointSettings{Aliases: []string{"w"}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	c, _ := f.container("web")
	ep := c.NetworkSettings.Networks["front"]
	if ep == nil || ep.NetworkID != id || ep.EndpointID == "" || !reflect.DeepEqual(ep.Aliases, []string{"w"}) {
		t.Fatalf("endpoint %+v", ep)
	}
	first := ep.EndpointID
	if err := f.ConnectNetwork(ctx, "front", "web", nil); err == nil {
		t.Error("connected twice")
	} else {
		dkAPIStatus(t, err, 403)
	}
	n, err := f.InspectNetwork(ctx, id)
	if err != nil || len(n.Containers) != 1 || n.Containers[c.ID].Name != "web" || n.Containers[c.ID].EndpointID != first {
		t.Fatalf("InspectNetwork = %+v, %v", n, err)
	}
	listed, _ := f.ListNetworks(ctx, nil)
	if len(listed) != 1 || listed[0].Containers != nil {
		t.Errorf("ListNetworks must leave Containers empty: %+v", listed)
	}
	if err := f.RemoveNetwork(ctx, "front"); !dockerapi.IsConflict(err) {
		t.Errorf("RemoveNetwork of a used network = %v, want a 409", err)
	}
	if err := f.DisconnectNetwork(ctx, "front", "web", false); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.DisconnectNetwork(ctx, "front", "web", false); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Errorf("second disconnect = %v, want a 404", err)
	}
	if err := f.ConnectNetwork(ctx, "front", "web", nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	c, _ = f.container("web")
	if c.NetworkSettings.Networks["front"].EndpointID == first {
		t.Error("reconnecting kept the endpoint id")
	}
	if err := f.DisconnectNetwork(ctx, "front", "web", false); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.RemoveNetwork(ctx, "front"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.RemoveNetwork(ctx, "front"); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Errorf("RemoveNetwork of an absent network = %v, want a 404", err)
	}
}

func TestDKFakeImageInspectAndRemove(t *testing.T) {
	f, ctx := newDKHost(t).docker, context.Background()
	img := dkImage("busybox:1.36", 10)
	img.RepoTags = append(img.RepoTags, "busybox:stable")
	f.putImage(img)
	f.putImage(dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100))
	if in, err := f.InspectImage(ctx, "busybox:stable"); err != nil || in.ID != img.ID {
		t.Fatalf("InspectImage by tag = %+v, %v", in, err)
	}
	if _, err := f.InspectImage(ctx, "nope:1"); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Errorf("InspectImage of an absent image = %v, want a 404", err)
	}
	items, err := f.RemoveImage(ctx, "busybox:stable", dockerapi.RemoveImageOptions{})
	if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(items, []dockerapi.ImageDeleteItem{{Untagged: "busybox:stable"}}) {
		t.Errorf("removing one of two tags = %v, %v", items, err)
	}
	user := dkContainer("web")
	user.Image = dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100).ID
	f.put(user)
	if _, err := f.RemoveImage(ctx, "nginx:1.27", dockerapi.RemoveImageOptions{}); !dockerapi.IsConflict(err) {
		t.Errorf("removing an image in use = %v, want a 409", err)
	}
	items, err = f.RemoveImage(ctx, "busybox:1.36", dockerapi.RemoveImageOptions{})
	if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(items, []dockerapi.ImageDeleteItem{{Untagged: "busybox:1.36"}, {Deleted: img.ID}}) {
		t.Errorf("removing the last tag = %v, %v", items, err)
	}
	if _, err := f.InspectImage(ctx, "busybox:1.36"); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Errorf("image still present: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestDKFakePull(t *testing.T) {
	f, ctx := newDKHost(t).docker, context.Background()
	if _, err := f.PullImage(ctx, "ghost:1"); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Errorf("PullImage with no scripted pull = %v, want a 404", err)
	}
	f.pulls["busybox:1.36"] = []dockerapi.PullMessage{{Status: "Pulling"}, {Status: "Downloading", ID: "l1", ProgressDetail: &dockerapi.ProgressDetail{Current: 1, Total: 2}}}
	s, err := f.PullImage(ctx, "busybox:1.36")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"Pulling", "Downloading"} {
		m, err := s.Next()
		if err != nil || m.Status != want {
			t.Fatalf("Next = %+v, %v; want %s", m, err, want)
		}
	}
	if _, err := f.InspectImage(ctx, "busybox:1.36"); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Error("the image appeared before the stream ended")
	}
	if _, err := s.Next(); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		t.Fatalf("Next at the end = %v, want io.EOF", err)
	}
	if _, err := f.InspectImage(ctx, "busybox:1.36"); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("the image is absent after the pull: %v", err)
	}

	f.pulls["bad:1"] = []dockerapi.PullMessage{{Status: "Pulling"}, {Error: "denied"}}
	s, _ = f.PullImage(ctx, "bad:1")
	_, _ = s.Next()
	if _, err := s.Next(); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "denied") {
		t.Errorf("a failure message gave %v, want its error", err)
	}
	if _, err := f.InspectImage(ctx, "bad:1"); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Error("a failed pull left an image")
	}
}

func TestDKFakeLogs(t *testing.T) {
	f, ctx := newDKHost(t).docker, context.Background()
	f.put(dkContainer("web"))
	id := dkID("web")
	f.logs[id] = []dockerapi.LogFrame{{Stream: "stdout", Data: []byte("1")}, {Stream: "stderr", Data: []byte("2")},
		{Stream: "stdout", Data: []byte("3")}}
	read := func(o dockerapi.LogsOptions) string {
		s, err := f.Logs(ctx, "web", o)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		var b strings.Builder
		for {
			fr, err := s.Next()
			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
				return b.String()
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			b.WriteString(fr.Stream[:3] + ":" + string(fr.Data) + " ")
		}
	}
	if got := read(dockerapi.LogsOptions{Stdout: true, Stderr: true}); got != "std:1 std:2 std:3 " {
		t.Errorf("both streams: %q", got)
	}
	if got := read(dockerapi.LogsOptions{Stderr: true}); got != "std:2 " {
		t.Errorf("stderr only: %q", got)
	}
	if got := read(dockerapi.LogsOptions{Stdout: true, Stderr: true, Tail: "2"}); got != "std:2 std:3 " {
		t.Errorf("tail 2: %q", got)
	}
	if _, err := f.Logs(ctx, "ghost", dockerapi.LogsOptions{Stdout: true}); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Errorf("Logs of an absent container = %v, want a 404", err)
	}
}

// TestDKFakeFollow: a followed stream serves its frames and then waits until
// it is closed or its context ends.
func TestDKFakeFollow(t *testing.T) {
	f := newDKHost(t).docker
	f.put(dkContainer("web"))
	f.logs[dkID("web")] = []dockerapi.LogFrame{{Stream: "stdout", Data: []byte("1")}}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	s, err := f.Logs(ctx, "web", dockerapi.LogsOptions{Stdout: true, Follow: true})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if fr, err := s.Next(); err != nil || string(fr.Data) != "1" {
		t.Fatalf("first frame = %+v, %v", fr, err)
	}
	res := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { _, err := s.Next(); res <- err }()
	select {
	case err := <-res:
		t.Fatalf("Next returned %v before the stream ended", err)
	case <-time.After(50 * time.Millisecond):
	}
	cancel()
	if err := <-res; !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		t.Errorf("after cancel: %v, want context.Canceled", err)
	}

	s, _ = f.Logs(context.Background(), "web", dockerapi.LogsOptions{Stdout: true, Follow: true})
	_, _ = s.Next()
	go func() { _, err := s.Next(); res <- err }()
	time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
	_ = s.Close()
	if err := <-res; !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		t.Errorf("after Close: %v, want io.EOF", err)
	}
}

func TestDKFakeStats(t *testing.T) {
	f, ctx := newDKHost(t).docker, context.Background()
	f.put(dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
	f.stats[dkID("web")] = []dockerapi.Stats{{Read: "a"}, {Read: "b"}}
	s, err := f.Stats(ctx, "web", false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if st, err := s.Next(); err != nil || st.Read != "a" {
		t.Errorf("one-shot sample = %+v, %v", st, err)
	}
	if _, err := s.Next(); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		t.Errorf("one-shot stream ended with %v, want io.EOF", err)
	}
	cctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	s, _ = f.Stats(cctx, "web", true)
	for _, want := range []string{"a", "b"} {
		if st, err := s.Next(); err != nil || st.Read != want {
			t.Errorf("streamed sample = %+v, %v; want %s", st, err, want)
		}
	}
	cancel()
	if _, err := s.Next(); !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		t.Errorf("after the samples: %v, want the context's error", err)
	}
	if _, err := f.Stats(ctx, "ghost", false); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Errorf("Stats of an absent container = %v, want a 404", err)
	}
}

func TestDKHostFiles(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	if err := h.WriteManaged(ctx, ID, "/var/lib/x", "config.json", []byte("{}"), 0o600, 0, 0); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if string(h.managed["/var/lib/x/config.json"]) != "{}" {
		t.Errorf("managed %v", h.managed)
	}
	if err := h.RemoveManaged(ctx, ID, "/var/lib/x", "config.json"); err != nil || len(h.managed) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("RemoveManaged: %v, %v", err, h.managed)
	}
	for name, err := range map[string]error{
		"WriteFile": h.WriteFile(ctx, ID, "/p", nil, 0o600), "Remove": h.Remove(ctx, ID, "/p"),
		"Rename": h.Rename(ctx, ID, "/a", "/b"), "WriteSysctl": h.WriteSysctl(ctx, ID, "k", "v"),
	} {
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s succeeded; only the managed-file methods work", name)
		}
	}

	h.files["/srv/p"] = dkFile{Mode: fs.ModeDir | 0o755, UID: 1000}
	h.files["/srv/p/compose.yaml"] = dkFile{Mode: 0o644, UID: 1000, Data: []byte("services: {}")}
	h.files["/srv/link"] = dkFile{Mode: 0o777, Symlink: true}
	k := h.dk()
	fi, err := k.d.lstat("/srv/p")
	if err != nil || !fi.IsDir() || fi.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t).Uid != 1000 || fi.Name() != "p" {
		t.Errorf("lstat dir = %v, %v", fi, err)
	}
	fi, _ = k.d.lstat("/srv/link")
	if fi.Mode()&fs.ModeSymlink == 0 {
		t.Errorf("lstat symlink mode %v", fi.Mode())
	}
	fi, _ = k.d.lstat("/srv/p/compose.yaml")
	if fi.Size() != 12 || fi.Mode().Perm() != 0o644 {
		t.Errorf("lstat file size %d mode %v", fi.Size(), fi.Mode())
	}
	if _, err := k.d.lstat("/srv/none"); !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		t.Errorf("lstat of a missing path = %v, want fs.ErrNotExist", err)
	}
	if b, err := k.d.readFile("/srv/p/compose.yaml"); err != nil || string(b) != "services: {}" {
		t.Errorf("readFile = %q, %v", b, err)
	}
	if _, err := k.d.readFile("/srv/none"); !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		t.Errorf("readFile of a missing path = %v, want fs.ErrNotExist", err)
	}
	h.secrets = [][]byte{[]byte("s3")}
	if s, err := k.d.secrets(ctx, h.env(""), "c"); err != nil || len(s) != 1 || string(s[0]) != "s3" {
		t.Errorf("secrets = %q, %v", s, err)
	}
	if k.d.docker != dockerAPI(h.docker) {
		t.Error("dk() does not use the host's fake Docker")
	}
}

func TestDKHostEnv(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	env := h.env("c1")
	if env.HostID != "h1" || env.ChangeID != "c1" || env.Principal.Scope != core.ScopeAdmin || env.Effects == nil ||
		env.DB != h.db || env.Sealer == nil || env.Clock == nil || env.Log == nil || env.Exec == nil || env.Files == nil {
		t.Errorf("env %+v", env)
	}
	if h.env("").Effects != nil {
		t.Error("an env without a change id must have no effects journal")
	}
	var n int
	if err := h.db.Read().QueryRow("SELECT count(*) FROM core_effects").Scan(&n); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("the host database lacks the core tables: %v", err)
	}
	sealed, err := env.Sealer.Seal("ad", []byte("x"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if b, err := env.Sealer.Open("ad", sealed); err != nil || string(b) != "x" {
		t.Errorf("sealer round trip = %q, %v", b, err)
	}
}

func TestDKJournal(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	j := h.env("c7").Effects
	seq, err := j.Intend(ctx, core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectModify, Resource: "docker.container:a"}, []byte("secret"))
	if err != nil || seq != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("Intend = %d, %v", seq, err)
	}
	if err := j.Made(ctx, seq, "docker.container:a", core.StateDoc{State: []byte(`{"id":"a"}`)}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := j.Made(ctx, seq, "docker.container:a", core.StateDoc{}); err == nil {
		t.Error("Made of a made effect succeeded")
	}
	seq2, _ := j.Intend(ctx, core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectModify, Resource: "docker.container:b"}, nil)
	if err := j.Skipped(ctx, seq2); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := j.Skipped(ctx, 9); err == nil {
		t.Error("Skipped of an unknown effect succeeded")
	}
	es := h.journal.effects()
	if len(es) != 2 || es[0].State != core.EffectMade || es[0].ChangeID != "c7" || es[0].Seq != 1 ||
		string(es[0].Post.State) != `{"id":"a"}` || es[1].State != core.EffectSkipped {
		t.Errorf("effects %+v", es)
	}
	if s, err := j.Secret(ctx, 1); err != nil || string(s) != "secret" {
		t.Errorf("Secret = %q, %v", s, err)
	}
	if s, err := j.Secret(ctx, 2); err != nil || s != nil {
		t.Errorf("Secret of an effect with none = %q, %v", s, err)
	}
	if listed, err := j.List(ctx); err != nil || len(listed) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("List = %v, %v", listed, err)
	}
}

Start: already running answers `false, nil`; else it sets `Running`, status `running` and `StartedAt` to now and answers `true`. A stream that ended with a failure message leaves no image. `RemoveImage(ref, o)`: 404 when absent; 409 when a container's image id equals the image's id and `o.Force` is false; removing a tag of an image that has more than one tag removes only that tag and answers `[{Untagged: ref}]`; otherwise it answers one `Untagged` item per tag and then `{Deleted: id}`, and the image is gone.

Any other filter key makes the list call return an error `fake: unsupported filter "<key>"`, so a test never passes by silently ignoring a filter.

```go
package policy

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

const edDoc = `// Tailnet policy
{
	// who may do what
	"acls": [
		{"action": "accept", "src": ["*"], "dst": ["*:*"]}, // allow all
	],
	"tagOwners": {
		"tag:web": ["autogroup:admin"], // web servers
	},
	"derpMap": {
		"Regions": {
			"900": {"RegionID": 900},
		},
	},
}
`

func edVal(s string) json.RawMessage { return json.RawMessage(s) }

func edCanon(t *testing.T, text string) string {
	t.Helper()
	c, err := Canonical([]byte(text))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("canonical of %q: %v", text, err)
	}
	return string(c)
}

func edInvalid(t *testing.T, err error, field string) {
	t.Helper()
	var e *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &e) {
		t.Fatalf("error %v, want *errcode.Error", err)
	}
	if e.Code != errcode.InvalidInput {
		t.Errorf("code %s, want %s", e.Code, errcode.InvalidInput)
	}
	if len(e.Fields) != 1 || e.Fields[0].Path != field {
		t.Errorf("fields %+v, want one at %s", e.Fields, field)
	}
}

// TestEDApplyEdits: each edit kind produces the expected document, keeps the
// comments around what it does not touch, and converges: applying the same
// edits to the result changes nothing, byte for byte.
func TestEDApplyEdits(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name      string
		in        string // edDoc when empty
		edits     []Edit
		want      string // the expected document; empty: the text is returned unchanged
		wantExact string // substrings the output must still contain
	}{
		{name: "set adds a member",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "set", Path: "/tagOwners/tag:db", Value: edVal(`["autogroup:admin"]`)}},
			want: `{"acls":[{"action":"accept","src":["*"],"dst":["*:*"]}],"tagOwners":{"tag:web":["autogroup:admin"],` +
				`"tag:db":["autogroup:admin"]},"derpMap":{"Regions":{"900":{"RegionID":900}}}}`,
			wantExact: "// allow all|// web servers|// who may do what|// Tailnet policy"},
		{name: "set replaces a member and keeps its comment",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "set", Path: "/tagOwners/tag:web", Value: edVal(`["group:ops"]`)}},
			want: `{"acls":[{"action":"accept","src":["*"],"dst":["*:*"]}],"tagOwners":{"tag:web":["group:ops"]},` +
				`"derpMap":{"Regions":{"900":{"RegionID":900}}}}`,
			wantExact: "// web servers|// allow all"},
		{name: "set an equal value is no change",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "set", Path: "/derpMap/Regions/900", Value: edVal(`{ "RegionID":900 }`)}}},
		{name: "set an equal object with other key order is no change",
			in:    `{"a": {"x": 1, "y": [1, 2]}}`,
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "set", Path: "/a", Value: edVal(`{"y":[1,2],"x":1}`)}}},
		{name: "delete removes a member",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "delete", Path: "/derpMap/Regions/900"}},
			want: `{"acls":[{"action":"accept","src":["*"],"dst":["*:*"]}],"tagOwners":{"tag:web":["autogroup:admin"]},` +
				`"derpMap":{"Regions":{}}}`,
			wantExact: "// web servers|// allow all"},
		{name: "delete an absent member is no change",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "delete", Path: "/tagOwners/tag:none"}}},
		{name: "addItem appends an element",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "addItem", Path: "/acls", Value: edVal(`{"action":"accept","src":["a"],"dst":["b:1"]}`)}},
			want: `{"acls":[{"action":"accept","src":["*"],"dst":["*:*"]},{"action":"accept","src":["a"],"dst":["b:1"]}],` +
				`"tagOwners":{"tag:web":["autogroup:admin"]},"derpMap":{"Regions":{"900":{"RegionID":900}}}}`,
			wantExact: "// allow all|// web servers"},
		{name: "addItem of a present element is no change, whatever its formatting",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "addItem", Path: "/acls",
				Value: edVal(`{ "dst": ["*:*"], "src": ["*"], "action": "accept" }`)}}},
		{name: "addItem to a string array",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "addItem", Path: "/tagOwners/tag:web", Value: edVal(`"group:ops"`)}},
			want: `{"acls":[{"action":"accept","src":["*"],"dst":["*:*"]}],"tagOwners":{"tag:web":["autogroup:admin","group:ops"]},` +
				`"derpMap":{"Regions":{"900":{"RegionID":900}}}}`,
			wantExact: "// web servers"},
		{name: "addItem creates an absent array",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "addItem", Path: "/grants", Value: edVal(`{"src":["*"],"dst":["*"],"ip":["*"]}`)}},
			want: `{"acls":[{"action":"accept","src":["*"],"dst":["*:*"]}],"tagOwners":{"tag:web":["autogroup:admin"]},` +
				`"derpMap":{"Regions":{"900":{"RegionID":900}}},"grants":[{"src":["*"],"dst":["*"],"ip":["*"]}]}`,
			wantExact: "// allow all"},
		{name: "removeItem removes every equal element",
			in:    `{"a": ["x", "y", "x", {"k": 1}, "x"]}`,
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "removeItem", Path: "/a", Value: edVal(`"x"`)}},
			want:  `{"a":["y",{"k":1}]}`},
		{name: "removeItem compares objects by canonical JSON",
			in:    `{"a": [{"k": 1, "j": 2}, {"k": 2}]}`,
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "removeItem", Path: "/a", Value: edVal(`{"j":2,"k":1}`)}},
			want:  `{"a":[{"k":2}]}`},
		{name: "removeItem with no match is no change",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "removeItem", Path: "/tagOwners/tag:web", Value: edVal(`"group:none"`)}}},
		{name: "removeItem from an absent array is no change",
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "removeItem", Path: "/grants", Value: edVal(`"x"`)}}},
		{name: "edits apply in order",
			edits: []Edit{
				{Op: "set", Path: "/tagOwners/tag:db", Value: edVal(`["group:a"]`)},
				{Op: "addItem", Path: "/tagOwners/tag:db", Value: edVal(`"group:b"`)},
				{Op: "removeItem", Path: "/tagOwners/tag:db", Value: edVal(`"group:a"`)},
				{Op: "delete", Path: "/derpMap"},
			},
			want: `{"acls":[{"action":"accept","src":["*"],"dst":["*:*"]}],` +
				`"tagOwners":{"tag:web":["autogroup:admin"],"tag:db":["group:b"]}}`},
		{name: "a pointer escapes ~1 and ~0",
			in:    `{"a/b": {"c~d": 1}}`,
			edits: []Edit{{Op: "set", Path: "/a~1b/c~0d", Value: edVal(`2`)}},
			want:  `{"a/b":{"c~d":2}}`},
		{name: "no edits",
			edits: nil},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			in := tc.in
			if in == "" {
				in = edDoc
			}
			orig := []byte(in)
			got, err := Apply(orig, tc.edits)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
			}
			if string(orig) != in {
				t.Fatal("Apply changed its input slice")
			}
			if tc.want == "" {
				if string(got) != in {
					t.Fatalf("no change expected, got\n%s", got)
				}
			} else if c, w := edCanon(t, string(got)), edCanon(t, tc.want); c != w {
				t.Fatalf("canonical\n got %s\nwant %s", c, w)
			}
			for _, s := range strings.Split(tc.wantExact, "|") {
				if s != "" && !strings.Contains(string(got), s) {
					t.Errorf("output lost %q:\n%s", s, got)
				}
			}
			again, err := Apply(got, tc.edits)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("second Apply: %v", err)
			}
			if string(again) != string(got) {
				t.Errorf("not convergent: the second Apply changed the text\nfirst:\n%s\nsecond:\n%s", got, again)
			}
		})
	}
}

```go
package policy

import (
	"fmt"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

func edLines(ops ...string) []core.DiffLine {
	out := make([]core.DiffLine, len(ops))
	for i, o := range ops {
		out[i] = core.DiffLine{Op: o[:1], Text: o[1:]}
	}
	return out
}

func TestEDDiff(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name          string
		before, after string
		want          []core.DiffLine
	}{
		{"equal texts have no lines", "a\nb\n", "a\nb\n", nil},
		{"both empty", "", "", nil},
		{"a changed line with three lines of context",
			"a\nb\nc\nd\ne\nf\ng\nh\n", "a\nb\nc\nD\ne\nf\ng\nh\n",
			edLines(" a", " b", " c", "-d", "+D", " e", " f", " g")},
		{"a line added at the end", "a\nb\n", "a\nb\nc\n", edLines(" a", " b", "+c")},
		{"a line removed at the start", "a\nb\nc\n", "b\nc\n", edLines("-a", " b", " c")},
		{"a line inserted in the middle", "a\nc\n", "a\nb\nc\n", edLines(" a", "+b", " c")},
		{"everything new", "", "a\nb\n", edLines("+a", "+b")},
		{"everything removed", "a\nb\n", "", edLines("-a", "-b")},
		{"a missing final newline alone is not a line change", "a\nb", "a\nb\n", nil},
		{"changes far apart are separated",
			"a\nb\nc\nd\ne\nf\ng\nh\ni\nj\nk\nl\nm\n", "A\nb\nc\nd\ne\nf\ng\nh\ni\nj\nk\nl\nM\n",
			edLines("-a", "+A", " b", " c", " d", " ...", " j", " k", " l", "-m", "+M")},
		{"changes close together form one hunk",
			"a\nb\nc\nd\ne\nf\n", "A\nb\nc\nd\ne\nF\n",
			edLines("-a", "+A", " b", " c", " d", " e", "-f", "+F")},
		{"a carriage return is part of the line", "a\r\nb\r\n", "a\nb\n",
			edLines("-a\r", "-b\r", "+a", "+b")},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got := Diff([]byte(tc.before), []byte(tc.after))
			if len(got) == 0 && len(tc.want) == 0 {
				return
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tc.want) {
				t.Errorf("got  %v\nwant %v", got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestEDDiffOfAnEdit: the diff of an applied edit shows the added lines and
// no removed one.
func TestEDDiffOfAnEdit(t *testing.T) {
	out, err := Apply([]byte(edDoc), []Edit{{Op: "set", Path: "/tagOwners/tag:db", Value: edVal(`["autogroup:admin"]`)}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var plus, minus int
	for _, l := range Diff([]byte(edDoc), out) {
		switch l.Op {
		case "+":
			plus++
		case "-":
			minus++
		}
	}
	if plus == 0 || minus != 0 {
		t.Errorf("%d added and %d removed lines, want some added and none removed", plus, minus)
	}
}

// TestEDDiffLargeMiddle: when the differing middle is too large to align
// (more than four million table cells), it is shown as removed then added,
// even where it has lines in common.
func TestEDDiffLargeMiddle(t *testing.T) {
	const n = 2500
	var a, b strings.Builder
	a.WriteString("head\n")
	b.WriteString("head\n")
	for i := range n {
		if i == n/2 {
			a.WriteString("common\n")
			b.WriteString("common\n")
			continue
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&a, "old %d\n", i)
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "new %d\n", i)
	}
	a.WriteString("tail\n")
	b.WriteString("tail\n")
	var plus, minus, common int
	for _, l := range Diff([]byte(a.String()), []byte(b.String())) {
		switch {
		case l.Op == "+":
			plus++
		case l.Op == "-":
			minus++
		case l.Text == "common":
			common++
		}
	}
	if plus != n || minus != n || common != 0 {
		t.Errorf("%d added, %d removed, %d common lines; want %d, %d, 0", plus, minus, common, n, n)
	}
}

// TestEDDiffAlignsSmallMiddle: below the limit the common line is kept.
func TestEDDiffAlignsSmallMiddle(t *testing.T) {
	got := Diff([]byte("head\nold 1\ncommon\nold 2\ntail\n"), []byte("head\nnew 1\ncommon\nnew 2\ntail\n"))
	want := edLines(" head", "-old 1", "+new 1", " common", "-old 2", "+new 2", " tail")
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("got  %v\nwant %v", got, want)
	}
}
```

Expected: FAIL with a build error naming the undefined `Canonical`, `Diff`, `Apply` and `Edit`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Package `policy`, package doc comment in `policy.go`; imports only the standard library, `internal/core`, `internal/core/errcode` and `github.com/tailscale/hujson`. Read `hujson`'s `Parse`, `Standardize`, `Value.Pack`, `Value.Find` and `Value.Patch` (in the module cache, `go list -m -f '{{.Dir}}' github.com/tailscale/hujson`) before you start: the parse tree keeps comments and whitespace, `Pack` reproduces the input byte for byte when nothing changed, and `Patch` applies RFC 6902 operations to the tree keeping the comments around untouched values.

1. `canonical.go`, `Canonical(text []byte) ([]byte, error)`: `hujson.Standardize` the text (comments and trailing commas removed), decode it with a `json.Decoder` that has `UseNumber` into an `any`, and encode that with a `json.Encoder` that has `SetEscapeHTML(false)`, trimming the encoder's final newline. Go sorts map keys, so object keys come out sorted; numbers keep their digits; no whitespace. A parse or decode failure (including a second value after the first, or empty text) is `policy: parse: <cause>`; an encode failure is `policy: encode: <cause>`. These are plain errors, not `errcode` errors.

2. `policy.go`, type `Edit` exactly as in Contracts "Tailnet policy package", and `Apply(text []byte, edits []Edit) ([]byte, error)`:
   - Parse `text` with `hujson.Parse`; a failure is the plain error `policy: parse: <cause>`. Apply the edits to the parsed tree in order; at the first failing edit return `nil` and the error, so nothing partial escapes. On success return `Value.Pack()`. Never call `Format`, `Standardize` or `Minimize` on the document, and never write into `text`: unrelated lines must come out byte for byte as they went in, and an edit that changes nothing must leave the packed text identical to the input.
   - Every refusal below is an `*errcode.Error` with `Code: errcode.InvalidInput`, `Detail: "edit <i>: <message>"` and `Fields: []errcode.FieldError{{Path: "/edits/<i>", Message: <message>}}`, where `<i>` is the zero-based index of the edit in `edits`.
   - Refuse: an `Op` other than `set`, `delete`, `addItem`, `removeItem`; a `Path` that is not a JSON Pointer with at least one token (it must start with `/`; the empty path and a path without the leading slash are refused; `~0` and `~1` are the only escapes, any other `~` sequence is refused); for `set`, `addItem` and `removeItem` an empty `Value`, or a `Value` for which `Canonical` fails.
   - Walk the pointer's tokens from the document root, except the last one. Each step needs the current value to be a JSON object and the token to be one of its members (the first member with that exact decoded name); a current value that is an array is refused as "goes through an array index" (this includes `-` and numeric tokens), any other non-object as "parent is not an object", and a missing member as "parent does not exist". The value reached must itself be an object (same refusals); it is the parent, and the last token names a member of it, present or not.
   - `set`: member absent → apply the one-operation patch `add` at `Path` with `Value`; member present and `Canonical(member.Pack())` equal to `Canonical(Value)` → no change; present and different → patch `replace`. A trailing comment after a replaced member stays.
   - `delete`: member present → patch `remove`; absent → no change.
   - `addItem` and `removeItem`: let the member be the target. `addItem` with the target absent creates it: patch `add` at `Path` with the one-element array `[Value]`. `removeItem` with the target absent is no change. A target that is present and not an array is refused ("is not an array"). Otherwise compare every element, as `Canonical(element.Pack())`, with `Canonical(Value)`: `addItem` appends (patch `add` at `Path + "/-"`) only when no element is equal; `removeItem` removes every equal element (patch `remove` at `Path + "/" + index`, from the highest index down so the indexes stay valid) and does nothing when none is equal.
   - Build each patch with `encoding/json` (an array of one object with `op`, `path` and, where needed, `value` as the raw JSON) and apply it with `Value.Patch`. The patched tree may not be re-indented; that is accepted.

3. `diff.go`, `Diff(before, after []byte) []core.DiffLine`: split each text at `"\n"` and drop one final empty piece (so a text with and without its last newline give the same lines; `\r` stays in the line). Equal line lists give `nil`. Otherwise trim the common prefix and suffix; align the differing middles with a longest-common-subsequence table of `int32` over `(len(a)+1)*(len(b)+1)` cells, filled from the end; when the table would exceed 4,000,000 cells, skip the alignment and show the whole middle of `before` as removed and then the whole middle of `after` as added. Walk the table from the start: equal lines are `" "`; otherwise, when the table value below (dropping the line of `before`) is at least the value to the right (dropping the line of `after`), emit the line of `before` as `"-"`, else the line of `after` as `"+"` (so on a tie removals come first). The prefix and suffix lines are `" "`. Then keep only the changed lines and the 3 lines of context before and after each; where lines between two kept lines are left out, put one line `{Op: " ", Text: "..."}` there; left-out lines before the first or after the last kept line are dropped without a marker.

		{"before the catch-all", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, Rule{Hostname: "b.example.com", Service: "http://b:80"},
			`{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inB + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, true},
		{"catch-all added to an empty configuration", `{}`, Rule{Hostname: "b.example.com", Service: "http://b:80"},
			`{"ingress":[` + inB + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, true},
		{"catch-all added after the existing rules", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `]}`, Rule{Hostname: "b.example.com", Service: "http://b:80"},
			`{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inB + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, true},
		{"an operator's own last rule counts as the catch-all", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,{"service":"http_status:503"}]}`, Rule{Hostname: "b.example.com", Service: "http://b:80"},
			`{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inB + `,{"service":"http_status:503"}]}`, true},
		{"equal rule already present", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, Rule{Hostname: "a.example.com", Service: "http://a:80"},
			`{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, false},
		{"hostnames compare without case", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, Rule{Hostname: "A.Example.COM", Service: "http://a:80"},
			`{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, false},
		{"noTLSVerify is written", `{"ingress":[` + inEnd + `]}`, Rule{Hostname: "b.example.com", Service: "https://b:443", NoTLSVerify: true},
			`{"ingress":[{"hostname":"b.example.com","originRequest":{"noTLSVerify":true},"service":"https://b:443"},` + inEnd + `]}`, true},
		{"other members and rules are carried over", `{"originRequest":{"connectTimeout":10},"ingress":[{"hostname":"a.example.com","originRequest":{"connectTimeout":5},"service":"http://a:80","x":[1,2]},` + inEnd + `]}`,
			Rule{Hostname: "b.example.com", Service: "http://b:80"},
			`{"ingress":[{"hostname":"a.example.com","originRequest":{"connectTimeout":5},"service":"http://a:80","x":[1,2]},` + inB + `,` + inEnd + `],"originRequest":{"connectTimeout":10}}`, true},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			in := inRead(t, tc.src)
			in.Ingress = append(make([]Rule, 0, 16), in.Ingress...)
			before := inJSON(t, in)
			out, changed, err := Add(in, tc.add)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if changed != tc.changed {
				t.Errorf("changed %v, want %v", changed, tc.changed)
			}
			if got := inJSON(t, out); got != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("got  %s\nwant %s", got, tc.want)
			}
			if after := inJSON(t, in); after != before {
				t.Errorf("Add changed its argument: %s, was %s", after, before)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestInAddRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	c := inRead(t, `{"ingress":[`+inA+`,`+inEnd+`]}`)
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		add  Rule
		want string
	}{
		{"another service", Rule{Hostname: "a.example.com", Service: "http://other:80"}, "a.example.com"},
		{"another noTLSVerify", Rule{Hostname: "a.example.com", Service: "http://a:80", NoTLSVerify: true}, "a.example.com"},
		{"another path", Rule{Hostname: "a.example.com", Path: "^/x", Service: "http://a:80"}, "a.example.com"},
		{"no hostname", Rule{Service: "http://a:80"}, "hostname"},
		{"no service", Rule{Hostname: "c.example.com"}, "service"},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			out, changed, err := Add(c, tc.add)
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatal("no error")
			}
			if !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "ingress: ") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.want) {
				t.Errorf("error %q", err)
			}
			if changed || len(out.Ingress) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("a refusal returned changed=%v and %d rules", changed, len(out.Ingress))
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestInRemove(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		src      string
		hostname string
		want     string
		changed  bool
	}{
		{"drops the rule", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inB + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, "b.example.com", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, true},
		{"without case", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inB + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, "B.EXAMPLE.com", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, true},
		{"every rule of the hostname", `{"ingress":[` + inB + `,{"hostname":"b.example.com","path":"^/x","service":"http://x:80"},` + inEnd + `]}`, "b.example.com", `{"ingress":[` + inEnd + `]}`, true},
		{"absent hostname", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, "b.example.com", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, false},
		{"the catch-all is never dropped", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, "", `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, false},
		{"unrelated rules and members are carried over", `{"warp-routing":{"enabled":true},"ingress":[{"hostname":"a.example.com","originRequest":{"connectTimeout":5},"service":"http://a:80","x":[1,2]},` + inB + `,` + inEnd + `]}`, "b.example.com",
			`{"ingress":[{"hostname":"a.example.com","originRequest":{"connectTimeout":5},"service":"http://a:80","x":[1,2]},` + inEnd + `],"warp-routing":{"enabled":true}}`, true},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			in := inRead(t, tc.src)
			in.Ingress = append(make([]Rule, 0, 16), in.Ingress...)
			before := inJSON(t, in)
			out, changed := Remove(in, tc.hostname)
			if changed != tc.changed {
				t.Errorf("changed %v, want %v", changed, tc.changed)
			}
			if got := inJSON(t, out); got != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("got  %s\nwant %s", got, tc.want)
			}
			if after := inJSON(t, in); after != before {
				t.Errorf("Remove changed its argument: %s, was %s", after, before)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestInLookup(t *testing.T) {
	c := inRead(t, `{"ingress":[`+inA+`,{"hostname":"b.example.com","originRequest":{"noTLSVerify":true},"path":"^/x","service":"https://b:443"},`+inEnd+`]}`)
	r, ok := Lookup(c, "B.example.com")
	if !ok || r.Hostname != "b.example.com" || r.Path != "^/x" || r.Service != "https://b:443" || !r.NoTLSVerify {
		t.Errorf("Lookup b: %+v %v", r, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := Lookup(c, "c.example.com"); ok {
		t.Error("Lookup found an absent hostname")
	}
	if _, ok := Lookup(c, ""); ok {
		t.Error("Lookup found the catch-all by an empty hostname")
	}
}

func TestInHash(t *testing.T) {
	base := `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `],"warp-routing":{"enabled":true,"x":1}}`
	h := Hash(inRead(t, base))
	if !regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`).MatchString(h) {
		t.Fatalf("hash %q is not 64 lowercase hex digits", h)
	}
	if got := Hash(inRead(t, `{"ingress":[{"service":"http_status:404"}]}`)); got != "d66fa8eea80c1402568e0afdc5007526058575873a20166b8da9a66c8e77c63a" {
		t.Errorf("hash of the bare catch-all %s", got)
	}
	same := map[string]string{
		"member order in an unnamed member": `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `],"warp-routing":{"x":1,"enabled":true}}`,
		"top-level member order":            `{"warp-routing":{"enabled":true,"x":1},"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `]}`,
		"rule member order":                 `{"ingress":[{"service":"http://a:80","hostname":"a.example.com"},{"service":"http_status:404"}],"warp-routing":{"enabled":true,"x":1}}`,
		"whitespace":                        "{\n \"ingress\": [ " + inA + ", " + inEnd + " ],\n \"warp-routing\": { \"enabled\": true, \"x\": 1 }\n}",
	}
	for name, src := range same {
		if got := Hash(inRead(t, src)); got != h {
			t.Errorf("%s changes the hash", name)
		}
	}
	plain := Hash(inRead(t, `{"ingress":[`+inA+`]}`))
	if got := Hash(inRead(t, `{"ingress":[{"hostname":"a.example.com","originRequest":{"noTLSVerify":false},"service":"http://a:80"}]}`)); got != plain {
		t.Error("an explicit noTLSVerify false changes the hash")
	}
	differs := map[string]string{
		"a changed service":        `{"ingress":[{"hostname":"a.example.com","service":"http://a:81"},` + inEnd + `],"warp-routing":{"enabled":true,"x":1}}`,
		"noTLSVerify true":         `{"ingress":[{"hostname":"a.example.com","originRequest":{"noTLSVerify":true},"service":"http://a:80"},` + inEnd + `],"warp-routing":{"enabled":true,"x":1}}`,
		"a changed unnamed member": `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inEnd + `],"warp-routing":{"enabled":false,"x":1}}`,
		"rule order":               `{"ingress":[` + inEnd + `,` + inA + `],"warp-routing":{"enabled":true,"x":1}}`,
		"an added rule":            `{"ingress":[` + inA + `,` + inB + `,` + inEnd + `],"warp-routing":{"enabled":true,"x":1}}`,
	}
	for name, src := range differs {
		if got := Hash(inRead(t, src)); got == h {
			t.Errorf("%s leaves the hash unchanged", name)
		}
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `internal/modules/cloudflare/ingress/ingress.go` (package `ingress`, a package doc comment, a doc comment on every exported identifier, error strings starting `ingress: `).

1. Types. `const CatchAll = "http_status:404"`. `Rule` has the four exported fields of Contracts plus two unexported maps, `extra` (the rule's members other than `hostname`, `path`, `service` and `originRequest`) and `originExtra` (the members of its `originRequest` other than `noTLSVerify`), each a `map[string]json.RawMessage` holding the raw values as read. `Config` has `Ingress []Rule` and an unexported `extra map[string]json.RawMessage` for every top-level member other than `ingress`. The raw values are what makes unnamed members survive an edit unchanged.
2. One private encode helper that every marshal and `Hash` uses: a `json.Encoder` with `SetEscapeHTML(false)` whose trailing newline is trimmed. A comment states why: `json.Marshal` re-escapes `<`, `>` and `&` inside a `Marshaler`'s output, which would alter raw members; the test therefore calls `MarshalJSON` directly. Encoding a map of `json.RawMessage` emits its keys sorted, so every object `MarshalJSON` builds has sorted keys.
3. `Rule.MarshalJSON` (value receiver) emits a sorted-key object: the `extra` members verbatim; `hostname` and `path` only when non-empty; `service` always; `originRequest` only when `NoTLSVerify` is true or `originExtra` is not empty, holding `originExtra` verbatim plus `"noTLSVerify":true` when set. `NoTLSVerify` false is never written, so an explicit `false` and an absent member are the same rule.
4. `Rule.UnmarshalJSON` (pointer receiver) first resets the receiver, decodes the object into `map[string]json.RawMessage`, decodes `hostname`, `path` and `service` as strings, decodes `originRequest` as an object and its `noTLSVerify` as a bool, and keeps every other member of the rule and of `originRequest` in the two maps (nil when none). Any decoding failure is returned as `ingress: <detail>`; the error never starts `ingress: ingress:`.
5. `Config.MarshalJSON` (value receiver) emits a sorted-key object of the `extra` members verbatim plus `ingress` (the rules, in order) only when there is at least one rule, so an empty configuration marshals as `{}`. `Config.UnmarshalJSON` (pointer receiver) resets the receiver, treats the literal `null` as an empty configuration, decodes the object, decodes `ingress` as a list of `Rule` (absent, `null` and `[]` all give no rules), and keeps the other members in `extra`. Errors are `ingress: ...` once, whether they come from the configuration or from a rule.
6. `Lookup(c, hostname)` returns the first rule whose hostname equals `hostname` ignoring case; an empty `hostname` never matches (the catch-all is not found by it).
7. `Add(c, r)`: a rule with an empty `Hostname` is refused with `ingress: a rule needs a hostname`, an empty `Service` with `ingress: a rule needs a service`. When `Lookup` finds a rule for the hostname: if its path, service and `NoTLSVerify` equal `r`'s it returns `c` unchanged with `changed` false; otherwise it is the error `ingress: hostname "<hostname>" already has a different rule`. Otherwise it returns a new configuration (all other members kept) whose rule list is a fresh slice, never sharing the argument's backing array: `r` is inserted before the catch-all, where the catch-all is the last rule when that rule has neither hostname nor path, so an operator's own last rule such as `http_status:503` counts and no second one is added; when the last rule is not a catch-all, `r` and a `Rule{Service: CatchAll}` are appended. `changed` is true. On any error the result is the zero `Config` and `changed` is false.
8. `Remove(c, hostname)` drops every rule whose hostname equals `hostname` ignoring case, into a fresh slice with the other rules carried over unchanged. An empty `hostname`, or one no rule has, returns `c` and `false`; the catch-all is therefore never dropped.
9. `Hash(c)` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `c`: take `c.MarshalJSON()`, decode it into `any` with `UseNumber` (so numbers keep their text), and encode it again with the helper of item 2, which sorts the keys of every nested object, including the raw members. Equal configurations that differ only in member order or whitespace hash alike, and so do an empty `ingress` and an absent one. The encoding cannot fail for a value built by `UnmarshalJSON` or from strings and booleans; `Hash` panics with an `ingress:` message rather than hash nothing.

Create `web/src/modules/docker/stream.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { act, renderHook } from "@testing-library/react"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { EvtSource } from "@/test/evt-source"
import { streamUrl, useStream, type StreamEnd } from "./stream"

interface StEvent {
  n: number
}

function stSource(index = 0): EvtSource {
  const source = EvtSource.instances[index]
  if (source === undefined) throw new Error(`no stream ${index} was opened`)
  return source
}

test("streamUrl addresses a module stream of a host with its parameters", () => {
  expect(streamUrl("h1", "docker", "logs", { container: "web", tail: "200" })).toBe("/api/v1/hosts/h1/streams/docker/logs?container=web&tail=200")
  expect(streamUrl("h1", "docker", "stats", {})).toBe("/api/v1/hosts/h1/streams/docker/stats")
})

test("streamUrl escapes the host id and the parameter values", () => {
  expect(streamUrl("h 1", "docker", "logs", { container: "a&b=c d" })).toBe("/api/v1/hosts/h%201/streams/docker/logs?container=a%26b%3Dc+d")
})

test("a null url opens no stream", () => {
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useStream<StEvent>(null))
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(0)
  expect(result.current).toEqual({ events: [], end: null })
})

test("data events are collected in order from one EventSource", () => {
  const { result, rerender } = renderHook(() => useStream<StEvent>("/s/1"))
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(1)
  expect(stSource().url).toBe("/s/1")
  act(() => {
    stSource().emit("data", { n: 1 })
    stSource().emit("data", { n: 2 })
  })
  expect(result.current.events).toEqual([{ n: 1 }, { n: 2 }])
  expect(result.current.end).toBeNull()
  rerender()
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(1)
  expect(result.current.events).toHaveLength(2)
})

test("only the last max events are kept", () => {
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useStream<StEvent>("/s/1", 3))
  act(() => {
    for (let n = 1; n <= 5; n++) stSource().emit("data", { n })
  })
  expect(result.current.events).toEqual([{ n: 3 }, { n: 4 }, { n: 5 }])
})

test("an end event is recorded and closes the stream", () => {
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useStream<StEvent>("/s/1"))
  act(() => {
    stSource().emit("data", { n: 1 })
    stSource().emit("end", { reason: "done" })
  })
  expect(result.current.end).toEqual({ reason: "done" })
  expect(stSource().closed).toBe(true)
  act(() => stSource().emit("data", { n: 2 }))
  expect(result.current.events).toEqual([{ n: 1 }])
})

test("an end event keeps the problem the agent sent", () => {
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useStream<StEvent>("/s/1"))
  const end: StreamEnd = { reason: "error", error: { type: "about:blank", title: "Unavailable", status: 503, detail: "the Docker daemon is not running", code: "docker.engine_unavailable" } }
  act(() => stSource().emit("end", end))
  expect(result.current.end).toEqual(end)
})

test("a failed connection ends the stream with the error reason instead of reconnecting", () => {
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useStream<StEvent>("/s/1"))
  act(() => stSource().fail())
  expect(result.current.end).toEqual({ reason: "error" })
  expect(stSource().closed).toBe(true)
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(1)
})

test("an event whose data is not JSON is dropped", () => {
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useStream<StEvent>("/s/1"))
  act(() => {
    stSource().emit("data", "not json")
    stSource().emit("data", { n: 1 })
  })
  expect(result.current.events).toEqual([{ n: 1 }])
})

test("a new url closes the old stream and starts again with no events and no end", () => {
  const { result, rerender } = renderHook(({ url }: { url: string | null }) => useStream<StEvent>(url), { initialProps: { url: "/s/1" as string | null } })
  act(() => {
    stSource(0).emit("data", { n: 1 })
    stSource(0).emit("end", { reason: "done" })
  })
  rerender({ url: "/s/2" })
  expect(stSource(0).closed).toBe(true)
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(2)
  expect(stSource(1).url).toBe("/s/2")
  expect(result.current).toEqual({ events: [], end: null })
  act(() => stSource(1).emit("data", { n: 7 }))
  expect(result.current.events).toEqual([{ n: 7 }])
  act(() => stSource(0).emit("data", { n: 99 }))
  expect(result.current.events).toEqual([{ n: 7 }])
  rerender({ url: null })
  expect(stSource(1).closed).toBe(true)
  expect(result.current).toEqual({ events: [], end: null })
})

test("unmounting closes the stream", () => {
  const { unmount } = renderHook(() => useStream<StEvent>("/s/1"))
  unmount()
  expect(stSource().closed).toBe(true)
})
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `types.ts`: the two constants (`DOCKER_MODULE = "docker"`, `DOCKER_ACTION_VERSION = 1`), `dockerKey(hostId, resource)` returning `["resource", hostId, "docker." + resource]` with `resource` the union `"engine" | "containers" | "images" | "networks" | "volumes" | "projects"` written in the signature, and one exported interface per name above. Each interface has exactly the JSON members of its Go struct in Contracts "Docker wire shapes", with the same names: a member with `omitempty` is optional (`?`), the rest are required; `time.Time` and `*time.Time` are `string`; `[]T` is `T[]`; `map[string]string` is `Record<string, string>`; `uint16`, `uint64`, `int` and `int64` are `number`. `LogLine.stream` and `LogEvent.stream` are `"stdout" | "stderr"`. `Pruned.images` is an inline list of `{ id: string; tags: string[]; size: number }`. The file imports nothing and exports no other name.
2. `fixtures.ts`: seven functions, each `(over: Partial<T> = {}) => T` returning a new object (new arrays too) with the defaults the tests pin, then `...over`. A private `IMAGE_ID` constant (`"sha256:" + "e3b0c442".repeat(8)`) is `dkContainer().imageId` and `dkImage().id`. The container id is `"a1b2c3d4".repeat(8)`. `dkDetail` builds its `id`, `name`, `image`, `imageId`, `created`, `state` and `ports` from `dkContainer()`, its mount from `dkVolume()` and its network from `dkNetwork()`, so the fixtures describe one `web` container; its two environment values are `[redacted]`. A test removes an optional member by passing it as `undefined`, which the spread already allows.
3. `stream.ts`:
   - `StreamEnd` as in Contracts. `streamUrl(hostId, module, name, params)` returns `/api/v1/hosts/<host>/streams/<module>/<name>` with each of the three segments `encodeURIComponent`-escaped, then `?` and `new URLSearchParams(params).toString()` only when that string is not empty.
   - `useStream<E>(url: string | null, max = 1000)` returns `{ events: E[]; end: StreamEnd | null }`. Keep one state value `{ url, events, end }` (a lint rule forbids resetting state inside an effect): when the state's `url` differs from the current `url`, the hook returns `{ events: [], end: null }`, and the first update from a new url starts from an empty state for that url.
   - An effect keyed on `url` and `max` opens one `new EventSource(url)` (nothing when `url` is null) and registers three listeners. `data`: parse the event's data as JSON and append it, keeping the last `max` events; an event whose data is not JSON is dropped; after an end nothing is appended. `end`: parse the data as a `StreamEnd` (when it is not JSON the end is `{ reason: "error" }`), close the source and record it. `error`: close the source and record `{ reason: "error" }` unless an end is already recorded, because every reconnect of a module stream replays it from the start and would duplicate the events.
   - A `live` flag, cleared in the effect's cleanup together with `source.close()`, makes every listener of a replaced or unmounted stream a no-op.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import type { Plan } from "@/api/types"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { tailnetKey } from "./types"
import { TailnetChange } from "./tailnet-change"

const TC_PLAN = "POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.authkey.create/v1/plan"
const TC_APPLY = "POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.authkey.create/v1/apply"
const TC_INPUT = { tags: ["tag:server"], expirySeconds: 3600 }

function tcPlan(over: Partial<Plan> = {}): Plan {
  return {
    planId: "p1", hostId: null, action: "tailnet.authkey.create", version: 1, inputHash: "h",
    diff: [{ op: "+", text: "create an auth key with tag:server" }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z", confirmation: null, ...over,
  }
}

const tcApplied = { id: "c1", hostId: null, state: "completed", class: "compensable", error: null, output: null, revertDeadline: null }

function TcHost({ bump }: { bump: (name: string) => number }) {
  const [input, setInput] = useState<Record<string, unknown> | null>(null)
  useQuery({ queryKey: tailnetKey("keys"), queryFn: () => Promise.resolve(bump("keys")) })
  useQuery({ queryKey: ["resource", "h1", "docker.engine"], queryFn: () => Promise.resolve(bump("engine")) })
  return (
    <>
      <button onClick={() => setInput(TC_INPUT)}>Open</button>
      <TailnetChange action="tailnet.authkey.create" title="Create an auth key" input={input} onClose={() => setInput(null)} />
    </>
  )
}

function tcRender(routes: Record<string, StubHandler>) {
  const calls = stubFetch({ "GET /api/v1/changes/c1": { body: { ...tcApplied, output: null } }, ...routes })
  const counts: Record<string, number> = {}
  const bump = (name: string) => (counts[name] = (counts[name] ?? 0) + 1)
  renderWithProviders(<TcHost bump={bump} />)
  return { calls, counts }
}

test("a null input opens no dialog and plans nothing", async () => {
  const { calls } = tcRender({ [TC_PLAN]: { body: tcPlan() } })
  await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Open" })).toBeTruthy())
  expect(screen.queryByRole("dialog")).toBeNull()
  expect(calls.filter((c) => c.method === "POST")).toHaveLength(0)
})

test("the dialog plans the action on the controller, without a host or an availability check", async () => {
  const { calls } = tcRender({ [TC_PLAN]: { body: tcPlan() } })
  await userEvent.setup().click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Open" }))
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Create an auth key" })
  expect(within(dialog).getByText("tailnet.authkey.create/v1 on the controller")).toBeTruthy()
  expect((await within(dialog).findByLabelText("Planned changes")).textContent).toBe("+ create an auth key with tag:server")
  const plans = calls.filter((c) => c.method === "POST")
  expect(plans.map((c) => [c.path, c.body])).toEqual([["/api/v1/actions/tailnet.authkey.create/v1/plan", { input: TC_INPUT }]])
  expect(calls.some((c) => c.path.includes("availability"))).toBe(false)
})

test("applying posts the plan without a revert timeout", async () => {
  const { calls } = tcRender({ [TC_PLAN]: { body: tcPlan() }, [TC_APPLY]: { body: tcApplied } })
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Open" }))
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Create an auth key" })
  const apply = await within(dialog).findByRole("button", { name: "Apply" })
  await waitFor(() => expect(apply.hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(false))
  await user.click(apply)
  await waitFor(() => expect(calls.some((c) => c.path === "/api/v1/actions/tailnet.authkey.create/v1/apply")).toBe(true))
  expect(calls.find((c) => c.path.endsWith("/apply"))?.body).toEqual({ planId: "p1" })
  expect(within(dialog).queryByLabelText("Revert after (seconds)")).toBeNull()
})

test("closing the dialog refetches the tailnet queries and no others", async () => {
  const { counts } = tcRender({ [TC_PLAN]: { body: tcPlan() } })
  const user = userEvent.setup()

When the dialog asks to close, it calls `onClose()` and then invalidates the queries whose key starts with `["tailnet"]` through `useQueryClient().invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["tailnet"] })`; it does not invalidate anything else.

import { useState } from "react"
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"

import type { Change, Plan } from "@/api/types"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { CloudflareChange } from "./cloudflare-change"
import { cloudflareKey } from "./types"

const CC_PLAN = "POST /api/v1/actions/cloudflare.hostname.add/v1/plan"
const CC_APPLY = "POST /api/v1/actions/cloudflare.hostname.add/v1/apply"
const CC_INPUT = { tunnel: "darkpanel-01JD0000000000000000000001", hostname: "app.example.com", service: "http://172.18.0.2:8080" }

function ccPlan(over: Partial<Plan> = {}): Plan {
  return {
    planId: "p-hn", hostId: null, action: "cloudflare.hostname.add", version: 1, inputHash: "h",
    diff: [{ op: "+", text: "route app.example.com to http://172.18.0.2:8080" }], guards: [],
    expiresAt: "2026-10-30T13:00:00Z", confirmation: null, ...over,
  }
}

function ccChange(over: Partial<Change> = {}): Change {
  return {
    id: "c-hn", hostId: null, action: "cloudflare.hostname.add", version: 1, class: "compensable", state: "completed", actor: "user:u1",
    createdAt: "2026-10-30T12:00:00Z", updatedAt: "2026-10-30T12:00:00Z", revertDeadline: null, output: null, error: null,
    compensatedBy: null, parentChangeId: null, owner: null, repairedBy: null, repairOutcome: null, override: null, ...over,
  }
}

function CcHost({ onClosed }: { onClosed: () => void }) {
  const [input, setInput] = useState<Record<string, unknown> | null>(null)
  return (
    <>
      <button onClick={() => setInput(CC_INPUT)}>Open</button>
      <CloudflareChange
        action="cloudflare.hostname.add"
        title="Add hostname"
        input={input}
        onClose={() => {
          setInput(null)
          onClosed()
        }}
      />
    </>
  )
}

function ccRender(routes: Record<string, StubHandler>) {
  const calls = stubFetch(routes)
  const closed = { count: 0 }
  const result = renderWithProviders(<CcHost onClosed={() => (closed.count += 1)} />)
  result.client.setQueryData(cloudflareKey("hostnames"), { hostnames: [] })
  result.client.setQueryData(["tailnet", "account"], { connected: false })
  return { calls, closed, ...result }
}

test("a null input keeps the dialog closed and plans nothing", () => {
  const { calls } = ccRender({ [CC_PLAN]: { body: ccPlan() } })
  expect(screen.queryByRole("dialog")).toBeNull()
  expect(calls).toHaveLength(0)
})

test("plans on the controller, shows the diff and applies the plan", async () => {
  const { calls } = ccRender({ [CC_PLAN]: { body: ccPlan() }, [CC_APPLY]: { body: ccChange() } })
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Open" }))
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Add hostname" })

  expect((await within(dialog).findByLabelText("Planned changes")).textContent).toBe("+ route app.example.com to http://172.18.0.2:8080")
  const apply = await within(dialog).findByRole("button", { name: "Apply" })
  await waitFor(() => expect(apply.hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(false))
  await user.click(apply)
  expect((await within(dialog).findByText("completed")).textContent).toBe("completed")
  expect(calls.filter((c) => c.method === "POST").map((c) => [c.path, c.body])).toEqual([
    ["/api/v1/actions/cloudflare.hostname.add/v1/plan", { input: CC_INPUT }],
    ["/api/v1/actions/cloudflare.hostname.add/v1/apply", { planId: "p-hn" }],
  ])
  expect(calls.some((c) => c.path.includes("/availability"))).toBe(false)

test("closing the dialog calls onClose once and refreshes the Cloudflare queries only", async () => {

  const { closed, client } = ccRender({ [CC_PLAN]: refusal })

  await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByRole("dialog")).toBeNull())
  expect(closed.count).toBe(1)
  expect(client.getQueryState(cloudflareKey("hostnames"))?.isInvalidated).toBe(true)
})

test("the open dialog has no accessibility violations", async () => {
  ccRender({ [CC_PLAN]: { body: ccPlan() } })
  await userEvent.setup().click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Open" }))
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Add hostname" })
  await within(dialog).findByLabelText("Planned changes")
  expect(await axe(dialog)).toHaveNoViolations()
})

### Task 11: logfilter: mask registered secrets across log frames

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/docker/logfilter/logfilter.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/docker/logfilter/logfilter_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing; the package imports only the standard library.
- Produces: Contracts "logfilter" exactly as stated there: `const Mask = "[redacted]"`, `type Filter`, `func New(secrets [][]byte) *Filter`, `func (f *Filter) Push(stream string, data []byte) []byte`, `func (f *Filter) Flush(stream string) []byte`. Tasks 25 and 36 build a filter per request from `deps.secrets` and pass every log frame of a Darkpanel-owned container through `Push` (and `Flush` at the end of the stream). Semantics this task fixes, which those tasks rely on:
  - A filter is not safe for concurrent use; a caller makes one per request and calls it from one goroutine.
  - Each stream name (`"stdout"`, `"stderr"`, any other string) has its own held bytes, so a secret is never joined across two streams.
  - Matching is left to right over the held bytes plus the new data. At each position the longest secret that starts there is replaced by `Mask` and scanning resumes after it, so matches never overlap.
  - Before a match is decided at a position, if the bytes from there to the end of the data are a proper prefix of some secret, nothing from that position on is emitted; those bytes are held. This holds even when a shorter secret already matches there, because a longer one may still complete. The first such position is the longest held suffix.
  - `Flush` runs the same scan with holding switched off: a complete secret in the held bytes becomes `Mask`, any other held bytes (a partial secret, which the container never finished writing) are returned unchanged, and the stream's held bytes are forgotten.
  - `New` ignores empty secrets and copies the others, so a caller that clears its slices afterwards does not change the filter. With no secret left, `Push` returns `data` as it is and holds nothing.

**Depends on:** none
**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
