```go
package logfilter

import (
	"math/rand/v2"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func lfSecrets(ss ...string) [][]byte {
	out := make([][]byte, len(ss))
	for i, s := range ss {
		out[i] = []byte(s)
	}
	return out
}

// lfRun pushes each chunk to stdout in order, flushes stdout, and returns
// everything emitted.
func lfRun(f *Filter, chunks ...string) string {
	var out strings.Builder
	for _, c := range chunks {
		out.Write(f.Push("stdout", []byte(c)))
	}
	out.Write(f.Flush("stdout"))
	return out.String()
}

func TestLfMaskValue(t *testing.T) {
	if Mask != "[redacted]" {
		t.Errorf("Mask = %q, want [redacted]", Mask)
	}
}

func TestLfWithoutSecretsDataPassesUnchanged(t *testing.T) {
	for name, f := range map[string]*Filter{
		"nil":           New(nil),
		"empty list":    New([][]byte{}),
		"empty secrets": New([][]byte{nil, {}}),
	} {
		if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("se"))); got != "se" {
			t.Errorf("%s: Push returned %q, want the data at once", name, got)
		}
		if got := string(f.Flush("stdout")); got != "" {
			t.Errorf("%s: Flush returned %q, want nothing held", name, got)
		}
	}
}

// lfCases are masked whole and at every split of the input into two or three
// pushes. The expected text is for the leftmost occurrence, the longest
// secret at that position, and scanning that resumes after the match.
var lfCases = []struct {
	name    string
	secrets []string
	text    string
	want    string
}{
	{"one occurrence", []string{"hunter2"}, "pw=hunter2 ok\n", "pw=[redacted] ok\n"},
	{"repeated and adjacent", []string{"hunter2"}, "hunter2hunter2 x hunter2", "[redacted][redacted] x [redacted]"},
	{"two secrets", []string{"alpha", "beta"}, "alpha beta gamma alphabeta", "[redacted] [redacted] gamma [redacted][redacted]"},
	{"one secret is a prefix of another", []string{"abc", "abcdef"}, "xabcdefy abcz abc", "x[redacted]y [redacted]z [redacted]"},
	{"the longer secret wins at one position", []string{"toke", "token"}, "token tokex", "[redacted] [redacted]x"},
	{"a false start is released", []string{"secret"}, "sesame secrecy secret", "sesame secrecy [redacted]"},
	{"a secret at the very end", []string{"end"}, "the end", "the [redacted]"},
	{"matches do not overlap", []string{"aa"}, "aaa", "[redacted]a"},
	{"a partial secret at the end stays", []string{"secret"}, "tail se", "tail se"},
	{"binary secret", []string{"\xff\x00k"}, "v=\xff\x00k;", "v=[redacted];"},
	{"secret with a newline", []string{"a\nb"}, "x a\nb y", "x [redacted] y"},
	{"nothing to mask", []string{"hunter2"}, "plain log line\n", "plain log line\n"},
}

func TestLfMasksWhole(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range lfCases {
		if got := lfRun(New(lfSecrets(c.secrets...)), c.text); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: got %q, want %q", c.name, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestLfMasksAtEverySplit(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range lfCases {
		for i := 0; i <= len(c.text); i++ {
			if got := lfRun(New(lfSecrets(c.secrets...)), c.text[:i], c.text[i:]); got != c.want {
				t.Errorf("%s: split at %d: got %q, want %q", c.name, i, got, c.want)
			}
			for j := i; j <= len(c.text); j++ {
				if got := lfRun(New(lfSecrets(c.secrets...)), c.text[:i], c.text[i:j], c.text[j:]); got != c.want {
					t.Errorf("%s: splits at %d and %d: got %q, want %q", c.name, i, j, got, c.want)
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestLfRandomSplitsAgreeAndLeakNothing(t *testing.T) {
	secrets := []string{"xy", "xyz", "zx"}
	r := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(7, 11)) //nolint:gosec // G404: a fixed seed makes the cases reproducible
	for n := 0; n < 500; n++ {
		var text strings.Builder
		for k := r.IntN(40); k > 0; k-- {
			text.WriteByte("xyzw"[r.IntN(4)])
		}
		var chunks []string
		rest := text.String()
		for len(rest) > 0 {
			cut := 1 + r.IntN(len(rest))
			chunks = append(chunks, rest[:cut])
			rest = rest[cut:]
		}
		whole := lfRun(New(lfSecrets(secrets...)), text.String())
		split := lfRun(New(lfSecrets(secrets...)), chunks...)
		if split != whole {
			t.Fatalf("text %q in chunks %q: got %q, whole push gives %q", text.String(), chunks, split, whole)
		}
		visible := strings.ReplaceAll(split, Mask, "|")
		for _, s := range secrets {
			if strings.Contains(visible, s) {
				t.Fatalf("text %q in chunks %q: output %q still holds %q", text.String(), chunks, split, s)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestLfHoldsBackOnlyTheLongestPrefixSuffix(t *testing.T) {
	f := New(lfSecrets("secret"))
	if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("abc se"))); got != "abc " {
		t.Errorf("first push returned %q, want %q", got, "abc ")
	}
	if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("cret ok"))); got != "[redacted] ok" {
		t.Errorf("second push returned %q, want %q", got, "[redacted] ok")
	}

	f = New(lfSecrets("secret"))
	if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("se"))); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("a prefix of the secret was emitted: %q", got)
	}
	if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("x"))); got != "sex" {
		t.Errorf("a false start returned %q, want %q", got, "sex")
	}

	f = New(lfSecrets("ab"))
	if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("aaaa"))); got != "aaa" {
		t.Errorf("repeated first bytes returned %q, want %q", got, "aaa")
	}
	if got := string(f.Flush("stdout")); got != "a" {
		t.Errorf("Flush returned %q, want %q", got, "a")
	}
}

func TestLfStreamsAreIndependent(t *testing.T) {
	f := New(lfSecrets("token"))
	if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("to"))); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("stdout returned %q, want the prefix held", got)
	}
	if got := string(f.Push("stderr", []byte("ken"))); got != "ken" {
		t.Errorf("stderr returned %q, want %q: stdout's held bytes are not stderr's", got, "ken")
	}
	if got := string(f.Flush("stderr")); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("stderr Flush returned %q, want nothing", got)
	}
	if got := string(f.Flush("stdout")); got != "to" {
		t.Errorf("stdout Flush returned %q, want %q", got, "to")
	}
}

func TestLfFlushMasksAHeldSecretAndForgets(t *testing.T) {
	f := New(lfSecrets("abc", "abcdef"))
	if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("xabc"))); got != "x" {
		t.Errorf("Push returned %q, want %q: abc may still grow into abcdef", got, "x")
	}
	if got := string(f.Flush("stdout")); got != "[redacted]" {
		t.Errorf("Flush returned %q, want %q", got, "[redacted]")
	}
	if got := string(f.Flush("stdout")); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("a second Flush returned %q, want nothing", got)
	}
	if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("def"))); got != "def" {
		t.Errorf("after Flush a push returned %q, want the earlier bytes forgotten", got)
	}
}

func TestLfNewCopiesTheSecrets(t *testing.T) {
	s := []byte("hunter2")
	f := New([][]byte{s})
	clear(s)
	if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("pw=hunter2"))); got != "pw=[redacted]" {
		t.Errorf("Push returned %q after the caller cleared its slice", got)
	}
}
```

Run: `mkdir -p /root/.cache/w3-tmp/11 && export TMPDIR=/root/.cache/w3-tmp/11 GOTOOLCHAIN=local && timeout 300 go test -count=1 ./internal/modules/docker/logfilter`
Expected: FAIL to build with `undefined: Filter`, `undefined: Mask` and `undefined: New`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `logfilter.go` starts with a package doc comment ("Package logfilter masks secrets that a module registered for a container in the container's log frames."). Declare `Mask`, the `Filter` struct and `New`, with a doc comment on each exported identifier.
2. `Filter` keeps the non-empty secrets (each a copy) and a map from stream name to the bytes held for it. `New` skips `nil` and zero-length secrets and returns a usable filter for an empty list.
3. One unexported scan function takes the bytes (held plus new data) and a flag for "final". It walks the bytes with an index. At each position, when not final, it checks whether the remaining bytes are shorter than some secret and are a prefix of it (`bytes.HasPrefix(secret, rest)` with `len(secret) > len(rest)`); if so it stops and returns the output so far and a copy of the remaining bytes as the held bytes. Otherwise it finds the longest secret for which `bytes.HasPrefix(rest, secret)`; if there is one it appends `Mask` and advances by its length; if not it appends the byte and advances by one. It returns the output and the held bytes (none when final).
4. `Push`: with no secrets return `data`. Otherwise scan the stream's held bytes followed by `data` (build a new slice; never append into the caller's `data`), store the returned held bytes for the stream (delete the map entry when none), and return the output.
5. `Flush`: take and delete the stream's held bytes and return the final scan of them (empty, not an error, when nothing was held).
6. The scan is quadratic only in the secret count times the buffer length, which is acceptable for log frames of at most a few hundred kilobytes; do not add an index, an automaton or concurrency. No comment explains what the code does; one comment states why a shorter match does not stop the holding (a longer secret may still complete).

The module's `Manifest()` is not changed: Task 57 registers `Migrations[core.SideController] = controllerMigrations()`. Decisions this task fixes, which Tasks 39–57 rely on:
  - Times are stored as fixed-width UTC text, layout `2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z`, so they sort as text; they load as UTC `time.Time` values equal to the stored instant.
  - The lists (`TagsAllowed`, `Capabilities`, `Tags`) are stored as JSON arrays; `nil` is stored as `[]` and always loads as an empty non-nil slice, so an account or a key row encodes as `[]`, never `null`.

It runs in the caller's transaction, sees that transaction's own writes, writes nothing, and returns an empty list when nothing blocks.

```go
package tailnet

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/store"
)

var tnT0 = time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

// tnHost is the controller side of one module test: a database with the core
// and tailnet migrations, a fake clock and an in-memory effects journal.
type tnHost struct {
	db      *store.DB
	clock   *coretest.FakeClock
	journal *tnJournal
}

func newTNHost(t *testing.T) *tnHost {
	t.Helper()
	return &tnHost{db: tnDB(t), clock: coretest.NewFakeClock(tnT0), journal: &tnJournal{}}
}

// env is the call environment of a controller-side action. The journal is
// attached only for a change; a plan or a read has none.
func (h *tnHost) env(changeID string) core.Env {
	env := core.Env{
		ChangeID:  changeID,
		Principal: core.Principal{Actor: "user:u1", UserID: "u1", Scope: core.ScopeAdmin},
		DB:        h.db,
		Sealer:    coretest.Sealer{},
		Clock:     h.clock,
		Log:       slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil)),
	}
	if changeID != "" {
		h.journal.changeID = changeID
		env.Effects = h.journal
	}
	return env
}

// tnJournal is an in-memory core.EffectJournal that keeps each effect's
// secret, as the real one does sealed.
type tnJournal struct {
	changeID string
	list     []core.Effect
	secrets  map[int][]byte
}

func (j *tnJournal) Intend(_ context.Context, e core.Effect, secret []byte) (int, error) {
	e.ChangeID, e.Seq, e.State = j.changeID, len(j.list)+1, core.EffectIntended
	j.list = append(j.list, e)
	if secret != nil {
		if j.secrets == nil {
			j.secrets = map[int][]byte{}
		}
		j.secrets[e.Seq] = append([]byte(nil), secret...)
	}
	return e.Seq, nil
}

func (j *tnJournal) intended(seq int) (*core.Effect, error) {
	if seq < 1 || seq > len(j.list) || j.list[seq-1].State != core.EffectIntended {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("fake: effect %d is not intended", seq)
	}
	return &j.list[seq-1], nil
}

func (j *tnJournal) Made(_ context.Context, seq int, resource string, post core.StateDoc) error {
	e, err := j.intended(seq)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	e.State, e.Resource, e.Post = core.EffectMade, resource, &post
	return nil
}

func (j *tnJournal) Skipped(_ context.Context, seq int) error {
	e, err := j.intended(seq)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	e.State = core.EffectSkipped
	return nil
}

func (j *tnJournal) List(context.Context) ([]core.Effect, error) { return j.effects(), nil }

func (j *tnJournal) Secret(_ context.Context, seq int) ([]byte, error) {
	if seq < 1 || seq > len(j.list) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("fake: no effect %d", seq)
	}
	return j.secrets[seq], nil
}

// effects are the journaled effects in the order intended.
func (j *tnJournal) effects() []core.Effect { return append([]core.Effect(nil), j.list...) }

func TestTnHostEnvAndJournal(t *testing.T) {
	h := newTNHost(t)
	if e := h.env(""); e.Effects != nil || e.ChangeID != "" {
		t.Errorf("env(\"\") = change %q, journal %v, want neither", e.ChangeID, e.Effects)
	}

	env := h.env("c1")
	if env.ChangeID != "c1" || env.HostID != "" || env.Principal.Scope != core.ScopeAdmin || env.DB != h.db || env.Effects == nil || env.Log == nil {
		t.Fatalf("env(c1) = %+v", env)
	}
	if !env.Clock.Now().Equal(tnT0) {
		t.Errorf("clock reads %v, want %v", env.Clock.Now(), tnT0)
	}
	ct, err := env.Sealer.Seal("ad", []byte("x"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if pt, err := env.Sealer.Open("ad", ct); err != nil || string(pt) != "x" {
		t.Errorf("sealer round trip = %q, %v", pt, err)
	}

	ctx := context.Background()
	first, err := env.Effects.Intend(ctx, core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectModify, Resource: "tailnet.policy:example.com"}, []byte("before text"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	second, err := env.Effects.Intend(ctx, core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: "tailnet.key:?darkpanel-c1"}, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if first != 1 || second != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("seqs = %d, %d, want 1, 2", first, second)
	}
	post := core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(`{"policy":{}}`), Version: json.RawMessage(`"etag-2"`)}
	if err := env.Effects.Made(ctx, first, "tailnet.policy:example.com", post); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := env.Effects.Skipped(ctx, second); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := env.Effects.Made(ctx, first, "tailnet.policy:example.com", post); err == nil {
		t.Error("an effect already made was made again")
	}
	got := h.journal.effects()
	if len(got) != 2 || got[0].ChangeID != "c1" || got[0].State != core.EffectMade || got[0].Post == nil || string(got[0].Post.Version) != `"etag-2"` || got[1].State != core.EffectSkipped {
		t.Errorf("effects = %+v", got)
	}
	if s, err := env.Effects.Secret(ctx, first); err != nil || string(s) != "before text" {
		t.Errorf("Secret = %q, %v", s, err)
	}
}
```

```go
package tailnet

// tnDB opens a temporary controller database with the core's and the
// tailnet's migrations applied.
func tnDB(t *testing.T) *store.DB {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	db, err := store.Open(ctx, filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "controller.db"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = db.Close() })
	set, err := store.CoreMigrations(store.SideController)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	res, err := store.Migrate(ctx, db, store.MigrateOptions{
		Side: store.SideController, BinaryVersion: "test", BackupRoot: filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "backups"),
		Keep: 5, Now: time.Now(),
	}, set, []store.MigrationSet{{Module: ID, FS: controllerMigrations()}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(res.Failed) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("tailnet migrations failed: %v", res.Failed[0].Err)
	}
	return db
}

func tnWrite(t *testing.T, db *store.DB, fn func(tx *sql.Tx) error) error {
	t.Helper()
	return db.Write(context.Background(), fn)
}

func tnExec(t *testing.T, db *store.DB, query string, args ...any) error {
	t.Helper()
	return tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		_, err := tx.Exec(query, args...)
		return err
	})
}

func TestTnMigrationCreatesStrictTables(t *testing.T) {
	db := tnDB(t)
	columns := func(table string) []string {
		rows, err := db.Read().Query(`SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info(?) ORDER BY cid`, table)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
		var out []string
		for rows.Next() {
			var name string
			if err := rows.Scan(&name); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			out = append(out, name)
		}
		return out
	}
	wantAccounts := []string{"id", "tailnet", "client_id", "client_secret_ct", "tags_allowed_json", "capabilities_json", "connected_at"}
	if got := columns("tailnet_accounts"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, wantAccounts) {
		t.Errorf("tailnet_accounts columns = %v, want %v", got, wantAccounts)
	}
	wantKeys := []string{"description", "kind", "owner_id", "requested_at", "expiry_seconds", "tags_json", "key_id", "state", "updated_at"}
	if got := columns("tailnet_keys"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, wantKeys) {
		t.Errorf("tailnet_keys columns = %v, want %v", got, wantKeys)
	}
	for _, table := range []string{"tailnet_accounts", "tailnet_keys"} {
		var strict int
		if err := db.Read().QueryRow(`SELECT strict FROM pragma_table_list WHERE name = ?`, table).Scan(&strict); err != nil || strict != 1 {
			t.Errorf("%s: strict = %d, %v, want 1", table, strict, err)
		}
	}
}

func TestTnMigrationConstraints(t *testing.T) {
	db := tnDB(t)
	insertKey := `INSERT INTO tailnet_keys (description, kind, owner_id, requested_at, expiry_seconds, tags_json, state, updated_at)
		VALUES (?, ?, 'o1', 't', 60, '[]', ?, 't')`
	if err := tnExec(t, db, insertKey, "darkpanel-c1", "change", "requested"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a valid key row: %v", err)
	}
	var keyID string
	if err := db.Read().QueryRow(`SELECT key_id FROM tailnet_keys`).Scan(&keyID); err != nil || keyID != "" {
		t.Errorf("key_id default = %q, %v, want empty", keyID, err)
	}
	for name, c := range map[string][]any{
		"an unknown kind":            {"darkpanel-c2", "other", "requested"},
		"an unknown state":           {"darkpanel-c2", "change", "gone"},
		"a description used already": {"darkpanel-c1", "enroll", "live"},
	} {
		if err := tnExec(t, db, insertKey, c...); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s was accepted", name)
		}
	}
	for _, state := range []string{"requested", "live", "uncertain", "used", "retired", "deleted"} {
		if err := tnExec(t, db, `UPDATE tailnet_keys SET state = ?`, state); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("state %q refused: %v", state, err)
		}
	}

	insertAccount := `INSERT INTO tailnet_accounts (id, tailnet, client_id, client_secret_ct, tags_allowed_json, capabilities_json, connected_at)
		VALUES (?, 'example.com', 'k', x'00', '[]', '[]', 't')`
	if err := tnExec(t, db, insertAccount, "c1"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a valid account row: %v", err)
	}
	if err := tnExec(t, db, insertAccount, "c2"); err == nil {
		t.Error("a second account row was accepted")
	}
}

func TestTnAccountRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	db := tnDB(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, ok, err := loadAccount(ctx, db.Read()); err != nil || ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadAccount on an empty table = ok %v, err %v", ok, err)
	}
	want := tnAccount("01JD0000000000000000000001")
	if err := tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertAccount(ctx, tx, want) }); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got, ok, err := loadAccount(ctx, db.Read())
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadAccount = ok %v, err %v", ok, err)
	}
	if !got.ConnectedAt.Equal(want.ConnectedAt) {
		t.Errorf("ConnectedAt = %v, want %v", got.ConnectedAt, want.ConnectedAt)
	}
	got.ConnectedAt, want.ConnectedAt = time.Time{}, time.Time{}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("loaded %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}

	var raw string
	if err := db.Read().QueryRow(`SELECT connected_at FROM tailnet_accounts`).Scan(&raw); err != nil || raw != "2026-10-30T12:00:00.123456789Z" {
		t.Errorf("stored connected_at = %q, %v, want fixed-width UTC text", raw, err)
	}

	err = tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := insertAccount(ctx, tx, tnAccount("01JD0000000000000000000002")); err == nil {
			t.Error("a second account was inserted")
		}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if again, _, _ := loadAccount(ctx, db.Read()); again.ID != "01JD0000000000000000000001" {
		t.Errorf("the account is %q after a refused insert, want the first", again.ID)
	}
}

func TestTnKeyRoundTripAndOrder(t *testing.T) {
	db := tnDB(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, ok, err := loadKey(ctx, db.Read(), "darkpanel-none"); err != nil || ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadKey of an absent key = ok %v, err %v", ok, err)
	}
	late := tnKey("darkpanel-c3", "live", tnT0.Add(2*time.Minute))
	late.KeyID = "kid-3"
	rows := []keyRow{late, tnKey("darkpanel-c2", "requested", tnT0), tnKey("darkpanel-c1", "uncertain", tnT0)}
	rows[2].Kind, rows[2].Tags = "enroll", nil
	for _, r := range rows {
		if err := tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertKey(ctx, tx, r) }); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	got, err := listKeys(ctx, db.Read())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var order []string
	for _, k := range got {
		order = append(order, k.Description)
	}
	if want := []string{"darkpanel-c1", "darkpanel-c2", "darkpanel-c3"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(order, want) {
		t.Errorf("listKeys order = %v, want by requested_at then description %v", order, want)
	}

	one, ok, err := loadKey(ctx, db.Read(), "darkpanel-c3")
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadKey = ok %v, err %v", ok, err)
	}
	if !one.RequestedAt.Equal(late.RequestedAt) || !one.UpdatedAt.Equal(late.UpdatedAt) {
		t.Errorf("times = %v, %v, want %v", one.RequestedAt, one.UpdatedAt, late.RequestedAt)
	}
	one.RequestedAt, one.UpdatedAt, late.RequestedAt, late.UpdatedAt = time.Time{}, time.Time{}, time.Time{}, time.Time{}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(one, late) {
		t.Errorf("loaded %+v, want %+v", one, late)
	}
	if empty, _, _ := loadKey(ctx, db.Read(), "darkpanel-c1"); empty.Tags == nil || len(empty.Tags) != 0 || empty.Kind != "enroll" {
		t.Errorf("a key without tags loads Tags %#v, kind %q, want an empty list and enroll", empty.Tags, empty.Kind)
	}

	for name, r := range map[string]keyRow{
		"a description used already": tnKey("darkpanel-c1", "live", tnT0),
		"an unknown state":           tnKey("darkpanel-c9", "gone", tnT0),
	} {
		if err := tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertKey(ctx, tx, r) }); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s was inserted", name)
		}
	}
}

func TestTnSetKeyState(t *testing.T) {
	db := tnDB(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	if err := tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertKey(ctx, tx, tnKey("darkpanel-c1", "requested", tnT0)) }); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	set := func(state, keyID string, at time.Time) error {
		return tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return setKeyState(ctx, tx, "darkpanel-c1", state, keyID, at) })
	}
	load := func() keyRow {
		k, ok, err := loadKey(ctx, db.Read(), "darkpanel-c1")
		if err != nil || !ok {
			t.Fatalf("loadKey = ok %v, err %v", ok, err)
		}
		return k
	}

	at := tnT0.Add(time.Minute)
	if err := set("live", "kid-1", at); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if k := load(); k.State != "live" || k.KeyID != "kid-1" || !k.UpdatedAt.Equal(at) || !k.RequestedAt.Equal(tnT0) {
		t.Errorf("after live: %+v", k)
	}
	at = at.Add(time.Hour)
	if err := set("used", "", at); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if k := load(); k.State != "used" || k.KeyID != "kid-1" || !k.UpdatedAt.Equal(at) {
		t.Errorf("an empty key id must keep the stored one: %+v", k)
	}

	before := load()
	if err := set("gone", "kid-2", at.Add(time.Hour)); err == nil {
		t.Error("an unknown state was set")
	}
	if got := load(); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, before) {
		t.Errorf("a refused state change wrote: %+v, was %+v", got, before)
	}
	err := tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return setKeyState(ctx, tx, "darkpanel-none", "live", "kid", at) })
	if err == nil {
		t.Error("a key that does not exist was updated")
	}
}

func TestTnCleanupPending(t *testing.T) {
	db := tnDB(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	pending := func() []string {
		var got []string
		err := tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
			var err error
			got, err = cleanupPending(ctx, tx)
			return err
		})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return got
	}
	if got := pending(); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("cleanupPending on an empty database = %v", got)
	}

	for i, state := range []string{"requested", "live", "uncertain", "used", "retired", "deleted"} {
		k := tnKey("darkpanel-k"+state, state, tnT0.Add(time.Duration(i)*time.Minute))
		if err := tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertKey(ctx, tx, k) }); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	want := []string{
		"key darkpanel-krequested is requested",
		"key darkpanel-kuncertain is uncertain",
		"key darkpanel-kretired is retired",
	}
	if got := pending(); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("keys: cleanupPending = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}

	tnEffect(t, db, "c1", 1, "tailnet.policy:example.com", "unresolved")
	tnEffect(t, db, "c1", 2, "tailnet.key:?darkpanel-c1", "made")
	tnEffect(t, db, "c2", 1, "cloudflare.tunnel:t1", "unresolved")
	tnEffect(t, db, "c2", 2, "tailnetx.policy:example.com", "unresolved")
	tnEffect(t, db, "c3", 1, "tailnet.device:n1", "unresolved")
	want = append(want, "effect c1#1 tailnet.policy:example.com is unresolved", "effect c3#1 tailnet.device:n1 is unresolved")
	if got := pending(); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("effects: cleanupPending = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestTnCleanupPendingSeesTheTransactionsOwnWrites(t *testing.T) {
	db := tnDB(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	err := tnWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := insertKey(ctx, tx, tnKey("darkpanel-c1", "requested", tnT0)); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		got, err := cleanupPending(ctx, tx)
		if want := []string{"key darkpanel-c1 is requested"}; err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("cleanupPending = %v, %v, want %v", got, err, want)
		}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

```go
package cloudflare

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/store"
)

// cfHost is a test controller: a database with the core and Cloudflare
// migrations, a manual clock and an in-memory effects journal.
type cfHost struct {
	db      *store.DB
	clock   *coretest.FakeClock
	journal *cfJournal
}

func newCFHost(t *testing.T) *cfHost {
	t.Helper()
	return &cfHost{
		db:      cfDB(t),
		clock:   coretest.NewFakeClock(time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)),
		journal: &cfJournal{},
	}
}

// env is the Env of an admin's controller-side change; Effects is the journal
// only when changeID is not empty.
func (h *cfHost) env(changeID string) core.Env {
	env := core.Env{
		Principal: core.Principal{Actor: "user:u1", Scope: core.ScopeAdmin},
		ChangeID:  changeID, DB: h.db, Sealer: coretest.Sealer{}, Clock: h.clock,
		Log: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil)),
	}
	if changeID != "" {
		h.journal.changeID = changeID
		env.Effects = h.journal
	}
	return env
}

// cfJournal is an in-memory core.EffectJournal.
type cfJournal struct {
	changeID string
	list     []core.Effect
	secrets  map[int][]byte
}

func (j *cfJournal) effects() []core.Effect { return append([]core.Effect(nil), j.list...) }

func (j *cfJournal) Intend(_ context.Context, e core.Effect, secret []byte) (int, error) {
	e.Seq, e.State, e.ChangeID = len(j.list)+1, core.EffectIntended, j.changeID
	j.list = append(j.list, e)
	if secret != nil {
		if j.secrets == nil {
			j.secrets = map[int][]byte{}
		}
		j.secrets[e.Seq] = append([]byte(nil), secret...)
	}
	return e.Seq, nil
}

func (j *cfJournal) find(seq int) (*core.Effect, error) {
	if seq < 1 || seq > len(j.list) || j.list[seq-1].State != core.EffectIntended {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("fake: effect %d is not intended", seq)
	}
	return &j.list[seq-1], nil
}

func (j *cfJournal) Made(_ context.Context, seq int, resource string, post core.StateDoc) error {
	e, err := j.find(seq)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	e.State, e.Resource, e.Post = core.EffectMade, resource, &post
	return nil
}

func (j *cfJournal) Skipped(_ context.Context, seq int) error {
	e, err := j.find(seq)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	e.State = core.EffectSkipped
	return nil
}

func (j *cfJournal) List(context.Context) ([]core.Effect, error) { return j.effects(), nil }

func (j *cfJournal) Secret(_ context.Context, seq int) ([]byte, error) {
	if s, ok := j.secrets[seq]; ok {
		return s, nil
	}
	return nil, errors.New("fake: no secret")
}

var _ core.EffectJournal = (*cfJournal)(nil)

// TestCFHostEnvAndJournal: env carries the host's database, sealer and clock,
// gives the journal only to a change, and the journal numbers effects from 1,
// moves them to made or skipped once, and keeps their secrets.
func TestCFHostEnvAndJournal(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newCFHost(t)
	if env := h.env(""); env.Effects != nil || env.DB != h.db || env.Sealer == nil || env.Clock == nil || env.ChangeID != "" {
		t.Errorf("env(\"\") = %+v", env)
	}
	env := h.env("c1")
	if env.Effects == nil || env.ChangeID != "c1" || env.Principal.Scope != core.ScopeAdmin {
		t.Fatalf("env(c1) = %+v", env)

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s2, _ := env.Effects.Intend(ctx, core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectModify, Resource: "cloudflare.ingress:t/h"}, nil)
	if s1 != 1 || s2 != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("seqs %d, %d; want 1, 2", s1, s2)
	}
	if err := env.Effects.Made(ctx, s1, "cloudflare.tunnel:t1", core.StateDoc{State: []byte(`{"name":"n"}`)}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := env.Effects.Skipped(ctx, s2); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := env.Effects.Skipped(ctx, s2); err == nil {
		t.Error("an effect was skipped twice")
	}
	got := h.journal.effects()
	if len(got) != 2 || got[0].State != core.EffectMade || got[0].Resource != "cloudflare.tunnel:t1" || got[0].Post == nil ||
		got[0].ChangeID != "c1" || got[1].State != core.EffectSkipped {
```

```go
package cloudflare

// cfDB opens a temporary controller database with the core's and the

func cfDB(t *testing.T) *store.DB {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	db, err := store.Open(ctx, filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "controller.db"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = db.Close() })
	set, err := store.CoreMigrations(store.SideController)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	res, err := store.Migrate(ctx, db, store.MigrateOptions{
		Side: store.SideController, BinaryVersion: "test", BackupRoot: filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "backups"),
		Keep: 5, Now: time.Now(),
	}, set, []store.MigrationSet{{Module: ID, FS: controllerMigrations()}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(res.Failed) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("cloudflare migrations failed: %v", res.Failed[0].Err)
	}
	return db
}

func cfAccount() account {
	return account{
		ID: "01J000000000000000000000A1", AccountID: "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef", TokenCT: []byte{0, 1, 2, 0xff},
		Capabilities: []cloud.Capability{
			{Name: "tunnels.read", State: cloud.CapabilityOK},
			{Name: "zones.read", State: cloud.CapabilityMissing, Detail: "cloud.permission_missing"},
			{Name: "tunnels.write", State: cloud.CapabilityUnverified},
		},
		ConnectedAt: cfT0,
	}
}

func cfTunnel(n int) tunnelRow {
	return tunnelRow{
		ID: fmt.Sprintf("tunnel-%d-0000", n), Name: fmt.Sprintf("darkpanel-01J00000000000000000000T%02d", n),
		ChangeID: fmt.Sprintf("01J00000000000000000000T%02d", n), CreatedAt: cfT0.Add(time.Duration(n) * time.Minute),
	}
}

func cfHostname(name, tunnelID, phase string) hostnameRow {
	return hostnameRow{Hostname: name, TunnelID: tunnelID, Service: "http://app:8080", Phase: phase, ChangeID: "01J00000000000000000000H01", UpdatedAt: cfT0}
}

// cfEffect inserts an effect row of a new change into core_effects.
func cfEffect(t *testing.T, db *store.DB, changeID string, seq int, resource, state string) {
	t.Helper()
	at := cfT0.Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z")
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO core_plans (id, host_id, action, version, actor, input_hash, state_hash,
			diff_json, guards_json, confirmation, created_at, expires_at)
			VALUES (?, '', 'cloudflare.tunnel.create', 1, 'user:u1', '', '', '[]', '[]', '', ?, ?)`, "p-"+changeID, at, at); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO core_changes (id, plan_id, host_id, action, version, class, compensated_by,
			actor, state, input_json, created_at, updated_at)
			VALUES (?, ?, '', 'cloudflare.tunnel.create', 1, 'compensable', '', 'user:u1', 'needs_repair', '{}', ?, ?)`,
			changeID, "p-"+changeID, at, at); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		_, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO core_effects (change_id, seq, kind, resource, local, inverse_local, before_json,
			state, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, 'create', ?, 0, 0, '{"state":null}', ?, ?, ?)`,
			changeID, seq, resource, state, at, at)
		return err
	})
}

// TestCFMigrationConstraints: the migration's own constraints hold, whatever
// the store functions check: one account row, unique tunnel names, a
// hostname's tunnel must exist, and the phase, health and flag columns take
// only their listed values.
func TestCFMigrationConstraints(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	db := cfDB(t)
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := insertAccount(ctx, tx, cfAccount()); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return insertTunnel(ctx, tx, cfTunnel(0))
	})
	tun := cfTunnel(0)
	cases := map[string]string{
		"second account": `INSERT INTO cloudflare_accounts (id, account_id, token_ct, capabilities_json, connected_at)
			VALUES ('other', 'x', x'00', '[]', '2026-10-30T12:00:00.000000000Z')`,
		"tunnel name taken": `INSERT INTO cloudflare_tunnels (id, name, change_id, created_at)
			VALUES ('other', '` + tun.Name + `', 'c', '2026-10-30T12:00:00.000000000Z')`,
		"drift 2": `INSERT INTO cloudflare_tunnels (id, name, change_id, drift, created_at)
			VALUES ('other', 'n', 'c', 2, '2026-10-30T12:00:00.000000000Z')`,
		"hostname without tunnel": `INSERT INTO cloudflare_hostnames (hostname, tunnel_id, service, phase, change_id, updated_at)
			VALUES ('a.example.com', 'missing', 's', 'active', 'c', '2026-10-30T12:00:00.000000000Z')`,
		"unknown phase": `INSERT INTO cloudflare_hostnames (hostname, tunnel_id, service, phase, change_id, updated_at)
			VALUES ('a.example.com', '` + tun.ID + `', 's', 'done', 'c', '2026-10-30T12:00:00.000000000Z')`,
		"unknown health": `INSERT INTO cloudflare_hostnames (hostname, tunnel_id, service, phase, change_id, health, updated_at)
			VALUES ('a.example.com', '` + tun.ID + `', 's', 'active', 'c', 'fine', '2026-10-30T12:00:00.000000000Z')`,
		"no_tls_verify 2": `INSERT INTO cloudflare_hostnames (hostname, tunnel_id, service, phase, change_id, no_tls_verify, updated_at)
			VALUES ('a.example.com', '` + tun.ID + `', 's', 'active', 'c', 2, '2026-10-30T12:00:00.000000000Z')`,
	}
	for name, q := range cases {
		err := db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, q); return err })
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: the insert succeeded", name)
		}
	}
	for _, table := range []string{"cloudflare_accounts", "cloudflare_tunnels", "cloudflare_hostnames"} {
		var strict int
		if err := db.Read().QueryRowContext(ctx, `SELECT strict FROM pragma_table_list(?)`, table).Scan(&strict); err != nil || strict != 1 {
			t.Errorf("%s: strict = %d, err %v; want a STRICT table", table, strict, err)
		}
	}
}

// TestCFAccountRoundTrip: an account is stored and read back whole, the
// sealed secret byte for byte, and a second account is refused.
func TestCFAccountRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	db := cfDB(t)
	if _, ok, err := loadAccount(ctx, db.Read()); err != nil || ok {
		t.Fatalf("empty database: ok %v, err %v", ok, err)
	}
	in := cfAccount()
	in.ConnectedAt = cfT0.In(time.FixedZone("x", 7*3600))
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertAccount(ctx, tx, in) })
	got, ok, err := loadAccount(ctx, db.Read())
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadAccount: ok %v, err %v", ok, err)
	}
	if got.ID != in.ID || got.AccountID != in.AccountID || !bytes.Equal(got.TokenCT, in.TokenCT) ||
		!reflect.DeepEqual(got.Capabilities, in.Capabilities) || !got.ConnectedAt.Equal(cfT0) {
		t.Errorf("loadAccount = %+v, want %+v", got, in)
	}
	err = db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		second := cfAccount()
		second.ID = "01J000000000000000000000A2"
		return insertAccount(ctx, tx, second)
	})
	if err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "cloudflare:") {
		t.Errorf("second insertAccount error = %v, want a cloudflare: error", err)
	}
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := deleteAccount(ctx, tx, "no-such-id"); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return deleteAccount(ctx, tx, in.ID)
	})
	if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(ctx, db.Read()); ok {
		t.Error("the account is still there after deleteAccount")
	}
}

// TestCFAccountWithoutCapabilities: an account with no capabilities is read
// back as an empty list, not an error.
func TestCFAccountWithoutCapabilities(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	db := cfDB(t)
	in := cfAccount()
	in.Capabilities = nil
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertAccount(ctx, tx, in) })
	got, ok, err := loadAccount(ctx, db.Read())
	if err != nil || !ok || len(got.Capabilities) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("loadAccount = %+v, %v, %v", got, ok, err)
	}
}

// TestCFTunnels: tunnels are found by id or by name and listed oldest first;
// the hash and the check are stored; a tunnel with hostnames cannot be
// deleted.
func TestCFTunnels(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	db := cfDB(t)
	t1, t0 := cfTunnel(1), cfTunnel(0)
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := insertTunnel(ctx, tx, t1); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return insertTunnel(ctx, tx, t0)
	})
	list, err := listTunnels(ctx, db.Read())
	if err != nil || len(list) != 2 || list[0].ID != t0.ID || list[1].ID != t1.ID {
		t.Fatalf("listTunnels = %+v, %v; want %s then %s", list, err, t0.ID, t1.ID)
	}
	for _, key := range []string{t0.ID, t0.Name} {
		got, ok, err := loadTunnel(ctx, db.Read(), key)
		if err != nil || !ok || got.ID != t0.ID || got.Name != t0.Name || got.ChangeID != t0.ChangeID ||
			!got.CreatedAt.Equal(t0.CreatedAt) || got.Drift || got.ConfigHash != "" || !got.CheckedAt.IsZero() {
			t.Errorf("loadTunnel(%q) = %+v, %v, %v", key, got, ok, err)
		}
	}
	if _, ok, err := loadTunnel(ctx, db.Read(), "missing"); err != nil || ok {
		t.Errorf("loadTunnel(missing): ok %v, err %v", ok, err)
	}

	checked := cfT0.Add(time.Hour)
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := setTunnelHash(ctx, tx, t0.ID, "abc123"); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return setTunnelCheck(ctx, tx, t0.ID, true, checked)
	})
	got, _, _ := loadTunnel(ctx, db.Read(), t0.ID)
	if got.ConfigHash != "abc123" || !got.Drift || !got.CheckedAt.Equal(checked) {
		t.Errorf("after setTunnelHash and setTunnelCheck: %+v", got)
	}
	other, _, _ := loadTunnel(ctx, db.Read(), t1.ID)
	if other.ConfigHash != "" || other.Drift {
		t.Errorf("another tunnel changed: %+v", other)
	}
	err = db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return setTunnelHash(ctx, tx, "missing", "x") })
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "missing") {
		t.Errorf("setTunnelHash of a missing tunnel: %v", err)
	}

	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
		return insertHostname(ctx, tx, cfHostname("a.example.com", t0.ID, "active"))
	})
	if err := db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return deleteTunnel(ctx, tx, t0.ID) }); err == nil {
		t.Error("deleteTunnel succeeded with a hostname row on the tunnel")
	}
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error { return deleteTunnel(ctx, tx, t1.ID) })
	if _, ok, _ := loadTunnel(ctx, db.Read(), t1.ID); ok {
		t.Error("the tunnel is still there after deleteTunnel")
	}
}

// TestCFHostnames: a hostname row is stored and read back, its phase moves
// with the zone and record ids kept when the call gives none, its health is
// recorded without touching its phase, and an unknown phase or hostname
// fails.
func TestCFHostnames(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	db := cfDB(t)
	tun := cfTunnel(0)
	in := cfHostname("b.example.com", tun.ID, "adding_rule")
	in.NoTLSVerify = true
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := insertTunnel(ctx, tx, tun); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := insertHostname(ctx, tx, cfHostname("c.example.com", tun.ID, "active")); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return insertHostname(ctx, tx, in)
	})
	list, err := listHostnames(ctx, db.Read())
	if err != nil || len(list) != 2 || list[0].Hostname != "b.example.com" || list[1].Hostname != "c.example.com" {
		t.Fatalf("listHostnames = %+v, %v; want b before c", list, err)
	}
	got, ok, err := loadHostname(ctx, db.Read(), "b.example.com")
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadHostname: ok %v, err %v", ok, err)
	}
	want := in
	want.Health = "unknown"
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("loadHostname = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
	if _, ok, err := loadHostname(ctx, db.Read(), "z.example.com"); err != nil || ok {
		t.Errorf("loadHostname(missing): ok %v, err %v", ok, err)
	}

	at1, at2, at3 := cfT0.Add(time.Minute), cfT0.Add(2*time.Minute), cfT0.Add(3*time.Minute)
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := setHostnamePhase(ctx, tx, "b.example.com", "adding_record", "zone1", "", at1); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := setHostnamePhase(ctx, tx, "b.example.com", "active", "", "rec1", at2); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return setHostnameHealth(ctx, tx, "b.example.com", "record_missing", at3)
	})
	got, _, _ = loadHostname(ctx, db.Read(), "b.example.com")
	if got.Phase != "active" || got.ZoneID != "zone1" || got.RecordID != "rec1" || !got.UpdatedAt.Equal(at2) ||
		got.Health != "record_missing" || !got.CheckedAt.Equal(at3) {
		t.Errorf("after the updates: %+v", got)
	}
	untouched, _, _ := loadHostname(ctx, db.Read(), "c.example.com")
	if untouched.Phase != "active" || untouched.RecordID != "" || untouched.Health != "unknown" {
		t.Errorf("another hostname changed: %+v", untouched)
	}

	for name, fn := range map[string]func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error{
		"unknown phase": func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
			return setHostnamePhase(ctx, tx, "b.example.com", "done", "", "", at1)
		},
		"unknown hostname": func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
			return setHostnamePhase(ctx, tx, "z.example.com", "active", "", "", at1)
		},
		"unknown health": func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
			return setHostnameHealth(ctx, tx, "b.example.com", "fine", at1)
		},
		"health of nobody": func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
			return setHostnameHealth(ctx, tx, "z.example.com", "ok", at1)
		},
	} {
		if err := db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return fn(ctx, tx) }); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: no error", name)
		}
	}

	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error { return deleteHostname(ctx, tx, "b.example.com") })
	if _, ok, _ := loadHostname(ctx, db.Read(), "b.example.com"); ok {
		t.Error("the hostname is still there after deleteHostname")
	}
	if _, ok, _ := loadHostname(ctx, db.Read(), "c.example.com"); !ok {
		t.Error("deleteHostname removed another hostname")
	}
}

// TestCFCleanupPending: only a hostname outside the active phase and an
// unresolved effect of this module block deleting the account.
func TestCFCleanupPending(t *testing.T) {
	db := cfDB(t)
	pending := func() []string {
		t.Helper()
		var out []string
		cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) (err error) {
			out, err = cleanupPending(ctx, tx)
			return err
		})
		return out
	}
	if got := pending(); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("empty database: pending %q", got)
	}

	tun := cfTunnel(0)
	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := insertTunnel(ctx, tx, tun); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return insertHostname(ctx, tx, cfHostname("a.example.com", tun.ID, "active"))
	})
	cfEffect(t, db, "01J00000000000000000000C01", 1, "cloudflare.tunnel:t1", string(core.EffectMade))
	cfEffect(t, db, "01J00000000000000000000C01", 2, "tailnet.policy:example.com", string(core.EffectUnresolved))
	cfEffect(t, db, "01J00000000000000000000C01", 3, "cloudflare.tunnel:t1", string(core.EffectIntended))
	if got := pending(); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("an active hostname, a made effect, an intended one and another module's unresolved one block: %q", got)
	}

	cfWrite(t, db, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := insertHostname(ctx, tx, cfHostname("b.example.com", tun.ID, "removing_record")); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return insertHostname(ctx, tx, cfHostname("0.example.com", tun.ID, "adding_rule"))
	})
	cfEffect(t, db, "01J00000000000000000000C02", 1, "cloudflare.dnsrecord:?darkpanel:01J00000000000000000000C02", string(core.EffectUnresolved))
	got := pending()
	want := []string{
		"hostname 0.example.com is in phase adding_rule",
		"hostname b.example.com is in phase removing_record",
		"unresolved effect 01J00000000000000000000C02#1 on cloudflare.dnsrecord:?darkpanel:01J00000000000000000000C02",
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("pending = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `migrations/controller/0001_cloudflare.sql`: begin with a comment in the style of `internal/modules/firewall/migrations/agent/0001_firewall.sql` (the module's own tables, times are fixed-width RFC 3339 UTC text). Create `cloudflare_accounts`, `cloudflare_tunnels` and `cloudflare_hostnames` exactly as Contracts "Cloudflare store" lists them: every table `STRICT`, every column with its type, `NOT NULL`, default, `CHECK` and `REFERENCES` as listed (`cloudflare_hostnames.tunnel_id` references `cloudflare_tunnels (id)`; the database opens with foreign keys on). Contracts says the account table holds at most one row; the database enforces it with this statement after the table: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX cloudflare_accounts_single ON cloudflare_accounts ((1));`. The file holds only SQL (the migration runner refuses any other statement kind it cannot run in a transaction).
2. `store.go`: `//go:embed migrations/controller/*.sql` into an `embed.FS`, and `controllerMigrations() fs.FS` returning `fs.Sub(..., "migrations/controller")` (panic on the error, which only an invalid constant path causes; say so in a comment, as `internal/modules/firewall/store.go` does). Declare `queryer`, `account`, `tunnelRow` and `hostnameRow` exactly as Contracts lists them.
3. Times: every stored time is UTC text in the layout `2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z` (a constant named `storeTimeFormat`). A zero `time.Time` is stored as `NULL` in the nullable columns `checked_at` and read back as the zero time; `connected_at`, `created_at` and `updated_at` are always written. Reads return times that are `Equal` to what was written.
4. Account: `loadAccount` reads the only row and answers `(account{}, false, nil)` when there is none; `capabilities_json` is the JSON array of `cloud.Capability`, written as `[]` for a nil slice and decoded to a non-nil or empty slice. `insertAccount` writes the row (the sealed `TokenCT` byte for byte); a second row fails with an error starting `cloudflare: insert account`. `deleteAccount` deletes the row with that id and is not an error when there is none.
5. Tunnels: `insertTunnel`; `loadTunnel(ctx, q, idOrName)` matches the id or the name and answers `(tunnelRow{}, false, nil)` when none matches; `listTunnels` orders by `created_at`, then `id`; `deleteTunnel` deletes by id, is not an error for an absent id, and fails (foreign key) while a hostname row references the tunnel; `setTunnelHash` sets `config_hash`; `setTunnelCheck` sets `drift` and `checked_at`. Both setters fail with an error that names the tunnel id when no row has it.
6. Hostnames: `insertHostname` writes every column, storing an empty `Health` as `unknown`; `loadHostname` answers `(hostnameRow{}, false, nil)` when absent; `listHostnames` orders by `hostname`; `setHostnamePhase` sets `phase` and `updated_at`, and sets `zone_id` or `record_id` only when the argument is not empty (an empty argument keeps the stored value); `setHostnameHealth` sets `health` and `checked_at` and nothing else; both fail with an error naming the hostname when no row has it, and an unknown phase or health fails on the table's `CHECK`; `deleteHostname` is not an error for an absent hostname.
7. `cleanupPending(ctx, tx)` returns, in this order, one string `hostname <hostname> is in phase <phase>` for each `cloudflare_hostnames` row whose phase is not `active` (by hostname), then one string `unresolved effect <change id>#<seq> on <resource>` for each `core_effects` row whose `state` is exactly `unresolved` and whose resource starts with `cloudflare.` (compare with `substr(resource, 1, 11) = 'cloudflare.'`, not `LIKE`; by change id, then seq). It does not count an `intended` effect: the disconnecting change itself has one while it checks. It returns an empty (nil) slice when nothing is pending, and an error only for a database failure.
8. Every error this file creates or wraps starts with `cloudflare:`. Close `*sql.Rows` with `defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()` (the repository's `errcheck` rule); close the first result set of `cleanupPending` before the second query runs.

```go
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

// mfAPI is a dockerAPI that answers only Version and Info; any other method
// panics on the nil embedded interface, which these tests never reach.
type mfAPI struct {
	dockerAPI
	version dockerapi.VersionInfo
	verErr  error
	info    dockerapi.SystemInfo
	infoErr error
}

func (a mfAPI) Version(context.Context) (dockerapi.VersionInfo, error) { return a.version, a.verErr }
func (a mfAPI) Info(context.Context) (dockerapi.SystemInfo, error)     { return a.info, a.infoErr }

func mfDK(a mfAPI) dk { return dk{d: deps{docker: a}} }

// mfDial is the error dockerapi's client returns when its dial fails: it
// wraps ErrUnavailable and the operating system's error.
func mfDial(errno syscall.Errno) error {
	return fmt.Errorf("dockerapi: GET /version: %w: %w", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable,
		&net.OpError{Op: "dial", Net: "unix", Err: os.NewSyscallError("connect", errno)})
}

func mfVersion(api string) dockerapi.VersionInfo {
	return dockerapi.VersionInfo{Version: "29.9.1", APIVersion: api, Os: "linux", Arch: "amd64"}
}

// mfRun runs the module's one preflight check against a.
func mfRun(t *testing.T, a mfAPI) error {
	t.Helper()
	checks := mfDK(a).preflight()
	if len(checks) != 1 || checks[0].ID != "docker.engine" {
		t.Fatalf("preflight = %+v, want the one check docker.engine", checks)
	}
	return checks[0].Run(context.Background(), core.Env{})
}

// TestMFPreflightPasses: a daemon whose API is 1.44 or later passes, compared
// as numbers (1.100 is later than 1.44, 2.0 later than 1.99).
func TestMFPreflightPasses(t *testing.T) {
	for _, api := range []string{"1.44", "1.45", "1.52", "1.100", "2.0"} {
		if err := mfRun(t, mfAPI{version: mfVersion(api)}); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("API %s: %v", api, err)
		}
	}
}

// TestMFPreflightFails: each reason is told apart, names what to do or what
// was found, and starts with the package name.
func TestMFPreflightFails(t *testing.T) {
	for name, c := range map[string]struct {
		api  mfAPI
		want []string
	}{
		"socket missing":           {mfAPI{verErr: mfDial(syscall.ENOENT)}, []string{"socket", "/var/run/docker.sock", "missing"}},
		"daemon refuses":           {mfAPI{verErr: mfDial(syscall.ECONNREFUSED)}, []string{"not reachable", "/var/run/docker.sock", "refused"}},
		"permission":               {mfAPI{verErr: mfDial(syscall.EACCES)}, []string{"not reachable", "permission denied"}},
		"API too old":              {mfAPI{version: mfVersion("1.43")}, []string{"1.43", "1.44"}},
		"API compared numerically": {mfAPI{version: mfVersion("1.9")}, []string{"1.9", "1.44"}},
		"old major":                {mfAPI{version: mfVersion("0.99")}, []string{"0.99"}},
		"unreadable API":           {mfAPI{version: mfVersion("abc")}, []string{`"abc"`}},
		"empty API":                {mfAPI{version: mfVersion("")}, []string{`""`}},
		"daemon error":             {mfAPI{verErr: &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 500, Message: "boom"}}, []string{"500", "boom"}},
	} {
		err := mfRun(t, c.api)
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: the check passed", name)
			continue
		}
		if !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "docker: ") {
			t.Errorf("%s: error %q does not start with the package name", name, err)
		}
		for _, w := range c.want {
			if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), w) {
				t.Errorf("%s: error %q lacks %q", name, err, w)
			}
		}
	}
}

// TestMFManifestDeclaresPreflight: the module's manifest carries the engine
// check. The check is not run: that would reach the host's Docker socket.
func TestMFManifestDeclaresPreflight(t *testing.T) {
	m := Module().Manifest()
	if m.ID != ID || m.Version != 1 || !m.DefaultEnabled {
		t.Errorf("manifest = %+v", m)
	}
	if len(m.Preflight) != 1 || m.Preflight[0].ID != "docker.engine" || m.Preflight[0].Run == nil {
		t.Errorf("Preflight = %+v, want the one check docker.engine", m.Preflight)
	}
}
```

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

func mfRead(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, a mfAPI) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	t.Helper()
	return mfDK(a).engineResource().Read(ctx, core.Env{})
}

// TestMFEngineResource: docker.engine is the resource of the Engine type.
func TestMFEngineResource(t *testing.T) {
	def := mfDK(mfAPI{}).engineResource()
	if def.Name != "docker.engine" || def.OutputType != reflect.TypeOf(Engine{}) {
		t.Errorf("resource = %q of %v", def.Name, def.OutputType)
	}
}

// TestMFEngineAvailable: an available engine reports the daemon's version
// and API, its platform and the container and image counts, and no reason.
func TestMFEngineAvailable(t *testing.T) {
	raw, err := mfRead(context.Background(), t, mfAPI{
		version: mfVersion("1.52"),
		info:    dockerapi.SystemInfo{Containers: 7, ContainersRunning: 3, Images: 12},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var got Engine
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &got); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := Engine{Available: true, Version: "29.9.1", APIVersion: "1.52", OS: "linux", Arch: "amd64", Containers: 7, Running: 3, Images: 12}
	if got != want {
		t.Errorf("engine = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(raw), "reason") {
		t.Errorf("an available engine carries a reason: %s", raw)
	}
}

// TestMFEngineUnavailable: an engine that cannot be used is still a
// successful read: available false and the preflight's reason, with no
// counts.
func TestMFEngineUnavailable(t *testing.T) {
	for name, c := range map[string]struct {
		api  mfAPI
		want string
	}{
		"socket missing": {mfAPI{verErr: mfDial(syscall.ENOENT)}, "missing"},
		"daemon down":    {mfAPI{verErr: mfDial(syscall.ECONNREFUSED)}, "not reachable"},
		"API too old":    {mfAPI{version: mfVersion("1.43"), info: dockerapi.SystemInfo{Containers: 9}}, "1.43"},
		"info fails":     {mfAPI{version: mfVersion("1.52"), infoErr: errors.New("boom")}, "boom"},
	} {
		raw, err := mfRead(context.Background(), t, c.api)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: Read failed: %v", name, err)
			continue
		}
		var got Engine
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &got); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if got.Available || !strings.HasPrefix(got.Reason, "docker: ") || !strings.Contains(got.Reason, c.want) ||
			got.Version != "" || got.Containers != 0 || got.Images != 0 {
			t.Errorf("%s: engine = %+v", name, got)
		}
	}
}

// TestMFEngineCancelled: a read cut off by its context fails instead of
// reporting the engine unavailable.
func TestMFEngineCancelled(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancel()
	if _, err := mfRead(ctx, t, mfAPI{verErr: context.Canceled}); !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		t.Errorf("Read error = %v, want context.Canceled", err)
	}
}
```

Run: `mkdir -p /root/.cache/w3-tmp/14 && TMPDIR=/root/.cache/w3-tmp/14 GOTOOLCHAIN=local timeout 300 go vet ./internal/modules/docker/`
Expected: FAIL to build, `engine_test.go` naming `mfDK(a).engineResource undefined (type dk has no field or method engineResource)`; `preflight_test.go` names `preflight` the same way.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `preflight.go`: `func (k dk) preflight() []core.PreflightCheck` returns one check with id `docker.engine` whose `Run` calls `k.probe` and returns its error. `probe(ctx)` calls `k.d.docker.Version(ctx)` once and decides, in this order (each error starts with `docker:`; use `dockerapi.DefaultSocket` and `dockerapi.MinAPIVersion`, never a literal copy):
   - the error wraps `dockerapi.ErrUnavailable` and `fs.ErrNotExist` (the client wraps the operating system's dial error with `%w`, so `errors.Is` sees both): `docker: the Docker socket /var/run/docker.sock is missing; install Docker Engine and start it`;
   - the error wraps `dockerapi.ErrUnavailable` only: `docker: the Docker daemon is not reachable on /var/run/docker.sock: <the error>`;
   - any other error: `docker: ask the daemon for its version: <the error>`;
   - the reported `APIVersion` is not `<major>.<minor>` with two non-negative integers: `docker: the daemon reports the API version "<value>", which is not <major>.<minor>`;
   - the API is older than `dockerapi.MinAPIVersion`, compared as the pair of integers (so `1.9` is older than `1.44` and `1.100` is newer): `docker: the Docker API is <value>; Docker Engine 25 (API 1.44) or later is needed`.
   Otherwise it returns the `VersionInfo`. The check never opens a connection other than that one call, and nothing here reads a file. Do not name a parameter `min` or `max` (the repository's `revive` rule `redefines-builtin-id`).
2. `engine.go`: `func (k dk) engineResource() core.ResourceDef` is `core.DefineResource(ID+".engine", k.engine)`, whose read func has the signature `func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (Engine, error)`. It calls `probe`; when that succeeds it calls `Info` once and answers `Engine{Available: true, Version: <VersionInfo.Version>, APIVersion: <VersionInfo.APIVersion>, OS: <VersionInfo.Os>, Arch: <VersionInfo.Arch>, Containers: <Info.Containers>, Running: <Info.ContainersRunning>, Images: <Info.Images>}`. When `probe` or `Info` fails it answers `Engine{Reason: <the probe error's text, or "docker: read the engine's counts: <the error>">}` with `Available` false and every other member zero, and a nil error: the resource is readable while the engine is not, so the web page can show the reason. The one exception is a read cut off by its own context (`ctx.Err() != nil`), which returns that error.
3. `docker.go`: make `Manifest()` use its receiver (`func (m module) Manifest()`) and add `Preflight: m.k.preflight()` to the returned `core.Manifest`; nothing else in the manifest changes (Task 44 adds actions and resources). Update the doc comment so it no longer says the manifest declares no check.
4. `docker_test.go`: delete `TestManifestIsASkeleton`, which compares the whole manifest and cannot hold once `Preflight` holds functions, and any import only it used; leave the rest of the file as Task 5 left it. `TestMFManifestDeclaresPreflight` replaces it.

```go
package docker

import (
	"errors"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

// TestEFOwner: the owner is the darkpanel.module label, and an owned object
// is refused with docker.owned naming the kind, the object and the module;
// the refusal committed nothing, so it is Definite.
func TestEFOwner(t *testing.T) {
	owned := map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm", "other": "x"}
	if got := ownerOf(owned); got != "npm" {
		t.Errorf("ownerOf = %q, want npm", got)
	}
	for _, labels := range []map[string]string{nil, {}, {"other": "x"}, {core.LabelModule: ""}} {
		if got := ownerOf(labels); got != "" {
			t.Errorf("ownerOf(%v) = %q, want empty", labels, got)
		}
		if err := refuseOwned("network", "web", labels); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("refuseOwned(%v) = %v, want nil", labels, err)
		}
	}
	err := refuseOwned("network", "web", owned)
	var coded *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != errcode.DockerOwned || coded.Detail != "network web belongs to module npm" {
		t.Fatalf("refuseOwned = %#v, want docker.owned %q", err, "network web belongs to module npm")
	}
	if !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Error("the refusal is not Definite")
	}
}
```

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/docker/dstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

// efAPI wraps a dockerAPI and replaces the answers a test needs to control;
// a nil hook delegates to the wrapped API.
type efAPI struct {
	dockerAPI
	containers func() []dockerapi.ContainerSummary
	networks   func() []dockerapi.Network
	extra      map[string]dockerapi.Network // networks InspectNetwork also finds
	inspectErr error                        // InspectContainer, InspectNetwork and InspectVolume fail with it
}

func (a efAPI) ListContainers(ctx context.Context, o dockerapi.ListContainersOptions) ([]dockerapi.ContainerSummary, error) {
	if a.containers != nil {
		return a.containers(), nil
	}
	return a.dockerAPI.ListContainers(ctx, o)
}

func (a efAPI) ListNetworks(ctx context.Context, f dockerapi.Filters) ([]dockerapi.Network, error) {
	if a.networks != nil {
		return a.networks(), nil
	}
	return a.dockerAPI.ListNetworks(ctx, f)
}

func (a efAPI) InspectNetwork(ctx context.Context, id string) (dockerapi.Network, error) {
	if n, ok := a.extra[id]; ok {
		return n, nil
	}
	return a.dockerAPI.InspectNetwork(ctx, id)
}

func (a efAPI) InspectContainer(ctx context.Context, id string) (dockerapi.ContainerJSON, error) {
	if a.inspectErr != nil {
		return dockerapi.ContainerJSON{}, a.inspectErr
	}
	return a.dockerAPI.InspectContainer(ctx, id)
}

// efState decodes a StateDoc's State so documents compare as JSON values.
func efState(t *testing.T, raw json.RawMessage) any {
	t.Helper()
	var v any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &v); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("state %q: %v", raw, err)
	}
	return v
}

// efSame fails unless got and want are the same JSON value.
func efSame(t *testing.T, what string, got, want json.RawMessage) {
	t.Helper()
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(efState(t, got), efState(t, want)) {
		t.Errorf("%s = %s, want %s", what, got, want)
	}
}

// efMust unwraps a dstate document; an error is a bug in the test's input.
func efMust(doc json.RawMessage, err error) json.RawMessage {
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	return doc
}

func efEffectOf(resource string, state core.EffectState) core.Effect {
	return core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectModify, Resource: resource, State: state}
}

// TestEFPhaseOf: an effect that is being or was undone is compared in the
// Restored form; every other state in the Recorded form.
func TestEFPhaseOf(t *testing.T) {
	for state, want := range map[core.EffectState]dstate.Phase{
		core.EffectIntended: dstate.Recorded, core.EffectMade: dstate.Recorded, core.EffectSkipped: dstate.Recorded,
		core.EffectUnresolved: dstate.Recorded, core.EffectAccepted: dstate.Recorded, core.EffectAbandoned: dstate.Recorded,
		core.EffectUndoing: dstate.Restored, core.EffectUndone: dstate.Restored,
	} {
		if got := phaseOf(core.Effect{State: state}); got != want {
			t.Errorf("phaseOf(%s) = %v, want %v", state, got, want)
		}
	}
}

// TestEFObserveContainer: a container is rendered with dstate in the phase
// of the effect, and a container that is gone is the null state.
func TestEFObserveContainer(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	c := dkContainer("web", dkRunning)
	h.docker.put(c)
	k := h.dk()
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		state core.EffectState
		phase dstate.Phase
	}{
		{core.EffectMade, dstate.Recorded}, {core.EffectIntended, dstate.Recorded},
		{core.EffectUndoing, dstate.Restored}, {core.EffectUndone, dstate.Restored},
	} {
		obs, err := k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), efEffectOf(containerResource(c.ID), tc.state))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		efSame(t, string(tc.state), obs.Current.State, efMust(dstate.ContainerRun(c, tc.phase)))
		if obs.Matches != 1 || !obs.Exclusive {
			t.Errorf("%s: matches %d, exclusive %v; want 1, true", tc.state, obs.Matches, obs.Exclusive)
		}
	}
	rec, _ := dstate.ContainerRun(c, dstate.Recorded)
	res, _ := dstate.ContainerRun(c, dstate.Restored)
	if reflect.DeepEqual(efState(t, rec), efState(t, res)) {
		t.Fatal("the Recorded and Restored documents of a running container are equal; the test cannot tell the phases apart")
	}

	gone, err := k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), efEffectOf(containerResource(dkID("gone")), core.EffectMade))
	if err != nil || string(gone.Current.State) != "null" || gone.Matches != 1 {
		t.Errorf("a missing container: %+v, %v; want the null state", gone, err)
	}
}

// TestEFObserveEndpoint: an endpoint is present when the container is on
// the network, absent when it is not or when the container is gone.
func TestEFObserveEndpoint(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	n := dkNetwork("web")
	other := dkNetwork("other")
	c := dkContainer("app", dkRunning)
	ep := &dockerapi.EndpointSettings{NetworkID: n.ID, EndpointID: "ep-1", Aliases: []string{"app"}}
	c.NetworkSettings.Networks = map[string]*dockerapi.EndpointSettings{"web": ep}
	h.docker.put(c)
	k := h.dk()

	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name         string
		container    string
		network      string
		state        core.EffectState
		ep           *dockerapi.EndpointSettings
		phase        dstate.Phase
		wantPresent  bool
		wantEndpoint string
	}{
		{"present, recorded", c.ID, n.ID, core.EffectMade, ep, dstate.Recorded, true, "ep-1"},
		{"present, restored", c.ID, n.ID, core.EffectUndone, ep, dstate.Restored, true, ""},
		{"other network", c.ID, other.ID, core.EffectMade, nil, dstate.Recorded, false, ""},
		{"container gone", dkID("gone"), n.ID, core.EffectMade, nil, dstate.Recorded, false, ""},
	} {
		obs, err := k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), efEffectOf(endpointResource(tc.container, tc.network), tc.state))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %v", tc.name, err)
		}
		efSame(t, tc.name, obs.Current.State, efMust(dstate.Endpoint(tc.container, tc.network, tc.ep, tc.phase)))
		if got := strings.Contains(string(obs.Current.State), `"present":true`); got != tc.wantPresent {
			t.Errorf("%s: present = %v, want %v (%s)", tc.name, got, tc.wantPresent, obs.Current.State)
		}
	}
}

// TestEFObserveNetwork: a network named by id is rendered with dstate, one
// that is gone is the null state, and a creation not yet named is found by
// its exact name.
func TestEFObserveNetwork(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	web, web2 := dkNetwork("web"), dkNetwork("web2")
	busy := dkNetwork("web")
	busy.ID = dkID("web again")
	busy.Containers = map[string]dockerapi.NetworkContainer{dkID("app"): {Name: "app"}}
	h.docker.putNetwork(web)
	h.docker.putNetwork(web2)
	k := h.dk()
	creation := core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: networkResource("?web"), State: core.EffectIntended,
		Recovery: &core.RecoveryID{Kind: "name", Value: "web"}}

	obs, err := k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), efEffectOf(networkResource(web.ID), core.EffectMade))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	efSame(t, "by id", obs.Current.State, efMust(dstate.NetworkCreated(&web)))

	obs, err = k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), efEffectOf(networkResource(dkID("gone")), core.EffectMade))
	if err != nil || string(obs.Current.State) != "null" {
		t.Errorf("a missing network: %+v, %v", obs, err)
	}

	obs, err = k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), creation)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if obs.Matches != 1 || obs.Resource != networkResource(web.ID) {
		t.Errorf("by name: matches %d, resource %q; want 1, %q (web2 must not match)", obs.Matches, obs.Resource, networkResource(web.ID))
	}
	efSame(t, "by name", obs.Current.State, efMust(dstate.NetworkCreated(&web)))

	none := core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: networkResource("?absent"), State: core.EffectIntended,
		Recovery: &core.RecoveryID{Kind: "name", Value: "absent"}}
	if obs, err = k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), none); err != nil || obs.Matches != 0 || string(obs.Current.State) != "null" {
		t.Errorf("no match: %+v, %v; want 0 matches and the null state", obs, err)
	}

	k.d.docker = efAPI{dockerAPI: h.docker, extra: map[string]dockerapi.Network{busy.ID: busy},
		networks: func() []dockerapi.Network { return []dockerapi.Network{web, busy} }}
	obs, err = k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), creation)
	if err != nil || obs.Matches != 2 || len(obs.Candidates) != 2 || string(obs.Current.State) != "null" {
		t.Fatalf("two matches: %+v, %v", obs, err)
	}
	want := []string{networkResource(web.ID), networkResource(busy.ID)}
	if want[0] > want[1] {
		want[0], want[1] = want[1], want[0]
	}
	if obs.Candidates[0].Resource != want[0] || obs.Candidates[1].Resource != want[1] {
		t.Errorf("candidates %q, %q; want %q in order", obs.Candidates[0].Resource, obs.Candidates[1].Resource, want)
	}
	for _, c := range obs.Candidates {
		if c.Resource == networkResource(busy.ID) && !strings.Contains(string(c.State.State), `"unused":false`) {
			t.Errorf("the candidate with a container is not marked used: %s", c.State.State)
		}
	}
}

// TestEFObserveNetworkByNameIsExact: Docker's name filter matches substrings,
// so the observation keeps only networks whose name is the whole name even
// when the daemon returns more.
func TestEFObserveNetworkByNameIsExact(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	web := dkNetwork("web")
	prefix := dkNetwork("web-extra")
	h.docker.putNetwork(web)
	h.docker.putNetwork(prefix)
	k := h.dk()
	k.d.docker = efAPI{dockerAPI: h.docker, networks: func() []dockerapi.Network { return []dockerapi.Network{prefix, web} }}
	creation := core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: networkResource("?web"), State: core.EffectIntended,
		Recovery: &core.RecoveryID{Kind: "name", Value: "web"}}
	obs, err := k.observe(context.Background(), h.env(""), creation)
	if err != nil || obs.Matches != 1 || obs.Resource != networkResource(web.ID) {
		t.Errorf("observation = %+v, %v; want the one network web", obs, err)
	}
}

// TestEFObserveVolume: a volume is rendered with whether any container,
// running or not, mounts it; a creation is found by its name.
func TestEFObserveVolume(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	v := dkVolume("data", map[string]string{"team": "a"})
	h.docker.putVolume(v)
	var mounts []dockerapi.ContainerSummary
	k := h.dk()
	k.d.docker = efAPI{dockerAPI: h.docker, containers: func() []dockerapi.ContainerSummary { return mounts }}

	obs, err := k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), efEffectOf(volumeResource("data"), core.EffectMade))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	efSame(t, "unused", obs.Current.State, efMust(dstate.VolumeCreated(&v, true)))

	mounts = []dockerapi.ContainerSummary{
		{Names: []string{"/other"}, Mounts: []dockerapi.MountPoint{{Type: "volume", Name: "elsewhere"}}},
		{Names: []string{"/app"}, State: "exited", Mounts: []dockerapi.MountPoint{{Type: "volume", Name: "data"}}},
	}
	obs, err = k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), efEffectOf(volumeResource("data"), core.EffectMade))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	efSame(t, "used", obs.Current.State, efMust(dstate.VolumeCreated(&v, false)))

	creation := core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: volumeResource("?data"), State: core.EffectIntended,
		Recovery: &core.RecoveryID{Kind: "name", Value: "data"}}
	obs, err = k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), creation)
	if err != nil || obs.Matches != 1 || obs.Resource != volumeResource("data") {
		t.Errorf("creation by name: %+v, %v", obs, err)
	}
	creation.Resource, creation.Recovery.Value = volumeResource("?absent"), "absent"
	obs, err = k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), creation)
	if err != nil || obs.Matches != 0 || string(obs.Current.State) != "null" {
		t.Errorf("absent creation: %+v, %v; want 0 matches and the null state", obs, err)
	}
	gone, err := k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), efEffectOf(volumeResource("absent"), core.EffectUndone))
	if err != nil || string(gone.Current.State) != "null" {
		t.Errorf("a missing volume: %+v, %v", gone, err)
	}
}

// TestEFObserveRefuses: a resource that is not a docker object is an error
// that starts with the package name, and a daemon that cannot be reached is
// docker.engine_unavailable.
func TestEFObserveRefuses(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	k := h.dk()
	for _, resource := range []string{"docker.thing:x", "docker.container", "docker.container:", "docker.container:?", "docker.container:?web", "docker.endpoint:?c1@n1", "firewall.rule:x",
		"docker.endpoint:c1", "docker.endpoint:@n1", "docker.endpoint:c1@"} {
		_, err := k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), efEffectOf(resource, core.EffectMade))
		if err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "docker: ") {
			t.Errorf("observe(%q) error = %v, want one starting with docker:", resource, err)
		}
	}
	k.d.docker = efAPI{dockerAPI: h.docker, inspectErr: fmt.Errorf("dockerapi: GET: %w", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable)}
	_, err := k.observe(ctx, h.env(""), efEffectOf(containerResource(dkID("web")), core.EffectMade))
	if coded := errcode.From(err); coded.Code != errcode.DockerEngineUnavailable {
		t.Errorf("a daemon that is down: code %q, want docker.engine_unavailable (%v)", coded.Code, err)
	}
}
```

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
```
