```go
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

// TestEFResources: the resource strings of the four docker effect nouns.
func TestEFResources(t *testing.T) {
	for got, want := range map[string]string{
		containerResource("c1"):      "docker.container:c1",
		endpointResource("c1", "n1"): "docker.endpoint:c1@n1",
		networkResource("n1"):        "docker.network:n1",
		networkResource("?web"):      "docker.network:?web",
		volumeResource("data"):       "docker.volume:data",
		volumeResource("?data"):      "docker.volume:?data",
	} {
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("resource = %q, want %q", got, want)
		}
	}
}

// TestEFDockerEffect: an Engine call is not Local and the daemon may still
// commit it for the commit window; a creation names its object by a
// recovery name and starts from the null state, whatever Before is passed.
func TestEFDockerEffect(t *testing.T) {
	before := json.RawMessage(`{"id":"c1","created":"x","running":false}`)
	mod := dockerEffect(core.EffectModify, containerResource("c1"), before)
	if mod.Kind != core.EffectModify || mod.Resource != "docker.container:c1" || mod.Local || mod.InverseLocal ||
		mod.CommitWait != 2*time.Minute || mod.Recovery != nil || string(mod.Before.State) != string(before) || mod.After != nil {
		t.Errorf("modify effect = %+v", mod)
	}
	for _, resource := range []string{networkResource("?web"), volumeResource("?web")} {
		c := dockerEffect(core.EffectCreate, resource, before)
		if c.Kind != core.EffectCreate || c.Resource != resource || c.Local || c.CommitWait != 2*time.Minute ||
			c.Recovery == nil || *c.Recovery != (core.RecoveryID{Kind: "name", Value: "web"}) || string(c.Before.State) != "null" {
			t.Errorf("creation effect of %s = %+v (recovery %+v)", resource, c, c.Recovery)
		}
	}
	if del := dockerEffect(core.EffectDelete, networkResource("n1"), before); del.Recovery != nil {
		t.Errorf("a deletion carries a recovery identity: %+v", del.Recovery)
	}
}

// TestEFEngineError: the dockerapi errors an action must tell its caller
// about become coded errors; any other error passes unchanged, and a mapped
// error keeps the Definite mark of the error it replaces.
func TestEFEngineError(t *testing.T) {
	unavailable := fmt.Errorf("dockerapi: GET /containers/x/json: %w", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable)
	notFound := &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 404, Message: "No such container"}
	empty := fmt.Errorf("dockerapi: InspectContainer: %w", dockerapi.ErrEmptyID)
	for name, c := range map[string]struct {
		in     error
		code   errcode.Code
		detail string
	}{
		"unavailable":  {unavailable, errcode.DockerEngineUnavailable, ""},
		"not found":    {notFound, errcode.NotFound, "container web not found"},
		"empty id":     {empty, errcode.InvalidInput, ""},
		"definite 404": {core.Definite(notFound), errcode.NotFound, "container web not found"},
	} {
		got := engineError("container", "web", c.in)
		var coded *errcode.Error
		if !errors.As(got, &coded) || coded.Code != c.code || (c.detail != "" && coded.Detail != c.detail) {
			t.Errorf("%s: engineError = %#v, want code %s", name, got, c.code)
			continue
		}
		if !errors.Is(got, c.in) {
			t.Errorf("%s: the mapped error lost its cause", name)
		}
		if core.IsDefinite(got) != core.IsDefinite(c.in) {
			t.Errorf("%s: Definite = %v, want %v", name, core.IsDefinite(got), core.IsDefinite(c.in))
		}
	}
	if got := engineError("container", "web", nil); got != nil {
		t.Errorf("engineError(nil) = %v", got)
	}
	for _, other := range []error{&dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 409, Message: "in use"}, &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 500}, errors.New("boom")} {
		got := engineError("container", "web", other)
		var coded *errcode.Error
		if !errors.Is(got, other) || errors.As(got, &coded) {
			t.Errorf("engineError(%v) = %v, want it unchanged", other, got)
		}
	}
}

// efStart is a call that starts container c and names it.
func efStart(h *dkHost, id string) func(context.Context) (string, error) {
	return func(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
		_, err := h.docker.StartContainer(ctx, id)
		return containerResource(id), err
	}
}

// TestEFRunModify: run journals the effect before the call and records it
// made with the Recorded state the container is in afterwards.
func TestEFRunModify(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	c := dkContainer("web")
	h.docker.put(c)
	before := efMust(dstate.ContainerRunning(c.ID, c.Created, false))
	e := dockerEffect(core.EffectModify, containerResource(c.ID), before)

	var intended []core.Effect
	do := func(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
		intended = h.journal.effects()
		return efStart(h, c.ID)(ctx)
	}
	if err := h.dk().run(ctx, h.env("c1"), e, do); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(intended) != 1 || intended[0].State != core.EffectIntended {
		t.Fatalf("effects when the call ran: %+v, want one intended", intended)
	}
	got := h.journal.effects()
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0].State != core.EffectMade || got[0].Resource != containerResource(c.ID) || got[0].Post == nil {
		t.Fatalf("effects = %+v, want one made", got)
	}
	after, err := h.docker.InspectContainer(ctx, c.ID)
	if err != nil || !after.State.Running {
		t.Fatalf("container after the call: %+v, %v", after.State, err)
	}
	efSame(t, "Post", got[0].Post.State, efMust(dstate.ContainerRun(after, dstate.Recorded)))
	efSame(t, "Before", got[0].Before.State, before)
	if got[0].Local || got[0].CommitWait != 2*time.Minute {
		t.Errorf("effect = %+v, want not Local with a two-minute commit window", got[0])
	}
}

// TestEFRunCreation: a creation is journaled under its recovery name and
// made under the id the call returned, with the created object's state.
func TestEFRunCreation(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	e := dockerEffect(core.EffectCreate, networkResource("?web"), nil)
	var id string
	do := func(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
		var err error
		id, err = h.docker.CreateNetwork(ctx, dockerapi.NetworkCreate{Name: "web"})
		return networkResource(id), err
	}
	if err := h.dk().run(ctx, h.env("c1"), e, do); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got := h.journal.effects()
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0].State != core.EffectMade || got[0].Resource != networkResource(id) || got[0].Recovery == nil {
		t.Fatalf("effects = %+v, want one made under docker.network:%s", got, id)
	}
	n, err := h.docker.InspectNetwork(ctx, id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	efSame(t, "Post", got[0].Post.State, efMust(dstate.NetworkCreated(&n)))
}

// TestEFRunFailures: a 4xx answer from the daemon changed nothing, so the
// effect is skipped and the error is Definite; any other failure leaves the
// effect intended and the error plain, because the call may still commit.
func TestEFRunFailures(t *testing.T) {
	for name, c := range map[string]struct {
		err      error
		definite bool
		state    core.EffectState
	}{
		"409 conflict": {&dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 409, Message: "in use"}, true, core.EffectSkipped},
		"404":          {&dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 404, Message: "gone"}, true, core.EffectSkipped},
		"wrapped 400":  {fmt.Errorf("dockerapi: %w", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 400}), true, core.EffectSkipped},
		"500":          {&dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 500, Message: "boom"}, false, core.EffectIntended},
		"reset":        {errors.New("read: connection reset by peer"), false, core.EffectIntended},
		"deadline":     {context.DeadlineExceeded, false, core.EffectIntended},
	} {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		e := dockerEffect(core.EffectModify, containerResource("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{}`))
		err := h.dk().run(context.Background(), h.env("c1"), e, func(context.Context) (string, error) { return "", c.err })
		if !errors.Is(err, c.err) || core.IsDefinite(err) != c.definite {
			t.Errorf("%s: run = %v (definite %v), want %v (definite %v)", name, err, core.IsDefinite(err), c.err, c.definite)
		}
		if got := h.journal.effects(); len(got) != 1 || got[0].State != c.state {
			t.Errorf("%s: effects = %+v, want one %s", name, got, c.state)
		}
	}
}

// efNoJournal is a journal whose Intend fails.
type efNoJournal struct{ core.EffectJournal }

func (efNoJournal) Intend(context.Context, core.Effect, []byte) (int, error) {
	return 0, errors.New("journal is full")
}

// TestEFRunNeedsAJournaledIntent: when the intent cannot be recorded the call
// is never made.
func TestEFRunNeedsAJournaledIntent(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	env := h.env("c1")
	env.Effects = efNoJournal{env.Effects}
	called := false
	e := dockerEffect(core.EffectModify, containerResource("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{}`))
	err := h.dk().run(context.Background(), env, e, func(context.Context) (string, error) { called = true; return "", nil })
	if err == nil || called || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "docker: ") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "journal is full") {
		t.Errorf("run = %v, call made %v; want a docker: error and no call", err, called)
	}
}

// TestEFRunUnsettled: a call that succeeded but whose resulting state cannot
// be read, or whose creation was not named, leaves the effect intended with
// an error, so the engine treats it as uncertain.
func TestEFRunUnsettled(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	c := dkContainer("web")
	h.docker.put(c)
	k := h.dk()
	k.d.docker = efAPI{dockerAPI: h.docker, inspectErr: fmt.Errorf("dockerapi: GET: %w", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable)}
	e := dockerEffect(core.EffectModify, containerResource(c.ID), json.RawMessage(`{}`))
	if err := k.run(ctx, h.env("c1"), e, efStart(h, c.ID)); err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "docker: ") {
		t.Errorf("unreadable post-state: run = %v", err)
	}
	if got := h.journal.effects(); len(got) != 1 || got[0].State != core.EffectIntended {
		t.Errorf("effects = %+v, want one intended", got)
	}

	h2 := newDKHost(t)
	create := dockerEffect(core.EffectCreate, networkResource("?web"), nil)
	err := h2.dk().run(ctx, h2.env("c1"), create, func(context.Context) (string, error) { return "", nil })
	if err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "docker: ") {
		t.Errorf("unnamed creation: run = %v", err)
	}
	if got := h2.journal.effects(); len(got) != 1 || got[0].State != core.EffectIntended {
		t.Errorf("effects = %+v, want one intended", got)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `effects.go`: the four resource functions return `docker.container:<id>`, `docker.endpoint:<container id>@<network id>`, `docker.network:<id>` and `docker.volume:<name>`. A creation's resource is built by the caller as `networkResource("?"+name)` or `volumeResource("?"+name)`, which gives `docker.network:?<name>`. Declare the four nouns as constants (`docker.container`, `docker.endpoint`, `docker.network`, `docker.volume`).
2. `dockerEffect(kind, resource, before)` returns a `core.Effect` with that kind and resource, `Local` and `InverseLocal` false, `CommitWait` `commitWait`, `Before` `core.StateDoc{State: before}` and no `After` (the post-state is not known before the call). For `core.EffectCreate` it sets `Before.State` to JSON `null` whatever `before` is (the engine refuses any other creation Before), and, when the resource's identity starts with `?`, sets `Recovery` to `{Kind: "name", Value: <the identity without "?">}`; the engine requires `Resource == noun + ":?" + Recovery.Value`. No other kind has a `Recovery`.
3. `(k dk) run(ctx, env, e, do)` does exactly this, in order:
   a. `env.Effects.Intend(ctx, e, nil)`; on error return `docker: journal <resource>: <err>` and never call `do`.
   b. `resource, err := do(ctx)`. When `err` is a `*dockerapi.APIError` (found with `errors.As`, also through wrapping) whose `StatusCode` is 400 to 499, the daemon refused before changing anything: call `Skipped`, and return the error wrapped in `core.Definite` (if `Skipped` itself fails, return `errors.Join` of the call error and the journal error, not Definite). Every other error (5xx, a transport error, a deadline) is returned as it is and the effect stays intended, which the engine settles as uncertain.
   c. On success an empty `resource` means `e.Resource`. A resource whose identity still starts with `?` is an error `docker: the call that made <resource> did not name its object` (effect left intended).
   d. Read the Recorded post-state by calling `k.observe` with a copy of `e` whose `Resource` is `resource` and whose `State` is `core.EffectIntended`; on an observation error return `docker: <resource> is unsettled: <err>` (effect left intended). Then `Made(ctx, seq, resource, obs.Current)`; on error return `docker: journal <resource>: <err>`.
   `run` does not compare the observation with anything: a docker effect has no predicted `After`.
4. `engineError(kind, name, err)`: nil stays nil; an error wrapping `dockerapi.ErrUnavailable` becomes `errcode.Wrap(errcode.DockerEngineUnavailable, err, "the Docker Engine is not reachable")`; `dockerapi.IsNotFound(err)` becomes `errcode.Wrap(errcode.NotFound, err, "<kind> <name> not found")`; an error wrapping `dockerapi.ErrEmptyID` becomes `errcode.Wrap(errcode.InvalidInput, err, "<kind> name or id is empty")`; anything else is returned as it is. Because `Wrap` keeps the input as the cause, a `core.Definite` input stays Definite and `errors.Is` still finds the original.
5. `owned.go`: `ownerOf(labels)` is `labels[core.LabelModule]` (a nil map gives ""). `refuseOwned(kind, name, labels)` is nil when the owner is "" and otherwise `core.Definite(errcode.New(errcode.DockerOwned, "<kind> <name> belongs to module <owner>"))`.
6. `observe.go`: `phaseOf(e)` is `dstate.Restored` when `e.State` is `core.EffectUndoing` or `core.EffectUndone` and `dstate.Recorded` otherwise. `(k dk) observe(ctx, env, e)` reads only the Docker Engine through `k.d.docker`, never writes, and splits `e.Resource` at the first `:` into noun and identity (a leading `?` marks a creation not yet named). A resource that is not `<noun>:<identity>` with a non-empty identity, whose noun is not one of the four, a `container` or `endpoint` resource with a `?`, or an `endpoint` identity that is not `<container id>@<network id>` with both parts, is an error starting `docker: ` that names the resource. For a named object the observation is `Matches` 1 and `Exclusive` true. Per noun, with the document built by `dstate` in `phaseOf(e)`:
   - `docker.container`: `InspectContainer`; `dstate.ContainerRun`; a 404 is the JSON `null` state.
   - `docker.endpoint`: `InspectContainer(container id)`; the endpoint is the entry of `NetworkSettings.Networks` whose `NetworkID` equals the network id (Docker keys the map by network name); `dstate.Endpoint(containerID, networkID, ep, phase)` with `ep` nil when there is none or when the container is gone (404).
   - `docker.network` by id: `InspectNetwork` (the list leaves `Containers` empty, so only the inspect tells whether it is in use); `dstate.NetworkCreated(&n)`; a 404 is `dstate.NetworkCreated(nil)`, the `null` state.
   - `docker.network:?<name>`: `ListNetworks` with the filter `name=<name>`, then keep only networks whose `Name` equals the name exactly (Docker's filter matches substrings, and the fake ignores it), `InspectNetwork` each (skip one that vanished with a 404), and build its `dstate.NetworkCreated` document. No match: `Matches` 0 and the `null` state. One match: `Matches` 1, `Resource` `networkResource(<id>)`, `Current` its document, `Exclusive` false. Several: `Matches` the count, `Current` the `null` state, `Candidates` one `{Resource, State}` per match sorted by resource.
   - `docker.volume`: `InspectVolume`, then `ListContainers` with `All: true` to decide `unused` (no container's `Mounts` entry has `Name` equal to the volume's name), then `dstate.VolumeCreated(&v, unused)`; a 404 is the `null` state. For `docker.volume:?<name>` the same read by name: found gives `Matches` 1 and `Resource` `volumeResource(<name>)`, absent gives `Matches` 0.
   Any error other than a 404 is returned through `engineError(kind, name, err)` with kind `container`, `network` or `volume`, so a daemon that is down is `docker.engine_unavailable`.
7. Error strings start with `docker:`; no log line, error or document carries an environment value or a label value beyond the names the tests show.

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"math"
	"net/http"
	"net/netip"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

// rsDocker answers the calls the four list resources make from its fields,
// so these tests do not depend on how fakeDocker renders summaries. Stats
// answers one sample per container id.
type rsDocker struct {
	dockerAPI
	containers []dockerapi.ContainerSummary
	images     []dockerapi.ImageSummary
	networks   []dockerapi.Network // Containers is returned by InspectNetwork only
	volumes    []dockerapi.Volume
	stats      map[string]dockerapi.Stats
	statsErr   map[string]error // by container id
	inspectErr map[string]error // by network id
	failList   map[string]error // by method name

	mu       sync.Mutex
	listed   []bool // the All option of each ListContainers call
	statsFor []string
}

func (d *rsDocker) ListContainers(_ context.Context, o dockerapi.ListContainersOptions) ([]dockerapi.ContainerSummary, error) {
	d.mu.Lock()
	d.listed = append(d.listed, o.All)
	d.mu.Unlock()
	if err := d.failList["ListContainers"]; err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return slices.Clone(d.containers), nil
}

func (d *rsDocker) ListImages(context.Context, dockerapi.ListImagesOptions) ([]dockerapi.ImageSummary, error) {
	if err := d.failList["ListImages"]; err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return slices.Clone(d.images), nil
}

func (d *rsDocker) ListNetworks(context.Context, dockerapi.Filters) ([]dockerapi.Network, error) {
	if err := d.failList["ListNetworks"]; err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	out := slices.Clone(d.networks)
	for i := range out {
		out[i].Containers = nil
	}
	return out, nil
}

func (d *rsDocker) InspectNetwork(_ context.Context, id string) (dockerapi.Network, error) {
	if err := d.inspectErr[id]; err != nil {
		return dockerapi.Network{}, err
	}
	for _, n := range d.networks {
		if n.ID == id {
			return n, nil
		}
	}
	return dockerapi.Network{}, &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: http.StatusNotFound, Message: "no such network"}
}

func (d *rsDocker) ListVolumes(context.Context, dockerapi.Filters) ([]dockerapi.Volume, error) {
	if err := d.failList["ListVolumes"]; err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return slices.Clone(d.volumes), nil
}

func (d *rsDocker) Stats(_ context.Context, id string, stream bool) (statsStream, error) {
	d.mu.Lock()
	d.statsFor = append(d.statsFor, fmt.Sprintf("%s stream=%t", id, stream))
	d.mu.Unlock()
	if err := d.statsErr[id]; err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &rsStream{s: d.stats[id]}, nil
}

type rsStream struct {
	s      dockerapi.Stats
	closed bool
}

func (r *rsStream) Next() (dockerapi.Stats, error) {
	if r.closed {
		return dockerapi.Stats{}, io.EOF
	}
	return r.s, nil
}

func (r *rsStream) Close() error { r.closed = true; return nil }

func rsRead(t *testing.T, d *rsDocker, def func(dk) core.ResourceDef, out any) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	k := h.dk()
	k.d.docker = d
	raw, err := def(k).Read(t.Context(), h.env(""))
	if err == nil && out != nil {
		if uerr := json.Unmarshal(raw, out); uerr != nil {
			t.Fatalf("decode %s: %v", raw, uerr)
		}
	}
	return raw, err
}

func rsSummary(id, name, imageID, state string, labels map[string]string) dockerapi.ContainerSummary {
	return dockerapi.ContainerSummary{ID: id, Names: []string{"/" + name}, Image: "img-" + name, ImageID: imageID,
		State: state, Status: state + " status", Created: 1_760_000_000, Labels: labels}
}

// rsSample is a stats sample with a CPU delta of 1e9 against a system delta
// of 10e9 on 4 CPUs (40 %), and 100 MiB of memory of which 20 MiB is
// inactive file cache.
func rsSample() dockerapi.Stats {
	return dockerapi.Stats{
		CPUStats:    dockerapi.CPUStats{CPUUsage: dockerapi.CPUUsage{TotalUsage: 2_000_000_000}, SystemCPUUsage: 20_000_000_000, OnlineCPUs: 4},
		PreCPUStats: dockerapi.CPUStats{CPUUsage: dockerapi.CPUUsage{TotalUsage: 1_000_000_000}, SystemCPUUsage: 10_000_000_000, OnlineCPUs: 4},
		MemoryStats: dockerapi.MemoryStats{Usage: 100 << 20, Limit: 1 << 30, Stats: map[string]uint64{"inactive_file": 20 << 20}},
	}
}

	for name, def := range map[string]core.ResourceDef{

	} {
		if def.Name != name || def.Read == nil || def.OutputType == nil {
			t.Errorf("resource %q: Name %q, Read nil %t, OutputType nil %t", name, def.Name, def.Read == nil, def.OutputType == nil)
		}
	}
}

func TestRsContainers(t *testing.T) {
	d := &rsDocker{

					"com.docker.compose.project": "shop", "com.docker.compose.service": "front", "darkpanel.module": "cloudflare"})
				c.Ports = []dockerapi.PortSummary{
					{IP: "::", PrivatePort: 80, PublicPort: 8080, Type: "tcp"},
					{PrivatePort: 443, Type: "tcp"},
					{IP: "0.0.0.0", PrivatePort: 80, PublicPort: 8080, Type: "tcp"},
				}
				return c
			}(),
			func() dockerapi.ContainerSummary {
				c := rsSummary("id-db", "db", "sha256:bbb", "exited", nil)
				c.Names = []string{"/app/db", "/db"} // a legacy link name first
				return c
			}(),
			rsSummary("id-cache", "cache", "sha256:aaa", "running", nil),
		},
		stats:    map[string]dockerapi.Stats{"id-web": rsSample()},
		statsErr: map[string]error{"id-cache": errors.New("stats failed")},
	}
	var got ContainerList
	if _, err := rsRead(t, d, dk.containersResource, &got); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(d.listed, []bool{true}) {
		t.Errorf("ListContainers All options = %v, want one call with All", d.listed)
	}
	slices.Sort(d.statsFor)
	if want := []string{"id-cache stream=false", "id-web stream=false"}; !slices.Equal(d.statsFor, want) {
		t.Errorf("stats reads = %v, want %v (running containers only, one sample each)", d.statsFor, want)
	}
	created := time.Unix(1_760_000_000, 0).UTC()
	want := []Container{
		{ID: "id-cache", Name: "cache", Image: "img-cache", ImageID: "sha256:aaa", State: "running", Status: "running status",
			Created: created, Ports: []Port{}},
		{ID: "id-db", Name: "db", Image: "img-db", ImageID: "sha256:bbb", State: "exited", Status: "exited status",
			Created: created, Ports: []Port{}},
		{ID: "id-web", Name: "web", Image: "img-web", ImageID: "sha256:aaa", State: "running", Status: "running status",
			Created: created,
			Ports: []Port{
				{IP: "0.0.0.0", PrivatePort: 80, PublicPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"},
				{IP: "::", PrivatePort: 80, PublicPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"},
				{PrivatePort: 443, Proto: "tcp"},
			},
			Labels:  map[string]string{"com.docker.compose.project": "shop", "com.docker.compose.service": "front", "darkpanel.module": "cloudflare"},
			Project: "shop", Service: "front", Owner: "cloudflare",
			Usage: &Usage{CPUPercent: 40, MemUsage: 80 << 20, MemLimit: 1 << 30}},
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Containers, want) {
		t.Errorf("containers\n got %+v\nwant %+v", got.Containers, want)
	}
}

func TestRsContainersEncodeEmptyListsAsArrays(t *testing.T) {
	d := &rsDocker{containers: []dockerapi.ContainerSummary{rsSummary("id-solo", "solo", "sha256:aaa", "exited", nil)}}
	raw, err := rsRead(t, d, dk.containersResource, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var doc struct {
		Containers []map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"containers"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &doc); err != nil || len(doc.Containers) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("decode %s: %v", raw, err)
	}
	c := doc.Containers[0]
	if string(c["ports"]) != "[]" {
		t.Errorf("ports = %s, want []", c["ports"])
	}
	for _, absent := range []string{"labels", "usage", "project", "service", "owner"} {
		if _, ok := c[absent]; ok {
			t.Errorf("member %q present for a container without it", absent)
		}
	}
	empty, err := rsRead(t, &rsDocker{}, dk.containersResource, nil)
	if err != nil || string(empty) != `{"containers":[]}` {
		t.Errorf("no containers: %s, %v; want {\"containers\":[]}", empty, err)
	}
}

func TestRsUsageOf(t *testing.T) {
	cpu := func(total, pre, system, preSystem uint64, online uint32) dockerapi.Stats {
		return dockerapi.Stats{
			CPUStats:    dockerapi.CPUStats{CPUUsage: dockerapi.CPUUsage{TotalUsage: total}, SystemCPUUsage: system, OnlineCPUs: online},
			PreCPUStats: dockerapi.CPUStats{CPUUsage: dockerapi.CPUUsage{TotalUsage: pre}, SystemCPUUsage: preSystem},
		}
	}
	mem := func(usage uint64, stats map[string]uint64) dockerapi.Stats {
		return dockerapi.Stats{MemoryStats: dockerapi.MemoryStats{Usage: usage, Limit: 1 << 30, Stats: stats}}
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name string
		in   dockerapi.Stats
		want Usage
	}{
		{"cpu delta ratio times online cpus", cpu(2e9, 1e9, 20e9, 10e9, 4), Usage{CPUPercent: 40}},
		{"zero online cpus count as one", cpu(2e9, 1e9, 20e9, 10e9, 0), Usage{CPUPercent: 10}},
		{"system counter unchanged", cpu(2e9, 1e9, 10e9, 10e9, 4), Usage{}},
		{"cpu counter went backwards", cpu(1e9, 2e9, 20e9, 10e9, 4), Usage{}},
		{"inactive file is subtracted", mem(100<<20, map[string]uint64{"inactive_file": 20 << 20}), Usage{MemUsage: 80 << 20, MemLimit: 1 << 30}},
		{"inactive file above usage is ignored", mem(10<<20, map[string]uint64{"inactive_file": 20 << 20}), Usage{MemUsage: 10 << 20, MemLimit: 1 << 30}},
		{"no inactive file", mem(10<<20, nil), Usage{MemUsage: 10 << 20, MemLimit: 1 << 30}},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got := usageOf(tc.in)
			if math.Abs(got.CPUPercent-tc.want.CPUPercent) > 1e-9 || got.MemUsage != tc.want.MemUsage || got.MemLimit != tc.want.MemLimit {
				t.Errorf("usageOf = %+v, want %+v", got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `resources.go`:

1. The four constructors are `core.DefineResource(ID+".containers", …)`, `".images"`, `".networks"`, `".volumes"` over methods `func (k dk) <read>(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (<List>, error)`. The reads ignore `env` and call `k.d.docker` only.
2. Errors. An error from the Engine that wraps `dockerapi.ErrUnavailable` (test with `errors.Is`) becomes `errcode.Wrap(errcode.DockerEngineUnavailable, err, "the Docker Engine cannot be reached")`; any other error is returned as `fmt.Errorf("docker: list containers: %w", err)` (the call's name in place of "list containers"). Task 15's `engineError` is not available to this task, so write a small `res`-prefixed helper for this mapping. Every list value is encoded with non-nil slices, so an empty list is `[]`, never `null`.
3. `docker.containers`: call `ListContainers(ctx, dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{All: true})` once. For each summary: `ID`, `Image`, `ImageID`, `State`, `Status` as given; `Name` is the first entry of `Names` that has no `/` after its leading one (Docker lists link aliases as `/other/alias`), without the leading `/`, else the first entry without it; `Created` is `time.Unix(Created, 0).UTC()`; `Ports` come from `PortSummary` (`Type` becomes `Proto`), sorted by `PrivatePort`, `PublicPort`, `Proto`, `IP`, and are never nil; `Labels` as given, nil when empty; `Project`, `Service` and `Owner` are the labels `com.docker.compose.project`, `com.docker.compose.service` and `darkpanel.module` read directly (Task 15's `ownerOf` is not available to this task). The list is sorted by `Name`. For every container whose `State` is `running`, read one sample: `Stats(ctx, id, false)` under a 5 second timeout derived from `ctx`, one `Next()`, then `Close()`, and set `Usage` to `usageOf` of the sample; a failure at any of those steps leaves `Usage` nil and is not an error. Run at most 8 sample reads at once, each goroutine writing only its own list element.
4. `usageOf`: `MemUsage` is `MemoryStats.Usage` minus `MemoryStats.Stats["inactive_file"]`, subtracted only when that member exists and is smaller than the usage; `MemLimit` is `MemoryStats.Limit`. `CPUPercent` is `docker stats`'s figure: `(cpuDelta / systemDelta) * onlineCPUs * 100` with `cpuDelta` the growth of `CPUStats.CPUUsage.TotalUsage` over `PreCPUStats`'s, `systemDelta` the growth of `SystemCPUUsage`, and `onlineCPUs` `CPUStats.OnlineCPUs` counted as 1 when it is 0. When either counter did not grow (the unsigned subtraction would wrap or divide by zero), `CPUPercent` is 0.
5. `docker.images`: call `ListImages(ctx, dockerapi.ListImagesOptions{})` and `ListContainers` with `All: true` once each. `Tags` and `Digests` are `RepoTags` and `RepoDigests` without the placeholder entries `<none>:<none>` and `<none>@<none>`, sorted and without duplicates; `Created` as for containers; `Size` as given; `Containers` are the names (same rule as for containers) of the containers whose `ImageID` equals the image id, sorted and without duplicates; `Dangling` is true when the image has neither a tag nor a digest. Order: images with a tag first, by first tag, then images without one, with ties by id.
6. `docker.networks`: call `ListNetworks(ctx, nil)`, then `InspectNetwork(ctx, id)` for each (the list leaves `Containers` empty). A network the inspect reports as not found (`dockerapi.IsNotFound`) was removed meanwhile and is skipped; another inspect error is returned wrapped. `Scope`, `Driver`, `Internal` as given, `IPv6` is `EnableIPv6`, `Subnets` are the valid `IPAM.Config[].Subnet` prefixes in `netip` text form, sorted; `Containers` are the `Name` of each `Containers` entry, sorted; `Owner` is the `darkpanel.module` label; `Created` is the parsed `Created` (`time.RFC3339Nano`, UTC), the zero time when it does not parse. Sorted by `Name`.
7. `docker.volumes`: call `ListVolumes(ctx, nil)` and `ListContainers` with `All: true` once. `Containers` are the names of the containers having a mount of `Type` `volume` whose `Name` is the volume's, sorted and without duplicates (bind mounts have no `Name` and are ignored); `Labels` as given, nil when empty; `Owner` is the `darkpanel.module` label; `Created` is the parsed `CreatedAt` as for networks. Sorted by `Name`.

```go
package fake

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/cloud/cloudfake"
)

// fkResult is one answer of the server.
type fkResult struct {
	Status int
	Header http.Header
	Body   string
}

// fkReq sends one request; token "" sends no Authorization header.
func fkReq(t *testing.T, s *Server, method, path, token string, header map[string]string, body string) fkResult {
	t.Helper()
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), method, s.URL()+path, strings.NewReader(body))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if token != "" {
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
	}
	for k, v := range header {
		req.Header.Set(k, v)
	}
	res, err := s.Client().Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = res.Body.Close() }()
	b, err := io.ReadAll(res.Body)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return fkResult{res.StatusCode, res.Header, string(b)}
}

// fkToken obtains an access token the way the module's client does.
func fkToken(t *testing.T, s *Server) string {
	t.Helper()
	r := fkTokenRequest(t, s, url.Values{"client_id": {ClientID}, "client_secret": {ClientSecret}, "grant_type": {"client_credentials"}})
	if r.Status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("token request answered %d: %s", r.Status, r.Body)
	}
	return fkDecode(t, r.Body)["access_token"].(string)
}

func fkTokenRequest(t *testing.T, s *Server, form url.Values) fkResult {
	t.Helper()
	return fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/oauth/token", "", map[string]string{"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"}, form.Encode())
}

func fkDecode(t *testing.T, body string) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	var m map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(body), &m); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("body %q is not a JSON object: %v", body, err)
	}
	return m
}

func TestFkOAuthToken(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	for name, form := range map[string]url.Values{
		"wrong secret": {"client_id": {ClientID}, "client_secret": {"nope"}, "grant_type": {"client_credentials"}},
		"wrong client": {"client_id": {"other"}, "client_secret": {ClientSecret}, "grant_type": {"client_credentials"}},
	} {
		if r := fkTokenRequest(t, s, form); r.Status != http.StatusUnauthorized {
			t.Errorf("%s: status %d, want 401", name, r.Status)
		}
	}
	if r := fkTokenRequest(t, s, url.Values{"client_id": {ClientID}, "client_secret": {ClientSecret}, "grant_type": {"password"}}); r.Status != http.StatusBadRequest {
		t.Errorf("wrong grant type: status %d, want 400", r.Status)
	}
	if s.Tokens() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Tokens = %d after refused requests, want 0", s.Tokens())
	}
	r := fkTokenRequest(t, s, url.Values{"client_id": {ClientID}, "client_secret": {ClientSecret}, "grant_type": {"client_credentials"}})
	doc := fkDecode(t, r.Body)
	if r.Status != http.StatusOK || doc["token_type"] != "Bearer" || doc["expires_in"] != float64(3600) || doc["access_token"] == "" {
		t.Fatalf("token answer %d %s", r.Status, r.Body)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(doc["scope"].(string), "devices:core") {
		t.Errorf("scope %q does not list the granted scopes", doc["scope"])
	}
	second := fkToken(t, s)
	if second == doc["access_token"] || s.Tokens() != 2 {
		t.Errorf("second token %q, Tokens = %d; want a distinct token and 2", second, s.Tokens())
	}
}

func TestFkAPIRequiresAnIssuedTokenAndTheTailnet(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	tok := fkToken(t, s)
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name, path, token string
		want              int
	}{
		{"no token", "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/devices", "", http.StatusUnauthorized},
		{"unknown token", "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/devices", "tskey-api-made-up", http.StatusUnauthorized},
		{"issued token", "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/devices", tok, http.StatusOK},
		{"default tailnet", "/api/v2/tailnet/-/devices", tok, http.StatusOK},
		{"other tailnet", "/api/v2/tailnet/other.org/devices", tok, http.StatusNotFound},
	} {
		if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, tc.path, tc.token, nil, ""); r.Status != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: status %d, want %d (%s)", tc.name, r.Status, tc.want, r.Body)
		}
	}
	if doc := fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/devices", "", nil, "").Body); doc["message"] == "" {
		t.Errorf("a refusal carries the provider's message member")
	}
}

func TestFkScopes(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	tok := fkToken(t, s)
	d := s.AddDevice(Device{Name: "web"})
	policy := `{"acls": []}`
	type call struct{ method, path, body string }
	var (
		listDevices  = call{http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/devices", ""}
		authorize    = call{http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/device/" + d + "/authorized", `{"authorized":true}`}
		getRoutes    = call{http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/device/" + d + "/routes", ""}
		setRoutes    = call{http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/device/" + d + "/routes", `{"routes":[]}`}
		listKeys     = call{http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/keys", ""}
		createKey    = call{http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/keys", `{"capabilities":{"devices":{"create":{"tags":["tag:a"]}}}}`}
		getPolicy    = call{http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/acl", ""}
		setPolicy    = call{http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/acl", policy}
		validatePol  = call{http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/acl/validate", policy}
		allEndpoints = []call{listDevices, authorize, getRoutes, setRoutes, listKeys, createKey, getPolicy, setPolicy, validatePol}
	)
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		scopes  []string
		allowed []call
	}{
		{[]string{"devices:core"}, []call{listDevices, authorize}},
		{[]string{"devices:core:read"}, []call{listDevices}},
		{[]string{"devices:routes"}, []call{getRoutes, setRoutes}},
		{[]string{"auth_keys"}, []call{listKeys, createKey}},
		{[]string{"policy_file:read"}, []call{getPolicy, validatePol}},
		{[]string{"policy_file"}, []call{getPolicy, setPolicy, validatePol}},
		{nil, nil},
	} {
		s.SetScopes(tc.scopes...)
		for _, c := range allEndpoints {
			want := http.StatusForbidden
			for _, a := range tc.allowed {
				if a == c {
					want = http.StatusOK
				}
			}
			if r := fkReq(t, s, c.method, c.path, tok, nil, c.body); r.Status != want {
				t.Errorf("scopes %v: %s %s answered %d, want %d (%s)", tc.scopes, c.method, c.path, r.Status, want, r.Body)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestFkFaultsComeFromTheSharedScaffolding(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	tok := fkToken(t, s)
	s.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/devices", cloudfake.Fault{Status: http.StatusTooManyRequests})
	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/devices", tok, nil, ""); r.Status != http.StatusTooManyRequests {
		t.Fatalf("faulted request answered %d, want 429", r.Status)
	}
	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/devices", tok, nil, ""); r.Status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("request after the fault answered %d, want 200", r.Status)
	}
	reqs := s.Cloud().Requests()
	last := reqs[len(reqs)-1]
	if last.Method != http.MethodGet || last.Header.Get("Authorization") != "Bearer "+tok {
		t.Errorf("request log last entry %+v does not show the bearer token", last)
	}
}
```

```go
package fake

func TestFkDevices(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	tok := fkToken(t, s)
	id := s.AddDevice(Device{Name: "web.example.ts.net", Hostname: "web", OS: "linux", User: "ann@example.com",
		Addresses: []string{"100.64.0.1"}, AdvertisedRoutes: []string{"10.0.0.0/24", "0.0.0.0/0"}, Tags: []string{"tag:srv"}})
	if id != "n1" {
		t.Fatalf("AddDevice assigned %q, want n1", id)
	}
	if got := s.AddDevice(Device{ID: "nodeX"}); got != "nodeX" {
		t.Fatalf("AddDevice with an id answered %q, want nodeX", got)
	}

	list := fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/devices?fields=all", tok, nil, "").Body)
	devs := list["devices"].([]any)
	if len(devs) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("list has %d devices, want 2", len(devs))
	}
	first := devs[0].(map[string]any)
	if first["id"] != "n1" || first["nodeId"] != "n1" || first["hostname"] != "web" || first["authorized"] != false {
		t.Errorf("first device %v", first)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(first["advertisedRoutes"], []any{"10.0.0.0/24", "0.0.0.0/0"}) || !reflect.DeepEqual(first["enabledRoutes"], []any{}) {
		t.Errorf("fields=all routes %v / %v", first["advertisedRoutes"], first["enabledRoutes"])
	}
	plain := fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/devices", tok, nil, "").Body)["devices"].([]any)[0].(map[string]any)
	if _, ok := plain["advertisedRoutes"]; ok {
		t.Errorf("a list without fields=all carries routes")
	}

	one := fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/device/n1?fields=all", tok, nil, "").Body)

		t.Errorf("device %v", one)
	}
	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, "/api/v2/device/none", tok, nil, ""); r.Status != http.StatusNotFound {
		t.Errorf("unknown device: status %d, want 404", r.Status)
	}

	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/device/n1/authorized", tok, nil, `{"authorized":true}`); r.Status != http.StatusOK {

	if !reflect.DeepEqual(routes["enabledRoutes"], []any{"10.0.0.0/24"}) || !reflect.DeepEqual(routes["advertisedRoutes"], []any{"10.0.0.0/24", "0.0.0.0/0"}) {
```

`internal/modules/tailnet/fake/keys_test.go`:

```go
package fake

import (
	"net/http"
	"reflect"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

const fkKeysPath = "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/keys"

func fkKeyBody(description string, expiry int, tags ...string) string {
	quoted := make([]string, len(tags))
	for i, tag := range tags {
		quoted[i] = `"` + tag + `"`
	}
	exp := ""
	if expiry != 0 {
		exp = `,"expirySeconds":` + strconv.Itoa(expiry)
	}
	return `{"capabilities":{"devices":{"create":{"reusable":true,"ephemeral":false,"preauthorized":true,"tags":[` +
		strings.Join(quoted, ",") + `]}}},"description":"` + description + `"` + exp + `}`
}

func TestFkKeyCreateRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	tok := fkToken(t, s)
	for name, body := range map[string]string{
		"no tags":             fkKeyBody("darkpanel-1", 0),
		"tag without prefix":  fkKeyBody("darkpanel-1", 0, "srv"),
		"description over 50": fkKeyBody(strings.Repeat("d", 51), 0, "tag:srv"),
		"expiry over 90 days": fkKeyBody("darkpanel-1", 7776001, "tag:srv"),
		"not json":            `{`,
	} {
		if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, fkKeysPath, tok, nil, body); r.Status != http.StatusBadRequest {
			t.Errorf("%s: status %d, want 400", name, r.Status)
		}
	}
	if len(s.Keys()) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("a refused create stored %d keys", len(s.Keys()))
	}
}

func TestFkKeyLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	tok := fkToken(t, s)
	before := time.Now().UTC().Add(-time.Second)
	r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, fkKeysPath, tok, nil, fkKeyBody("darkpanel-01J0", 3600, "tag:srv", "tag:db"))
	if r.Status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("create: %d %s", r.Status, r.Body)
	}
	created := fkDecode(t, r.Body)
	id, _ := created["id"].(string)
	secret, _ := created["key"].(string)
	if id == "" || !strings.HasPrefix(secret, "tskey-auth-") || created["description"] != "darkpanel-01J0" {
		t.Fatalf("create answer %s", r.Body)
	}
	create := created["capabilities"].(map[string]any)["devices"].(map[string]any)["create"].(map[string]any)
	if create["reusable"] != true || create["preauthorized"] != true || create["ephemeral"] != false ||
		!reflect.DeepEqual(create["tags"], []any{"tag:srv", "tag:db"}) {
		t.Errorf("capabilities %v", create)
	}
	exp, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, created["expires"].(string))
	if err != nil || exp.Before(before.Add(time.Hour)) || exp.After(time.Now().Add(time.Hour+time.Minute)) {
		t.Errorf("expires %v (%v), want about an hour from now", created["expires"], err)
	}
	keys := s.Keys()
	if len(keys) != 1 || keys[0].ID != id || keys[0].Key != secret || keys[0].Description != "darkpanel-01J0" ||
		!reflect.DeepEqual(keys[0].Tags, []string{"tag:srv", "tag:db"}) || !keys[0].Reusable || !keys[0].Preauthorized || keys[0].Ephemeral {
		t.Errorf("stored keys %+v", keys)
	}

	s.AddKey(Key{Description: "darkpanel-enroll-h1", Tags: []string{"tag:srv"}, Expires: time.Now().Add(time.Hour)})
	s.AddKey(Key{ID: "old", Revoked: true})
	list := fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, fkKeysPath, tok, nil, "").Body)["keys"].([]any)
	var ids []string
	for _, e := range list {
		ids = append(ids, e.(map[string]any)["id"].(string))
	}
	if len(ids) != 2 || ids[0] != id || ids[1] == "old" {
		t.Errorf("list ids %v, want the created key then the added one and not the revoked one", ids)
	}

	one := fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, fkKeysPath+"/"+id, tok, nil, "").Body)
	if one["id"] != id || one["description"] != "darkpanel-01J0" {
		t.Errorf("get %v", one)
	}
	if _, leaked := one["key"]; leaked {
		t.Errorf("get returns the key secret")
	}
	if old := fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, fkKeysPath+"/old", tok, nil, "").Body); old["revoked"] == nil {
		t.Errorf("a revoked key shows no revoked member: %v", old)
	}

	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodDelete, fkKeysPath+"/"+id, tok, nil, ""); r.Status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("delete: %d %s", r.Status, r.Body)
	}
	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, fkKeysPath+"/"+id, tok, nil, ""); r.Status != http.StatusNotFound {
		t.Errorf("get after delete: status %d, want 404", r.Status)
	}
	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodDelete, fkKeysPath+"/"+id, tok, nil, ""); r.Status != http.StatusNotFound {
		t.Errorf("second delete: status %d, want 404", r.Status)
	}
	if len(s.Keys()) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("Keys has %d entries after deleting one of three, want 2", len(s.Keys()))
	}
}

func TestFkKeyDefaultExpiry(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	tok := fkToken(t, s)
	fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, fkKeysPath, tok, nil, fkKeyBody("darkpanel-2", 0, "tag:srv"))
	k := s.Keys()[0]
	if got := k.Expires.Sub(k.Created); got != 90*24*time.Hour {
		t.Errorf("default expiry %v, want 90 days", got)
	}
}
```

`internal/modules/tailnet/fake/policy_test.go`:

```go
package fake

import (
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

const (
	fkACL      = "/api/v2/tailnet/example.com/acl"
	fkHuJSON   = "application/hujson"
	fkNewStyle = "{\n\t// keep this note\n\t\"acls\": [],\n}\n"
)

func TestFkPolicyRead(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	tok := fkToken(t, s)
	text, etag := s.Policy()
	if !strings.Contains(text, "//") || etag == "" {
		t.Fatalf("default policy %q etag %q: want a commented policy and an etag", text, etag)
	}

	r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, fkACL, tok, map[string]string{"Accept": fkHuJSON}, "")
	if r.Status != http.StatusOK || r.Body != text || r.Header.Get("ETag") != etag || !strings.HasPrefix(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"), fkHuJSON) {
		t.Errorf("hujson read: %d etag %q type %q body %q", r.Status, r.Header.Get("ETag"), r.Header.Get("Content-Type"), r.Body)
	}
	j := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, fkACL, tok, map[string]string{"Accept": "application/json"}, "")
	if strings.Contains(j.Body, "//") || fkDecode(t, j.Body)["acls"] == nil || j.Header.Get("ETag") != etag {
		t.Errorf("json read: etag %q body %q", j.Header.Get("ETag"), j.Body)
	}

	next := s.SetPolicy(fkNewStyle)
	if got, gotTag := s.Policy(); got != fkNewStyle || gotTag != next || next == etag {
		t.Errorf("after SetPolicy: text %q etag %q (returned %q, was %q)", got, gotTag, next, etag)
	}
	if again := s.SetPolicy(fkNewStyle); again != next {
		t.Errorf("same text gave etag %q, want %q", again, next)
	}
}

func TestFkPolicyWriteIsConditional(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	tok := fkToken(t, s)
	_, etag := s.Policy()
	hdr := func(match string) map[string]string {
		return map[string]string{"Content-Type": fkHuJSON, "Accept": fkHuJSON, "If-Match": match}
	}

	stale := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, fkACL, tok, hdr(`"stale"`), fkNewStyle)
	if stale.Status != http.StatusPreconditionFailed {
		t.Fatalf("stale If-Match: status %d, want 412", stale.Status)
	}
	if text, _ := s.Policy(); text == fkNewStyle {
		t.Fatalf("a refused write changed the policy")
	}

	ok := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, fkACL, tok, hdr(etag), fkNewStyle)
	_, now := s.Policy()
	if ok.Status != http.StatusOK || ok.Header.Get("ETag") != now || now == etag {
		t.Fatalf("matching If-Match: status %d, answered etag %q, stored %q, old %q", ok.Status, ok.Header.Get("ETag"), now, etag)
	}
	if text, _ := s.Policy(); text != fkNewStyle {
		t.Errorf("stored policy %q, want the posted text with its comment", text)
	}

	unquoted := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, fkACL, tok, hdr(strings.Trim(now, `"`)), "{}")
	if unquoted.Status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Errorf("If-Match without quotes: status %d, want 200", unquoted.Status)
	}
	bad := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, fkACL, tok, map[string]string{"Content-Type": fkHuJSON}, `{"acls": [`)
	if bad.Status != http.StatusBadRequest || fkDecode(t, bad.Body)["message"] == "" {
		t.Errorf("unparseable policy: %d %s, want 400 with a message", bad.Status, bad.Body)
	}
}

func TestFkPolicyValidate(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	tok := fkToken(t, s)
	_, etag := s.Policy()
	valid := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, fkACL+"/validate", tok, map[string]string{"Content-Type": fkHuJSON}, fkNewStyle)
	if valid.Status != http.StatusOK || strings.TrimSpace(valid.Body) != "" {
		t.Errorf("valid policy: %d %q, want 200 with an empty body", valid.Status, valid.Body)
	}
	for name, body := range map[string]string{"truncated": `{"acls": [`, "not an object": `[1]`} {
		r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, fkACL+"/validate", tok, map[string]string{"Content-Type": fkHuJSON}, body)
		doc := fkDecode(t, r.Body)
		if r.Status != http.StatusBadRequest || doc["message"] == "" || doc["data"] == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: %d %s, want 400 with message and data", name, r.Status, r.Body)
		}
	}
	if _, now := s.Policy(); now != etag {
		t.Errorf("validate changed the policy")
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

The server wraps a `cloudfake.Server` created with `cloudfake.New(tb)` and registers every endpoint with its `Handle(method, pattern, handler)` (patterns use `{t}` and `{id}` wildcards, read with `r.PathValue`). All state (scopes, issued tokens, devices, keys, policy text and ETag, a sequence counter) sits behind one `sync.Mutex`; the fake is safe for concurrent use. Every JSON answer carries `Content-Type: application/json`; every refusal is `{"message": "<text>"}`.

`fake.go`: constants `ClientID`, `ClientSecret`, `Tailnet` (Contracts); `Server`; `New(tb testing.TB) *Server` (calls `tb.Helper()`, starts the cloud server, holds all five scopes `devices:core`, `devices:routes`, `auth_keys`, `policy_file`, `devices:posture_attributes`, no devices or keys, the default policy of `policy.go`); `URL()`, `Client()`, `Cloud()` delegate to the cloud server; `SetScopes(scopes ...string)` replaces the granted set (copying the slice); `Tokens()` is the number of tokens issued.

1. `POST /api/v2/oauth/token` (no bearer needed): parses the form body. `grant_type` other than `client_credentials` answers 400 `{"error":"unsupported_grant_type"}`; `client_id` or `client_secret` not `ClientID`/`ClientSecret` answers 401 `{"error":"invalid_client"}`; otherwise it records a new token `tskey-api-fake-<n>` (n counting from 1) and answers 200 `{"access_token", "token_type":"Bearer", "expires_in":3600, "scope": <the granted scopes joined by a space>}`. A refused request issues nothing. Tokens never expire in the fake; a test that needs a 401 uses `Cloud().Fail`.
2. Every other endpoint is wrapped by one guard, checked in this order: no `Authorization: Bearer <t>` header with an issued token answers 401 `{"message":"API token invalid"}`; the endpoint's scope not granted answers 403 `{"message":"calling actor does not have enough permissions to perform this function"}`; a `{t}` that is neither `Tailnet` nor `-` answers 404. The scope each endpoint needs:

| Endpoint | Granted when the scope set holds |
|---|---|
| `GET …/devices`, `GET /api/v2/device/{id}` | `devices:core` or `devices:core:read` |
| `POST …/authorized`, `POST …/expire`, `DELETE /api/v2/device/{id}` | `devices:core` |
| `GET …/routes` | `devices:routes` or `devices:routes:read` |
| `POST …/routes` | `devices:routes` |
| `GET …/keys`, `GET …/keys/{id}` | `auth_keys` or `auth_keys:read` |
| `POST …/keys`, `DELETE …/keys/{id}` | `auth_keys` |
| `GET …/acl`, `POST …/acl/validate` | `policy_file` or `policy_file:read` |
| `POST …/acl` | `policy_file` |

`devices.go` (`Device` as in Contracts; `AddDevice` stores a copy, assigns `n<sequence>` to an empty `ID` using the shared counter, replaces a stored device with the same id, and answers the id; `Device(id)` answers a copy):

3. A device renders as `{"id": ID, "nodeId": ID, "name", "hostname", "os", "user", "addresses", "tags", "authorized", "keyExpiryDisabled"}` with `lastSeen` and `expires` only when set, nil slices as `[]`, and `advertisedRoutes` and `enabledRoutes` only when the request has the query `fields=all`.
4. `GET /api/v2/tailnet/{t}/devices` answers `{"devices": [...]}` in insertion order. `GET /api/v2/device/{id}` answers the device; an unknown id answers 404 `{"message":"device not found"}` (the same for every `/api/v2/device/{id}…` endpoint). `POST …/authorized` with `{"authorized": bool}` sets the flag and answers 200 `{}`; an undecodable body answers 400. `POST …/expire` sets `Expires` to the current time (RFC 3339) and answers 200 `{}`. `DELETE /api/v2/device/{id}` removes the device and answers 200 with an empty body. `GET …/routes` answers `{"advertisedRoutes": [...], "enabledRoutes": [...]}` (never null); `POST …/routes` with `{"routes": [...]}` stores the list as `EnabledRoutes` exactly as given (no intersection with the advertised ones) and answers the same document; a body without a `routes` member answers 400.

`keys.go` (`Key` as in Contracts; `Keys()` answers copies in creation order; `AddKey(k)` assigns `k<sequence>` to an empty `ID` and the current time to a zero `Created`, and appends):

5. `POST /api/v2/tailnet/{t}/keys` takes `{"capabilities":{"devices":{"create":{"reusable","ephemeral","preauthorized","tags"}}},"expirySeconds","description"}`. It answers 400 for: an undecodable body, no tags or a tag not starting `tag:`, a description over 50 bytes, `expirySeconds` negative or over 7776000; nothing is stored then. `expirySeconds` 0 means 7776000 (90 days). It stores a `Key` with id `k<sequence>`, secret `tskey-auth-<id>-secret`, `Created` now (UTC), `Expires` `Created` plus the expiry, and the requested fields, and answers 200 with the key object plus `key` (the secret).
6. The key object is `{"id", "description", "created", "expires", "capabilities": {"devices": {"create": {"reusable", "ephemeral", "preauthorized", "tags"}}}}` with times RFC 3339 and `revoked` (the creation time as a string) only for a revoked key. `GET …/keys` answers `{"keys": [{"id": …}, …]}` in creation order and leaves out revoked keys. `GET …/keys/{id}` answers the key object without `key`; an unknown id answers 404 `{"message":"key not found"}`. `DELETE …/keys/{id}` removes the key and answers 200 with an empty body; an unknown id answers 404.

`policy.go` (`SetPolicy`, `Policy`):

7. The default policy is a HuJSON object with a comment and one accept-everything rule, so tests can see comments survive. An ETag is `"` + the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the text + `"`, with the quotes; the same text always has the same ETag. `SetPolicy(text)` stores the text unchecked and answers the new ETag; `Policy()` answers the text and ETag.
8. `GET …/acl` answers 200 with the ETag header. When `Accept` contains `application/hujson` the body is the stored text with that content type; otherwise it is the text standardized with `hujson.Standardize` as `application/json`.
9. A policy is valid when `hujson.Parse` accepts it and its value is an object. `POST …/acl` with an invalid body answers 400 `{"message": "invalid policy: …", "data": []}` and stores nothing. When the request has an `If-Match` header whose value (with surrounding quotes removed) differs from the stored ETag (quotes removed) it answers 412 `{"message":"precondition failed, invalid old hash"}` and stores nothing; without the header it writes unconditionally. A successful write stores the body text verbatim and answers 200 as `GET` does, with the new ETag header.
10. `POST …/acl/validate` answers 200 with an empty body for a valid policy and the same 400 body as item 9 for an invalid one; it never changes the stored policy.

```go
package fake

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/cloud/cloudfake"
)

// fkResult is one answer of the server.
type fkResult struct {
	Status int
	Body   string
}

// fkReq sends one request with the server's token; an empty token sends none.
func fkReq(t *testing.T, s *Server, method, path, token, body string) fkResult {
	t.Helper()
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), method, s.URL()+path, strings.NewReader(body))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if token != "" {
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
	}
	res, err := s.Client().Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = res.Body.Close() }()
	b, err := io.ReadAll(res.Body)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return fkResult{res.StatusCode, string(b)}
}

// fkEnvelope is Cloudflare's answer envelope.
type fkEnvelope struct {
	Success bool `json:"success"`
	Errors  []struct {
		Code    int    `json:"code"`
		Message string `json:"message"`
	} `json:"errors"`
	Messages   []any           `json:"messages"`
	Result     json.RawMessage `json:"result"`
	ResultInfo *struct {
		Count      int `json:"count"`
		TotalCount int `json:"total_count"`
	} `json:"result_info"`
}

func fkDecode(t *testing.T, r fkResult) fkEnvelope {
	t.Helper()
	var e fkEnvelope
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(r.Body), &e); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("body %q is not an envelope: %v", r.Body, err)
	}
	if e.Errors == nil || e.Messages == nil {
		t.Fatalf("envelope %q lacks errors or messages arrays", r.Body)
	}
	return e
}

func fkObject(t *testing.T, raw json.RawMessage) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	var m map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("result %s is not an object: %v", raw, err)
	}
	return m
}

func fkList(t *testing.T, e fkEnvelope) []map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	var l []map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Result, &l); err != nil || l == nil {
		t.Fatalf("result %s is not an array: %v", e.Result, err)
	}
	if e.ResultInfo == nil || e.ResultInfo.Count != len(l) || e.ResultInfo.TotalCount != len(l) {
		t.Fatalf("result_info %+v does not describe %d items", e.ResultInfo, len(l))
	}
	return l
}

func fkAccount(suffix string) string { return "/accounts/" + AccountID + suffix }

func TestFkAuthAndPermissions(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	zone := s.AddZone("example.com")
	tunnels, zones, records := fkAccount("/cfd_tunnel"), "/zones", "/zones/"+zone+"/dns_records"

	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, tunnels, "", ""); r.Status != http.StatusUnauthorized || fkDecode(t, r).Success {
		t.Errorf("no token: %d %s, want 401 with success false", r.Status, r.Body)
	}
	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, tunnels, "wrong", ""); r.Status != http.StatusUnauthorized {
		t.Errorf("wrong token: status %d, want 401", r.Status)
	}
	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, "/accounts/ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff/cfd_tunnel", Token, ""); r.Status != http.StatusForbidden {
		t.Errorf("another account: status %d, want 403", r.Status)
	}

	for _, tc := range []struct {
		perms                                 []string
		tunnelsOK, zonesOK, recordsOK, verify bool
	}{
		{[]string{PermTunnelWrite, PermZoneRead, PermDNSWrite}, true, true, true, true},
		{[]string{PermTunnelWrite}, true, false, false, true},
		{[]string{PermZoneRead}, false, true, false, true},
		{[]string{PermDNSWrite}, false, false, true, true},
		{nil, false, false, false, true},
	} {
		s.SetPermissions(tc.perms...)
		for path, want := range map[string]bool{tunnels: tc.tunnelsOK, zones: tc.zonesOK, records: tc.recordsOK, fkAccount("/tokens/verify"): tc.verify} {
			r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, path, Token, "")
			if (r.Status == http.StatusOK) != want {
				t.Errorf("permissions %v: GET %s answered %d, want ok=%t", tc.perms, path, r.Status, want)
			}
			if !want {
				e := fkDecode(t, r)
				if r.Status != http.StatusForbidden || e.Success || len(e.Errors) != 1 || e.Errors[0].Code != 10000 {
					t.Errorf("permissions %v: GET %s refusal %d %s, want 403 with error code 10000", tc.perms, path, r.Status, r.Body)
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestFkVerifyToken(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, fkAccount("/tokens/verify"), Token, "")
	e := fkDecode(t, r)
	if r.Status != http.StatusOK || !e.Success || fkObject(t, e.Result)["status"] != "active" {
		t.Errorf("verify: %d %s", r.Status, r.Body)
	}
}

func TestFkBothBasePathsServeTheAPI(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	for _, prefix := range []string{"", "/client/v4"} {
		if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, prefix+fkAccount("/cfd_tunnel"), Token, ""); r.Status != http.StatusOK {
			t.Errorf("prefix %q: status %d, want 200", prefix, r.Status)
		}
	}
}

func TestFkFaultsComeFromTheSharedScaffolding(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	path := fkAccount("/cfd_tunnel")
	s.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodPost, path, cloudfake.Fault{LoseResponse: true})
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), http.MethodPost, s.URL()+path, strings.NewReader(`{"name":"darkpanel-1","config_src":"cloudflare"}`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+Token)
	if res, err := s.Client().Do(req); err == nil {
		_ = res.Body.Close()
		t.Fatalf("a lost response reached the client")
	}
	if got := s.Tunnels(); len(got) != 1 || got[0].Name != "darkpanel-1" {
		t.Errorf("tunnels after a lost response = %+v, want the write committed", got)
	}
	reqs := s.Cloud().Requests()
	if len(reqs) != 1 || reqs[0].Header.Get("Authorization") != "Bearer "+Token {
		t.Errorf("request log %+v", reqs)
	}
}
```

```go
package fake

import (
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"reflect"
	"testing"

func TestFkTunnelLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	base := fkAccount("/cfd_tunnel")
	for name, body := range map[string]string{
		"no name":         `{"config_src":"cloudflare"}`,
		"locally managed": `{"name":"x","config_src":"local"}`,
		"not json":        `{`,
	} {
		if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, base, Token, body); r.Status != http.StatusBadRequest {
			t.Errorf("create %s: status %d, want 400", name, r.Status)
		}
	}
	r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, base, Token, `{"name":"darkpanel-01J0","config_src":"cloudflare"}`)
	created := fkObject(t, fkDecode(t, r).Result)
	id, _ := created["id"].(string)
	if r.Status != http.StatusOK || id == "" || created["name"] != "darkpanel-01J0" || created["status"] != "inactive" || created["deleted_at"] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("create: %d %s", r.Status, r.Body)
	}
	if dup := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, base, Token, `{"name":"darkpanel-01J0","config_src":"cloudflare"}`); dup.Status != http.StatusConflict {
		t.Errorf("duplicate name: status %d, want 409", dup.Status)
	}
	other := s.AddTunnel("legacy")

	named := fkList(t, fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, base+"?is_deleted=false&name=legacy", Token, "")))
	if len(named) != 1 || named[0]["id"] != other {
		t.Errorf("list by name = %v, want only the legacy tunnel", named)
	}
	if all := fkList(t, fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, base+"?is_deleted=false", Token, ""))); len(all) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("list = %d tunnels, want 2", len(all))
	}

	s.SetConnections(id, 2)
	one := fkObject(t, fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, base+"/"+id, Token, "")).Result)
	conns, _ := one["connections"].([]any)
	if one["status"] != "healthy" || len(conns) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("tunnel with two connections: status %v, %d connection entries", one["status"], len(conns))
	}
	if c := conns[0].(map[string]any); c["colo_name"] == "" || c["origin_ip"] == "" || c["opened_at"] == "" || c["client_version"] == "" {
		t.Errorf("connection entry %v lacks members", c)
	}

	connectors := fkList(t, fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, base+"/"+id+"/connections", Token, "")))
	if len(connectors) != 1 || len(connectors[0]["conns"].([]any)) != 2 || connectors[0]["version"] == "" {
		t.Errorf("connections endpoint = %v, want one connector with two conns", connectors)
	}
	s.SetConnections(other, 0)
	if none := fkList(t, fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, base+"/"+other+"/connections", Token, ""))); len(none) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("connections of an idle tunnel = %v, want none", none)
	}

	tok := fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, base+"/"+id+"/token", Token, ""))
	var encoded string
	if err := json.Unmarshal(tok.Result, &encoded); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("token result %s is not a string", tok.Result)
	}
	raw, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(encoded)
	if err != nil || !json.Valid(raw) || !reflect.DeepEqual(fkObject(t, raw)["t"], id) {
		t.Errorf("token %q does not decode to a document naming the tunnel (%v)", encoded, err)
	}

	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodDelete, base+"/"+id, Token, ""); r.Status != http.StatusBadRequest {
		t.Errorf("delete with connections: status %d, want 400", r.Status)
	}
	s.SetConnections(id, 0)
	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodDelete, base+"/"+id, Token, ""); r.Status != http.StatusOK || fkObject(t, fkDecode(t, r).Result)["id"] != id {
		t.Fatalf("delete: %d %s", r.Status, r.Body)
	}
	if got := s.Tunnels(); len(got) != 1 || got[0].ID != other {
		t.Errorf("Tunnels after delete = %+v, want only the legacy tunnel", got)
	}
	for _, path := range []string{base + "/" + id, base + "/" + id + "/token", base + "/" + id + "/configurations"} {
		if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, path, Token, ""); r.Status != http.StatusNotFound {
			t.Errorf("GET %s after delete: status %d, want 404", path, r.Status)
		}
	}
}

func TestFkTunnelConfiguration(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	id := s.AddTunnel("darkpanel-1")
	path := fkAccount("/cfd_tunnel/" + id + "/configurations")

	fresh := fkObject(t, fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, path, Token, "")).Result)
	if fresh["config"] != nil || fresh["tunnel_id"] != id || s.Configuration(id) != nil {
		t.Errorf("a new tunnel has configuration %v / %s", fresh["config"], s.Configuration(id))
	}

	good := `{"ingress":[{"hostname":"a.example.com","service":"http://web:80"},{"service":"http_status:404"}]}`
	r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPut, path, Token, `{"config":`+good+`}`)
	put := fkObject(t, fkDecode(t, r).Result)
	if r.Status != http.StatusOK || put["version"] != float64(1) {
		t.Fatalf("put: %d %s", r.Status, r.Body)
	}
	if string(s.Configuration(id)) != good {
		t.Errorf("stored configuration %s, want the posted config member byte for byte", s.Configuration(id))
	}
	got := fkObject(t, fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, path, Token, "")).Result)
	cfg, _ := json.Marshal(got["config"])
	if !json.Valid(cfg) || got["version"] != float64(1) || string(cfg) != good {
		t.Errorf("get after put: version %v config %s", got["version"], cfg)
	}

	for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
		body string
		code int
	}{
		"no catch-all":          {`{"config":{"ingress":[{"hostname":"a.example.com","service":"http://web:80"}]}}`, 1015},
		"empty ingress":         {`{"config":{"ingress":[]}}`, 1015},
		"catch-all with a path": {`{"config":{"ingress":[{"path":"/x","service":"http_status:404"}]}}`, 1015},
		"no config member":      {`{}`, 1001},
	} {
		r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPut, path, Token, tc.body)
		if e := fkDecode(t, r); r.Status != http.StatusBadRequest || len(e.Errors) != 1 || e.Errors[0].Code != tc.code {
			t.Errorf("%s: %d %s, want 400 with code %d", name, r.Status, r.Body, tc.code)
		}
	}
	if string(s.Configuration(id)) != good {
		t.Errorf("a refused put changed the configuration to %s", s.Configuration(id))
	}

	replaced := `{"ingress":[{"service":"http_status:404"}],"warp-routing":{"enabled":true}}`
	s.SetConfiguration(id, json.RawMessage(replaced))
	if string(s.Configuration(id)) != replaced {
		t.Errorf("SetConfiguration then Configuration = %s", s.Configuration(id))
	}
	again := fkObject(t, fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, path, Token, "")).Result)
	if again["version"] != float64(2) {
		t.Errorf("version after SetConfiguration = %v, want 2", again["version"])
	}
	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPut, fkAccount("/cfd_tunnel/none/configurations"), Token, `{"config":{}}`); r.Status != http.StatusNotFound {
		t.Errorf("put for an unknown tunnel: status %d, want 404", r.Status)
	}
}
```

```go
func TestFkDNSRecords(t *testing.T) {
	s := New(t)
	zone := s.AddZone("example.com")
	base := "/zones/" + zone + "/dns_records"

	r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, base, Token, fkRecordBody("a.example.com", "t1.cfargotunnel.com", "darkpanel:01J0"))
	rec := fkObject(t, fkDecode(t, r).Result)
	id, _ := rec["id"].(string)
	if r.Status != http.StatusOK || id == "" || rec["proxied"] != true || rec["comment"] != "darkpanel:01J0" || rec["type"] != "CNAME" {

	want := []Record{{ID: id, Type: "CNAME", Name: "a.example.com", Content: "t1.cfargotunnel.com", Comment: "darkpanel:01J0", Proxied: true}}
	if got := s.Records(zone); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("Records = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}

	if dup := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, base, Token, fkRecordBody("a.example.com", "t1.cfargotunnel.com", "other")); dup.Status != http.StatusBadRequest ||
		fkDecode(t, dup).Errors[0].Code != 81058 {
		t.Errorf("identical record: %d %s, want 400 with code 81058", dup.Status, dup.Body)
	}
	if bad := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, base, Token, `{"type":"CNAME"}`); bad.Status != http.StatusBadRequest {
		t.Errorf("record without a name: status %d, want 400", bad.Status)

	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodPost, "/zones/nozone/dns_records", Token, fkRecordBody("a", "b", "")); r.Status != http.StatusNotFound {

	}

	own := s.AddRecord(zone, Record{Type: "A", Name: "b.example.com", Content: "192.0.2.1", Comment: "mine"})
	if own == "" || own == id {

	for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
		query string
		ids   []string
	}{
		"nothing":       {"", []string{id, own}},
		"name":          {"name=b.example.com", []string{own}},
		"exact comment": {"comment.exact=darkpanel:01J0", []string{id}},
		"comment part":  {"comment.contains=panel", []string{id}},
		"type":          {"type=A", []string{own}},
		"no match":      {"name=" + url.QueryEscape("c.example.com"), nil},
	} {
		var got []string
		for _, m := range fkList(t, fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, base+"?"+tc.query, Token, ""))) {
			got = append(got, m["id"].(string))
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tc.ids) {
			t.Errorf("filter %s: ids %v, want %v", name, got, tc.ids)
		}
	}

	one := fkObject(t, fkDecode(t, fkReq(t, s, http.MethodGet, base+"/"+id, Token, "")).Result)
	if one["content"] != "t1.cfargotunnel.com" || one["zone_id"] != zone {
		t.Errorf("get = %v", one)
	}
	if r := fkReq(t, s, http.MethodDelete, base+"/"+id, Token, ""); r.Status != http.StatusOK || fkObject(t, fkDecode(t, r).Result)["id"] != id {
		t.Fatalf("delete: %d %s", r.Status, r.Body)
	}
	for _, method := range []string{http.MethodGet, http.MethodDelete} {
		if r := fkReq(t, s, method, base+"/"+id, Token, ""); r.Status != http.StatusNotFound || fkDecode(t, r).Errors[0].Code != 81044 {
			t.Errorf("%s of a deleted record: %d %s, want 404 with code 81044", method, r.Status, r.Body)
		}
	}
	if got := s.Records(zone); len(got) != 1 || got[0].ID != own {
		t.Errorf("Records after delete = %+v, want only the added record", got)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

The server wraps a `cloudfake.Server` from `cloudfake.New(tb)`. All state (permissions, zones, tunnels, configurations, records, a sequence counter) sits behind one `sync.Mutex`; the fake is safe for concurrent use. Handlers are registered through one helper `route(method, path, permission, handler)` that registers the guarded handler twice, at `path` and at `/client/v4` + `path`, so `URL()` is a valid base URL with or without the API prefix (Task 32's client may use either). Path patterns use `{a}`, `{id}` and `{z}` wildcards, read with `r.PathValue`.

Every answer is Cloudflare's envelope `{"success", "errors", "messages", "result"}` with `errors` and `messages` always arrays and `result_info` (`page` 1, `per_page`, `count`, `total_count`, `total_pages` 1) on list answers; a list result is always an array, `[]` when empty. A refusal is `{"success": false, "errors": [{"code", "message"}], "messages": [], "result": null}`.

`fake.go`: constants `Token`, `AccountID`, `PermTunnelWrite`, `PermZoneRead`, `PermDNSWrite` (Contracts); `New(tb testing.TB) *Server` (calls `tb.Helper()`, holds all three permissions); `URL()`, `Client()`, `Cloud()` delegate to the cloud server; `SetPermissions(perms ...string)` replaces the held set; `AddZone(name)` stores a zone with a 32-hex-digit id and answers it.

1. The guard checks, in order: `Authorization` not `Bearer ` + `Token` answers 401 with error code 1000 ("Invalid API Token"); an `{a}` other than `AccountID`, or the endpoint's permission not held, answers 403 with error code 10000 ("Authentication error"). Permission by endpoint: `PermTunnelWrite` for every `/accounts/{a}/cfd_tunnel…` path with any method; `PermZoneRead` for `GET /zones`; `PermDNSWrite` for every `/zones/{z}/dns_records…` path with any method; none for `GET /accounts/{a}/tokens/verify`, which answers 200 `{"id": "fake-token-id", "status": "active"}`.
2. `GET /zones` answers `{id, name, status:"active", account:{id, name}}` for each zone in creation order, only the zone named by the `name` query when given.

`tunnels.go` (`Tunnel` as in Contracts; ids are `00000000-0000-4000-8000-` + a 12-digit zero-padded sequence number from the shared counter; `AddTunnel(name)` stores a tunnel created now and answers its id; `Tunnels()` answers copies of the stored tunnels in creation order; `SetConnections(id, n)` sets the count, ignoring an unknown id):

3. A tunnel renders as `{"id", "account_tag": AccountID, "name", "status", "created_at", "deleted_at": null, "connections": [...], "tun_type": "cfd_tunnel", "remote_config": true}` with `status` `healthy` when `Connections > 0`, else `inactive`, and `connections` one entry per connection: `{"id": "conn-<i>", "uuid": "conn-<i>", "colo_name": "fake01", "origin_ip": "198.51.100.<i>", "opened_at", "is_pending_reconnect": false, "client_id", "client_version": "2026.1.0"}` with i from 1.
4. `GET /accounts/{a}/cfd_tunnel` lists the stored tunnels, only those whose name equals the `name` query when it is given (the `is_deleted` query is accepted and ignored: deleted tunnels are not stored). `POST` takes `{"name", "config_src"}`: an undecodable body, an empty name or a `config_src` other than `cloudflare` answers 400 with code 1001; a name already stored answers 409 with code 1013; otherwise it stores the tunnel and answers its object. `GET …/{id}` answers the object; an unknown id answers 404 with code 1003 (the same for every `…/cfd_tunnel/{id}…` endpoint).
5. `DELETE …/{id}` answers 400 with code 1022 while `Connections > 0`; otherwise it removes the tunnel and its configuration and answers its object with `deleted_at` set. `GET …/{id}/token` answers a string result: the standard base64 of a JSON object `{"a": AccountID, "t": <tunnel id>, "s": "fake-tunnel-secret"}`. `GET …/{id}/connections` answers `[]` when the tunnel has no connections and otherwise one connector `{"id", "version": "2026.1.0", "arch": "linux_amd64", "run_at", "conns": [one entry per connection with id, uuid, colo_name, origin_ip, opened_at, is_pending_reconnect]}`.
6. Configuration: `GET …/{id}/configurations` answers `{"tunnel_id", "source": "cloudflare", "created_at", "version", "config"}` with `config` null and `version` 0 until one is stored. `PUT` takes `{"config": <object>}`; a body without a `config` member, or undecodable, answers 400 with code 1001. When the config has an `ingress` member, the list must be non-empty and its last rule must have neither `hostname` nor `path`, else 400 with code 1015 ("The last ingress rule must match all URLs (it must not have a hostname or path)"); a config without `ingress` is accepted. A stored config is the exact bytes of the `config` member (`json.RawMessage`, cloned), its `version` counts stored writes from 1, and the answer is the same document as `GET`. A refused `PUT` changes nothing. `Configuration(id)` answers the stored bytes (cloned), nil when none; `SetConfiguration(id, raw)` stores `raw` without validation and bumps the version.

`dns.go` (`Record` as in Contracts; ids are `rec` + a 29-digit hex sequence number; `AddRecord(zoneID, r)` appends and answers the id, assigning one when `r.ID` is empty; `Records(zoneID)` answers copies in creation order):

7. A record renders as `{"id", "zone_id", "type", "name", "content", "comment", "proxied", "ttl": 1, "created_on", "modified_on"}`. Every `/zones/{z}/dns_records…` endpoint answers 404 with code 7003 for a zone that was not added.
8. `GET /zones/{z}/dns_records` lists the zone's records, narrowed by whichever of the queries `name` (exact), `type` (exact), `comment.exact` and `comment.contains` are given; other queries are ignored. `POST` takes `{"type", "name", "content", "comment", "proxied", "ttl"}`: an undecodable body or an empty type, name or content answers 400 with code 9005; a record with the same type, name and content already in the zone answers 400 with code 81058; otherwise it stores the record and answers its object. `GET …/{id}` answers the record and `DELETE …/{id}` removes it and answers `{"id": <id>}`; an unknown id answers 404 with code 81044.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Each test file keeps its own helpers under its own prefix (`dc`, `nt`, `vt`, `pt`). Plan requests go to `POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/<action>/v1/plan` with the body `{input}`; the stubs answer a plan whose confirmation is null unless a test says otherwise.

Create `web/src/modules/docker/docker-change.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test, vi } from "vitest"
import type { Plan } from "@/api/types"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { DockerChange } from "./docker-change"
import { dockerKey } from "./types"

function dcPlan(action: string, over: Partial<Plan> = {}): Plan {
  return {
    planId: "p1", hostId: "h1", action, version: 1, inputHash: "h",
    diff: [{ op: "~", text: `${action} web` }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z", confirmation: null, ...over,
  }
}

const DC_DONE = { id: "c1", state: "completed", class: "compensable", error: null, output: null, revertDeadline: null }

function dcAvailable(action: string): StubHandler {
  return { body: { module: "docker", available: true, reason: null, actions: [{ name: action, available: true, reason: null }] } }
}

function dcRender(action: string, input: Record<string, unknown> | null, routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}) {
  const calls = stubFetch({
    "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/modules/docker/availability": dcAvailable(action),
    [`POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/${action}/v1/plan`]: { body: dcPlan(action) },
    [`POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/${action}/v1/apply`]: { body: DC_DONE },
    ...routes,
  })
  const onClose = vi.fn()
  const result = renderWithProviders(<DockerChange hostId="h1" action={action} title="Start web" input={input} onClose={onClose} />)
  return { calls, onClose, ...result }
}

test("stays closed and asks nothing while the input is null", () => {
  const { calls } = dcRender("docker.container.start", null)
  expect(screen.queryByRole("dialog")).toBeNull()
  expect(calls).toEqual([])
})

test("plans the action on the host and applies it without a revert timeout", async () => {
  const { calls } = dcRender("docker.container.start", { container: "web" })
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Start web" })
  expect((await within(dialog).findByLabelText("Planned changes")).textContent).toBe("~ docker.container.start web")
  expect(within(dialog).queryByLabelText("Revert after (seconds)")).toBeNull()
  const apply = within(dialog).getByRole("button", { name: "Apply" })
  await waitFor(() => expect(apply.hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(false))
  await userEvent.setup().click(apply)
  await waitFor(() => expect(calls.some((c) => c.path.endsWith("/apply"))).toBe(true))
  expect(calls.find((c) => c.path.endsWith("/plan"))?.path).toBe("/api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.container.start/v1/plan")
  expect(calls.find((c) => c.path.endsWith("/plan"))?.body).toEqual({ input: { container: "web" } })
  expect(calls.find((c) => c.path.endsWith("/apply"))?.body).toEqual({ planId: "p1" })
})

test("an action that asks for the typed name applies only after it is typed", async () => {
  const action = "docker.compose.down"
  const { calls } = dcRender(action, { project: "blog" }, { [`POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/${action}/v1/plan`]: { body: dcPlan(action, { confirmation: "blog" }) } })
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Start web" })
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  const apply = await within(dialog).findByRole("button", { name: "Apply" })

})

})
```

```tsx
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
```
