const NT_LIST = "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/resources/docker/networks"

function ntPlan(call: FetchCall) {
  const action = call.path.split("/")[6] ?? ""
  return { body: { planId: "p1", hostId: "h1", action, version: 1, inputHash: "h", diff: [{ op: "~", text: action }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z", confirmation: null } }
}

function ntNetworks(): DockerNetwork[] {
  return [
    dkNetwork({ id: "n1", name: "bridge", driver: "bridge", scope: "local", internal: false, ipv6: false, subnets: ["172.17.0.0/16"], containers: ["web", "db"], owner: undefined }),
    dkNetwork({ id: "n2", name: "backend", driver: "bridge", scope: "local", internal: true, ipv6: true, subnets: ["10.9.0.0/24", "fd00::/64"], containers: [], owner: undefined }),
    dkNetwork({ id: "n3", name: "darkpanel-tunnel", driver: "bridge", scope: "local", internal: false, ipv6: false, subnets: ["172.31.255.0/28"], containers: ["cloudflared"], owner: "cloudflare" }),
  ]
}

function ntRender(networks: DockerNetwork[] = ntNetworks(), routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}) {
  const calls = stubFetch({
    [NT_LIST]: { body: { networks } },
    "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/modules/docker/availability": { body: { module: "docker", available: true, reason: null, actions: [] } },
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.network.create/v1/plan": ntPlan,
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.network.remove/v1/plan": ntPlan,
    ...routes,
  })
  const result = renderWithProviders(<NetworksTab hostId="h1" />)
  return { calls, ...result }
}

function ntRow(n: number): HTMLElement {
  const row = within(screen.getByRole("table", { name: "Docker networks" })).getAllByRole("row")[n]
  if (row === undefined) throw new Error(`no row ${n}`)
  return row
}

function ntCells(n: number): (string | null)[] {
  return within(ntRow(n)).getAllByRole("cell").map((c) => c.textContent)
}

function ntPlanBodies(calls: FetchCall[]): unknown[] {
  return calls.filter((c) => c.method === "POST" && c.path.endsWith("/plan")).map((c) => c.body)
}

```tsx
import { screen, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import { formatTime } from "@/lib/format"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type FetchCall, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { dkProject } from "./fixtures"
import { ProjectsTab } from "./projects-tab"
import type { DockerProject } from "./types"

const PT_LIST = "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/resources/docker/projects"
const PT_RAN = "2026-10-29T12:00:00Z"

function ptPlan(call: FetchCall) {
  const action = call.path.split("/")[6] ?? ""
  return { body: { planId: "p1", hostId: "h1", action, version: 1, inputHash: "h", diff: [{ op: "~", text: action }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z", confirmation: null } }
}

function ptProjects(): DockerProject[] {
  return [
    dkProject({
      name: "blog", directory: "/srv/blog", files: ["/srv/blog/compose.yaml", "/srv/blog/compose.prod.yaml"], envFiles: ["/srv/blog/.env"],
      profiles: ["web"], configHash: "abc123", hashChanged: true, containers: ["blog-web-1", "blog-db-1"], running: 1, lastRun: PT_RAN,
    }),
    dkProject({
      name: "mail", directory: "/srv/mail", files: ["/srv/mail/compose.yaml"], envFiles: [], profiles: [], configHash: "", hashChanged: false,
      containers: [], running: 0, lastRun: undefined,
    }),
  ]
}

function ptRender(projects: DockerProject[] = ptProjects(), routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}) {
  const calls = stubFetch({
    [PT_LIST]: { body: { projects } },
    "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/modules/docker/availability": { body: { module: "docker", available: true, reason: null, actions: [] } },
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.compose.up/v1/plan": ptPlan,
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.compose.down/v1/plan": ptPlan,
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.compose.pull/v1/plan": ptPlan,
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.compose.restart/v1/plan": ptPlan,
    ...routes,
  })
  renderWithProviders(<ProjectsTab hostId="h1" />)
  return calls
}

async function ptProject(name: string): Promise<HTMLElement> {
  return screen.findByRole("region", { name: `Project ${name}` })
}

function ptValue(section: HTMLElement, label: string): string | null | undefined {
  return within(section).getByText(label, { selector: "dt" }).nextElementSibling?.textContent
}

function ptPlanned(calls: FetchCall[]): { path: string; body: unknown }[] {
  return calls.filter((c) => c.method === "POST" && c.path.endsWith("/plan")).map((c) => ({ path: c.path, body: c.body }))
}

test("shows each project's files, containers and last run", async () => {
  ptRender()
  const blog = await ptProject("blog")
  expect(ptValue(blog, "Directory")).toBe("/srv/blog")
  expect(ptValue(blog, "Compose files")).toBe("/srv/blog/compose.yaml, /srv/blog/compose.prod.yaml")
  expect(ptValue(blog, "Env files")).toBe("/srv/blog/.env")
  expect(ptValue(blog, "Containers")).toBe("blog-web-1, blog-db-1")
  expect(ptValue(blog, "Last run")).toBe(formatTime(PT_RAN))
  expect(within(blog).getByText("1 of 2 running").textContent).toBe("1 of 2 running")
  const mail = await ptProject("mail")
  expect(ptValue(mail, "Env files")).toBe("none")
  expect(ptValue(mail, "Containers")).toBe("none")
  expect(ptValue(mail, "Last run")).toBe("never")
})

test("a changed hash and unreadable files are called out", async () => {
  ptRender()
  const blog = await ptProject("blog")
  expect(within(blog).getByText("The Compose files changed since the last run.").textContent).toBe("The Compose files changed since the last run.")
  expect(within(blog).queryByText("The Compose files cannot be read.")).toBeNull()
  const mail = await ptProject("mail")
  expect(within(mail).getByText("The Compose files cannot be read.").textContent).toBe("The Compose files cannot be read.")
  expect(within(mail).queryByText("The Compose files changed since the last run.")).toBeNull()
})

test("says so when no Compose project was found", async () => {
  ptRender([])
  expect((await screen.findByText("No Compose projects")).textContent).toBe("No Compose projects")
})

test("shows the reason when the projects cannot be read", async () => {
  ptRender([], {
    [PT_LIST]: { status: 503, body: { type: "about:blank", title: "Docker unavailable", status: 503, detail: "the Docker daemon is not reachable", code: "docker.engine_unavailable" } },
  })
  expect((await screen.findByRole("alert")).textContent).toBe("the Docker daemon is not reachable")
})

test.each([
  ["Up", "docker.compose.up", "Start project blog"],
  ["Down", "docker.compose.down", "Take down project blog"],
  ["Pull", "docker.compose.pull", "Pull images of project blog"],
  ["Restart", "docker.compose.restart", "Restart project blog"],
])("%s plans %s with the project name and leaves the stored profiles alone", async (button, action, title) => {
  const calls = ptRender()
  await ptProject("blog")
  await userEvent.setup().click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: `${button} blog` }))
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: title })
  await within(dialog).findByLabelText("Planned changes")
  expect(ptPlanned(calls)).toEqual([{ path: `/api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/${action}/v1/plan`, body: { input: { project: "blog" } } }])
})

test.each([
  ["a new list", "web, worker", ["web", "worker"]],
  ["extra spaces and an empty entry", "  web ,, worker  ", ["web", "worker"]],
  ["an emptied field", "", []],
])("%s typed in Profiles replaces the stored list in the input", async (_name, typed, want) => {
  const calls = ptRender()
  const blog = await ptProject("blog")
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  const field = within(blog).getByLabelText("Profiles")
  expect((field as HTMLInputElement).value).toBe("web")
  await user.clear(field)
  if (typed !== "") await user.type(field, typed)
  await user.click(within(blog).getByRole("button", { name: "Restart blog" }))
  await within(await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Restart project blog" })).findByLabelText("Planned changes")
  expect(ptPlanned(calls).map((c) => c.body)).toEqual([{ input: { project: "blog", profiles: want } }])
})

test("typing the stored list again sends no profiles", async () => {
  const calls = ptRender()
  const blog = await ptProject("blog")
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  const field = within(blog).getByLabelText("Profiles")
  await user.clear(field)
  await user.type(field, "web")
  await user.click(within(blog).getByRole("button", { name: "Pull blog" }))
  await within(await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Pull images of project blog" })).findByLabelText("Planned changes")
  expect(ptPlanned(calls).map((c) => c.body)).toEqual([{ input: { project: "blog" } }])
})

test("the projects have no accessibility violations", async () => {
  ptRender()
  await ptProject("blog")
  expect(await axe(screen.getByRole("list", { name: "Compose projects" }))).toHaveNoViolations()
})

1. `docker-change.tsx`: export `DockerChange` with props `{ hostId: string; action: string; title: string; input: Record<string, unknown> | null; onClose: () => void }`; `null` keeps the dialog closed. It renders one `ChangeDialog` with `open` true exactly when `input` is not null, `title`, `input` (undefined when null) and `target={{ name: action, version: DOCKER_ACTION_VERSION, hostId, module: DOCKER_MODULE }}`. `module` makes the dialog check the module's availability on the host; `revertible` is not set, because a Docker change is not reverted by a timer, so no revert timeout is asked and the apply request carries only the plan id (and the typed confirmation when the plan asks for one). When the dialog asks to close, it calls `onClose()` and then `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["resource", hostId] })` from `useQueryClient()`; it invalidates nothing else and ignores a request to open.

2. What the three tabs share. Props `{ hostId: string }`. One `useQuery` with `queryKey: dockerKey(hostId, "<resource>")` and `queryFn: () => readResource<{ <resource>: T[] }>(hostId, DOCKER_MODULE, "<resource>")`. While pending: `<Spinner aria-label="Loading <resource>" />` (`networks`, `volumes`, `projects`). On error: `<Alert variant="destructive" role="alert">` holding `<AlertDescription>` with `errorMessage(query.error)`. One `useState<Pending | null>` where `Pending` is `{ action, title, input }`, passed to one `DockerChange` rendered after the content with `action={pending?.action ?? "<the tab's create action>"}`, `title={pending?.title ?? ""}`, `input={pending?.input ?? null}` and an `onClose` that clears it (the fallback action is never planned, because a null input keeps the dialog closed). A list with no rows shows `EmptyState` instead of the table.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Both files keep their helpers under their own prefix (`lp`, `sp`). A stream's URL is checked through `new URL(source.url, "http://localhost")` (path and query parameters), so the order of the parameters is not pinned. `act` wraps every emitted event, because the events update component state.

Create `web/src/modules/docker/logs-panel.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { act, screen } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import { EvtSource } from "@/test/evt-source"
import { renderWithProviders } from "@/test/utils"
import { LogsPanel } from "./logs-panel"

function lpSource(n: number): EvtSource {
  const source = EvtSource.instances[n]
  if (source === undefined) throw new Error(`no stream ${n} was opened`)
  return source
}

function lpParams(source: EvtSource): { path: string; query: Record<string, string> } {
  const url = new URL(source.url, "http://localhost")
  return { path: url.pathname, query: Object.fromEntries(url.searchParams) }
}

function lpLines(): (string | null)[] {
  return Array.from(screen.getByRole("log", { name: "Container logs" }).children).map((line) => line.textContent)
}

function lpRender() {
  return renderWithProviders(<LogsPanel hostId="h1" containerId="web" />)
}

test("follows the container's log with the last 200 lines", () => {
  lpRender()
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(1)
  expect(lpParams(lpSource(0))).toEqual({ path: "/api/v1/hosts/h1/streams/docker/logs", query: { container: "web", follow: "true", tail: "200" } })
  expect(screen.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Follow" }).getAttribute("aria-checked")).toBe("true")
  expect(screen.getByText("Waiting for output").textContent).toBe("Waiting for output")
})

test("shows each line in order, marks stderr and renders text literally", () => {
  lpRender()
  act(() => {
    lpSource(0).emit("data", { stream: "stdout", text: "starting\n" })
    lpSource(0).emit("data", { stream: "stderr", text: "boom\r\n" })
    lpSource(0).emit("data", { stream: "stdout", text: "<b>bold</b>\n" })
  })
  expect(lpLines()).toEqual(["starting", "boom", "<b>bold</b>"])
  const log = screen.getByRole("log", { name: "Container logs" })
  expect(Array.from(log.children).map((l) => l.getAttribute("data-stream"))).toEqual(["stdout", "stderr", "stdout"])
  expect(log.querySelector("b")).toBeNull()
  expect(screen.queryByText("Waiting for output")).toBeNull()
})

test("unticking Follow reads the tail once: it reopens the stream without follow", async () => {
  lpRender()
  act(() => lpSource(0).emit("data", { stream: "stdout", text: "old\n" }))
  await userEvent.setup().click(screen.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Follow" }))
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(2)
  expect(lpSource(0).closed).toBe(true)
  expect(lpParams(lpSource(1)).query).toEqual({ container: "web", tail: "200" })
  expect(lpLines()).toEqual([])
  expect(screen.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Follow" }).getAttribute("aria-checked")).toBe("false")
})

test("choosing another tail reopens the stream with it", async () => {
  lpRender()
  await userEvent.setup().selectOptions(screen.getByLabelText("Tail"), "all")
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(2)
  expect(lpParams(lpSource(1)).query).toEqual({ container: "web", follow: "true", tail: "all" })
})

test.each([
  ["done", undefined, "The log ended."],
  ["overflow", undefined, "The stream fell behind and was closed."],
  ["expired", undefined, "The stream reached its time limit."],
  ["revoked", undefined, "Access to the stream was revoked."],
  ["error", { type: "about:blank", title: "Not found", status: 404, detail: "container web was not found", code: "not_found" }, "container web was not found"],
  ["error", undefined, "The stream failed."],
] as const)("an %s end says why, and Reconnect reads the log again", async (reason, error, message) => {
  lpRender()
  act(() => {
    lpSource(0).emit("data", { stream: "stdout", text: "line\n" })
    lpSource(0).emit("end", error === undefined ? { reason } : { reason, error })
  })
  expect(screen.getByText(message).textContent).toBe(message)
  await userEvent.setup().click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Reconnect" }))
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(2)
  expect(lpParams(lpSource(1)).query).toEqual({ container: "web", follow: "true", tail: "200" })
  expect(screen.queryByText(message)).toBeNull()
  expect(lpLines()).toEqual([])
})

test("a log that ended with no output says so", () => {
  lpRender()
  act(() => lpSource(0).emit("end", { reason: "done" }))
  expect(screen.getByText("No log output.").textContent).toBe("No log output.")
  expect(screen.queryByText("Waiting for output")).toBeNull()
})

test("closes the stream when the panel goes away", () => {
  const { unmount } = lpRender()
  expect(lpSource(0).closed).toBe(false)
  unmount()
  expect(lpSource(0).closed).toBe(true)
})

test("the panel has no accessibility violations", async () => {
  lpRender()
  act(() => {
    lpSource(0).emit("data", { stream: "stdout", text: "starting\n" })
    lpSource(0).emit("end", { reason: "expired" })
  })
  expect(await axe(screen.getByRole("log", { name: "Container logs" }).parentElement ?? document.body)).toHaveNoViolations()
})
```

Create `web/src/modules/docker/stats-panel.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { act, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import { EvtSource } from "@/test/evt-source"
import { renderWithProviders } from "@/test/utils"
import { StatsPanel } from "./stats-panel"
import type { StatsEvent } from "./types"

function spSource(n: number): EvtSource {
  const source = EvtSource.instances[n]
  if (source === undefined) throw new Error(`no stream ${n} was opened`)
  return source
}

function spSample(over: Partial<StatsEvent> = {}): StatsEvent {
  return { read: "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z", cpuPercent: 12.345, memUsage: 268435456, memLimit: 1073741824, netRx: 5242880, netTx: 1024, pids: 12, ...over }
}

function spValue(label: string): string | null | undefined {
  return within(screen.getByLabelText("Container usage")).getByText(label, { selector: "dt" }).nextElementSibling?.textContent
}

function spRender() {
  return renderWithProviders(<StatsPanel hostId="h1" containerId="web" />)
}

test("opens the stats stream of the container and waits for the first sample", () => {
  spRender()
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(1)
  const url = new URL(spSource(0).url, "http://localhost")
  expect(url.pathname).toBe("/api/v1/hosts/h1/streams/docker/stats")
  expect(Object.fromEntries(url.searchParams)).toEqual({ container: "web" })
  expect(screen.getByText("Waiting for the first sample").textContent).toBe("Waiting for the first sample")
  expect(screen.queryByLabelText("Container usage")).toBeNull()
})

test("shows the latest sample and replaces it with the next", () => {
  spRender()
  act(() => spSource(0).emit("data", spSample()))
  expect(spValue("CPU")).toBe("12.3 %")
  expect(spValue("Memory")).toBe("256 MiB of 1.0 GiB (25.0 %)")
  expect(spValue("Received")).toBe("5.0 MiB")
  expect(spValue("Sent")).toBe("1.0 KiB")
  expect(spValue("Processes")).toBe("12")
  expect(screen.queryByText("Waiting for the first sample")).toBeNull()
  act(() => spSource(0).emit("data", spSample({ cpuPercent: 0, memUsage: 536870912, pids: 3 })))
  expect(spValue("CPU")).toBe("0.0 %")
  expect(spValue("Memory")).toBe("512 MiB of 1.0 GiB (50.0 %)")
  expect(spValue("Processes")).toBe("3")
})

test("a container without a memory limit shows only its usage", () => {
  spRender()
  act(() => spSource(0).emit("data", spSample({ memLimit: 0 })))
  expect(spValue("Memory")).toBe("256 MiB")
})

test("an end keeps the last sample, says why and Reconnect opens the stream again", async () => {
  spRender()
  act(() => {
    spSource(0).emit("data", spSample())
    spSource(0).emit("end", { reason: "error", error: { type: "about:blank", title: "Conflict", status: 409, detail: "container web is not running", code: "request.invalid_input" } })
  })
  expect(screen.getByText("container web is not running").textContent).toBe("container web is not running")
  expect(spValue("CPU")).toBe("12.3 %")
  await userEvent.setup().click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Reconnect" }))
  expect(EvtSource.instances).toHaveLength(2)
  expect(screen.queryByText("container web is not running")).toBeNull()
  expect(screen.getByText("Waiting for the first sample").textContent).toBe("Waiting for the first sample")
})

test("a done end says the stream ended", () => {
  spRender()
  act(() => spSource(0).emit("end", { reason: "done" }))
  expect(screen.getByText("The stats stream ended.").textContent).toBe("The stats stream ended.")
})

test("closes the stream when the panel goes away", () => {
  const { unmount } = spRender()
  expect(spSource(0).closed).toBe(false)
  unmount()
  expect(spSource(0).closed).toBe(true)
})

test("the panel has no accessibility violations", async () => {
  const { container } = spRender()
  act(() => spSource(0).emit("data", spSample()))
  expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations()
})
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Every file exports only React components (lint runs with `--max-warnings 0`, and `react-refresh/only-export-components` warns on other exports); helpers stay module-private. Use only components that `web/src` already imports from `darkraise-ui/components/*` (`alert`, `button`, `checkbox`, `label`).

1. `stream-end.tsx`: export `StreamEndNotice({ end, done, onReconnect })` with `end: StreamEnd`, `done: string` (the message for a normal end) and `onReconnect: () => void`. It renders `<Alert role="status">` (variant `default` when `end.reason` is `done`, else `warning`) whose `AlertDescription` holds a `<span>` with the message and a `Button size="sm" variant="outline"` reading "Reconnect" that calls `onReconnect`. Messages by reason: `done` the `done` prop; `overflow` "The stream fell behind and was closed."; `expired` "The stream reached its time limit."; `revoked` "Access to the stream was revoked."; `error` the `detail` of `end.error` when it is not empty, else "The stream failed.". The `switch` over `end.reason` must name every reason, so adding one to `StreamEnd` fails the type check.

2. `logs-panel.tsx`: export `LogsPanel({ hostId, containerId })`.
   - State in `LogsPanel`: `follow` (initially true), `tail` (initially `"200"`) and `attempt` (a counter, initially 0). Controls row: a `Checkbox` (id `logs-follow`, `onCheckedChange`, `checked === true`) with `Label` "Follow"; a `Label` "Tail" (`htmlFor` `logs-tail`) and a native `<select id="logs-tail">` with the options `50`, `200`, `1000` and `all`, styled with `rounded-md border border-input bg-background px-2 py-1 text-sm`.
   - Below the controls, `LogFeed` (private) rendered with `key={attempt}` and the props `hostId`, `containerId`, `follow`, `tail` and `onReconnect` (increments `attempt`, which remounts the feed and so opens a new stream). `LogFeed` calls `useStream<LogEvent>(streamUrl(hostId, DOCKER_MODULE, "logs", params))` with the default `max` (the last 1,000 lines are kept) where `params` is `{ container: containerId, tail }` plus `follow: "true"` only while following. A changed `follow` or `tail` therefore changes the URL, and `useStream` reopens the stream with no events.
   - The lines: `<div role="log" aria-label="Container logs" aria-live="off" tabIndex={0}>` with classes `max-h-96 overflow-auto rounded-md bg-muted p-3 font-mono text-xs` (it scrolls, so it must be focusable for keyboard users; `aria-live` is off so a screen reader is not flooded). Its only children are one `<div>` per event, in order (key: index), with `data-stream` set to the event's `stream`, class `whitespace-pre-wrap` (plus `text-destructive` for `stderr`) and the event's text as a plain React text child with one trailing `\n` or `\r\n` removed (never as HTML).
   - After the region: `<p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">` "Waiting for output" while there are no events and no end; "No log output." when there are no events and the stream ended; and `StreamEndNotice` with `done="The log ended."` when the stream ended.

3. `stats-panel.tsx`: export `StatsPanel({ hostId, containerId })`.
   - `StatsPanel` holds an `attempt` counter and renders `StatsFeed` (private) with `key={attempt}` and an `onReconnect` that increments it.
   - `StatsFeed` calls `useStream<StatsEvent>(streamUrl(hostId, DOCKER_MODULE, "stats", { container: containerId }), 1)`; only the latest sample is shown, taken as `events[events.length - 1]` (the TypeScript `lib` is ES2020, which has no `Array.prototype.at`). With no sample and no end it shows `<p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">` "Waiting for the first sample". With a sample it shows `<dl aria-label="Container usage">` with the rows (muted `<dt>`, then `<dd>`): CPU `<cpuPercent to one decimal> %`; Memory `<formatBytes(memUsage)> of <formatBytes(memLimit)> (<memUsage / memLimit * 100 to one decimal> %)`, or only `formatBytes(memUsage)` when `memLimit` is not above zero; Received `formatBytes(netRx)`; Sent `formatBytes(netTx)`; Processes `pids`. The last sample stays on screen after the stream ends. When the stream ended it also shows `StreamEndNotice` with `done="The stats stream ended."`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

The tests replace `CapabilityList` with a stub (`vi.mock("@/components/capability-list")`) that lists `<name>: <state>`, so they pin that the panel hands the account's capabilities over, not the list's own markup. The account read is `POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.account.get/v1/read`, answered as `{ output }`; plans go to `POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.account.<connect|disconnect>/v1/plan` (controller-side, so there is no host in the path and no availability request).

Create `web/src/modules/tailnet/account-panel.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test, vi } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import { formatTime } from "@/lib/format"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type FetchCall, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { AccountPanel } from "./account-panel"
import { tnAccount } from "./fixtures"
import type { TailnetAccountStatus } from "./types"

vi.mock("@/components/capability-list", () => ({
  CapabilityList: ({ capabilities }: { capabilities: { name: string; state: string }[] }) => (
    <ul aria-label="Capabilities">
      {capabilities.map((c) => (
        <li key={c.name}>{`${c.name}: ${c.state}`}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  ),
}))

const AP_GET = "POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.account.get/v1/read"
const AP_CONNECTED_AT = "2026-10-29T08:15:00Z"

const apDisconnected: TailnetAccountStatus = { connected: false }
const apConnected: TailnetAccountStatus = {
  connected: true,
  account: tnAccount({
    tailnet: "example.com",
    clientId: "k123CNTRL",
    tagsAllowed: ["tag:server", "tag:darkpanel"],
    capabilities: [
      { name: "devices:core", state: "ok" },
      { name: "auth_keys", state: "unverified" },
    ],
    connectedAt: AP_CONNECTED_AT,
  }),
}

function apPlan(call: FetchCall) {
  const action = call.path.split("/")[4] ?? ""
  return {
    body: {
      planId: "p1", hostId: null, action, version: 1, inputHash: "h", diff: [{ op: "~", text: action }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z",
      confirmation: action === "tailnet.account.disconnect" ? "example.com" : null,
    },
  }
}

function apRender(status: TailnetAccountStatus, routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}) {
  const calls = stubFetch({
    [AP_GET]: { body: { output: status } },
    "POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.account.connect/v1/plan": apPlan,
    "POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.account.disconnect/v1/plan": apPlan,
    ...routes,
  })
  const result = renderWithProviders(<AccountPanel />)
  return { calls, ...result }
}

function apValue(label: string): string | null | undefined {
  return within(screen.getByLabelText("Tailnet account")).getByText(label, { selector: "dt" }).nextElementSibling?.textContent
}

function apPlanned(calls: FetchCall[]): { path: string; body: unknown }[] {
  return calls.filter((c) => c.method === "POST" && c.path.endsWith("/plan")).map((c) => ({ path: c.path, body: c.body }))
}

async function apFill(user: ReturnType<typeof userEvent.setup>, form: HTMLElement, values: { tailnet?: string; clientId?: string; secret?: string; tags?: string }) {
  if (values.tailnet !== undefined) await user.type(within(form).getByLabelText("Tailnet"), values.tailnet)
  if (values.clientId !== undefined) await user.type(within(form).getByLabelText("OAuth client ID"), values.clientId)
  if (values.secret !== undefined) await user.type(within(form).getByLabelText("OAuth client secret"), values.secret)
  if (values.tags !== undefined) await user.type(within(form).getByLabelText("Allowed tags"), values.tags)
}

test("shows the reason when the account cannot be read", async () => {
  apRender(apDisconnected, { [AP_GET]: { status: 503, body: { type: "about:blank", title: "Unavailable", status: 503, detail: "the controller database is busy", code: "internal" } } })
  expect((await screen.findByRole("alert")).textContent).toBe("the controller database is busy")
})

  expect(within(form).getByText("Each tag must look like tag:name.").textContent).toBe("Each tag must look like tag:name.")
  expect(plan.hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(true)
  await user.clear(within(form).getByLabelText("Allowed tags"))

  expect(within(form).queryByText("Each tag must look like tag:name.")).toBeNull()
  expect(plan.hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(false)
})

test("the connect form forgets what was typed, the secret included, once the change closes", async () => {
  apRender(apDisconnected)

test("an applied connection shows the account once the dialog closes", async () => {
  let reads = 0
  const { calls } = apRender(apDisconnected, {
    [AP_GET]: () => ({ body: { output: ++reads === 1 ? apDisconnected : apConnected } }),
    "POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.account.connect/v1/apply": {
      body: { id: "c1", state: "completed", class: "compensable", error: null, output: null, revertDeadline: null },
    },
  })

1. `AccountPanel()`: one `useQuery` with `queryKey: tailnetKey("account")` and `queryFn: () => readAction<TailnetAccountStatus>("tailnet.account.get", TAILNET_ACTION_VERSION)` (the key starts with `"tailnet"`, so `TailnetChange` refetches it when a change closes). While pending: `<Spinner aria-label="Loading the tailnet account" />`. On error: `<Alert variant="destructive" role="alert">` with `errorMessage(query.error)`. Otherwise a `Card` with `CardTitle` "Tailnet account" whose content holds either the connected view (when `connected` is true and `account` is present) or the not-connected view (otherwise), then the change dialog. State: `pending: { action, title, input } | null`. The change dialog is mounted only while `pending` is not null: `<TailnetChange action title input onClose={() => setPending(null)} />`.

2. Not connected: the paragraph "No tailnet is connected." and the connect form's button.
   - `ConnectForm` (private, own local state) renders a `Button` "Connect" that opens a `Dialog` titled "Connect a tailnet", whose description says that the OAuth client secret is kept sealed and never shown again and that the next step shows what connecting does before anything is saved. It holds `<form aria-label="Tailnet connection">` with `Label`/`Input` pairs, `autoComplete="off"`, ids as given: Tailnet (`tailnet-name`, placeholder `example.com`), OAuth client ID (`tailnet-client-id`), OAuth client secret (`tailnet-client-secret`, `type="password"`), Allowed tags (`tailnet-tags`, placeholder `tag:server, tag:darkpanel`, `aria-invalid` while a tag is malformed, `aria-describedby` the help text id `tailnet-tags-help`).
   - The tags text is split on commas and whitespace, empty entries dropped. A tag is well formed when it matches `^tag:\S+$` (the module checks the rest). The help text under the field reads "Each tag must look like tag:name." in the destructive colour while any tag is malformed, and otherwise "The tags this client may give to devices and auth keys, separated by commas or spaces." in the muted colour.
   - The submit `Button type="submit"` reads "Plan" and is disabled until the tailnet, client id and client secret are not blank after trimming, there is at least one tag and every tag is well formed.
   - Submitting (call `preventDefault`) calls the panel's `onPlan` with action `tailnet.account.connect`, title `Connect tailnet <trimmed tailnet>` and input `{ tailnet, clientId, clientSecret, tagsAllowed }`: the first three trimmed, `tagsAllowed` the parsed list in the order typed. It then closes the form dialog and resets the draft to empty, so the secret is no longer held by the form; the panel keeps it only in `pending` until the change dialog closes, where `setPending(null)` drops it.

3. Connected: `<dl aria-label="Tailnet account">` with the rows Tailnet, OAuth client (the client id), Allowed tags (joined by `, `) and Connected (`formatTime(connectedAt)`); a heading "Capabilities" (`h3`, `text-sm font-medium`) above `<CapabilityList capabilities={account.capabilities} />`; and a row with a destructive `Button` "Disconnect" and a `Checkbox` (id `tailnet-abandon`) labelled "Abandon pending cleanup". Disconnect sets the pending change `tailnet.account.disconnect`, title `Disconnect <tailnet>`, input `{}`, or `{ abandonCleanup: true }` while the box is ticked (the type-the-tailnet-name confirmation comes from the plan). While the box is ticked, a muted paragraph says that disconnecting then deletes the credentials even if auth keys Darkpanel created are not yet deleted from the tailnet, and that those keys stay there. A refusal such as `cloud.cleanup_pending` is shown by the change dialog's own error alert.

}

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `web/src/modules/cloudflare/account-panel.tsx`, matching the style of `web/src/modules/firewall/status-panel.tsx` (darkraise-ui `Card`, `Alert`, `Button`, `Input`, `Label`, `Checkbox`, `Spinner`; `Tailwind` classes as there). `AccountPanel` is one named export with a doc comment.

1. Read the account with `useQuery({ queryKey: cloudflareKey("account"), queryFn: () => readAction<CloudflareAccountStatus>("cloudflare.account.get", CLOUDFLARE_ACTION_VERSION, {}) })`. While pending render `<Spinner aria-label="Loading the Cloudflare account" />`; on error render a destructive `Alert` with `role="alert"` whose only text is `errorMessage(error)`.
2. Both states render inside one `Card` titled "Cloudflare account". Keep component state for the account id text, the API token text, the abandon checkbox, and `pending: { action; title; input } | null`.
3. Not connected (`status.connected` is false, or `account` is absent): a `<form>` with the paragraph "No Cloudflare account is connected.", a labelled text `Input` "Account ID" (`required`, `autoComplete="off"`), a labelled `Input` "API token" (`type="password"`, `required`, `autoComplete="off"`), and the help list below, then a submit `Button` "Connect". Rely on the native `required` attributes: a form with an empty field must not submit and must plan nothing. On submit call `preventDefault` and set `pending` to action `cloudflare.account.connect`, title "Connect Cloudflare", input `{ accountId: <the id trimmed>, apiToken: <the token as typed> }`.
4. The help is the sentence "The token needs these permissions:" followed by a `<ul aria-label="Required token permissions">` with one `<li>` per permission, in this order: "Account: Cloudflare Tunnel Write (shown as Cloudflare Tunnel: Edit in the dashboard)", "Zone: Zone Read on the zones you will use", "Zone: DNS Write on the zones you will use (shown as DNS: Edit)". Then read the "Account" bullet of `docs/dforge/specs/2026-10-21-v1-completion-design.md` section 7.1: if the contract check of Task 1 recorded a further permission there (spec 7.1 says it records the final list "in the connect dialog's help text"), add one more `<li>` for each, worded as the spec words it; if it recorded none, the list has exactly the three items. The test accepts three or more items.
5. Connected: a `<dl aria-label="Cloudflare account">` with the rows "Account ID" (the `accountId`, monospace) and "Connected" (`formatTime(account.connectedAt)`), each as `<dt>`/`<dd>` pairs in a `div className="contents"` as `status-panel.tsx` does. Below it a `<div role="group" aria-label="Token capabilities">` holding an `<h3>` "Token capabilities" and `<CapabilityList capabilities={account.capabilities} />` with the capabilities passed through unchanged (the list itself words a missing capability whose detail is `cloud.unavailable` or `cloud.rate_limited` as "could not check"). Then a `Checkbox` with a `Label` "Abandon pending cleanup" and a destructive `Button` "Disconnect". The button sets `pending` to action `cloudflare.account.disconnect`, title "Disconnect Cloudflare", input `{ abandonCleanup: true }` when the checkbox is ticked and `{}` otherwise. The typed account-id confirmation comes from the plan and is handled by the change dialog; the panel adds nothing for it.
6. Render `<CloudflareChange action title input onClose />` only while `pending` is not null (mount it conditionally, so it works whether or not `CloudflareChange` accepts a null input). Its `onClose` sets `pending` to null, clears the API token text and unticks the abandon checkbox; it keeps the account id text. `CloudflareChange` already refetches `["cloudflare"]` when the dialog closes, so the panel adds no invalidation of its own.
7. No secret is kept: the token lives only in the input's state, is sent only in the plan request body, and is cleared when the dialog closes.

import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import type { Plan } from "@/api/types"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type FetchCall, type StubResponse } from "@/test/utils"
import { DevicesPage } from "./devices-page"
import { tnDevice } from "./fixtures"

const DV_LIST = "POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.device.list/v1/read"

const dvWeb = tnDevice({
  id: "n1",
  name: "web-1.example.ts.net",
  addresses: ["100.64.0.1"],
  tags: ["tag:server"],
  authorized: true,
  advertisedRoutes: ["10.0.0.0/24", "192.168.1.0/24", "0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"],
  enabledRoutes: ["10.0.0.0/24"],
  exitNode: true,
  exitNodeEnabled: false,
})
const dvLaptop = tnDevice({ id: "n2", name: "laptop.example.ts.net", addresses: ["100.64.0.2"], tags: [], authorized: false, advertisedRoutes: [], enabledRoutes: [], exitNode: false, exitNodeEnabled: false })

const dvDevices: StubResponse = { body: { output: { devices: [dvWeb, dvLaptop] } } }

function dvPlan(action: string, over: Partial<Plan> = {}): StubResponse {
  return { body: { planId: "p1", hostId: null, action, version: 1, inputHash: "h", diff: [{ op: "~", text: "change the device" }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z", confirmation: null, ...over } }
}

const dvApplied: StubResponse = { body: { id: "c1", state: "completed", class: "compensable", error: null, output: null, revertDeadline: null } }

function dvBodies(calls: FetchCall[], suffix: string): unknown[] {
  return calls.filter((c) => c.method === "POST" && c.path.endsWith(suffix)).map((c) => c.body)
}

function dvReads(calls: FetchCall[]): number {
  return calls.filter((c) => c.path.endsWith("tailnet.device.list/v1/read")).length
}

function dvRow(name: string): HTMLElement {
  const row = screen.getByText(name).closest("tr")
  if (row === null) throw new Error(`no row for ${name}`)
  return row
}

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Both pages follow the style of `web/src/modules/firewall/rules-table.tsx` (darkraise-ui `Table`, `Badge`, `Button`, `EmptyState`) and of `web/src/pages/create-host-dialog.tsx` (the one-time secret). Each is a named export with a doc comment.

`devices-page.tsx` exports `DevicesPage`:

1. Read the devices with `useQuery({ queryKey: tailnetKey("devices"), queryFn: () => readAction<{ devices: TailnetDevice[] }>("tailnet.device.list", TAILNET_ACTION_VERSION, {}) })`. Pending: `<Spinner aria-label="Loading the devices" />`. An `ApiError` whose `code` is `cloud.not_connected`: an `Alert` with `role="status"` reading "No tailnet account is connected. " + a `Link` to `/tailnet` with the text "Connect an account" + " first." Any other error: a destructive `Alert` with `role="alert"` whose only text is `errorMessage(error)`. No devices: `EmptyState` titled "No devices".
2. Otherwise a `Table aria-label="Tailnet devices"` with the columns Name, Addresses (joined by ", ", monospace), OS, Tags (joined by ", "), Status, Routes, Last seen and an `sr-only` "Actions" head. Status is a `Badge` "Authorized" or "Pending approval". Routes is a summary: for the advertised routes other than `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0`, "<enabled count> of <count> approved"; when the device is an exit node, "exit node approved" or "exit node not approved" (by `exitNodeEnabled`); the parts joined by ", "; "none" when there are neither. Last seen is `formatTime(lastSeen)`, or "—" when absent.
3. Row actions are small `Button`s whose `aria-label` carries the device name: "Authorize <name>" only for an unauthorized device; "Routes of <name>" only when `advertisedRoutes` is not empty; "Expire <name>" and "Delete <name>" always. Authorize, Expire and Delete set a `pending` state `{ action, title, input: { device: <the device id> } }` with the actions `tailnet.device.authorize`, `tailnet.device.expire`, `tailnet.device.delete` and the titles "Authorize <name>", "Expire <name>", "Delete <name>". The typed confirmation of expire and delete (the device name) comes from the plan and is handled by the change dialog.
4. "Routes of <name>" opens a local `RoutesDialog` (a darkraise-ui `Dialog`, titled "Routes of <name>") mounted only while a device is chosen, so its state starts fresh each time. It offers one `Checkbox` with a `Label` per advertised route other than the exit pair, labelled with the CIDR and ticked when it is in `enabledRoutes`; and, when `exitNode` is true, one checkbox labelled "Exit node (0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0)" ticked when `exitNodeEnabled`. The exit pair is never offered as separate checkboxes. "Cancel" closes it and plans nothing. "Review" closes it and sets `pending` to action `tailnet.device.set-routes`, title "Approve routes for <name>", input `{ device: <id>, routes }`, where `routes` is the ticked plain routes in their advertised order followed by `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` when the exit node is ticked; unticking everything sends `[]` (the action takes the full approved list).
5. Render `<TailnetChange action title input onClose />` only while `pending` is not null; its `onClose` sets `pending` to null. `TailnetChange` refetches `["tailnet"]` when the dialog closes, so the list is read again without code here.

`keys-page.tsx` exports `KeysPage`:

1. Read `tailnetKey("keys")` with `readAction<{ keys: AuthKeyRow[] }>("tailnet.authkey.list", TAILNET_ACTION_VERSION, {})` and `tailnetKey("account")` with `readAction<TailnetAccountStatus>("tailnet.account.get", TAILNET_ACTION_VERSION, {})`; the two reads are independent, so one failing does not hide the other.
2. A `Card` "Create an auth key". While the account read is pending, a `Spinner aria-label="Loading the account"`. When `connected` is false, an `Alert` with `role="status"` reading "No tailnet account is connected. " + a `Link` to `/tailnet` "Connect an account" + " first." and no form. When connected, a `<form>` with a `<fieldset>` whose `<legend>` is "Tags" holding one labelled `Checkbox` per entry of the account's `tagsAllowed` (label: the tag, monospace); labelled `Checkbox`es "Reusable", "Ephemeral" and "Pre-authorized"; a labelled `Input` "Expiry (seconds)" starting at `86400`; a submit `Button` "Create key".
3. Submit validates before anything is planned: no tag ticked sets the message "Choose at least one tag."; an expiry that is not all digits, is zero, or is above 7776000 sets "Enter a whole number of seconds from 1 to 7776000." (the checks run in that order). A message renders in a destructive `Alert` with `role="alert"` inside the form and plans nothing. Otherwise the input is `{ tags, expirySeconds }` plus `reusable: true`, `ephemeral: true` and `preauthorized: true` only for the ticked flags (a false flag is omitted), and the phase becomes "plan".
4. Use `ChangeDialog` directly, not `TailnetChange`, because the created key exists only in the apply answer and `TailnetChange` takes no `onApplied`: `open` while the phase is "plan", title "Create an auth key", `target={{ name: "tailnet.authkey.create", version: TAILNET_ACTION_VERSION }}`, `input`, `onApplied`. Closing it without applying resets the phase and invalidates `["tailnet"]`. `onApplied(change)` does nothing when `changeError(change) !== null || changeInProgress(change)` (the change dialog then shows the failure), and otherwise stores `change.output` in component state when it is an object with string members `key` and `description` (else stores null) and moves to the phase "created".
5. The phase "created" opens a `Dialog` titled "Auth key created". With a key it says "Copy the key now. It will not be shown again." and shows a darkraise-ui `Clipboard` (`ClipboardLabel` "Auth key <description>", a `ClipboardInput` and a `ClipboardTrigger` "Copy", exactly as `create-host-dialog.tsx` does for the enrollment token) and "Expires <formatTime(expires)>.". Without a key it says "The key exists, but it cannot be shown." and a destructive `Alert` with `role="alert"`: "The key was created, but the controller did not return it." "Done" (and closing the dialog) clears the stored key, returns to the phase "closed" and invalidates `["tailnet"]`. The key is held only in this component's state; it is never put in the query cache, a query key or the DOM after "Done".
6. Keys: a `Table aria-label="Auth keys"` with the columns Description (monospace), Kind, State, Requested, Expires and Key ID (monospace; empty when absent), times through `formatTime`. No keys: `EmptyState` titled "No auth keys". A failed keys read: a destructive `Alert` with `role="alert"` whose only text is `errorMessage(error)`; pending: `Spinner aria-label="Loading the auth keys"`.

The pinned Compose is 5.6.0, which is not on this host, and Global Constraints allow no network read in this task. The allowlists therefore come from the compose-spec schema embedded in the host's Compose plugin (`docker compose version` prints v5.1.4; `go version -m /usr/libexec/docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose` shows it was built with `github.com/compose-spec/compose-go/v2 v2.11.0`, 2026-10-30). The check is closed: a key that Compose 5.6.0 adds is refused until the schema file and the lists are refreshed, which fails safe. The command only reads the plugin file as bytes; it never runs it.

Create `internal/modules/docker/compose/validate_test.go`:

```go
package compose

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"os"
	"slices"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

// cvConfig is a valid resolved configuration of the project "shop"; each
// mutation changes it for one case.
func cvConfig(mutate ...func(*Config)) Config {
	c := Config{
		Name:    "shop",
		TopKeys: []string{"name", "networks", "services", "volumes"},
		Services: map[string]Service{
			"web": {Keys: []string{"image", "networks", "volumes"}, Image: "nginx:1.27", Networks: []string{"default"}, Volumes: []string{"data"}},
		},
		Networks: map[string]Object{"default": {Keys: []string{"name"}, Name: "shop_default"}},
		Volumes:  map[string]Object{"data": {Keys: []string{"name"}, Name: "shop_data"}},
	}
	for _, m := range mutate {
		m(&c)
	}
	return c
}

func cvService(c *Config, name string, edit func(*Service)) {
	s := c.Services[name]
	edit(&s)
	c.Services[name] = s
}

// cvFacts answers Owner from owners, keyed "<kind> <name>", and ImagePresent
// for the listed references.
func cvFacts(images []string, owners map[string]string) Facts {
	return Facts{
		ImagePresent: func(ref string) bool { return slices.Contains(images, ref) },
		Owner:        func(kind, name string) string { return owners[kind+" "+name] },
	}
}

func cvRefusal(t *testing.T, err error, code errcode.Code, detail string) {
	t.Helper()
	var e *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &e) {
		t.Fatalf("Validate returned %v, want an *errcode.Error with code %s", err, code)
	}
	if e.Code != code || e.Detail != detail {
		t.Fatalf("Validate refused with %s %q, want %s %q", e.Code, e.Detail, code, detail)
	}
}

func TestCVValidateRefuses(t *testing.T) {
	const (
		owned       = errcode.DockerOwned
		unavailable = errcode.DockerComposeUnavailable
	)
	rows := []struct {
		name    string
		project string
		mutate  func(*Config)
		facts   Facts
		code    errcode.Code
		detail  string
	}{
		{"project darkpanel", "darkpanel", nil, cvFacts(nil, nil), owned, "project darkpanel is reserved for Darkpanel modules"},
		{"project with the prefix", "darkpanel-npm", nil, cvFacts(nil, nil), owned, "project darkpanel-npm is reserved for Darkpanel modules"},
		{"project prefix in another case", "DarkPanelEdge", nil, cvFacts(nil, nil), owned, "project DarkPanelEdge is reserved for Darkpanel modules"},
		{"service sets the owner label", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.Labels = map[string]string{"darkpanel.module": "npm"} })
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), owned, "service web sets the darkpanel.module label"},
		{"network sets the owner label", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.Networks["default"] = Object{Keys: []string{"labels", "name"}, Name: "shop_default", Labels: map[string]string{"darkpanel.module": "npm"}}
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), owned, "network default sets the darkpanel.module label"},
		{"volume sets the owner label", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.Volumes["data"] = Object{Keys: []string{"labels", "name"}, Name: "shop_data", Labels: map[string]string{"darkpanel.module": "npm"}}
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), owned, "volume data sets the darkpanel.module label"},
		{"container name of an owned container", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.ContainerName = "npm-app" })
		}, cvFacts(nil, map[string]string{"container npm-app": "npm"}), owned, "container npm-app belongs to module npm"},
		{"network of an owned network", "shop", nil,
			cvFacts(nil, map[string]string{"network shop_default": "panel"}), owned, "network shop_default belongs to module panel"},
		{"volume of an owned volume", "shop", nil,
			cvFacts(nil, map[string]string{"volume shop_data": "npm"}), owned, "volume shop_data belongs to module npm"},
		{"network without a resolved name uses the project prefix", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.Networks["default"] = Object{Keys: []string{}}
		}, cvFacts(nil, map[string]string{"network shop_default": "panel"}), owned, "network shop_default belongs to module panel"},
		{"provider service", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.Services["llm"] = Service{Keys: []string{"provider"}, Provider: true}
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), unavailable, "service llm uses a provider, which would run a program on the host"},
		{"top-level key outside the allowlist", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.TopKeys = []string{"models", "name", "services"}
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), unavailable, `top-level key "models" is not supported`},
		{"service key outside the allowlist", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.Keys = []string{"image", "models"} })
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), unavailable, `service web: key "models" is not supported`},
		{"provider key without the provider flag", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.Keys = []string{"image", "provider"} })
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), unavailable, `service web: key "provider" is not supported`},
		{"network key outside the allowlist", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.Networks["default"] = Object{Keys: []string{"name", "wireguard"}, Name: "shop_default"}
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), unavailable, `network default: key "wireguard" is not supported`},
		{"volume key outside the allowlist", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.Volumes["data"] = Object{Keys: []string{"name", "snapshot"}, Name: "shop_data"}
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), unavailable, `volume data: key "snapshot" is not supported`},
		{"config key outside the allowlist", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.TopKeys = []string{"configs", "name", "services"}
			c.Configs = map[string]Object{"app": {Keys: []string{"content", "exec"}}}
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), unavailable, `config app: key "exec" is not supported`},
		{"secret key outside the allowlist", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.TopKeys = []string{"name", "secrets", "services"}
			c.Secrets = map[string]Object{"pw": {Keys: []string{"file", "command"}}}
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), unavailable, `secret pw: key "command" is not supported`},
		{"build of an image that is not present", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.Keys = []string{"build"}; s.Image = ""; s.Build = true })
		}, cvFacts([]string{"nginx:1.27"}, nil), unavailable, "service web builds image shop-web, which is not present locally; Compose is run with --no-build"},
		{"build with a named image that is not present", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.Keys = []string{"build", "image"}; s.Image = "app:1"; s.Build = true })
		}, cvFacts([]string{"shop-web"}, nil), unavailable, "service web builds image app:1, which is not present locally; Compose is run with --no-build"},
		{"build with no facts about images", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.Keys = []string{"build"}; s.Image = ""; s.Build = true })
		}, Facts{}, unavailable, "service web builds image shop-web, which is not present locally; Compose is run with --no-build"},
		{"the first provider by service name", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.Services["b"] = Service{Keys: []string{"provider"}, Provider: true}
			c.Services["a"] = Service{Keys: []string{"provider"}, Provider: true}
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil), unavailable, "service a uses a provider, which would run a program on the host"},
		{"ownership is checked before the other refusals", "shop", func(c *Config) {
			c.Services["llm"] = Service{Keys: []string{"provider"}, Provider: true}
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.ContainerName = "npm-app" })
		}, cvFacts(nil, map[string]string{"container npm-app": "npm"}), owned, "container npm-app belongs to module npm"},
	}
	for _, r := range rows {
		t.Run(r.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			var mutate []func(*Config)
			if r.mutate != nil {
				mutate = append(mutate, r.mutate)
			}
			cvRefusal(t, Validate(r.project, cvConfig(mutate...), r.facts), r.code, r.detail)
		})
	}
}

func TestCVValidateAccepts(t *testing.T) {
	rows := []struct {
		name   string
		mutate func(*Config)
		facts  Facts
	}{
		{"a plain project", nil, cvFacts(nil, nil)},
		{"extension keys at every level", func(c *Config) {
			c.TopKeys = []string{"name", "networks", "services", "volumes", "x-meta"}
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.Keys = append(s.Keys, "x-note") })
			c.Networks["default"] = Object{Keys: []string{"name", "x-net"}, Name: "shop_default"}
			c.Volumes["data"] = Object{Keys: []string{"name", "x-vol"}, Name: "shop_data"}
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil)},
		{"every allowed service key", func(c *Config) {
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.Keys = slices.Clone(ServiceKeys) })
		}, cvFacts(nil, nil)},
		{"a build whose image is present", func(c *Config) {
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.Keys = []string{"build"}; s.Image = ""; s.Build = true })
		}, cvFacts([]string{"shop-web"}, nil)},
		{"a build with a named image that is present", func(c *Config) {
			cvService(c, "web", func(s *Service) { s.Keys = []string{"build", "image"}; s.Image = "app:1"; s.Build = true })
		}, cvFacts([]string{"app:1"}, nil)},
		{"objects another project owns nothing of", nil, cvFacts(nil, map[string]string{"network other_default": "panel"})},
		{"no facts at all", nil, Facts{}},
	}
	for _, r := range rows {
		t.Run(r.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			var mutate []func(*Config)
			if r.mutate != nil {
				mutate = append(mutate, r.mutate)
			}
			if err := Validate("shop", cvConfig(mutate...), r.facts); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("Validate = %v, want nil", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCVValidateAsksForTheEngineNamesOnly(t *testing.T) {
	var asked []string
	facts := Facts{
		ImagePresent: func(string) bool { return true },
		Owner: func(kind, name string) string {
			asked = append(asked, kind+" "+name)
			return ""
		},
	}

	want := []string{"container db1", "network shop_default", "volume shop_data"}
	if !slices.Equal(asked, want) {
		t.Fatalf("Owner was asked about %q, want %q", asked, want)
	}
}

// cvSchema is the part of the compose-spec JSON schema the allowlists come from.
type cvSchema struct {
	Properties map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"properties"`
	Defs       map[string]struct {
		Properties map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"properties"`
	} `json:"$defs"`
}

func cvKeys(m map[string]json.RawMessage, without ...string) []string {
	var keys []string
	for k := range m {
		if !slices.Contains(without, k) {
			keys = append(keys, k)
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(keys)
	return keys
}

func TestCVKeyListsAreTheSchemasMinusHostPrograms(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/schema/compose-spec.json")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var s cvSchema
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &s); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, k := range []string{"models", "provider"} {
		if _, ok := s.Defs["service"].Properties[k]; !ok {
			t.Fatalf("the schema's service has no %q member; the exclusions below would mean nothing", k)
		}
	}
	top := cvKeys(s.Properties, "version", "include", "models")
	rows := []struct {
		name string
		got  []string
		want []string
	}{
		{"TopLevelKeys", TopLevelKeys, top},
		{"ServiceKeys", ServiceKeys, cvKeys(s.Defs["service"].Properties, "models", "provider")},
		{"NetworkKeys", NetworkKeys, cvKeys(s.Defs["network"].Properties)},
		{"VolumeKeys", VolumeKeys, cvKeys(s.Defs["volume"].Properties)},
		{"ConfigKeys", ConfigKeys, cvKeys(s.Defs["config"].Properties)},
		{"SecretKeys", SecretKeys, cvKeys(s.Defs["secret"].Properties)},
	}
	if !slices.Equal(top, []string{"configs", "name", "networks", "secrets", "services", "volumes"}) {
		t.Fatalf("the schema's top-level members are %q", top)
	}
	for _, r := range rows {
		if !slices.Equal(r.got, r.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s = %q, want %q", r.name, r.got, r.want)
		}
		for _, k := range r.got {
			if strings.HasPrefix(k, "x-") {
				t.Errorf("%s lists the extension key %q; extension keys are accepted by prefix", r.name, k)
			}
		}
	}
}

A comment above the block says: the lists are the keys the compose-spec schema documents for containers, networks, volumes, configs and secrets; the source is the schema embedded in docker-compose v5.1.4, i.e. `https://github.com/compose-spec/compose-go/blob/v2.11.0/schema/compose-spec.json`, copied to `testdata/schema/compose-spec.json`; the top-level set is only the six members a resolved configuration has (a resolved configuration has neither `version` nor `include`); `models` and `provider` are left out of the service keys, and `models` of the top-level keys, because they hand work to a program on the host (inference for `models`: Compose serves it through a host plugin; it is outside the five object kinds spec 3 allows either way). Keys starting with `x-` are Compose extension fields and are always accepted.
2. `Facts` as in Contracts "compose refusals", with a doc comment saying a nil `ImagePresent` finds no image and a nil `Owner` finds no owner, so a zero `Facts` is valid.
3. `Validate` checks in this fixed order and returns the first refusal; every loop over services or objects runs in sorted name order so the answer is deterministic. Every refusal is `errcode.New(code, detail)` with exactly these details (`%s` is the plain name, `%q` a Go-quoted key):
   - `docker.owned`, `project <project> is reserved for Darkpanel modules`, when `strings.ToLower(project)` starts with `darkpanel`.
   - For each service: `docker.owned`, `service <name> sets the darkpanel.module label`, when its `Labels` has the key `darkpanel.module` (any value); then, for a non-empty `ContainerName` only, `docker.owned`, `container <container name> belongs to module <owner>` when `f.Owner("container", containerName)` is not `""`.
   - For each network, then each volume (by key): `docker.owned`, `<kind> <key> sets the darkpanel.module label`, when the object's `Labels` has that key; then the Engine name is `Object.Name`, or `<project>_<key>` when `Name` is `""`, and `docker.owned`, `<kind> <engine name> belongs to module <owner>` when `f.Owner(kind, name)` is not `""` (`kind` is `"network"` or `"volume"`). External objects are checked the same way.
   - `docker.compose_unavailable`, `service <name> uses a provider, which would run a program on the host`, for the first service with `Provider` true.
   - Unsupported keys, all `docker.compose_unavailable`: first `c.TopKeys` in the order given: `top-level key <%q key> is not supported`; then each service's `Keys` in the order given: `service <name>: key <%q key> is not supported`; then the same shape, `network <key>: …`, `volume <key>: …`, `config <key>: …`, `secret <key>: …`, for `c.Networks`, `c.Volumes`, `c.Configs`, `c.Secrets` against `NetworkKeys`, `VolumeKeys`, `ConfigKeys`, `SecretKeys`. A key is accepted when it starts with `x-` or is in the list.
   - `docker.compose_unavailable`, `service <name> builds image <image>, which is not present locally; Compose is run with --no-build`, for the first service with `Build` true whose `ImageName(project, name, service)` is not reported present by `f.ImagePresent` (a nil `ImagePresent` reports none).
4. Nothing else: no logging, no I/O, no global state, no wrapping in `core.Definite`.

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"math"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/docker/logfilter"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

// stDocker wraps the fake engine with log and stats streams the test controls,
// and records how the streams were opened.
type stDocker struct {
	*fakeDocker
	frames  []dockerapi.LogFrame
	samples []dockerapi.Stats
	block   bool  // after the frames, Next waits for the context instead of ending the stream
	endErr  error // after the frames, Next fails with this instead of io.EOF

	logIDs    []string
	logOpts   []dockerapi.LogsOptions
	statIDs   []string
	statFlags []bool
	closed    int
}

func (d *stDocker) Logs(ctx context.Context, id string, o dockerapi.LogsOptions) (logStream, error) {
	d.logIDs = append(d.logIDs, id)
	d.logOpts = append(d.logOpts, o)
	return &stLogStream{ctx: ctx, d: d, frames: d.frames}, nil
}

func (d *stDocker) Stats(ctx context.Context, id string, stream bool) (statsStream, error) {
	d.statIDs = append(d.statIDs, id)
	d.statFlags = append(d.statFlags, stream)
	return &stStatsStream{ctx: ctx, d: d, samples: d.samples}, nil
}

// stEnd is what a stream answers once its scripted items are used up.
func (d *stDocker) stEnd(ctx context.Context) error {
	switch {
	case d.endErr != nil:
		return d.endErr
	case d.block:
		<-ctx.Done()
		return ctx.Err()
	}
	return io.EOF
}

type stLogStream struct {
	ctx    context.Context
	d      *stDocker
	frames []dockerapi.LogFrame
}

func (s *stLogStream) Next() (dockerapi.LogFrame, error) {
	if len(s.frames) == 0 {
		return dockerapi.LogFrame{}, s.d.stEnd(s.ctx)
	}
	f := s.frames[0]
	s.frames = s.frames[1:]
	return f, nil
}

func (s *stLogStream) Close() error { s.d.closed++; return nil }

type stStatsStream struct {
	ctx     context.Context
	d       *stDocker
	samples []dockerapi.Stats
}

func (s *stStatsStream) Next() (dockerapi.Stats, error) {
	if len(s.samples) == 0 {
		return dockerapi.Stats{}, s.d.stEnd(s.ctx)
	}
	v := s.samples[0]
	s.samples = s.samples[1:]
	return v, nil
}

func (s *stStatsStream) Close() error { s.d.closed++; return nil }

// stSetup puts the containers into a fresh host and points a dk at the wrapped engine.
func stSetup(t *testing.T, cs ...dockerapi.ContainerJSON) (*dkHost, dk, *stDocker) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	for _, c := range cs {
		h.docker.put(c)
	}
	d := &stDocker{fakeDocker: h.docker}
	k := h.dk()
	k.d.docker = d
	return h, k, d
}

// stCollect runs def with the JSON params and returns the events it emitted.
func stCollect(ctx context.Context, h *dkHost, def core.StreamDef, params string) ([]any, error) {
	var got []any
	err := def.Run(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(params), func(e any) error {
		got = append(got, e)
		return nil
	})
	return got, err
}

// stText joins the text of the log events of one stream.
func stText(events []any, stream string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, e := range events {
		if ev := e.(LogEvent); ev.Stream == stream {
			b.WriteString(ev.Text)
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}

func stOwned(name string) dockerapi.ContainerJSON {
	return dkContainer(name, dkRunning, dkLabels(map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"}))
}

func stFrame(stream, text string) dockerapi.LogFrame {
	return dockerapi.LogFrame{Stream: stream, Data: []byte(text)}
}

func TestStStreamDefs(t *testing.T) {
	k := newDKHost(t).dk()
	logs, stats := k.logsStream(), k.statsStream()
	if logs.Name != "logs" || logs.ParamsType != reflect.TypeFor[LogsParams]() || logs.EventType != reflect.TypeFor[LogEvent]() {
		t.Errorf("logs stream = %s, %v, %v; want logs, LogsParams, LogEvent", logs.Name, logs.ParamsType, logs.EventType)
	}
	if stats.Name != "stats" || stats.ParamsType != reflect.TypeFor[StatsParams]() || stats.EventType != reflect.TypeFor[StatsEvent]() {
		t.Errorf("stats stream = %s, %v, %v; want stats, StatsParams, StatsEvent", stats.Name, stats.ParamsType, stats.EventType)
	}
}

func TestStLogsEmitsFramesInOrder(t *testing.T) {
	h, k, d := stSetup(t, dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
	d.frames = []dockerapi.LogFrame{stFrame("stdout", "one\n"), stFrame("stderr", "two\n")}
	got, err := stCollect(context.Background(), h, k.logsStream(), `{"container":"web"}`)
	want := []any{LogEvent{Stream: "stdout", Text: "one\n"}, LogEvent{Stream: "stderr", Text: "two\n"}}
	if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("events %v (%v), want %v", got, err, want)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(d.logIDs, []string{dkID("web")}) || d.closed != 1 {
		t.Errorf("logs opened for %v and closed %d times, want the container's full id once", d.logIDs, d.closed)
	}
}

func TestStLogsOptions(t *testing.T) {
	noon := time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 11, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	tests := []struct {
		name, params string
		want         dockerapi.LogsOptions
	}{
		{"defaults", `{"container":"web"}`, dockerapi.LogsOptions{Stdout: true, Stderr: true, Tail: "200"}},
		{"follow and every line", `{"container":"web","follow":true,"tail":"all"}`, dockerapi.LogsOptions{Follow: true, Stdout: true, Stderr: true}},
		{"count and since", `{"container":"web","tail":"5","since":"2026-10-30T11:00:00Z"}`, dockerapi.LogsOptions{Stdout: true, Stderr: true, Tail: "5", Since: noon}},
		{"since with an offset", `{"container":"web","since":"2026-10-30T13:00:00+02:00"}`, dockerapi.LogsOptions{Stdout: true, Stderr: true, Tail: "200", Since: noon}},
		{"no lines", `{"container":"web","tail":"0"}`, dockerapi.LogsOptions{Stdout: true, Stderr: true, Tail: "0"}},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, k, d := stSetup(t, dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
			if _, err := stCollect(context.Background(), h, k.logsStream(), tc.params); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if len(d.logOpts) != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("logs opened %d times, want once", len(d.logOpts))
			}
			got := d.logOpts[0]
			if !got.Since.Equal(tc.want.Since) {
				t.Errorf("since %v, want %v", got.Since, tc.want.Since)
			}
			got.Since, tc.want.Since = time.Time{}, time.Time{}
			if got != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("options %+v, want %+v", got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestStLogsRefusesBadParams(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct{ name, params, path string }{
		{"empty container", `{"container":""}`, "/container"},
		{"no container", `{}`, "/container"},
		{"since not a time", `{"container":"web","since":"yesterday"}`, "/since"},
		{"negative tail", `{"container":"web","tail":"-1"}`, "/tail"},
		{"tail not a number", `{"container":"web","tail":"many"}`, "/tail"},
		{"fractional tail", `{"container":"web","tail":"1.5"}`, "/tail"},
		{"unknown member", `{"container":"web","bogus":1}`, ""},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, k, d := stSetup(t, dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
			got, err := stCollect(context.Background(), h, k.logsStream(), tc.params)
			e := errcode.From(err)
			if e.Code != errcode.InvalidInput || len(got) != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("got %v and %v, want %s and no events", got, err, errcode.InvalidInput)
			}
			if tc.path != "" && (len(e.Fields) != 1 || e.Fields[0].Path != tc.path) {
				t.Errorf("fields %+v, want one at %s", e.Fields, tc.path)
			}
			if calls := h.docker.calls(); len(calls) != 0 || len(d.logIDs) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("the engine was called (%v, %v) before the parameters were checked", calls, d.logIDs)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestStLogsMasksSecretsOfOwnedContainers(t *testing.T) {
	h, k, d := stSetup(t, stOwned("npm-app"), dkContainer("plain", dkRunning))
	var asked []string
	k.d.secrets = func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, id string) ([][]byte, error) {
		asked = append(asked, id)
		return [][]byte{[]byte("hunter2")}, nil
	}

	d.frames = []dockerapi.LogFrame{stFrame("stdout", "login pass=hun"), stFrame("stdout", "ter2 ok\n"), stFrame("stderr", "hunter2\n")}
	got, err := stCollect(context.Background(), h, k.logsStream(), `{"container":"npm-app"}`)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if out, errText := stText(got, "stdout"), stText(got, "stderr"); out != "login pass="+logfilter.Mask+" ok\n" || errText != logfilter.Mask+"\n" {
		t.Errorf("stdout %q and stderr %q, want the secret masked in both, across frames", out, errText)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(asked, []string{dkID("npm-app")}) {
		t.Errorf("secrets asked for %v, want the owned container's id", asked)
	}

	asked = nil
	d.frames = []dockerapi.LogFrame{stFrame("stdout", "pass=hunter2\n")}
	got, err = stCollect(context.Background(), h, k.logsStream(), `{"container":"plain"}`)
	if text := stText(got, "stdout"); err != nil || text != "pass=hunter2\n" || len(asked) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("unlabelled container: text %q, secrets asked %v (%v), want the text unchanged and no lookup", text, asked, err)
	}
}

func TestStLogsSplitsLargeFrames(t *testing.T) {
	h, k, d := stSetup(t, dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
	out := strings.Repeat("a", 20000)
	errText := strings.Repeat("€", 5000)
	d.frames = []dockerapi.LogFrame{stFrame("stdout", out), stFrame("stderr", errText)}
	got, err := stCollect(context.Background(), h, k.logsStream(), `{"container":"web"}`)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

		ev := e.(LogEvent)
		if len(ev.Text) > 8192 || !utf8.ValidString(ev.Text) {

	}
}

func TestStLogsEnds(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("reader gone", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, k, d := stSetup(t, dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
		d.frames = []dockerapi.LogFrame{stFrame("stdout", "a\n"), stFrame("stdout", "b\n"), stFrame("stdout", "c\n")}
		gone := errors.New("reader gone")
		emitted := 0
		err := k.logsStream().Run(context.Background(), h.env(""), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`), func(any) error {
			emitted++
			return gone
		})
		if !errors.Is(err, gone) || emitted != 1 || d.closed != 1 {
			t.Errorf("err = %v after %d events, stream closed %d times; want the emit error after 1 event and one close", err, emitted, d.closed)
		}
	})
	t.Run("context cancelled while following", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, k, d := stSetup(t, dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
		d.frames, d.block = []dockerapi.LogFrame{stFrame("stdout", "a\n")}, true
		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
		defer cancel()
		err := k.logsStream().Run(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web","follow":true}`), func(any) error {
			cancel()
			return nil
		})
		if err != nil || d.closed != 1 {
			t.Errorf("err = %v, stream closed %d times; want nil and one close", err, d.closed)
		}
	})
	t.Run("stream fails", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, k, d := stSetup(t, dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
		d.frames, d.endErr = []dockerapi.LogFrame{stFrame("stdout", "a\n")}, errors.New("connection reset")
		got, err := stCollect(context.Background(), h, k.logsStream(), `{"container":"web"}`)
		if !errors.Is(err, d.endErr) || len(got) != 1 || d.closed != 1 {
			t.Errorf("got %v and %v, closed %d times; want the frame, the stream's error and one close", got, err, d.closed)
		}
	})
}

func TestStLogFilter(t *testing.T) {
	broken := errors.New("sealed store unreadable")
	tests := []struct {
		name     string
		labels   map[string]string
		secrets  [][]byte
		err      error
		wantAsk  bool
		wantPush string
	}{
		{"unlabelled container is not filtered", nil, [][]byte{[]byte("hunter2")}, nil, false, "pass=hunter2"},
		{"owned container is filtered", map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"}, [][]byte{[]byte("hunter2")}, nil, true, "pass=" + logfilter.Mask},
		{"owned container without secrets", map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"}, nil, nil, true, "pass=hunter2"},
		{"lookup error is returned as is", map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"}, nil, broken, true, ""},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			k := h.dk()
			var asked []string
			k.d.secrets = func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, id string) ([][]byte, error) {
				asked = append(asked, id)
				return tc.secrets, tc.err
			}
			c := dkContainer("app", dkLabels(tc.labels))
			f, err := k.logFilter(context.Background(), h.env(""), c)
			if tc.err != nil {
				if !errors.Is(err, tc.err) || f != nil {
					t.Errorf("logFilter = %v, %v; want a nil filter and %v unchanged", f, err, tc.err)
				}
			} else if got := string(f.Push("stdout", []byte("pass=hunter2"))); err != nil || got != tc.wantPush {
				t.Errorf("filtered %q (%v), want %q", got, err, tc.wantPush)
			}
			if tc.wantAsk && !reflect.DeepEqual(asked, []string{c.ID}) {
				t.Errorf("secrets asked for %v, want the container's id", asked)
			}
			if !tc.wantAsk && len(asked) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("secrets asked for %v, want no lookup for an unlabelled container", asked)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestStStatsEmitsSamples(t *testing.T) {
	h, k, d := stSetup(t, dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
	idle := dockerapi.Stats{
		Read:        "2026-10-30T12:00:02.5Z",
		CPUStats:    dockerapi.CPUStats{CPUUsage: dockerapi.CPUUsage{TotalUsage: 300}, SystemCPUUsage: 2000, OnlineCPUs: 2},
		PreCPUStats: dockerapi.CPUStats{CPUUsage: dockerapi.CPUUsage{TotalUsage: 300}, SystemCPUUsage: 2000, OnlineCPUs: 2},
		MemoryStats: dockerapi.MemoryStats{Usage: 500, Limit: 4096},
	}
	d.samples = []dockerapi.Stats{stSample(), idle}
	got, err := stCollect(context.Background(), h, k.statsStream(), `{"container":"web"}`)
	if err != nil || len(got) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("events %v (%v), want two", got, err)
	}
	first, second := got[0].(StatsEvent), got[1].(StatsEvent)
	if math.Abs(first.CPUPercent-40) > 1e-9 {
		t.Errorf("first sample cpuPercent = %v, want 40 (200/1000 of the host's time over 2 CPUs)", first.CPUPercent)
	}
	first.CPUPercent = 0
	if want := (StatsEvent{Read: "2026-10-30T12:00:01.5Z", MemUsage: 800, MemLimit: 4096, NetRx: 15, NetTx: 27, Pids: 7}); first != want {
		t.Errorf("first event %+v, want %+v", first, want)
	}
	if want := (StatsEvent{Read: "2026-10-30T12:00:02.5Z", MemUsage: 500, MemLimit: 4096}); second != want {
		t.Errorf("second event %+v, want %+v", second, want)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(d.statIDs, []string{dkID("web")}) || !reflect.DeepEqual(d.statFlags, []bool{true}) || d.closed != 1 {
		t.Errorf("stats opened for %v (stream %v), closed %d times; want the full id once, streaming, closed once", d.statIDs, d.statFlags, d.closed)
	}
}

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `internal/modules/docker/logsecrets.go`:

1. `func (k dk) logFilter(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, c dockerapi.ContainerJSON) (*logfilter.Filter, error)`: when `ownerOf(c.Config.Labels)` is `""` it returns `logfilter.New(nil)` without calling `k.d.secrets`; otherwise it calls `k.d.secrets(ctx, env, c.ID)`, returns `nil` and that error unchanged when it fails, and returns `logfilter.New` over the secrets it answers (no secrets: a filter that passes data through).

In `internal/modules/docker/streams.go`, name every private helper with a `stream` or `log` prefix so it cannot collide with another task's identifier in this package:

2. `func (k dk) logsStream() core.StreamDef` returns `core.DefineStream("logs", …)` over `LogsParams` and `LogEvent`. The run function does, in this order:
   1. Check the parameters before any Engine call. A failure is a `*errcode.Error` with code `request.invalid_input` and exactly one `errcode.FieldError`: `container` empty gives path `/container`; `since` non-empty and rejected by `time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, …)` gives `/since`; `tail` that is not `""`, `"all"` or a non-negative decimal integer in canonical form (`strconv.Atoi` succeeds, the result is at least 0 and `strconv.Itoa` of it equals `tail`) gives `/tail`. Members outside `LogsParams` are refused by `DefineStream` itself.
   2. Build `dockerapi.LogsOptions{Follow: p.Follow, Stdout: true, Stderr: true, Since: <parsed or zero>, Tail: …}` with `Tail` `"200"` for `""`, `""` (every line) for `"all"`, and otherwise `tail` as given. `Timestamps` stays false.
   3. `InspectContainer(ctx, p.Container)`; on error return `engineError("container", p.Container, err)`. A container the module owns is allowed: logs are read only.
   4. `k.logFilter(ctx, env, c)`; on error return it unchanged, before the log stream is opened.
   5. `Logs(ctx, c.ID, opts)` with the container's full id from the inspect; on error return `engineError("container", p.Container, err)`. `defer` closing the stream.
   6. Loop on `Next()`. For a frame, pass `Data` through `filter.Push(frame.Stream, frame.Data)` and emit the bytes it returns as `LogEvent{Stream: frame.Stream, Text: …}`, in chunks of at most 8192 bytes, each chunk cut at a UTF-8 rune start (move the cut back from the limit to the nearest rune-start byte; when the chunk has none, cut at the limit). The chunking keeps every serialized event under the transport's 64 KiB limit even when JSON escaping turns a byte into six. Emit nothing for an empty result (the filter is holding bytes back). An error from `emit` is returned unchanged.
   7. On `io.EOF`, emit the masked remainder of `filter.Flush("stdout")` and then of `filter.Flush("stderr")`, chunked the same way, and return nil. On any other error from `Next`: return nil when `ctx.Err() != nil` (the reader left), else `fmt.Errorf("docker: logs of %s: %w", p.Container, err)`. Test `io.EOF` first, then the context.
3. `func (k dk) statsStream() core.StreamDef` returns `core.DefineStream("stats", …)` over `StatsParams` and `StatsEvent`: an empty `container` is `request.invalid_input` with the field path `/container` before any Engine call; then `InspectContainer` (error through `engineError("container", p.Container, err)`), `Stats(ctx, c.ID, true)` (same mapping), `defer` closing the stream, and a loop on `Next()`. Each sample becomes `StatsEvent{Read: sample.Read, CPUPercent, MemUsage, MemLimit: from usageOf(sample), NetRx and NetTx: sums of RxBytes and TxBytes over sample.Networks, Pids: sample.PidsStats.Current}`; an `emit` error is returned unchanged; `io.EOF` or a finished context ends the stream with nil, any other error is `fmt.Errorf("docker: stats of %s: %w", p.Container, err)`.
4. Neither function writes the journal or the database, and neither takes a lock.

var pjNow = time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

// pjSummary is a container of a Compose project as the Engine lists it; an empty
// label value leaves the label out.
func pjSummary(name, project, dir, files, envFiles string) dockerapi.ContainerSummary {
	labels := map[string]string{}
	for k, v := range map[string]string{
		"com.docker.compose.project":                  project,
		"com.docker.compose.project.working_dir":      dir,
		"com.docker.compose.project.config_files":     files,
		"com.docker.compose.project.environment_file": envFiles,
	} {
		if v != "" {
			labels[k] = v
		}
	}
	return dockerapi.ContainerSummary{ID: dkID(name), Names: []string{"/" + name}, State: "running", Labels: labels}
}
