```go
	defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
	var cols []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var c string
		if err := rows.Scan(&c); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		cols = append(cols, c)
	}
	want := []string{"name", "directory", "files_json", "env_files_json", "profiles_json", "run_hash", "first_seen", "last_run"}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(cols, want) {
		t.Errorf("columns %v, want %v", cols, want)
	}
	var strict int
	if err := db.Read().QueryRow(`SELECT strict FROM pragma_table_list('docker_projects')`).Scan(&strict); err != nil || strict != 1 {
		t.Errorf("strict = %d (%v), want a STRICT table", strict, err)
	}
}

func TestPjConfigHash(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	k := h.dk()
	put := func(path, data string) { h.files[path] = dkFile{Data: []byte(data)} }
	put("/srv/blog/compose.yaml", "services: {}\n")
	put("/srv/blog/.env", "A=1\n")
	base := projectRow{Name: "blog", Files: []string{"/srv/blog/compose.yaml"}, EnvFiles: []string{"/srv/blog/.env"}}

	hash := k.configHash(base)
	if !regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`).MatchString(hash) || hash != k.configHash(base) {
		t.Fatalf("hash %q, want 64 hex digits that repeat", hash)
	}

	changed := func(name string, mutate func(*projectRow)) {
		t.Helper()
		p := base
		mutate(&p)
		if got := k.configHash(p); got == hash || got == "" {
			t.Errorf("%s: hash %q, want a different hash from %q", name, got, hash)
		}
	}
	put("/srv/blog/.env", "A=2\n")
	changed("an env file's bytes change", func(*projectRow) {})
	put("/srv/blog/.env", "A=1\n")
	put("/srv/blog/compose.yaml", "services: {web: {}}\n")
	changed("a compose file's bytes change", func(*projectRow) {})
	put("/srv/blog/compose.yaml", "services: {}\n")
	put("/srv/blog/other.yaml", "services: {}\n")
	changed("a file has another path and the same bytes", func(p *projectRow) { p.Files = []string{"/srv/blog/other.yaml"} })
	changed("an env file is dropped", func(p *projectRow) { p.EnvFiles = nil })

	put("/a", "ab")
	put("/b", "c")
	left := k.configHash(projectRow{Files: []string{"/a", "/b"}})
	put("/a", "a")
	put("/b", "bc")
	if right := k.configHash(projectRow{Files: []string{"/a", "/b"}}); right == left {
		t.Error("moving a byte from one file to the next gave the same hash, want the file boundary part of the hash")
	}
	put("/a", "x")
	put("/b", "y")
	if k.configHash(projectRow{Files: []string{"/a", "/b"}}) == k.configHash(projectRow{Files: []string{"/b", "/a"}}) {
		t.Error("two orders of the same files gave the same hash, want the order part of the hash")
	}

	if got := k.configHash(projectRow{Files: []string{"/srv/blog/compose.yaml", "/srv/blog/gone.yaml"}}); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("hash %q with an unreadable file, want empty", got)
	}
	if got := k.configHash(projectRow{Files: []string{"/srv/blog/compose.yaml"}, EnvFiles: []string{"/srv/blog/gone.env"}}); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("hash %q with an unreadable env file, want empty", got)
	}
}
```

Create `internal/modules/docker/migrations/agent/0001_docker.sql` with this content:

```sql
-- The Compose projects the docker module has seen (spec 3, Discovery), read
-- and written only through internal/modules/docker. Times are fixed-width
-- RFC 3339 UTC text, so they compare as text; the *_json columns hold JSON
-- arrays of strings.
CREATE TABLE docker_projects (
    name           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    directory      TEXT NOT NULL,
    files_json     TEXT NOT NULL,
    env_files_json TEXT NOT NULL,
    profiles_json  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    run_hash       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    first_seen     TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_run       TEXT
) STRICT;
```

In `internal/modules/docker/store.go`, copy the shape of `internal/modules/firewall/store.go` (`//go:embed migrations/agent/*.sql`, `fs.Sub`). Name every private helper with a `project` prefix so it cannot collide with another task's identifier in this package:

1. `agentMigrations() fs.FS` returns the embedded `migrations/agent` directory.
2. Times are stored as `t.UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z")` and parsed with the same layout; `last_run` is SQL `NULL` until the first run, and `LastRun` is the zero time then.
3. `projectRow` is exactly as Contracts gives it. Every slice a read returns (`Files`, `EnvFiles`, `Profiles`) is non-nil, an empty list when the stored JSON array is empty.
4. `discoverProjects(ctx, db, now, cs)` runs in one `db.Write` transaction. For each summary whose label `com.docker.compose.project` is non-empty and not yet handled in this call, it inserts a row with `INSERT OR IGNORE`: `directory` from `com.docker.compose.project.working_dir` (`""` when the label is absent), `files_json` from the comma-separated `com.docker.compose.project.config_files`, `env_files_json` from the comma-separated `com.docker.compose.project.environment_file` (absent label: `[]`), empty parts dropped, `profiles_json` `[]`, `run_hash` `""`, `first_seen` `now`. A project with partial labels is still recorded, so it stays listed while its actions refuse with a reason. The first container of a project in the slice decides its row. It never updates or deletes a row.
5. `loadProject` finds one row by name (`ok` false and a nil error for none); `listProjects` returns every row ordered by name. Both read through `db.Read()`.
6. `setProjectRun(ctx, tx, name, profiles, runHash, at)` updates `profiles_json` (a nil list is stored as `[]`), `run_hash` and `last_run` of one row inside the caller's transaction, and returns an error naming the project when no row was updated.
7. `func (k dk) configHash(p projectRow) string` reads each file of `p.Files` and then of `p.EnvFiles` with `k.d.readFile` and returns the lowercase hex SHA-256 of, for each file in that order, the path's length as 8 bytes big-endian, the path, the data's length as 8 bytes big-endian, and the data. The length prefixes make a byte moved between neighbouring files change the hash. Any read error gives `""`.

In `internal/modules/docker/projects.go`:

8. `func (k dk) projectsResource() core.ResourceDef` is `core.DefineResource("docker.projects", …)` returning `ProjectList`. It calls `ListContainers(ctx, dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{All: true})` (stopped containers still name their project); an error is `engineError("containers", "", err)` and nothing is written. It then calls `discoverProjects(ctx, env.DB, env.Clock.Now(), containers)` and `listProjects`, and builds one `Project` per stored row, ordered by name: `Files`, `EnvFiles` and `Profiles` as stored; `ConfigHash` from `k.configHash(row)`; `Containers` the names (first entry of `Names`, without the leading `/`), sorted, of the listed containers whose compose project label equals the row's name, an empty non-nil list when there are none; `Running` the number of those whose `State` is `running`; `HashChanged` true only when `row.RunHash` and `ConfigHash` are both non-empty and differ; `FirstSeen` the row's; `LastRun` a pointer to the row's last run, nil when it never ran. An empty result serializes as `{"projects":[]}`, never `null`.
9. The resource only reads the Engine and writes `docker_projects` rows through `discoverProjects`; it takes no lock and journals nothing.

Spec 3 fixes the semantics: the effect kind is `container.run`, the post-state is `Id`, `Created`, `Running`, `StartedAt`, `FinishedAt`, and the state an undo restores is `Id`, `Created`, `Running` as before the action. `dstate` renders both, and `observe` picks the form from the effect's state, so the handler never builds a comparator document itself. `crDocker` wraps the fake engine to record the timeouts the stop and restart calls receive. The tests call the handlers through the action's erased `Handler` functions and play the engine's undo (compare with the recorded state, run the inverse with `State` `undoing` and `UndoTo` the before-state, compare with the before-state) by hand. They expect the fake's `RestartContainer` to start a container that is stopped, as Docker does.

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/docker/dstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

const crCreated = "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z"

// crDocker records the timeouts the stop and restart calls are given.
type crDocker struct {
	*fakeDocker
	timeouts []time.Duration
}

func (d *crDocker) StopContainer(ctx context.Context, id string, timeout time.Duration) (bool, error) {
	d.timeouts = append(d.timeouts, timeout)
	return d.fakeDocker.StopContainer(ctx, id, timeout)
}

func (d *crDocker) RestartContainer(ctx context.Context, id string, timeout time.Duration) error {
	d.timeouts = append(d.timeouts, timeout)
	return d.fakeDocker.RestartContainer(ctx, id, timeout)
}

// crModule registers the three actions the way the module's manifest will.
type crModule struct{ k dk }

func (m crModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: ID, Version: 1, Actions: []core.ActionDef{m.k.containerStart(), m.k.containerStop(), m.k.containerRestart()}}
}

func crDef(k dk, action string) core.ActionDef {
	switch action {
	case "docker.container.start":
		return k.containerStart()
	case "docker.container.stop":
		return k.containerStop()
	}
	return k.containerRestart()
}

// crSetup holds a container "web", running or stopped, behind a dk whose engine is a crDocker.
func crSetup(t *testing.T, running bool, opts ...func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON)) (*dkHost, dk, *crDocker) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	if running {
		opts = append(opts, dkRunning)
	}
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("web", opts...))
	d := &crDocker{fakeDocker: h.docker}
	k := h.dk()
	k.d.docker = d
	return h, k, d
}

func crIn(ref string) json.RawMessage { return json.RawMessage(`{"container":"` + ref + `"}`) }

// crSame compares two State documents as JSON values.
func crSame(t *testing.T, a, b json.RawMessage) bool {
	t.Helper()
	var va, vb any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(a, &va); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("state %s: %v", a, err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &vb); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("state %s: %v", b, err)
	}
	return reflect.DeepEqual(va, vb)
}

func crState(t *testing.T, raw json.RawMessage) ContainerState {
	t.Helper()
	var s ContainerState
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return s
}

func TestCrActionDefinitions(t *testing.T) {

}

func TestCrPlan(t *testing.T) {
	head := core.DiffLine{Op: " ", Text: "container web (" + dkID("web")[:12] + ")"}
	line := func(op, text string) core.DiffLine { return core.DiffLine{Op: op, Text: text} }
	tests := []struct {
		name, action string
		running      bool
		want         []core.DiffLine
	}{
		{"start a stopped container", "docker.container.start", false, []core.DiffLine{head, line("-", "state: stopped"), line("+", "state: running")}},
		{"start a running container", "docker.container.start", true, []core.DiffLine{head, line(" ", "state: running (already running)")}},
		{"stop a running container", "docker.container.stop", true, []core.DiffLine{head, line("-", "state: running"), line("+", "state: stopped")}},
		{"stop a stopped container", "docker.container.stop", false, []core.DiffLine{head, line(" ", "state: stopped (already stopped)")}},
		{"restart a running container", "docker.container.restart", true, []core.DiffLine{head, line(" ", "state: running"), line("+", "restart: stop with a 10 s timeout, then start")}},
		{"restart a stopped container", "docker.container.restart", false, []core.DiffLine{head, line("-", "state: stopped"), line("+", "state: running")}},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, k, _ := crSetup(t, tc.running)
			out, err := crDef(k, tc.action).Handler.Plan(context.Background(), h.env(""), crIn("web"))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(out.Diff, tc.want) || len(out.StateHash) != 64 || out.Confirmation != "" || len(out.Guards) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("plan %+v, want diff %v, a 64-digit state hash, no confirmation and no guards", out, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCrPlanStateHash(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	hash := func(running bool, opts ...func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON)) string {
		h, k, _ := crSetup(t, running, opts...)
		out, err := k.containerStart().Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), crIn("web"))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return out.StateHash
	}
	stopped, running := hash(false), hash(true)
	if stopped == running {
		t.Error("a stopped and a running container have the same state hash")
	}
	if again := hash(true, func(c *dockerapi.ContainerJSON) { c.State.StartedAt = "2026-10-02T00:00:00Z" }); again != running {
		t.Error("a later start time changed the state hash, want identity and running flag only")
	}
	if other := hash(true, func(c *dockerapi.ContainerJSON) { c.ID = dkID("recreated") }); other == running {
		t.Error("a recreated container (another id) has the same state hash")
	}
}

func TestCrRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	owned := dkLabels(map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"})
	tests := []struct {

	}{

		{"unknown container", "ghost", nil, nil, errcode.NotFound},
		{"owned container", "web", nil, []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON){owned}, errcode.DockerOwned},
		{"engine unavailable", "web", func(h *dkHost) { h.docker.fail("InspectContainer", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable) }, nil, errcode.DockerEngineUnavailable},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {

				} else {

				}

				}
			})

func TestCrApply(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name, action  string
		running       bool
		wantRunning   bool
		wantBefore    bool // the running flag journaled as the state an undo restores
		call          string
		wantTimeouts  []time.Duration
		wantNoCallsOf []string
	}{
		{"start a stopped container", "docker.container.start", false, true, false, "StartContainer", nil, []string{"StopContainer", "RestartContainer"}},
		{"start a running container", "docker.container.start", true, true, true, "StartContainer", nil, []string{"StopContainer", "RestartContainer"}},
		{"stop a running container", "docker.container.stop", true, false, true, "StopContainer", []time.Duration{stopTimeout}, []string{"StartContainer", "RestartContainer"}},
		{"stop a stopped container", "docker.container.stop", false, false, false, "StopContainer", []time.Duration{stopTimeout}, []string{"StartContainer", "RestartContainer"}},
		{"restart a running container", "docker.container.restart", true, true, true, "RestartContainer", []time.Duration{stopTimeout}, []string{"StartContainer", "StopContainer"}},
		{"restart a stopped container", "docker.container.restart", false, true, true, "RestartContainer", []time.Duration{stopTimeout}, []string{"StartContainer", "StopContainer"}},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, k, d := crSetup(t, tc.running)
			h.clock.Advance(time.Minute)
			raw, err := crDef(k, tc.action).Handler.Apply(context.Background(), h.env("c1"), crIn("web"))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if got, want := crState(t, raw), (ContainerState{ID: dkID("web"), Name: "web", Running: tc.wantRunning}); got != want {
				t.Errorf("output %+v, want %+v", got, want)
			}
			c, _ := h.docker.container(dkID("web"))
			if c.State.Running != tc.wantRunning {
				t.Errorf("container running = %v, want %v", c.State.Running, tc.wantRunning)
			}
			calls := h.docker.calls()
			if !slices.Contains(calls, tc.call) {
				t.Errorf("engine calls %v, want %s", calls, tc.call)
			}
			for _, other := range tc.wantNoCallsOf {
				if slices.Contains(calls, other) {
					t.Errorf("engine calls %v include %s", calls, other)
				}
			}
			if !slices.Equal(d.timeouts, tc.wantTimeouts) {
				t.Errorf("stop timeouts %v, want %v", d.timeouts, tc.wantTimeouts)
			}

			effects := h.journal.effects()
			if len(effects) != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("%d effects journaled, want 1", len(effects))
			}
			e := effects[0]
			if e.Kind != core.EffectModify || e.Resource != containerResource(dkID("web")) || e.Local || e.CommitWait != commitWait || e.State != core.EffectMade {
				t.Errorf("effect %+v, want a made, non-local modify of the container with the Engine's commit wait", e)
			}
			before, _ := dstate.ContainerRunning(dkID("web"), crCreated, tc.wantBefore)
			after, _ := dstate.ContainerRun(c, dstate.Recorded)
			if !crSame(t, e.Before.State, before) {
				t.Errorf("before %s, want %s", e.Before.State, before)
			}
			if e.Post == nil || !crSame(t, e.Post.State, after) {
				t.Errorf("post %+v, want the recorded state %s", e.Post, after)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCrApplyJournalsBeforeTheCall(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("the daemon refuses", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, k, _ := crSetup(t, false)
		h.docker.fail("StartContainer", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 400, Message: "bad request"})
		_, err := k.containerStart().Handler.Apply(context.Background(), h.env("c1"), crIn("web"))
		effects := h.journal.effects()
		if !core.IsDefinite(err) || len(effects) != 1 || effects[0].State != core.EffectSkipped {
			t.Errorf("err = %v (definite %v), effects %+v; want a definite refusal and a skipped effect", err, core.IsDefinite(err), effects)
		}
	})
	t.Run("the call fails without an answer", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, k, _ := crSetup(t, false)
		h.docker.fail("StartContainer", errors.New("connection reset"))
		_, err := k.containerStart().Handler.Apply(context.Background(), h.env("c1"), crIn("web"))
		effects := h.journal.effects()
		if err == nil || core.IsDefinite(err) || len(effects) != 1 || effects[0].State != core.EffectIntended {
			t.Errorf("err = %v (definite %v), effects %+v; want an uncertain error and an intended effect", err, core.IsDefinite(err), effects)
		}
	})
}

func TestCrVerify(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		action  string
		running bool // the state Verify requires
	}{
		{"docker.container.start", true},
		{"docker.container.restart", true},
		{"docker.container.stop", false},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.action, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, k, _ := crSetup(t, !tc.running)
			def := crDef(k, tc.action)
			ctx := context.Background()
			out, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), crIn("web"))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), crIn("web"), out); err != nil {
				t.Errorf("verify after apply: %v", err)
			}
			if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), crIn("web"), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err != nil {
				t.Errorf("verify without the output, as recovery calls it: %v", err)
			}
			c, _ := h.docker.container(dkID("web"))
			c.State.Running = !tc.running
			h.docker.put(c)
			if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), crIn("web"), out); err == nil {
				t.Error("verify passed with the container in the other state, want an error")
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestCrUndo applies each action, then plays the engine's undo of the
// journaled effect: compare with the recorded state, run the inverse, compare
// with the state the undo restores.
func TestCrUndo(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name, action string
		running      bool
		wantRunning  bool // after the undo
		noop         bool // the inverse changes nothing
	}{
		{"undo a start of a stopped container", "docker.container.start", false, false, false},
		{"undo a start of a running container", "docker.container.start", true, true, true},
		{"undo a stop of a running container", "docker.container.stop", true, true, false},
		{"undo a stop of a stopped container", "docker.container.stop", false, false, true},
		{"undo a restart of a running container", "docker.container.restart", true, true, true},
		{"undo a restart of a stopped container", "docker.container.restart", false, true, true},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			ctx := context.Background()
			h, k, _ := crSetup(t, tc.running)
			def := crDef(k, tc.action)
			if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), crIn("web")); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			e := h.journal.effects()[0]

			now, err := def.Handler.Observe(ctx, h.env("c1"), e)
			if err != nil || !crSame(t, now.Current.State, e.Post.State) {
				t.Fatalf("observed %s (%v) before the undo, want the recorded state %s", now.Current.State, err, e.Post.State)
			}

			h.clock.Advance(time.Minute)
			applied, _ := h.docker.container(dkID("web"))
			e.State, e.UndoTo = core.EffectUndoing, &e.Before
			if _, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, h.env("c1"), e); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			undone, _ := h.docker.container(dkID("web"))
			if undone.State.Running != tc.wantRunning {
				t.Errorf("running = %v after the undo, want %v", undone.State.Running, tc.wantRunning)
			}
			if tc.noop && !reflect.DeepEqual(applied, undone) {
				t.Errorf("the inverse changed the container: %+v -> %+v", applied.State, undone.State)
			}
			after, err := def.Handler.Observe(ctx, h.env("c1"), e)
			if err != nil || !crSame(t, after.Current.State, e.Before.State) {
				t.Errorf("observed %s (%v) after the undo, want the journaled before-state %s", after.Current.State, err, e.Before.State)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCrInverseRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	setup := func(t *testing.T) (*dkHost, core.ActionDef, core.Effect) {
		t.Helper()
		h, k, _ := crSetup(t, false)
		def := k.containerStart()
		if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), crIn("web")); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		e := h.journal.effects()[0]
		e.State, e.UndoTo = core.EffectUndoing, &e.Before
		return h, def, e
	}
	t.Run("the container is gone", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, def, e := setup(t)
		if err := h.docker.RemoveContainer(ctx, "web", dockerapi.RemoveContainerOptions{Force: true}); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		_, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, h.env("c1"), e)
		if c := errcode.From(err).Code; c != errcode.NotFound || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Errorf("err = %v (definite %v), want %s marked definite", err, core.IsDefinite(err), errcode.NotFound)
		}
	})
	t.Run("the daemon refuses", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, def, e := setup(t)
		h.docker.fail("StopContainer", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 409, Message: "conflict"})
		if _, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, h.env("c1"), e); !core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Errorf("err = %v, want a definite refusal", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("the call fails without an answer", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, def, e := setup(t)
		h.docker.fail("StopContainer", errors.New("connection reset"))
		if _, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, h.env("c1"), e); err == nil || core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Errorf("err = %v, want an error that is not definite", err)
		}
	})
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `internal/modules/docker/container_run.go`. Name private identifiers with a `run` or `container` prefix so they cannot collide with another task's identifiers in this package:

1. One handler type `runHandler{k dk; op containerOp}` serves the three actions, with `type containerOp int` and constants `opContainerStart`, `opContainerStop`, `opContainerRestart`. Each constructor returns `core.DefineMutating(core.ActionSpec{Name, Summary, Version: 1, Class: core.ClassCompensable, Side: core.SideAgent, LockKeys: []string{lockKey}}, runHandler{…})`; `ApplyTimeout` stays at the 30 s default. Because `runHandler` implements `Observe` and `Inverse`, `DefineMutating` finds them as the action's observer and undoer.
2. A private method `inspect(ctx, in ContainerInput)` shared by Plan and Apply: an empty `in.Container` is a `*errcode.Error` `request.invalid_input` with one `FieldError` at `/container`; then `k.d.docker.InspectContainer`, whose error goes through `engineError("container", in.Container, err)`; then `refuseOwned("container", <name without the leading "/">, c.Config.Labels)`. Every failure of `inspect` is wrapped with `core.Definite`, because nothing committed. It returns the `dockerapi.ContainerJSON`.
3. `Plan` returns `core.PlanOutcome` with no guards and no confirmation. `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 of `dstate.ContainerRun(c, dstate.Restored)`, so a recreated container or a changed running flag makes the plan stale, and a later start time does not. `Diff` is the line `{" ", "container <name> (<first 12 characters of the id>)"}` followed by these lines (`Op` then `Text`):
   - start, stopped: `-` `state: stopped`, `+` `state: running`; start, running: ` ` `state: running (already running)`
   - stop, running: `-` `state: running`, `+` `state: stopped`; stop, stopped: ` ` `state: stopped (already stopped)`
   - restart, running: ` ` `state: running`, `+` `restart: stop with a 10 s timeout, then start`; restart, stopped: `-` `state: stopped`, `+` `state: running`
4. `Apply` inspects again with `inspect` (the container may have changed since the plan), then calls `k.run` once with the effect `dockerEffect(core.EffectModify, containerResource(c.ID), before)`. `before` is `dstate.ContainerRunning(c.ID, c.Created, running)` with `running` the container's flag, except for restart, where it is always `true`: spec 3 says a restart itself is not reversed, so its undo only starts the container if it is stopped. The `do` function calls `StartContainer(ctx, c.ID)`, `StopContainer(ctx, c.ID, stopTimeout)` or `RestartContainer(ctx, c.ID, stopTimeout)` and returns `containerResource(c.ID)` with the error exactly as the Engine call gave it (so `run` can tell a 4xx refusal from a failure with no answer). The error `run` returns goes through `engineError("container", in.Container, err)`, which keeps the `core.Definite` mark. On success it inspects the container once more and returns `ContainerState{ID, Name without the leading "/", Running}` from it. Starting a running container or stopping a stopped one still goes through `run`; the Engine answers that it changed nothing.
5. `Verify` ignores its `out` (recovery passes the zero value): it inspects `in.Container` and returns an error naming the container when `State.Running` is not `true` for start and restart or not `false` for stop; an inspect error goes through `engineError`.
6. `Observe` is `h.k.observe(ctx, env, e)`.
7. `Inverse` leaves the container in the running state its effect's `Before.State` (`{"running": bool}`) names, touching no other resource: take the container id from `e.Resource` with `strings.CutPrefix(e.Resource, containerResource(""))`; `running: true` calls `StartContainer`, `running: false` calls `StopContainer(ctx, id, stopTimeout)`; both do nothing when the container is already in that state. An Engine error goes through `engineError("container", id, err)` and is wrapped with `core.Definite` when it is a 4xx answer (`*dockerapi.APIError` with a status from 400 to 499, which includes not found); any other failure is returned unwrapped so the engine treats the undo as uncertain. It returns an empty `core.InverseResult`.

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"slices"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"

// rmRecorder passes every call to the wrapped client and records the options
// of RemoveContainer.
type rmRecorder struct {
	dockerAPI
	opts []dockerapi.RemoveContainerOptions
}

func (r *rmRecorder) RemoveContainer(ctx context.Context, id string, o dockerapi.RemoveContainerOptions) error {
	r.opts = append(r.opts, o)
	return r.dockerAPI.RemoveContainer(ctx, id, o)
}

// rmModule registers one action, so the registry's own checks run on it.
type rmModule struct{ def core.ActionDef }

func (m rmModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: ID, Version: 1, Actions: []core.ActionDef{m.def}}
}

// rmRefused asserts err is a definite refusal with the given code and returns it.
func rmRefused(t *testing.T, err error, code errcode.Code) *errcode.Error {
	t.Helper()
	var coded *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != code {
		t.Fatalf("error %v, want code %s", err, code)
	}
	if !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Errorf("error %v is not marked definite", err)
	}
	return coded
}

func TestRMPlan(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	id12 := dkID("web")[:12]
	owned := dkLabels(map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"})
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		put     []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON)
		input   string
		code    errcode.Code // "" when the plan is accepted
		field   string       // the field a refusal names
		diff    []core.DiffLine
		confirm string
	}{
		{name: "stopped by name", input: `{"container":"web"}`, confirm: "web", diff: []core.DiffLine{
			{Op: "-", Text: "container web (" + id12 + ")"},
			{Op: " ", Text: "its writable layer is deleted and cannot be restored"},
		}},
		{name: "stopped by id", input: `{"container":"` + dkID("web") + `"}`, confirm: "web", diff: []core.DiffLine{
			{Op: "-", Text: "container web (" + id12 + ")"},
			{Op: " ", Text: "its writable layer is deleted and cannot be restored"},
		}},
		{name: "running with force and volumes", put: []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON){dkRunning},
			input: `{"container":"web","force":true,"volumes":true}`, confirm: "web", diff: []core.DiffLine{
				{Op: "-", Text: "container web (" + id12 + ")"},
				{Op: " ", Text: "its writable layer is deleted and cannot be restored"},
				{Op: " ", Text: "the running container is killed first"},
				{Op: " ", Text: "its anonymous volumes are deleted"},
			}},
		{name: "running without force", put: []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON){dkRunning},
			input: `{"container":"web"}`, code: errcode.InvalidInput, field: "/force"},
		{name: "empty name", input: `{"container":""}`, code: errcode.InvalidInput, field: "/container"},
		{name: "absent", input: `{"container":"ghost"}`, code: errcode.NotFound},
		{name: "owned", put: []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON){owned}, input: `{"container":"web"}`, code: errcode.DockerOwned},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			h.docker.put(dkContainer("web", tt.put...))
			def := h.dk().containerRemove()
			out, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(tt.input))
			if tt.code != "" {
				coded := rmRefused(t, err, tt.code)
				if tt.field != "" && !slices.ContainsFunc(coded.Fields, func(f errcode.FieldError) bool { return f.Path == tt.field }) {
					t.Errorf("fields %v, want one at %s", coded.Fields, tt.field)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !slices.Equal(out.Diff, tt.diff) {
				t.Errorf("diff %v, want %v", out.Diff, tt.diff)
			}
			if out.Confirmation != tt.confirm {
				t.Errorf("confirmation %q, want %q", out.Confirmation, tt.confirm)
			}
			if slices.Contains(h.docker.calls(), "RemoveContainer") {
				t.Error("a plan removed the container")
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestRMPlanStateHash: the hash is stable while the container is, and changes
// when the container starts, so a plan made before a start is refused.
func TestRMPlanStateHash(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("web"))
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("db"))
	def := h.dk().containerRemove()
	plan := func(name string) string {
		t.Helper()
		out, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"`+name+`","force":true}`))
		if err != nil || out.StateHash == "" {
			t.Fatalf("plan %s: hash %q, error %v", name, out.StateHash, err)
		}
		return out.StateHash
	}
	first := plan("web")
	if again := plan("web"); again != first {
		t.Errorf("a second plan hashes %s, want %s", again, first)
	}
	if other := plan("db"); other == first {
		t.Error("two containers hash alike")
	}
	if _, err := h.docker.StartContainer(ctx, "web"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if started := plan("web"); started == first {
		t.Error("the hash did not change when the container started")
	}
}

func TestRMApply(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	t.Run("stopped container", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.put(dkContainer("web"))
		before, _ := h.docker.container("web")
		def := h.dk().containerRemove()
		raw, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		var out Removed
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &out); err != nil || out != (Removed{ID: before.ID, Name: "web"}) {
			t.Errorf("output %s (%v), want id %s name web", raw, err, before.ID)
		}
		if _, ok := h.docker.container("web"); ok {
			t.Error("the container is still there")
		}
		effects := h.journal.effects()
		if len(effects) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("%d effects, want 1", len(effects))
		}
		e := effects[0]
		wantBefore, err := dstate.ContainerRun(before, dstate.Recorded)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if e.Kind != core.EffectDelete || e.Resource != containerResource(before.ID) || e.State != core.EffectMade ||
			e.Local || e.CommitWait != commitWait {
			t.Errorf("effect %+v, want a made non-local delete of %s with commit wait %s", e, containerResource(before.ID), commitWait)
		}
		if string(e.Before.State) != string(wantBefore) {
			t.Errorf("before %s, want %s", e.Before.State, wantBefore)
		}
		if e.Post == nil || string(e.Post.State) != "null" {
			t.Errorf("post %+v, want the absent state null", e.Post)
		}
	})
	t.Run("running container with force and volumes", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.put(dkContainer("web", dkRunning))
		k := h.dk()
		rec := &rmRecorder{dockerAPI: k.d.docker}
		k.d.docker = rec
		if _, err := k.containerRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web","force":true,"volumes":true}`)); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if want := []dockerapi.RemoveContainerOptions{{Force: true, Volumes: true}}; !slices.Equal(rec.opts, want) {
			t.Errorf("remove options %v, want %v", rec.opts, want)
		}
	})
	t.Run("the daemon refuses", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.put(dkContainer("web"))
		h.docker.fail("RemoveContainer", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 409, Message: "removal in progress"})
		_, err := h.dk().containerRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`))
		if err == nil || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Fatalf("error %v, want a definite refusal", err)
		}
		if effects := h.journal.effects(); len(effects) != 1 || effects[0].State != core.EffectSkipped {
			t.Errorf("effects %+v, want one skipped", effects)
		}
		if _, ok := h.docker.container("web"); !ok {
			t.Error("the container is gone")
		}
	})
	t.Run("the daemon fails", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.put(dkContainer("web"))
		h.docker.fail("RemoveContainer", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 500, Message: "boom"})
		_, err := h.dk().containerRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`))
		if err == nil || core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Fatalf("error %v, want an uncertain failure", err)
		}
		if effects := h.journal.effects(); len(effects) != 1 || effects[0].State != core.EffectIntended {
			t.Errorf("effects %+v, want one left intended", effects)
		}
	})
	t.Run("refused again at apply", func(t *testing.T) {
		for name, tt := range map[string]struct {
			opts []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON)
			code errcode.Code
		}{
			"owned":   {[]func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON){dkLabels(map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"})}, errcode.DockerOwned},
			"running": {[]func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON){dkRunning}, errcode.InvalidInput},
		} {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			h.docker.put(dkContainer("web", tt.opts...))
			_, err := h.dk().containerRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`))
			_ = rmRefused(t, err, tt.code)
			if len(h.journal.effects()) != 0 || slices.Contains(h.docker.calls(), "RemoveContainer") {
				t.Errorf("%s: apply journaled an effect or called RemoveContainer", name)
			}
		}
	})
}

func TestRMVerify(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("web"))
	def := h.dk().containerRemove()
	id := dkID("web")
	present := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`), json.RawMessage(`{"id":"`+id+`","name":"web"}`))
	if present == nil {
		t.Error("verify passed with the container still there")
	}
	if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`), json.RawMessage(`{"id":"`+id+`","name":"web"}`)); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("verify after the removal: %v", err)
	}
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("web"))
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err == nil {
		t.Error("verify without an output passed with a container of that name present")
	}
}

// TestRMObserve: a settle finds the container's recorded state while it is
// there and the absent state once it is removed.
func TestRMObserve(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("web"))
	def := h.dk().containerRemove()
	h.docker.fail("RemoveContainer", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 500, Message: "boom"})
	if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("apply succeeded")
	}
	e := h.journal.effects()[0]
	obs, err := def.Handler.Observe(ctx, h.env("c1"), e)
	if err != nil || string(obs.Current.State) != string(e.Before.State) {
		t.Errorf("observation %s (%v), want the journaled before-state %s", obs.Current.State, err, e.Before.State)
	}
	if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c2"), json.RawMessage(`{"container":"web"}`)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	obs, err = def.Handler.Observe(ctx, h.env("c2"), e)
	if err != nil || string(obs.Current.State) != "null" {
		t.Errorf("observation %s (%v), want null", obs.Current.State, err)
	}
}

func TestRMDefinition(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	def := h.dk().containerRemove()
	s := def.Spec
	if s.Name != "docker.container.remove" || s.Version != 1 || s.Class != core.ClassIrreversible || s.Side != core.SideAgent ||
		!slices.Equal(s.LockKeys, []string{"docker"}) {
		t.Errorf("spec %+v", s)
	}
	if def.Handler.Inverse != nil || def.Handler.Observe == nil {
		t.Errorf("inverse %v observe %v, want no inverse and an observer", def.Handler.Inverse != nil, def.Handler.Observe != nil)
	}
	if _, err := core.NewRegistry(rmModule{def}); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("the registry refuses the action: %v", err)
	}
	v := schema.NewValidator()
	for input, field := range map[string]string{
		`{"container":"web"}`:                             "",
		`{"container":"web","force":true,"volumes":true}`: "",
		`{}`:                                "/container",
		`{"container":"web","x":1}`:         "/x",
		`{"container":"web","force":"yes"}`: "/force",
	} {
		err := v.ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(input))
		var coded *errcode.Error
		switch {
		case field == "" && err != nil:
			t.Errorf("input %s: %v, want it accepted", input, err)
		case field != "" && (!errors.As(err, &coded) || !slices.ContainsFunc(coded.Fields, func(f errcode.FieldError) bool { return f.Path == field })):
			t.Errorf("input %s: %v, want a refusal naming %s", input, err, field)
		}
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `container_remove.go` (package `docker`):

1. `func (k dk) containerRemove() core.ActionDef` returns `core.DefineMutating[ContainerRemoveInput, Removed]` with the spec `Name: "docker.container.remove"`, a one-line `Summary`, `Version: 1`, `Class: core.ClassIrreversible`, `Side: core.SideAgent`, `LockKeys: []string{lockKey}` and no `ApplyTimeout` (the 30 s default holds). The handler is `containerRemoveHandler{k dk}` with `Plan`, `Apply`, `Verify` and `Observe` and no `Inverse`: the action is irreversible, so the registry refuses an undo handler on it.
2. One private method of the handler, `target(ctx, in)`, serves Plan and Apply. It returns the inspected `dockerapi.ContainerJSON` or one of these refusals, checked in this order and each wrapped in `core.Definite` because nothing has changed yet:
   - `in.Container == ""`: `*errcode.Error` with code `request.invalid_input` and one `FieldError` at path `/container` (the production client refuses an empty id, the fake does not, so the check is the handler's own).
   - `InspectContainer(ctx, in.Container)` fails: `engineError("container", in.Container, err)` (an absent container becomes `not_found`).
   - `refuseOwned("container", <name without the leading "/">, c.Config.Labels)`: `docker.owned`.
   - the container is running and `in.Force` is false: `request.invalid_input` with the detail `container <name> is running; stop it first or set force` and one `FieldError` at path `/force`.
3. `Plan` calls `target`, then renders `dstate.ContainerRun(c, dstate.Recorded)`. `Diff` is, in order: `{"-", "container <name> (<first 12 characters of the id>)"}`, `{" ", "its writable layer is deleted and cannot be restored"}`, then `{" ", "the running container is killed first"}` only when the container is running, then `{" ", "its anonymous volumes are deleted"}` only when `in.Volumes`. `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 of that state document, so a start, stop or recreate between plan and apply changes it. `Confirmation` is the container name without the leading slash, whatever the input named (id or name).
4. `Apply` calls `target` again (the engine re-plans before apply, but this is the last check before deleting). It renders the same Recorded document as the effect's before-state, builds `dockerEffect(core.EffectDelete, containerResource(c.ID), before)` and calls `k.run` with a `do` that calls `RemoveContainer(ctx, c.ID, dockerapi.RemoveContainerOptions{Force: in.Force, Volumes: in.Volumes})`. It removes by the id found, not by the input, so a container created under the same name in the meantime is untouched. `do` returns `containerResource(c.ID)` and the call's error passed through `engineError("container", in.Container, err)`; `run` journals made or skipped. The output is `Removed{ID: c.ID, Name: <name without the leading "/">}`.
5. `Verify` inspects `out.ID`, or `in.Container` when `out.ID` is empty (startup recovery passes the zero output): no error from the Engine is `fmt.Errorf("docker: container %s still exists", id)`, a not-found answer is success, any other error goes through `engineError`.
6. `Observe` returns `k.observe(ctx, env, e)` unchanged.

No file outside this task's block changes; `docker.go`'s `Manifest()` stays as it is (Task 44 registers the action). The constructor is called only by tests until then, which the lint accepts.

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

// imRecorder passes every call to the wrapped client and records the
// arguments of RemoveImage; with fixed set it answers the given items.
type imRecorder struct {
	dockerAPI
	refs  []string
	opts  []dockerapi.RemoveImageOptions
	fixed []dockerapi.ImageDeleteItem
	set   bool
}

func (r *imRecorder) RemoveImage(ctx context.Context, ref string, o dockerapi.RemoveImageOptions) ([]dockerapi.ImageDeleteItem, error) {
	r.refs = append(r.refs, ref)
	r.opts = append(r.opts, o)
	items, err := r.dockerAPI.RemoveImage(ctx, ref, o)
	if r.set {
		return r.fixed, err
	}
	return items, err
}

// imModule registers actions, so the registry's own checks run on them.
type imModule struct{ defs []core.ActionDef }

func (m imModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: ID, Version: 1, Actions: m.defs}
}

// imUses makes a container run the image with the given id.
func imUses(id string, running bool) func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON) {
	return func(c *dockerapi.ContainerJSON) {
		c.Image = id
		c.State.Running = running
		c.State.Status = "exited"
		if running {
			c.State.Status = "running"
		}
	}
}

// imRefused asserts err is a definite refusal with the given code and returns it.
func imRefused(t *testing.T, err error, code errcode.Code) *errcode.Error {
	t.Helper()
	var coded *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != code {
		t.Fatalf("error %v, want code %s", err, code)
	}
	if !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Errorf("error %v is not marked definite", err)
	}
	return coded
}

func TestImRemovePlan(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	img := dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100)
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		users   []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON)
		input   string
		code    errcode.Code // "" when the plan is accepted
		field   string
		detail  string // text the refusal's detail holds
		extra   []core.DiffLine
		confirm string
	}{
		{name: "unused", input: `{"image":"nginx:1.27"}`, confirm: "nginx:1.27"},
		{name: "stopped container uses it", users: []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON){imUses(img.ID, false)},
			input: `{"image":"nginx:1.27"}`, code: errcode.DockerInUse, detail: "web"},
		{name: "stopped container uses it, forced", users: []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON){imUses(img.ID, false)},
			input: `{"image":"nginx:1.27","force":true}`, confirm: "nginx:1.27",
			extra: []core.DiffLine{{Op: " ", Text: "stopped containers keep a reference to the deleted image: web"}}},
		{name: "running container uses it, forced", users: []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON){imUses(img.ID, true)},
			input: `{"image":"nginx:1.27","force":true}`, code: errcode.DockerInUse, detail: "web"},
		{name: "by id", input: `{"image":"` + img.ID + `"}`, confirm: img.ID},
		{name: "absent", input: `{"image":"ghost:1"}`, code: errcode.NotFound},
		{name: "empty", input: `{"image":""}`, code: errcode.InvalidInput, field: "/image"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			h.docker.putImage(img)
			if tt.users != nil {
				h.docker.put(dkContainer("web", tt.users...))
			}
			def := h.dk().imageRemove()
			out, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(tt.input))
			if tt.code != "" {
				coded := imRefused(t, err, tt.code)
				if tt.detail != "" && !strings.Contains(coded.Detail, tt.detail) {
					t.Errorf("detail %q does not name %q", coded.Detail, tt.detail)
				}
				if tt.field != "" && !slices.ContainsFunc(coded.Fields, func(f errcode.FieldError) bool { return f.Path == tt.field }) {
					t.Errorf("fields %v, want one at %s", coded.Fields, tt.field)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			want := append([]core.DiffLine{
				{Op: "-", Text: "image " + tt.confirm},
				{Op: " ", Text: "id " + img.ID},
				{Op: " ", Text: "size 100 bytes"},
			}, tt.extra...)
			if !slices.Equal(out.Diff, want) {
				t.Errorf("diff %v, want %v", out.Diff, want)
			}
			if out.Confirmation != tt.confirm {
				t.Errorf("confirmation %q, want %q", out.Confirmation, tt.confirm)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestImRemoveStateHash: the hash is stable while the image and the
// containers that use it are, and changes when a container starts using it.
func TestImRemoveStateHash(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	img := dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100)
	h.docker.putImage(img)
	def := h.dk().imageRemove()
	plan := func() string {
		t.Helper()
		out, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(`{"image":"nginx:1.27","force":true}`))
		if err != nil || out.StateHash == "" {
			t.Fatalf("plan: hash %q, error %v", out.StateHash, err)
		}
		return out.StateHash
	}
	first := plan()
	if again := plan(); again != first {
		t.Errorf("a second plan hashes %s, want %s", again, first)
	}
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("web", imUses(img.ID, false)))
	if used := plan(); used == first {
		t.Error("the hash did not change when a container began to use the image")
	}
}

func TestImRemoveApply(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	t.Run("removes and reports", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.putImage(dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100))
		k := h.dk()
		rec := &imRecorder{dockerAPI: k.d.docker, set: true, fixed: []dockerapi.ImageDeleteItem{{Untagged: "nginx:1.27"}, {Deleted: "sha256:aaa"}, {Deleted: "sha256:bbb"}}}
		k.d.docker = rec
		raw, err := k.imageRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"image":"nginx:1.27"}`))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if want := `{"untagged":["nginx:1.27"],"deleted":["sha256:aaa","sha256:bbb"]}`; string(raw) != want {
			t.Errorf("output %s, want %s", raw, want)
		}
		if !slices.Equal(rec.refs, []string{"nginx:1.27"}) || !slices.Equal(rec.opts, []dockerapi.RemoveImageOptions{{}}) {
			t.Errorf("RemoveImage called with %v %v, want the reference as given and no options", rec.refs, rec.opts)
		}
		if len(h.journal.effects()) != 0 {
			t.Error("an image removal journaled an effect; spec 3 has no comparator for images")
		}
	})
	t.Run("an empty answer reports empty lists", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.putImage(dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100))
		k := h.dk()
		k.d.docker = &imRecorder{dockerAPI: k.d.docker, set: true, fixed: []dockerapi.ImageDeleteItem{}}
		raw, err := k.imageRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"image":"nginx:1.27","force":true}`))
		if want := `{"untagged":[],"deleted":[]}`; err != nil || string(raw) != want {
			t.Errorf("output %s (%v), want %s", raw, err, want)
		}
	})
	t.Run("force is passed on", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.putImage(dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100))
		k := h.dk()
		rec := &imRecorder{dockerAPI: k.d.docker}
		k.d.docker = rec
		if _, err := k.imageRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"image":"nginx:1.27","force":true}`)); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !slices.Equal(rec.opts, []dockerapi.RemoveImageOptions{{Force: true}}) {
			t.Errorf("options %v, want force", rec.opts)
		}
	})
	t.Run("the daemon refuses", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.putImage(dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100))
		h.docker.fail("RemoveImage", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 409, Message: "conflict"})
		_, err := h.dk().imageRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"image":"nginx:1.27"}`))
		if err == nil || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Errorf("error %v, want a definite refusal", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("the daemon fails", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.putImage(dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100))
		h.docker.fail("RemoveImage", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 500, Message: "boom"})
		_, err := h.dk().imageRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"image":"nginx:1.27"}`))
		if err == nil || core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Errorf("error %v, want an uncertain failure", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("refused again at apply", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		img := dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100)
		h.docker.putImage(img)
		h.docker.put(dkContainer("web", imUses(img.ID, true)))
		k := h.dk()
		rec := &imRecorder{dockerAPI: k.d.docker}
		k.d.docker = rec
		_, err := k.imageRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"image":"nginx:1.27","force":true}`))
		_ = imRefused(t, err, errcode.DockerInUse)
		if len(rec.refs) != 0 {
			t.Error("RemoveImage was called")
		}
	})
}

func TestImRemoveVerify(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	h.docker.putImage(dkImage("nginx:1.27", 100))
	def := h.dk().imageRemove()
	in, out := json.RawMessage(`{"image":"nginx:1.27"}`), json.RawMessage(`{"untagged":[],"deleted":[]}`)
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), in, out); err == nil {
		t.Error("verify passed with the image still there")
	}
	if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), in); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), in, out); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("verify after the removal: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestImRemoveDefinition(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	def := h.dk().imageRemove()
	s := def.Spec
	if s.Name != "docker.image.remove" || s.Version != 1 || s.Class != core.ClassIrreversible || s.Side != core.SideAgent ||
		!slices.Equal(s.LockKeys, []string{"docker"}) {
		t.Errorf("spec %+v", s)
	}
	if _, err := core.NewRegistry(imModule{[]core.ActionDef{def}}); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("the registry refuses the action: %v", err)
	}
	imCheckInputs(t, def, map[string]string{
		`{"image":"nginx"}`: "", `{"image":"nginx","force":true}`: "", `{}`: "/image", `{"image":"nginx","x":1}`: "/x",
	})
}

// imCheckInputs validates each input against def's schema: field "" means
// accepted, otherwise the refusal names that field.
func imCheckInputs(t *testing.T, def core.ActionDef, inputs map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	v := schema.NewValidator()
	for input, field := range inputs {
		err := v.ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(input))
		var coded *errcode.Error
		switch {
		case field == "" && err != nil:
			t.Errorf("%s input %s: %v, want it accepted", def.Spec.Name, input, err)
		case field != "" && (!errors.As(err, &coded) || !slices.ContainsFunc(coded.Fields, func(f errcode.FieldError) bool { return f.Path == field })):
			t.Errorf("%s input %s: %v, want a refusal naming %s", def.Spec.Name, input, err, field)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
// imPruneHost holds two dangling images (one sharing 100 of its 300 bytes),
// a tagged image, and a dangling image a container uses. dangling lists the
// two prunable images in the order the plan shows them: by id.
type imPruneHost struct {
	*dkHost
	dangling []dockerapi.ImageSummary
	used     dockerapi.ImageSummary
}

func imPruneSetup(t *testing.T) *imPruneHost {
	t.Helper()
	h := &imPruneHost{dkHost: newDKHost(t)}
	old := dkImage("old", 300)
	old.RepoTags, old.SharedSize = nil, 100
	older := dkImage("older", 50)
	older.RepoTags = []string{"<none>:<none>"}
	tagged := dkImage("tagged:1", 999)
	h.used = dkImage("used", 70)
	h.used.RepoTags = nil
	h.dangling = []dockerapi.ImageSummary{old, older}
	slices.SortFunc(h.dangling, func(a, b dockerapi.ImageSummary) int { return strings.Compare(a.ID, b.ID) })
	// The daemon lists the larger id first, so the plan has to sort.
	for _, i := range []dockerapi.ImageSummary{h.dangling[1], tagged, h.used, h.dangling[0]} {
		h.docker.putImage(i)
	}
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("web", imUses(h.used.ID, false)))
	return h
}

func imSize(i dockerapi.ImageSummary) int64 { return i.Size - max(i.SharedSize, 0) }
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Both constructors return `core.DefineMutating` with `Version: 1`, `Class: core.ClassIrreversible`, `Side: core.SideAgent`, `LockKeys: []string{lockKey}`, a one-line `Summary`, no `ApplyTimeout`, and a handler with `Plan`, `Apply` and `Verify` but no `Inverse` and no `Observe`.

`image_remove.go`:

1. `imageCallError(kind, name string, err error) error` is the one place an image call's error is mapped: it returns `engineError(kind, name, err)`, wrapped in `core.Definite` when the error is a `*dockerapi.APIError` with a status from 400 to 499 (the daemon answered before changing anything), unchanged otherwise, and nil for nil. `image_prune.go` uses it too.
2. `imageUsers` holds the sorted names of the running containers, of the other containers, and the sorted ids of all containers that run one image; `(dk).imageUsersOf(ctx, imageID)` fills it from `ListContainers(All: true)` by comparing each summary's `ImageID` with the image id, taking the name from `Names[0]` without its leading `/`, and counting a summary as running when its `State` is `running`.
3. The handler's private `target(ctx, in)` serves Plan and Apply and returns the `dockerapi.ImageInspect` and the users, or a refusal wrapped in `core.Definite`, checked in this order: an empty `in.Image` is `request.invalid_input` with one `FieldError` at `/image`; `InspectImage(ctx, in.Image)` failing is `engineError("image", in.Image, err)` (absent: `not_found`); running containers using the image are `docker.in_use` with the detail `image <ref> is used by running containers: <names joined by ", ">`, even with `force` (the daemon cannot remove such an image); stopped containers using it without `in.Force` are `docker.in_use` with the detail `image <ref> is used by stopped containers: <names>; set force to remove it anyway`.
4. `Plan`: `Diff` is `{"-", "image <in.Image>"}`, `{" ", "id <the image id>"}`, `{" ", "size <Size> bytes"}`, then, only when stopped containers use it (so `force` is set), `{" ", "stopped containers keep a reference to the deleted image: <names joined by ", ">"}`. `Confirmation` is `in.Image` exactly as given. `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 of a JSON document holding the image id, its sorted `RepoTags` and the sorted ids of the containers using it, so a container that starts using the image after the plan changes it.
5. `Apply` calls `target` again, then `RemoveImage(ctx, in.Image, dockerapi.RemoveImageOptions{Force: in.Force})` (the reference as given, so removing one tag only untags), mapping its error with `imageCallError("image", in.Image, err)`. The output is `RemovedImage` with `Untagged` taken from the answer items' `Untagged` fields and `Deleted` from their `Deleted` fields, skipping empty ones, and both lists non-nil so they encode as `[]`.
6. `Verify`: `InspectImage(ctx, in.Image)` succeeding is `fmt.Errorf("docker: image %s still exists", in.Image)`, a not-found answer is success, any other error goes through `engineError`.

`image_prune.go`:

1. `imagePruneSize(i dockerapi.ImageSummary) int64` is the bytes removing the image alone reclaims: `Size` minus `SharedSize` when `SharedSize` is above zero (the daemon sends -1 when it did not compute it), else `Size`.
2. The handler's private `list(ctx)` returns the prunable images: `ListImages` with `SharedSize: true` and the filter `dangling=true`, minus every image any container uses (`ListContainers(All: true)`, comparing `ImageID`), minus every image that has a tag other than `<none>:<none>` (the module checks this itself, so a daemon that ignores the filter cannot make it remove a tagged image), sorted by id. Errors go through `engineError`.
3. `Plan`: one `{"-", "image <id> (<imagePruneSize> bytes)"}` line per image in that order, then `{" ", "reclaims <total> bytes from <n> images"}`; with no image the diff is the single line `{" ", "no unused dangling images to remove"}`. `Confirmation` is `prune`. `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 of one `<id> <size>` line per image, in order.
4. `Apply` computes `list` again and calls `RemoveImage(ctx, id, dockerapi.RemoveImageOptions{})` for each image in order. An image the daemon reports as not found is skipped; any other error stops the run and is returned through `imageCallError("image", id, err)` (the images removed so far stay removed). The output is `Pruned` with one `PrunedImage{ID, Tags, Size}` per removed image (`Tags` the image's `RepoTags` without `<none>:<none>`, never nil; `Size` from `imagePruneSize`), `Reclaimed` the sum of the sizes, and `Images` non-nil.
5. `Verify` inspects each id in `out.Images`: a present image is `fmt.Errorf("docker: image %s still exists", id)`, not found is success, other errors go through `engineError`. With the zero output (startup recovery) there is nothing to compare and it succeeds.

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"net/netip"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/docker/dstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

// obRecorder passes every call to the wrapped client and records what
// CreateNetwork and CreateVolume were asked for.
type obRecorder struct {
	dockerAPI
	networks []dockerapi.NetworkCreate
	volumes  []dockerapi.VolumeCreate
}

func (r *obRecorder) CreateNetwork(ctx context.Context, n dockerapi.NetworkCreate) (string, error) {
	r.networks = append(r.networks, n)
	return r.dockerAPI.CreateNetwork(ctx, n)
}

func (r *obRecorder) CreateVolume(ctx context.Context, v dockerapi.VolumeCreate) (dockerapi.Volume, error) {
	r.volumes = append(r.volumes, v)
	return r.dockerAPI.CreateVolume(ctx, v)
}

// obModule registers actions, so the registry's own checks run on them.
type obModule struct{ defs []core.ActionDef }

func (m obModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: ID, Version: 1, Actions: m.defs}
}

// obRefused asserts err is a definite refusal with the given code and returns it.
func obRefused(t *testing.T, err error, code errcode.Code) *errcode.Error {
	t.Helper()
	var coded *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != code {
		t.Fatalf("error %v, want code %s", err, code)
	}
	if !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Errorf("error %v is not marked definite", err)
	}
	return coded
}

// obHasField reports whether a refusal names the field path.
func obHasField(e *errcode.Error, path string) bool {
	return slices.ContainsFunc(e.Fields, func(f errcode.FieldError) bool { return f.Path == path })
}

// obCheckInputs validates each input against def's schema: field "" means
// accepted, otherwise the refusal names that field.
func obCheckInputs(t *testing.T, def core.ActionDef, inputs map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	v := schema.NewValidator()
	for input, field := range inputs {
		err := v.ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(input))
		var coded *errcode.Error
		switch {
		case field == "" && err != nil:
			t.Errorf("%s input %s: %v, want it accepted", def.Spec.Name, input, err)
		case field != "" && (!errors.As(err, &coded) || !obHasField(coded, field)):
			t.Errorf("%s input %s: %v, want a refusal naming %s", def.Spec.Name, input, err, field)
		}
	}
}

// obShared is a network that containers a and b are attached to.
func obShared(h *dkHost) dockerapi.Network {
	n := dkNetwork("shared")
	n.Containers = map[string]dockerapi.NetworkContainer{dkID("b"): {Name: "b"}, dkID("a"): {Name: "a"}}
	h.docker.putNetwork(n)
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("a", dkOnNetwork(n.ID)))
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("b", dkOnNetwork(n.ID)))
	return n
}

func TestObNetworkCreatePlan(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		input string
		field string // the field a refusal names; "" when the plan is accepted
		diff  []core.DiffLine
	}{
		{name: "defaults", input: `{"name":"web-net"}`, diff: []core.DiffLine{
			{Op: "+", Text: "network web-net"}, {Op: " ", Text: "driver bridge"},
		}},
		{name: "everything", input: `{"name":"app","internal":true,"attachable":true,"ipv6":true,"subnet":"10.9.0.0/24","gateway":"10.9.0.1","labels":{"team":"a","env":"x"}}`,
			diff: []core.DiffLine{
				{Op: "+", Text: "network app"}, {Op: " ", Text: "driver bridge"}, {Op: " ", Text: "internal"}, {Op: " ", Text: "attachable"},
				{Op: " ", Text: "IPv6 enabled"}, {Op: " ", Text: "subnet 10.9.0.0/24"}, {Op: " ", Text: "gateway 10.9.0.1"},
				{Op: " ", Text: "label env=x"}, {Op: " ", Text: "label team=a"},
			}},
		{name: "empty name", input: `{"name":""}`, field: "/name"},
		{name: "bad name", input: `{"name":"-x"}`, field: "/name"},
		{name: "name taken", input: `{"name":"taken"}`, field: "/name"},
		{name: "reserved label", input: `{"name":"a","labels":{"darkpanel.module":"npm"}}`, field: "/labels"},
		{name: "bad driver", input: `{"name":"a","driver":"Bad Driver"}`, field: "/driver"},
		{name: "not a prefix", input: `{"name":"a","subnet":"nope"}`, field: "/subnet"},
		{name: "host bits set", input: `{"name":"a","subnet":"10.9.0.5/24"}`, field: "/subnet"},
		{name: "IPv6 subnet without ipv6", input: `{"name":"a","subnet":"2001:db8::/64"}`, field: "/subnet"},
		{name: "gateway without subnet", input: `{"name":"a","gateway":"10.9.0.1"}`, field: "/gateway"},
		{name: "gateway outside the subnet", input: `{"name":"a","subnet":"10.9.0.0/24","gateway":"10.8.0.1"}`, field: "/gateway"},
		{name: "gateway not an address", input: `{"name":"a","subnet":"10.9.0.0/24","gateway":"gw"}`, field: "/gateway"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			h.docker.putNetwork(dkNetwork("taken"))
			out, err := h.dk().networkCreate().Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(tt.input))
			if tt.field != "" {
				if coded := obRefused(t, err, errcode.InvalidInput); !obHasField(coded, tt.field) {
					t.Errorf("fields %v, want one at %s", coded.Fields, tt.field)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !slices.Equal(out.Diff, tt.diff) {
				t.Errorf("diff %v, want %v", out.Diff, tt.diff)
			}
			if out.StateHash == "" || out.Confirmation != "" {
				t.Errorf("hash %q confirmation %q, want a hash and no confirmation", out.StateHash, out.Confirmation)
			}
			if slices.Contains(h.docker.calls(), "CreateNetwork") {
				t.Error("a plan created the network")
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestObNetworkCreateStateHash(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	def := h.dk().networkCreate()
	plan := func(input string) string {
		t.Helper()
		out, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(input))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return out.StateHash
	}
	first := plan(`{"name":"a"}`)
	if again := plan(`{"name":"a"}`); again != first {
		t.Errorf("a second plan hashes %s, want %s", again, first)
	}
	for _, other := range []string{`{"name":"b"}`, `{"name":"a","internal":true}`, `{"name":"a","labels":{"k":"v"}}`} {
		if plan(other) == first {
			t.Errorf("input %s hashes like the plain one", other)
		}
	}
}

func TestObNetworkCreateApply(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	t.Run("creates and journals", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		k := h.dk()
		rec := &obRecorder{dockerAPI: k.d.docker}
		k.d.docker = rec
		raw, err := k.networkCreate().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"),
			json.RawMessage(`{"name":"app","internal":true,"attachable":true,"ipv6":true,"subnet":"10.9.0.0/24","gateway":"10.9.0.1","labels":{"team":"a"}}`))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		yes := true
		want := dockerapi.NetworkCreate{Name: "app", Driver: "bridge", Internal: true, Attachable: true, EnableIPv6: &yes,
			IPAM:   &dockerapi.IPAM{Config: []dockerapi.IPAMConfig{{Subnet: netip.MustParsePrefix("10.9.0.0/24"), Gateway: netip.MustParseAddr("10.9.0.1")}}},
			Labels: map[string]string{"team": "a"}}
		if len(rec.networks) != 1 || !reflect.DeepEqual(rec.networks[0], want) {
			t.Fatalf("CreateNetwork requests %+v, want %+v", rec.networks, want)
		}
		made, err := h.docker.InspectNetwork(ctx, "app")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		var out Created
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &out); err != nil || out != (Created{ID: made.ID, Name: "app"}) {
			t.Errorf("output %s (%v), want id %s name app", raw, err, made.ID)
		}
		effects := h.journal.effects()
		if len(effects) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("%d effects, want 1", len(effects))
		}
		e := effects[0]
		wantPost, err := dstate.NetworkCreated(&made)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if e.Kind != core.EffectCreate || e.Resource != networkResource(made.ID) || e.State != core.EffectMade || e.Local || e.CommitWait != commitWait {
			t.Errorf("effect %+v, want a made non-local create of %s with commit wait %s", e, networkResource(made.ID), commitWait)
		}
		if e.Recovery == nil || *e.Recovery != (core.RecoveryID{Kind: "name", Value: "app"}) {
			t.Errorf("recovery %+v, want the name app", e.Recovery)
		}
		if string(e.Before.State) != "null" || e.Post == nil || string(e.Post.State) != string(wantPost) {
			t.Errorf("before %s post %+v, want null and %s", e.Before.State, e.Post, wantPost)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a name taken since the plan", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.putNetwork(dkNetwork("app"))
		_, err := h.dk().networkCreate().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"name":"app"}`))
		_ = obRefused(t, err, errcode.InvalidInput)
		if len(h.journal.effects()) != 0 {
			t.Error("a refused apply journaled an effect")
		}
	})
	t.Run("the daemon refuses", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.fail("CreateNetwork", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 400, Message: "invalid subnet"})
		_, err := h.dk().networkCreate().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"name":"app"}`))
		if err == nil || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Fatalf("error %v, want a definite refusal", err)
		}
		effects := h.journal.effects()
		if len(effects) != 1 || effects[0].State != core.EffectSkipped || effects[0].Resource != "docker.network:?app" {
			t.Errorf("effects %+v, want one skipped creation of docker.network:?app", effects)
		}
	})
	t.Run("the daemon fails", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		h.docker.fail("CreateNetwork", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 500, Message: "boom"})
		_, err := h.dk().networkCreate().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"name":"app"}`))
		if err == nil || core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Fatalf("error %v, want an uncertain failure", err)
		}
		if effects := h.journal.effects(); len(effects) != 1 || effects[0].State != core.EffectIntended {
			t.Errorf("effects %+v, want one left intended", effects)
		}
	})
}

// TestObNetworkCreateUndo: the inverse removes the network while it is
// unused, leaves it and refuses when a container joined, and succeeds
// when it is already gone; observation then reads absent.
func TestObNetworkCreateUndo(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	apply := func(t *testing.T, h *dkHost) (core.ActionDef, core.Effect) {
		t.Helper()
		def := h.dk().networkCreate()
		if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), json.RawMessage(`{"name":"app"}`)); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return def, h.journal.effects()[0]
	}
	t.Run("unused", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		def, e := apply(t, h)
		if _, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, h.env("c1"), e); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, err := h.docker.InspectNetwork(ctx, "app"); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
			t.Errorf("the network is still there: %v", err)
		}
		e.State = core.EffectUndone
		obs, err := def.Handler.Observe(ctx, h.env("c1"), e)
		if err != nil || string(obs.Current.State) != "null" {
			t.Errorf("observation %s (%v), want null", obs.Current.State, err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a container joined", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		def, e := apply(t, h)
		n, _ := h.docker.InspectNetwork(ctx, "app")
		h.docker.put(dkContainer("web", dkOnNetwork(n.ID)))
		_, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, h.env("c1"), e)
		if coded := obRefused(t, err, errcode.DockerInUse); !strings.Contains(coded.Detail, "web") {
			t.Errorf("detail %q does not name web", coded.Detail)
		}
		if _, err := h.docker.InspectNetwork(ctx, "app"); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("the network was removed: %v", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("already gone", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		def, e := apply(t, h)
		n, _ := h.docker.InspectNetwork(ctx, "app")
		if err := h.docker.RemoveNetwork(ctx, n.ID); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, h.env("c1"), e); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("inverse of an absent network: %v", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("the daemon refuses", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		def, e := apply(t, h)
		h.docker.fail("RemoveNetwork", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 409, Message: "in use"})
		if _, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, h.env("c1"), e); err == nil || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Errorf("error %v, want a definite refusal", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a resource that is not a created network", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		def := h.dk().networkCreate()
		if _, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, h.env("c1"), core.Effect{Resource: "docker.network:?app"}); err == nil {
			t.Error("inverse of an unnamed creation succeeded")
		}
	})
}

func TestObNetworkCreateVerify(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	def := h.dk().networkCreate()
	in := json.RawMessage(`{"name":"app"}`)
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), in, json.RawMessage(`{"id":"","name":""}`)); err == nil {
		t.Error("verify passed with no network")
	}
	raw, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), in)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), in, raw); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("verify with the output: %v", err)
	}
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("c1"), in, json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("verify without an output finds the network by name: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestObNetworkRemovePlan(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	old := dkNetwork("old")
	h.docker.putNetwork(old)
	owned := dkNetwork("npm-net")
	owned.Labels = map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"}
	h.docker.putNetwork(owned)
	bridge := dkNetwork("bridge")
	h.docker.putNetwork(bridge)
	shared := obShared(h)
	def := h.dk().networkRemove()
	plan := func(id string) (core.PlanOutcome, error) {
		return def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(`{"network":"`+id+`"}`))
	}

	out, err := plan(old.ID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	wantDiff := []core.DiffLine{{Op: "-", Text: "network old (" + old.ID[:12] + ")"}, {Op: " ", Text: "driver bridge"}}
	if !slices.Equal(out.Diff, wantDiff) || out.Confirmation != "old" || out.StateHash == "" {
		t.Errorf("plan %+v, want diff %v, confirmation old and a hash", out, wantDiff)
	}
	if _, err := plan(shared.ID); err == nil {
		t.Error("a network in use was planned")
	} else if coded := obRefused(t, err, errcode.DockerInUse); !strings.Contains(coded.Detail, "a, b") {
		t.Errorf("detail %q does not name the containers a, b in order", coded.Detail)
	}
	_, err = plan(owned.ID)
	_ = obRefused(t, err, errcode.DockerOwned)
	_, err = plan(bridge.ID)
	if coded := obRefused(t, err, errcode.InvalidInput); !obHasField(coded, "/network") {
		t.Errorf("fields %v, want one at /network", coded.Fields)
	}
	_, err = plan("ghost")
	_ = obRefused(t, err, errcode.NotFound)
	_, err = plan("")
	if coded := obRefused(t, err, errcode.InvalidInput); !obHasField(coded, "/network") {
		t.Errorf("fields %v, want one at /network", coded.Fields)
	}
	if slices.Contains(h.docker.calls(), "RemoveNetwork") {
		t.Error("a plan removed a network")
	}
	// A container that joins changes the document the hash covers.
	other := dkNetwork("other")
	h.docker.putNetwork(other)
	first, _ := plan(other.ID)
	other.Labels = map[string]string{"k": "v"}
	h.docker.putNetwork(other)
	if second, _ := plan(other.ID); second.StateHash == first.StateHash {
		t.Error("the hash did not change with the network's labels")
	}
}

func TestObNetworkRemoveApply(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	input := func(n dockerapi.Network) json.RawMessage { return json.RawMessage(`{"network":"` + n.ID + `"}`) }
	t.Run("removes and journals", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		old := dkNetwork("old")
		h.docker.putNetwork(old)
		raw, err := h.dk().networkRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), input(old))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		var out Removed
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &out); err != nil || out != (Removed{ID: old.ID, Name: "old"}) {
			t.Errorf("output %s (%v), want id %s name old", raw, err, old.ID)
		}
		if _, err := h.docker.InspectNetwork(ctx, old.ID); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
			t.Errorf("the network is still there: %v", err)
		}
		wantBefore, _ := dstate.NetworkCreated(&old)
		effects := h.journal.effects()
		if len(effects) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("%d effects, want 1", len(effects))
		}
		e := effects[0]
		if e.Kind != core.EffectDelete || e.Resource != networkResource(old.ID) || e.State != core.EffectMade || e.Local || e.CommitWait != commitWait ||
			string(e.Before.State) != string(wantBefore) || e.Post == nil || string(e.Post.State) != "null" {
			t.Errorf("effect %+v, want a made non-local delete from %s to null", e, wantBefore)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a container joined since the plan", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		shared := obShared(h)
		_, err := h.dk().networkRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), input(shared))
		_ = obRefused(t, err, errcode.DockerInUse)
		if len(h.journal.effects()) != 0 || slices.Contains(h.docker.calls(), "RemoveNetwork") {
			t.Error("a refused apply journaled an effect or called RemoveNetwork")
		}
	})
	t.Run("the daemon refuses", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		old := dkNetwork("old")
		h.docker.putNetwork(old)
		h.docker.fail("RemoveNetwork", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 403, Message: "forbidden"})
		_, err := h.dk().networkRemove().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), input(old))
		if err == nil || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Fatalf("error %v, want a definite refusal", err)
		}
		if effects := h.journal.effects(); len(effects) != 1 || effects[0].State != core.EffectSkipped {
			t.Errorf("effects %+v, want one skipped", effects)
		}
	})
	t.Run("the daemon fails, then settle observes", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		old := dkNetwork("old")
		h.docker.putNetwork(old)
		def := h.dk().networkRemove()
		h.docker.fail("RemoveNetwork", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 500, Message: "boom"})
		if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("c1"), input(old)); err == nil || core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Fatalf("error %v, want an uncertain failure", err)
		}
		e := h.journal.effects()[0]
		if e.State != core.EffectIntended {
			t.Fatalf("effect state %s, want intended", e.State)
		}
		if obs, err := def.Handler.Observe(ctx, h.env("c1"), e); err != nil || string(obs.Current.State) != string(e.Before.State) {
			t.Errorf("observation %s (%v), want the before-state %s", obs.Current.State, err, e.Before.State)
		}
		if err := h.docker.RemoveNetwork(ctx, old.ID); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if obs, err := def.Handler.Observe(ctx, h.env("c1"), e); err != nil || string(obs.Current.State) != "null" {
			t.Errorf("observation %s (%v), want null", obs.Current.State, err)
		}
```

```go
package docker

import (

// obMounts makes a container mount the named volumes.
func obMounts(names ...string) func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON) {
	return func(c *dockerapi.ContainerJSON) {
		for _, n := range names {
			c.Mounts = append(c.Mounts, dockerapi.MountPoint{Type: "volume", Name: n, Destination: "/" + n, RW: true})
		}
	}
}

func TestObVolumeCreatePlan(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		input string
		field string // the field a refusal names; "" when the plan is accepted
		diff  []core.DiffLine
	}{
		{name: "defaults", input: `{"name":"data"}`, diff: []core.DiffLine{{Op: "+", Text: "volume data"}, {Op: " ", Text: "driver local"}}},
		{name: "labels", input: `{"name":"data","driver":"local","labels":{"team":"a","env":"x"}}`, diff: []core.DiffLine{
			{Op: "+", Text: "volume data"}, {Op: " ", Text: "driver local"}, {Op: " ", Text: "label env=x"}, {Op: " ", Text: "label team=a"},
		}},
		{name: "empty name", input: `{"name":""}`, field: "/name"},
		{name: "bad name", input: `{"name":"a/b"}`, field: "/name"},
		{name: "name taken", input: `{"name":"taken"}`, field: "/name"},
		{name: "reserved label", input: `{"name":"data","labels":{"darkpanel.module":"npm"}}`, field: "/labels"},
		{name: "bad driver", input: `{"name":"data","driver":"Bad Driver"}`, field: "/driver"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			h.docker.putVolume(dkVolume("taken", nil))
			out, err := h.dk().volumeCreate().Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(tt.input))
			if tt.field != "" {
				if coded := obRefused(t, err, errcode.InvalidInput); !obHasField(coded, tt.field) {
					t.Errorf("fields %v, want one at %s", coded.Fields, tt.field)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !slices.Equal(out.Diff, tt.diff) || out.StateHash == "" || out.Confirmation != "" {
				t.Errorf("plan %+v, want diff %v, a hash and no confirmation", out, tt.diff)
			}

				t.Error("a plan created the volume")
			}
		})
	}
}

		if effects := h.journal.effects(); len(effects) != 1 || effects[0].State != core.EffectSkipped || effects[0].Resource != "docker.volume:?data" {

		}

	h.docker.putVolume(dkVolume("old", map[string]string{"k": "v"}))

		t.Error("the hash did not change with the volume's labels")
	}
```
