- [ ] **Step 2: Run tests to verify they fail**

Run: `mkdir -p /root/.cache/w3-tmp/30 && TMPDIR=/root/.cache/w3-tmp/30 GOTOOLCHAIN=local timeout 300 go test -count=1 -run 'TestOb' ./internal/modules/docker/`
Expected: FAIL to build with `h.dk().networkCreate undefined (type dk has no field or method networkCreate)` and the same for `networkRemove`, `volumeCreate` and `volumeRemove`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Common to the four constructors: `core.DefineMutating` with `Version: 1`, `Side: core.SideAgent`, `LockKeys: []string{lockKey}`, a one-line `Summary` and no `ApplyTimeout`. The create actions have `Class: core.ClassCompensable` and set neither `CompensatedBy` nor `ForwardOnly`, because their handler implements `Inverse` (the registry requires exactly one compensation mechanism); the remove actions have `Class: core.ClassIrreversible` and no `Inverse`. Every handler implements `Observe` as `k.observe(ctx, env, e)`. Handler types are `networkCreateHandler`, `networkRemoveHandler` (in `network_manage.go`), `volumeCreateHandler` and `volumeRemoveHandler` (in `volume_manage.go`), each `struct{ k dk }`. Every refusal below is wrapped in `core.Definite` and, unless it comes from `engineError` or `refuseOwned`, is an `*errcode.Error`.

Shared helpers (declared in `network_manage.go`, used by `volume_manage.go`):
- `manageNamePattern` is `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{0,127}$` and `manageDriverPattern` is `^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$`.
- `manageInvalid(path, msg string) error` returns the definite `request.invalid_input` refusal with that message as its detail and one `FieldError` at `path`.
- `manageLabels(labels)` refuses a map holding the key `core.LabelModule` with `manageInvalid("/labels", ...)`: module-owned objects carry that label and Darkpanel's own undo and remove refusals depend on it.
- `manageLabelLines(labels)` renders `{" ", "label <k>=<v>"}` lines with keys sorted.
- `manageHash(v any)` is the hex SHA-256 of `json.Marshal(v)`.
- `manageNetworkUsers(n dockerapi.Network)` is the sorted names in `n.Containers`; `(dk).manageVolumeUsers(ctx, name)` is the sorted names (from `Names[0]` without the leading `/`) of the containers in `ListContainers(All: true)` that have a mount of `Type == "volume"` and that `Name`, errors through `engineError`.

`docker.network.create` (`NetworkCreateInput` to `Created`):
1. A private `request(ctx, in)` builds the `dockerapi.NetworkCreate` and the diff for Plan and Apply, or refuses, checking in this order: the name against `manageNamePattern` (`/name`); labels (`manageLabels`); the driver, default `bridge`, against `manageDriverPattern` (`/driver`); the subnet, when given, parsed with `netip.ParsePrefix` and equal to its masked form, else `/subnet`, and an IPv6 subnet needs `in.IPv6` (`/subnet`); the gateway, when given, an address inside the subnet (`/gateway`, also when no subnet is given); a network of that exact name in `ListNetworks(ctx, dockerapi.Filters{"name": {in.Name}})` compared by exact `Name` (the daemon's filter matches substrings), refused as `/name` "network <name> already exists". The request carries `Name`, `Driver`, `Internal`, `Attachable`, `Labels` as given, `EnableIPv6` a pointer to true only when `in.IPv6`, and `IPAM` only when a subnet is given: one `IPAMConfig` with the `Subnet` and the `Gateway` (zero when none). It never adds `core.LabelModule`.
2. `Plan` returns the diff `{"+", "network <name>"}`, `{" ", "driver <driver>"}`, then `{" ", "internal"}`, `{" ", "attachable"}`, `{" ", "IPv6 enabled"}`, `{" ", "subnet <prefix>"}`, `{" ", "gateway <address>"}` each only when set, then the label lines; `StateHash` is `manageHash` of the request; no `Confirmation`.
3. `Apply` calls `request` again (a name taken since the plan is refused before any effect), builds the effect with `dockerEffect(core.EffectCreate, networkResource("?"+name), json.RawMessage("null"))` and sets `e.Recovery = &core.RecoveryID{Kind: "name", Value: name}` itself, so the recovery identity does not depend on how `dockerEffect` derives it. `k.run`'s `do` calls `CreateNetwork(ctx, request)` and returns `networkResource(id)` of the id it got, with the error through `engineError("network", name, err)`. The output is `Created{ID: id, Name: name}`.
4. `Inverse(ctx, env, e)` takes the id from `e.Resource` by cutting the prefix `docker.network:`; a resource without the prefix, with an empty id or an id starting `?` is a plain error. It inspects the network: not found returns `core.InverseResult{}` and nil (already absent is the state an undo wants); a network with containers is a definite `docker.in_use` refusal with the detail `network <name> is used by containers: <names joined by ", ">`; otherwise `RemoveNetwork(ctx, id)`, where success and not found return nil, any other 4xx `*dockerapi.APIError` is returned through `engineError` wrapped in `core.Definite`, and anything else through `engineError` unwrapped. The inverse does not use `k.run`: the engine journals the undo itself.
5. `Verify` inspects `out.ID`, or `in.Name` when `out.ID` is empty (startup recovery), through `InspectNetwork`; an error goes through `engineError`, and a network whose `Name` is not `in.Name` is `fmt.Errorf("docker: network %s is named %s, want %s", ...)`.

`docker.network.remove` (`NetworkInput` to `Removed`):
1. A private `target(ctx, in)` checks in this order: an empty `in.Network` is `/network` invalid input; `InspectNetwork(ctx, in.Network)` failing is `engineError("network", in.Network, err)`; the predefined networks `bridge`, `host` and `none` are `/network` invalid input ("network <name> is predefined and cannot be removed"); `refuseOwned("network", n.Name, n.Labels)`; a network with containers is the `docker.in_use` refusal above.
2. `Plan`: diff `{"-", "network <name> (<first 12 characters of the id>)"}`, `{" ", "driver <driver>"}`; `Confirmation` the network name; `StateHash` is `manageHash` of `dstate.NetworkCreated(&n)`.
3. `Apply` calls `target` again, uses `dstate.NetworkCreated(&n)` as the before-state of `dockerEffect(core.EffectDelete, networkResource(n.ID), before)`, and `k.run`'s `do` calls `RemoveNetwork(ctx, n.ID)` and returns `networkResource(n.ID)`, errors through `engineError`. The output is `Removed{ID: n.ID, Name: n.Name}`.
4. `Verify` inspects `out.ID`, or `in.Network` when empty: present is `fmt.Errorf("docker: network %s still exists", ref)`, not found is success.

`docker.volume.create` (`VolumeCreateInput` to `Created`): as `network.create`, with these differences.
1. `request` checks the name (`/name`), labels, the driver (default `local`, `/driver`), and then `InspectVolume(ctx, in.Name)`: success is `/name` "volume <name> already exists" (the daemon's create returns an existing volume unchanged, and an undo would then remove a volume this change did not create), not found proceeds, any other error goes through `engineError`. The request is `dockerapi.VolumeCreate{Name, Driver, Labels}`.
2. `Plan` diff: `{"+", "volume <name>"}`, `{" ", "driver <driver>"}`, then the label lines; `StateHash` is `manageHash` of the request.
3. `Apply`: effect `dockerEffect(core.EffectCreate, volumeResource("?"+name), json.RawMessage("null"))` with `Recovery` `{Kind: "name", Value: name}`; `do` calls `CreateVolume` and returns `volumeResource(v.Name)`. The output is `Created{ID: name, Name: name}`.
4. `Inverse`: the name comes from `e.Resource` by cutting `docker.volume:` (same plain-error cases); an absent volume returns nil; a volume with users (`manageVolumeUsers`) is the definite `docker.in_use` refusal "volume <name> is used by containers: <names>"; otherwise `RemoveVolume(ctx, name, false)` with the same error mapping as the network inverse.
5. `Verify` inspects `in.Name`; an error (absent included) goes through `engineError`.

`docker.volume.remove` (`VolumeInput` to `Removed`): `target` checks an empty `in.Volume` (`/volume`), `InspectVolume` through `engineError`, `refuseOwned("volume", v.Name, v.Labels)`, then users (`docker.in_use` as above). `Plan`: diff `{"-", "volume <name>"}`, `{" ", "the data in the volume is deleted and cannot be restored"}`; `Confirmation` the name; `StateHash` is `manageHash` of `dstate.VolumeCreated(&v, true)`. `Apply`: `target` again, effect `dockerEffect(core.EffectDelete, volumeResource(v.Name), <VolumeCreated(&v, true)>)`, `do` calls `RemoveVolume(ctx, v.Name, false)` (never forced: a forced removal ignores a missing volume and hides a conflict) and returns `volumeResource(v.Name)`; the output is `Removed{ID: v.Name, Name: v.Name}`. `Verify` inspects `in.Volume`: present is an error, not found is success.

The two actions toggle one effect, the endpoint of a container on a network (`docker.endpoint:<container id>@<network id>`, kind modify). The journaled `Before` is the state an undo restores (`dstate.Restored`), so an undo of a disconnect reconnects with the aliases and static addresses the endpoint had, and an undo of a connect disconnects. The engine journals, observes and compares; this task writes only the calls, the checks and the two `Inverse` methods. Tests drive a real agent engine over the fake Engine, because undo is only meaningful with the engine's journal and comparison.

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"net/netip"
	"path/filepath"
	"reflect"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/lifecycle"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/store"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/docker/dstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

var epUser = core.Principal{Actor: "user:u1", UserID: "u1", Scope: core.ScopeOperate, Source: "203.0.113.7"}

// epModule registers only the two actions under test.
type epModule struct{ k dk }

func (m epModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: ID, Version: 1, DefaultEnabled: true,
		Actions: []core.ActionDef{m.k.networkConnect(), m.k.networkDisconnect()}}
}

type epConnectCall struct {
	Network, Container string
	Endpoint           *dockerapi.EndpointSettings
}

type epDisconnectCall struct {
	Network, Container string
	Force              bool
}

// epDocker records the arguments of the two calls under test and makes the
// stored endpoint carry the aliases and static addresses it was given, so
// the tests do not depend on how the fake copies endpoint settings.
type epDocker struct {
	*fakeDocker
	mu          sync.Mutex
	connects    []epConnectCall
	disconnects []epDisconnectCall
}

func (d *epDocker) ConnectNetwork(ctx context.Context, network, container string, ep *dockerapi.EndpointSettings) error {
	d.mu.Lock()
	d.connects = append(d.connects, epConnectCall{network, container, ep})
	d.mu.Unlock()
	if err := d.fakeDocker.ConnectNetwork(ctx, network, container, ep); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if c, ok := d.container(container); ok && ep != nil {
		for _, e := range c.NetworkSettings.Networks {
			if e != nil && e.NetworkID == network {
				e.Aliases, e.IPAMConfig = ep.Aliases, ep.IPAMConfig
			}
		}
		d.put(c)
	}
	return nil
}

func (d *epDocker) DisconnectNetwork(ctx context.Context, network, container string, force bool) error {
	d.mu.Lock()
	d.disconnects = append(d.disconnects, epDisconnectCall{network, container, force})
	d.mu.Unlock()
	return d.fakeDocker.DisconnectNetwork(ctx, network, container, force)
}

// epSeed gives the container's endpoint on networkID the aliases, a static
// IPv4 address and an endpoint id.
func epSeed(t *testing.T, c dockerapi.ContainerJSON, networkID string, aliases []string, ipv4 string) dockerapi.ContainerJSON {
	t.Helper()
	found := false
	for _, ep := range c.NetworkSettings.Networks {
		if ep == nil || ep.NetworkID != networkID {
			continue
		}
		ep.EndpointID, ep.Aliases = "seeded-endpoint", aliases
		ep.IPAMConfig = &dockerapi.EndpointIPAMConfig{IPv4Address: netip.MustParseAddr(ipv4)}
		found = true
	}
	if !found {
		t.Fatalf("container %s has no endpoint on network %s", c.Name, networkID)
	}
	return c
}

func epDB(t *testing.T) *store.DB {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	db, err := store.Open(ctx, filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "agent.db"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = db.Close() })
	set, err := store.CoreMigrations(store.SideAgent)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	res, err := store.Migrate(ctx, db, store.MigrateOptions{
		Side: store.SideAgent, BinaryVersion: "test", BackupRoot: filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "backups"),
		Keep: 5, Now: time.Now(),
	}, set, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(res.Failed) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("core migrations failed: %v", res.Failed[0].Err)
	}
	return db
}

type epFixture struct {
	t   *testing.T
	rec *epDocker
	eng *lifecycle.Engine
}

// newEPFixture is an agent engine serving the two actions over a fake
// Engine that holds ctr and nw.
func newEPFixture(t *testing.T, ctr dockerapi.ContainerJSON, nw dockerapi.Network) *epFixture {
	t.Helper()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	h.docker.put(ctr)
	h.docker.putNetwork(nw)
	rec := &epDocker{fakeDocker: h.docker}
	k := h.dk()
	k.d.docker = rec
	reg, err := core.NewRegistry(epModule{k: k})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	eng, err := lifecycle.New(lifecycle.Config{
		Side: core.SideAgent, Registry: reg, Validator: schema.NewValidator(), Journal: &coretest.MemJournal{}, Redact: schema.Redact,
		Base: core.Env{HostID: "h1", DB: epDB(t), Sealer: coretest.Sealer{}, Clock: h.clock, Log: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil))},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(eng.Close)
	return &epFixture{t: t, rec: rec, eng: eng}
}

func (f *epFixture) plan(action, input string) (core.PlanView, error) {
	f.t.Helper()
	return f.eng.Plan(context.Background(), epUser, core.ActionRef{Name: action, Version: 1}, json.RawMessage(input), core.PlanOptions{})
}

// apply plans and applies action, failing the test when the plan is refused.
func (f *epFixture) apply(action, input string) (core.ChangeView, error) {
	f.t.Helper()
	pv, err := f.plan(action, input)
	if err != nil {
		f.t.Fatalf("plan %s: %v", action, err)
	}
	return f.eng.Apply(context.Background(), epUser, pv.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
}

// undo undoes change id and waits until the undo has settled.
func (f *epFixture) undo(id string) core.ChangeView {
	f.t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, err := f.eng.Undo(ctx, epUser, id, nil); err != nil {
		f.t.Fatalf("undo %s: %v", id, err)
	}
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for {
		v, err := f.eng.Change(ctx, id)
		if err != nil {
			f.t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if v.State != core.StateUndoing {
			return v
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			f.t.Fatalf("change %s is still undoing", id)
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

func (f *epFixture) effects(id string) []core.EffectView {
	f.t.Helper()
	effs, err := f.eng.Effects(context.Background(), id)
	if err != nil {
		f.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return effs
}

// endpoint is the container's endpoint on the network, as the fake holds it.
func (f *epFixture) endpoint(containerID, networkID string) (dockerapi.EndpointSettings, bool) {
	f.t.Helper()
	c, ok := f.rec.container(containerID)
	if !ok {
		f.t.Fatalf("the fake has no container %s", containerID)
	}
	for _, ep := range c.NetworkSettings.Networks {
		if ep != nil && ep.NetworkID == networkID {
			return *ep, true
		}
	}
	return dockerapi.EndpointSettings{}, false
}

func epJSONEqual(t *testing.T, what string, got, want json.RawMessage) {
	t.Helper()
	var g, w any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(got, &g); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %s is not JSON: %v", what, got, err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(want, &w); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(g, w) {
		t.Errorf("%s = %s, want %s", what, got, want)
	}
}

func epWantRefusal(t *testing.T, err error, code errcode.Code, path, part string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("no error, want %s", code)
	}
	e := errcode.From(err)
	if e.Code != code {
		t.Fatalf("error = %v, want code %s", err, code)
	}
	if path != "" && (len(e.Fields) == 0 || e.Fields[0].Path != path) {
		t.Errorf("fields %+v, want the first at %s", e.Fields, path)
	}
	if part != "" && !strings.Contains(e.Detail, part) {
		t.Errorf("detail %q does not contain %q", e.Detail, part)
	}
}

func epInput(network, container, extra string) string {
	if extra != "" {
		extra = "," + extra
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf(`{"network":%q,"container":%q%s}`, network, container, extra)
}

func TestEPConnectAppliesAndUndoes(t *testing.T) {
	web, backend := dkContainer("web", dkRunning), dkNetwork("backend")
	f := newEPFixture(t, web, backend)
	in := epInput(backend.ID, "web", `"aliases":["api"],"ipv4":"172.20.0.9"`)

	pv, err := f.plan("docker.network.connect", in)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	wantDiff := []core.DiffLine{
		{Op: "+", Text: "container web joins network backend"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "alias api"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "ipv4 172.20.0.9"},
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(pv.Diff, wantDiff) {
		t.Errorf("diff %+v, want %+v", pv.Diff, wantDiff)
	}
	if len(f.rec.connects) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("planning connected the container: %+v", f.rec.connects)
	}

	cv, err := f.eng.Apply(context.Background(), epUser, pv.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
	if err != nil || cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("apply = %+v, %v; want a completed change", cv, err)
	}
	ep, on := f.endpoint(web.ID, backend.ID)
	if !on || ep.EndpointID == "" {
		t.Fatalf("endpoint %+v (on %v), want the container on the network", ep, on)
	}
	if len(f.rec.connects) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("connect calls %+v, want one", f.rec.connects)
	}
	got := f.rec.connects[0]
	if got.Network != backend.ID || got.Container != web.ID || got.Endpoint == nil ||
		!reflect.DeepEqual(got.Endpoint.Aliases, []string{"api"}) || got.Endpoint.IPAMConfig == nil ||
		got.Endpoint.IPAMConfig.IPv4Address != netip.MustParseAddr("172.20.0.9") || got.Endpoint.IPAMConfig.IPv6Address.IsValid() {
		t.Errorf("connect call %+v (endpoint %+v), want the ids, alias api and static address 172.20.0.9", got, got.Endpoint)
	}
	var view EndpointView
	if err := json.Unmarshal(cv.Output, &view); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	wantView := EndpointView{Network: "backend", NetworkID: backend.ID, Container: "web", EndpointID: ep.EndpointID, Aliases: []string{"api"}, IPv4: "172.20.0.9"}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(view, wantView) {
		t.Errorf("output %+v, want %+v", view, wantView)
	}

	effs := f.effects(cv.ID)
	if len(effs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("effects %+v, want one", effs)
	}
	e := effs[0]
	if e.Resource != endpointResource(web.ID, backend.ID) || e.Kind != core.EffectModify || e.State != core.EffectMade || e.Local {
		t.Errorf("effect %+v, want a made, non-local modify of the endpoint", e)
	}
	wantBefore, err := dstate.Endpoint(web.ID, backend.ID, nil, dstate.Restored)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	wantPost, err := dstate.Endpoint(web.ID, backend.ID, &ep, dstate.Recorded)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	epJSONEqual(t, "before", e.Before.State, wantBefore)
	if e.Post == nil {
		t.Fatal("the effect has no post state")
	}
	epJSONEqual(t, "post", e.Post.State, wantPost)

	uv := f.undo(cv.ID)
	if uv.State != core.StateReverted {
		t.Fatalf("undo settled %s (%+v), want reverted", uv.State, uv.Error)
	}
	if _, on := f.endpoint(web.ID, backend.ID); on {
		t.Error("the container is still on the network after the undo")
	}
	if want := []epDisconnectCall{{backend.ID, web.ID, false}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(f.rec.disconnects, want) {
		t.Errorf("disconnect calls %+v, want %+v", f.rec.disconnects, want)
	}
	if s := f.effects(cv.ID)[0].State; s != core.EffectUndone {
		t.Errorf("effect is %s after the undo, want undone", s)
	}
}

func TestEPConnectRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	backend := dkNetwork("backend")
	ownedNet := dkNetwork("backend", func(n *dockerapi.Network) { n.Labels = map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"} })
	web := dkContainer("web", dkRunning)
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		ctr   dockerapi.ContainerJSON
		net   dockerapi.Network
		input string
		code  errcode.Code
		path  string
		part  string
	}{
		{"empty container", web, backend, epInput(backend.ID, "", ""), errcode.InvalidInput, "/container", ""},
		{"empty network", web, backend, epInput("", "web", ""), errcode.InvalidInput, "/network", ""},
		{"unparsable ipv4", web, backend, epInput(backend.ID, "web", `"ipv4":"nope"`), errcode.InvalidInput, "/ipv4", ""},
		{"ipv6 in ipv4", web, backend, epInput(backend.ID, "web", `"ipv4":"fd00::1"`), errcode.InvalidInput, "/ipv4", ""},
		{"ipv4 in ipv6", web, backend, epInput(backend.ID, "web", `"ipv6":"10.0.0.1"`), errcode.InvalidInput, "/ipv6", ""},
		{"bad alias", web, backend, epInput(backend.ID, "web", `"aliases":["ok","bad alias"]`), errcode.InvalidInput, "/aliases/1", ""},
		{"unknown container", web, backend, epInput(backend.ID, "ghost", ""), errcode.NotFound, "", "ghost"},
		{"unknown network", web, backend, epInput("ghost", "web", ""), errcode.NotFound, "", "ghost"},
		{"owned container", dkContainer("web", dkLabels(map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"})), backend, epInput(backend.ID, "web", ""), errcode.DockerOwned, "", "container web belongs to module npm"},
		{"owned network", web, ownedNet, epInput(ownedNet.ID, "web", ""), errcode.DockerOwned, "", "network backend belongs to module npm"},
		{"already connected", dkContainer("web", dkRunning, dkOnNetwork(backend.ID)), backend, epInput(backend.ID, "web", ""), errcode.InvalidInput, "", "already connected"},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newEPFixture(t, tc.ctr, tc.net)
			_, err := f.plan("docker.network.connect", tc.input)
			epWantRefusal(t, err, tc.code, tc.path, tc.part)
			if len(f.rec.connects) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("connect calls %+v, want none", f.rec.connects)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestEPDisconnectAppliesAndUndoes(t *testing.T) {
	for _, force := range []bool{false, true} {
		t.Run("force="+strconv.FormatBool(force), func(t *testing.T) {
			backend := dkNetwork("backend")
			web := epSeed(t, dkContainer("web", dkRunning, dkOnNetwork(backend.ID)), backend.ID, []string{"web", "api"}, "172.20.0.9")
			f := newEPFixture(t, web, backend)
			seeded, _ := f.endpoint(web.ID, backend.ID)
			in := epInput(backend.ID, "web", "")
			if force {
				in = epInput(backend.ID, "web", `"force":true`)
			}

			pv, err := f.plan("docker.network.disconnect", in)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			wantDiff := []core.DiffLine{
				{Op: "-", Text: "container web leaves network backend"},
				{Op: "-", Text: "alias api"},
				{Op: "-", Text: "alias web"},
				{Op: "-", Text: "ipv4 172.20.0.9"},
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(pv.Diff, wantDiff) {
				t.Errorf("diff %+v, want %+v", pv.Diff, wantDiff)
			}

			cv, err := f.eng.Apply(context.Background(), epUser, pv.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
			if err != nil || cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
				t.Fatalf("apply = %+v, %v; want a completed change", cv, err)
			}
			if _, on := f.endpoint(web.ID, backend.ID); on {
				t.Fatal("the container is still on the network")
			}
			if want := []epDisconnectCall{{backend.ID, web.ID, force}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(f.rec.disconnects, want) {
				t.Errorf("disconnect calls %+v, want %+v", f.rec.disconnects, want)
			}
			var view EndpointView
			if err := json.Unmarshal(cv.Output, &view); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			wantView := EndpointView{Network: "backend", NetworkID: backend.ID, Container: "web", EndpointID: "seeded-endpoint", Aliases: []string{"api", "web"}, IPv4: "172.20.0.9"}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(view, wantView) {
				t.Errorf("output %+v, want the detached endpoint %+v", view, wantView)
			}

			e := f.effects(cv.ID)[0]
			wantBefore, err := dstate.Endpoint(web.ID, backend.ID, &seeded, dstate.Restored)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			wantPost, err := dstate.Endpoint(web.ID, backend.ID, nil, dstate.Recorded)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			epJSONEqual(t, "before", e.Before.State, wantBefore)
			if e.Post == nil {
				t.Fatal("the effect has no post state")
			}
			epJSONEqual(t, "post", e.Post.State, wantPost)

			uv := f.undo(cv.ID)
			if uv.State != core.StateReverted {
				t.Fatalf("undo settled %s (%+v), want reverted", uv.State, uv.Error)
			}
			if _, on := f.endpoint(web.ID, backend.ID); !on {
				t.Error("the container is not back on the network after the undo")
			}
			if len(f.rec.connects) != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("connect calls %+v, want the one reconnect", f.rec.connects)
			}
			re := f.rec.connects[0]
			if re.Network != backend.ID || re.Container != web.ID || re.Endpoint == nil ||
				!reflect.DeepEqual(re.Endpoint.Aliases, []string{"api", "web"}) || re.Endpoint.IPAMConfig == nil ||
				re.Endpoint.IPAMConfig.IPv4Address != netip.MustParseAddr("172.20.0.9") {
				t.Errorf("reconnect %+v (endpoint %+v), want the journaled aliases and static address", re, re.Endpoint)
			}
			if s := f.effects(cv.ID)[0].State; s != core.EffectUndone {
				t.Errorf("effect is %s after the undo, want undone", s)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestEPApplyRefusedByTheDaemon(t *testing.T) {
	backend := dkNetwork("backend")
	tests := []struct {
		name, action, method string
		ctr                  dockerapi.ContainerJSON
		connected            bool
	}{
		{"connect", "docker.network.connect", "ConnectNetwork", dkContainer("web", dkRunning), false},
		{"disconnect", "docker.network.disconnect", "DisconnectNetwork", dkContainer("web", dkRunning, dkOnNetwork(backend.ID)), true},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newEPFixture(t, tc.ctr, backend)
			f.rec.fail(tc.method, &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 403, Message: "refused"})
			cv, err := f.apply(tc.action, epInput(backend.ID, "web", ""))
			if cv.State != core.StateFailed {
				t.Fatalf("apply = %+v, %v; want a failed change", cv, err)
			}
			if _, on := f.endpoint(tc.ctr.ID, backend.ID); on != tc.connected {
				t.Errorf("container on the network = %v, want it unchanged (%v)", on, tc.connected)
			}
			effs := f.effects(cv.ID)
			if len(effs) != 1 || effs[0].State != core.EffectSkipped {
				t.Errorf("effects %+v, want one skipped effect: the daemon refused before changing anything", effs)
			}
		})
	}
}

	ctx := context.Background()

	f := newEPFixture(t, web, backend)

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `internal/modules/docker/network_connect.go`. Declare no top-level identifier whose name does not start with `endpoint`, `connect` or `disconnect`, apart from `networkConnect` and `networkDisconnect`: other Docker tasks share the package. Error strings start with `docker:` unless they are client-safe `*errcode.Error` details.

1. **Declarations.** `networkConnect` returns `core.DefineMutating[ConnectInput, EndpointView]` and `networkDisconnect` returns `core.DefineMutating[DisconnectInput, EndpointView]`, each with an `ActionSpec` of `Name` (`docker.network.connect`, `docker.network.disconnect`), a one-sentence `Summary`, `Version` 1, `Class` `core.ClassCompensable`, `Side` `core.SideAgent` and `LockKeys` `[]string{lockKey}`. No `CompensatedBy`, `Guards`, `Converges` or `ApplyTimeout`: the `Undoer` is the single compensation mechanism. The handlers are two struct types holding the `dk`, each with `Plan`, `Apply`, `Verify`, `Observe` and `Inverse` methods; `Observe` is `k.observe(ctx, env, e)` unchanged.

2. **Resolving the target** (one shared method of `dk`, used by Plan, Apply and Verify of both actions). Given the input's container and network strings, in this order: an empty container is a `request.invalid_input` refusal with the field `/container`, an empty network one with `/network` (both `*errcode.Error` with a `Fields` entry, wrapped in `core.Definite`); `InspectContainer` and `InspectNetwork` of the strings as given, each failure passed through `engineError("container", name, err)` or `engineError("network", name, err)`; `refuseOwned("container", <name without Docker's leading "/">, <the container's Config.Labels>)` and `refuseOwned("network", <network name>, <network Labels>)`. The endpoint is the entry of `NetworkSettings.Networks` whose `NetworkID` equals the inspected network's `ID` (match on the id, never on the map key); none means the container is not on the network. The result holds the container, the network, the container's display name and the endpoint pointer (nil when absent). Every later call to the Engine passes the resolved container id and network id, never the input strings.

3. **Connect input checks, before any Engine call** (all `request.invalid_input` with a `Fields` entry, `core.Definite`): each alias must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,62}$` (field `/aliases/<index>`); `ipv4`, when given, must parse with `netip.ParseAddr` and be IPv4 (field `/ipv4`); `ipv6`, when given, must parse, be IPv6 and not an IPv4-mapped address (field `/ipv6`). Then resolve; a container already on the network is refused with `request.invalid_input` (`core.Definite`, no field) and the detail `container <name> is already connected to network <network name>`. The endpoint settings sent to the Engine are nil when there is no alias and no address, otherwise `dockerapi.EndpointSettings{Aliases: <as given>}` with an `IPAMConfig` holding the given addresses (nil `IPAMConfig` when none is given).

4. **Disconnect checks.** Resolve; a container not on the network is refused with `request.invalid_input` (`core.Definite`, no field) and the detail `container <name> is not connected to network <network name>`. `DisconnectInput.Force` is passed to `DisconnectNetwork` as given.

5. **Plan** returns `core.PlanOutcome` with `Guards` an empty slice and these diff lines, the operation first.
   - Connect: `{"+", "container <name> joins network <network name>"}`, then one `{"+", "alias <alias>"}` per alias in input order, then `{"+", "ipv4 <canonical address>"}` and `{"+", "ipv6 <canonical address>"}` for the addresses given.
   - Disconnect: `{"-", "container <name> leaves network <network name>"}`, then one `{"-", "alias <alias>"}` per alias of the current endpoint in sorted order, then `{"-", "ipv4 <address>"}` and `{"-", "ipv6 <address>"}` for the endpoint's static `IPAMConfig` addresses.
   - `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 of the container id, the network id and `string(dstate.Endpoint(containerID, networkID, <current endpoint or nil>, dstate.Recorded))`, joined by `"\n"`. It therefore changes when the endpoint appears, disappears or is renewed (new `EndpointID`, other aliases) between plan and apply.

6. **Apply** repeats the checks of steps 3 or 4 (a refusal there changes nothing and is `core.Definite`), then builds the effect with `dockerEffect(core.EffectModify, endpointResource(containerID, networkID), <the Restored document of the current endpoint, nil for a connect>)` and runs the call through `k.run`: the `do` function calls `ConnectNetwork(ctx, networkID, containerID, settings)` or `DisconnectNetwork(ctx, networkID, containerID, force)` and returns the effect's resource with the Engine error exactly as the client returned it (do not map it first: `run` classifies a daemon refusal by its HTTP status). After `run` succeeds, Apply resolves the target again and returns the `EndpointView`: for a connect the new endpoint, for a disconnect the endpoint as it was before the call, with `Network` and `Container` the names, `NetworkID`, `EndpointID`, `Aliases` sorted, `IPv4` the static `IPAMConfig` address when set and otherwise the endpoint's `IPAddress`, and `IPv6` likewise from `IPAMConfig` and then `GlobalIPv6Address`.

7. **Verify** is read-only and ignores its output argument (recovery passes a zero one): it resolves the target again and fails with a `docker:` error when a connected container is not on the network, or a disconnected one still is.

8. **Inverse** acts only from `e.Before.State`, never from the input. Decode its members `container`, `network`, `present`, `aliases` and `ipamConfig` (`ipv4`, `ipv6`) as Contracts "dstate" defines them.
   - Connect: call `DisconnectNetwork(ctx, network, container, false)`.
   - Disconnect: require `present` true, then call `ConnectNetwork(ctx, network, container, settings)` with the journaled aliases and static addresses (nil settings when it had neither).
   - A document that lacks the container or network id (or, for a disconnect, `present`) is a `core.Definite` `docker:` error. A `*dockerapi.APIError` with a 4xx status from the Engine is returned wrapped in `core.Definite`, since the daemon refused before changing anything; any other error is returned as it is. The result is `core.InverseResult{}`: the endpoint's identity is stable, so nothing is recreated under a new name.

The `apRaw` tests register Cloudflare's documented v4 answers on a bare `cloudfake` server and pin the requests the client makes; `TestAPAgainstTheFake*` run the same client against Task 18's fake and so also check that the two agree. `cfWith` sets `baseURL` to `srv.URL()`; if the merged fake serves its paths under a prefix, append that prefix in `cfWith` only.

```go
package cloudflare

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/cloud"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/cloud/cloudfake"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/cloudflare/fake"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/cloudflare/ingress"
)

func apNoSleep(context.Context, time.Duration) error { return nil }

// cfWith is the module's dependencies pointed at the fake server, with
// retries that do not wait.
func cfWith(srv *fake.Server) cf {
	return cf{d: deps{baseURL: srv.URL(), http: srv.Client(), sleep: apNoSleep}}
}

var apClock = coretest.NewFakeClock(time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))

const apAccount = "acct1"

// apRaw is a bare cloudfake server and an api over it; the tests register
// the provider's answers they need.
func apRaw(t *testing.T) (*cloudfake.Server, *api) {
	t.Helper()
	srv := cloudfake.New(t)
	a, err := cf{d: deps{baseURL: srv.URL(), http: srv.Client(), sleep: apNoSleep}}.newAPI(apAccount, []byte("tok"), apClock)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return srv, a
}

// apReply writes Cloudflare's envelope around result.
func apReply(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, success bool, code int, result any) {
	errs := []map[string]any{}
	if !success {
		errs = append(errs, map[string]any{"code": code, "message": "failed"})
	}
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]any{"success": success, "errors": errs, "messages": []any{}, "result": result})
}

func apOK(result any) http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) { apReply(w, 200, true, 0, result) }
}

func apQuery(t *testing.T, r cloudfake.Request) url.Values {
	t.Helper()
	q, err := url.ParseQuery(r.RawQuery)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return q
}

func apCount(srv *cloudfake.Server, method string) int {
	n := 0
	for _, r := range srv.Requests() {
		if r.Method == method {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

func apWantCode(t *testing.T, err error, code errcode.Code) *errcode.Error {
	t.Helper()
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("no error, want %s", code)
	}
	e := errcode.From(err)
	if e.Code != code {
		t.Fatalf("error = %v, want code %s", err, code)
	}
	return e
}

func TestAPRequestsCarryTheTokenAndTheAccountPath(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apRaw(t)
	srv.Handle(http.MethodGet, "/accounts/"+apAccount+"/cfd_tunnel", apOK([]any{}))
	if _, err := a.Tunnels(context.Background(), ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := a.Tunnels(context.Background(), "darkpanel-c1"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	reqs := srv.Requests()
	if len(reqs) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("%d requests, want one per call", len(reqs))
	}
	if got := reqs[0].Header.Get("Authorization"); got != "Bearer tok" {
		t.Errorf("Authorization %q, want Bearer tok", got)
	}
	if got := reqs[0].Header.Get("Accept"); !strings.Contains(got, "application/json") {
		t.Errorf("Accept %q, want JSON", got)
	}
	first, second := apQuery(t, reqs[0]), apQuery(t, reqs[1])
	if first.Get("is_deleted") != "false" || first.Has("name") {
		t.Errorf("first query %v, want is_deleted=false and no name", first)
	}
	if second.Get("is_deleted") != "false" || second.Get("name") != "darkpanel-c1" {
		t.Errorf("second query %v, want is_deleted=false and the name", second)
	}
}

func TestAPConnectionsReadBothAnswerShapes(t *testing.T) {
	conn := func(id, colo string) map[string]any {
		return map[string]any{"id": id, "colo_name": colo, "origin_ip": "203.0.113.5", "opened_at": "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z"}
	}
	flat := conn("conn1", "FRA")
	flat["client_version"] = "2026.9.0"
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		result []any
		want   []string
	}{
		{"connectors with their connections", []any{map[string]any{"id": "client1", "version": "2026.9.0", "conns": []any{conn("conn1", "FRA"), conn("conn2", "AMS")}}},
			[]string{"conn1 FRA 203.0.113.5 2026.9.0", "conn2 AMS 203.0.113.5 2026.9.0"}},
		{"flat connections", []any{flat}, []string{"conn1 FRA 203.0.113.5 2026.9.0"}},
		{"none", []any{}, nil},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			srv, a := apRaw(t)
			srv.Handle(http.MethodGet, "/accounts/"+apAccount+"/cfd_tunnel/t1/connections", apOK(tc.result))
			got, err := a.Connections(context.Background(), "t1")
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			var lines []string
			for _, c := range got {
				lines = append(lines, strings.Join([]string{c.ID, c.ColoName, c.OriginIP, c.ClientVersion}, " "))
				if !c.OpenedAt.Equal(time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 9, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)) {
					t.Errorf("connection %s opened at %v", c.ID, c.OpenedAt)
				}
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(lines, tc.want) {
				t.Errorf("connections %q, want %q", lines, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAPConfigurationRoundTripKeepsUnknownMembers(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apRaw(t)
	const config = `{"ingress":[{"hostname":"app.example.com","service":"http://web:80","originRequest":{"noTLSVerify":true,"connectTimeout":"10s"}},{"service":"http_status:404"}],"warp-routing":{"enabled":false}}`
	srv.Handle(http.MethodGet, "/accounts/"+apAccount+"/cfd_tunnel/t1/configurations",
		apOK(map[string]any{"tunnel_id": "t1", "version": 3, "source": "cloudflare", "config": json.RawMessage(config)}))
	srv.Handle(http.MethodGet, "/accounts/"+apAccount+"/cfd_tunnel/t2/configurations",
		apOK(map[string]any{"tunnel_id": "t2", "version": 0, "source": "cloudflare", "config": nil}))
	srv.Handle(http.MethodPut, "/accounts/"+apAccount+"/cfd_tunnel/t1/configurations", apOK(map[string]any{"tunnel_id": "t1", "version": 4}))

	cfg, err := a.Configuration(context.Background(), "t1")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(cfg.Ingress) != 2 || cfg.Ingress[0].Hostname != "app.example.com" || cfg.Ingress[0].Service != "http://web:80" ||
		!cfg.Ingress[0].NoTLSVerify || cfg.Ingress[1].Service != ingress.CatchAll {
		t.Fatalf("configuration %+v, want the two rules", cfg)
	}
	if err := a.PutConfiguration(context.Background(), "t1", cfg); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	put := srv.Requests()[1]
	if put.Method != http.MethodPut {
		t.Fatalf("second request is %s, want PUT", put.Method)
	}
	var body, want map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(put.Body, &body); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(`{"config":`+config+`}`), &want); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(body, want) {
		t.Errorf("PUT body %s, want the configuration wrapped under config with its other members", put.Body)
	}

	empty, err := a.Configuration(context.Background(), "t2")
	if err != nil || len(empty.Ingress) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("configuration of a tunnel never configured = %+v (%v), want an empty one", empty, err)
	}
}

func TestAPDNSRecords(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apRaw(t)
	rec := map[string]any{"id": "r1", "type": "CNAME", "name": "app.example.com", "content": "t1.cfargotunnel.com", "proxied": true, "comment": "darkpanel:c1"}
	srv.Handle(http.MethodGet, "/zones/z1/dns_records", apOK([]any{rec}))
	srv.Handle(http.MethodPost, "/zones/z1/dns_records", apOK(rec))
	srv.Handle(http.MethodGet, "/zones/z1/dns_records/r1", apOK(rec))
	srv.Handle(http.MethodDelete, "/zones/z1/dns_records/r1", apOK(map[string]string{"id": "r1"}))
	ctx := context.Background()
	want := DNSRecord{ID: "r1", Type: "CNAME", Name: "app.example.com", Content: "t1.cfargotunnel.com", Proxied: true, Comment: "darkpanel:c1"}

	list, err := a.DNSRecords(ctx, "z1", "app.example.com", "darkpanel:c1")
	if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(list, []DNSRecord{want}) {
		t.Fatalf("records %+v (%v), want %+v", list, err, want)
	}
	if _, err := a.DNSRecords(ctx, "z1", "", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	created, err := a.CreateDNSRecord(ctx, "z1", DNSRecord{Type: "CNAME", Name: "app.example.com", Content: "t1.cfargotunnel.com", Proxied: true, Comment: "darkpanel:c1"})
	if err != nil || created != want {
		t.Fatalf("created %+v (%v), want %+v", created, err, want)
	}
	one, err := a.DNSRecord(ctx, "z1", "r1")
	if err != nil || one != want {
		t.Fatalf("record %+v (%v), want %+v", one, err, want)
	}
	if err := a.DeleteDNSRecord(ctx, "z1", "r1"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	reqs := srv.Requests()
	filtered, unfiltered := apQuery(t, reqs[0]), apQuery(t, reqs[1])
	if filtered.Get("name") != "app.example.com" || filtered.Get("comment.exact") != "darkpanel:c1" {
		t.Errorf("filtered query %v, want the name and the exact comment", filtered)
	}
	if unfiltered.Has("name") || unfiltered.Has("comment.exact") {
		t.Errorf("unfiltered query %v, want no filter", unfiltered)
	}
	var body map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(reqs[2].Body, &body); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	wantBody := map[string]any{"type": "CNAME", "name": "app.example.com", "content": "t1.cfargotunnel.com", "proxied": true, "comment": "darkpanel:c1", "ttl": float64(1)}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(body, wantBody) {
		t.Errorf("create body %v, want %v", body, wantBody)
	}
	if last := reqs[4]; last.Method != http.MethodDelete || last.Path != "/zones/z1/dns_records/r1" {
		t.Errorf("last request %s %s, want the record's delete", last.Method, last.Path)
	}
}

func TestAPMissingObjectsAreNotFound(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		method string
		path   string
		call   func(a *api) error
	}{
		{"tunnel", http.MethodGet, "/accounts/" + apAccount + "/cfd_tunnel/t9", func(a *api) error { _, err := a.Tunnel(ctx, "t9"); return err }},
		{"tunnel delete", http.MethodDelete, "/accounts/" + apAccount + "/cfd_tunnel/t9", func(a *api) error { return a.DeleteTunnel(ctx, "t9") }},
		{"tunnel token", http.MethodGet, "/accounts/" + apAccount + "/cfd_tunnel/t9/token", func(a *api) error { _, err := a.TunnelToken(ctx, "t9"); return err }},
		{"configuration", http.MethodGet, "/accounts/" + apAccount + "/cfd_tunnel/t9/configurations", func(a *api) error { _, err := a.Configuration(ctx, "t9"); return err }},
		{"record", http.MethodGet, "/zones/z1/dns_records/r9", func(a *api) error { _, err := a.DNSRecord(ctx, "z1", "r9"); return err }},
		{"record delete", http.MethodDelete, "/zones/z1/dns_records/r9", func(a *api) error { return a.DeleteDNSRecord(ctx, "z1", "r9") }},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			srv, a := apRaw(t)
			srv.Handle(tc.method, tc.path, func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) { apReply(w, 404, false, 1003, nil) })
			err := tc.call(a)
			e := apWantCode(t, err, errcode.NotFound)
			if !strings.Contains(e.Detail, "9") {
				t.Errorf("detail %q does not name the object", e.Detail)
			}
			if cloud.Status(err) != http.StatusNotFound {
				t.Errorf("cloud.Status = %d, want 404 kept in the error chain", cloud.Status(err))
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAPFailuresMapToTheCloudCodes(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	tests := []struct {
		name     string
		method   string
		path     string
		status   int
		body     string
		call     func(a *api) error
		code     errcode.Code
		detail   string
		definite bool
	}{
		{"success false on a read", http.MethodGet, "/accounts/" + apAccount + "/cfd_tunnel", 200,
			`{"success":false,"errors":[{"code":1000,"message":"x"}],"result":null}`,
			func(a *api) error { _, err := a.Tunnels(ctx, ""); return err }, errcode.CloudUnavailable, "", false},
		{"success false on a write", http.MethodPost, "/accounts/" + apAccount + "/cfd_tunnel", 200,
			`{"success":false,"errors":[{"code":1000,"message":"x"}],"result":null}`,
			func(a *api) error { _, err := a.CreateTunnel(ctx, "n"); return err }, errcode.CloudUncertainOutcome, "", false},
		{"unreadable answer on a read", http.MethodGet, "/zones", 200, `not json`,
			func(a *api) error { _, err := a.Zones(ctx); return err }, errcode.CloudUnavailable, "", false},
		{"refused write", http.MethodPost, "/accounts/" + apAccount + "/cfd_tunnel", 400,
			`{"success":false,"errors":[{"code":1010,"message":"bad"}],"result":null}`,
			func(a *api) error { _, err := a.CreateTunnel(ctx, "n"); return err }, errcode.InvalidInput, "cloudflare answered 400 (1010)", true},
		{"missing permission", http.MethodGet, "/zones", 403,
			`{"success":false,"errors":[{"code":10000,"message":"Authentication error"}],"result":null}`,
			func(a *api) error { _, err := a.Zones(ctx); return err }, errcode.CloudPermissionMissing, "cloudflare answered 403 (10000)", false},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			srv, a := apRaw(t)
			srv.Handle(tc.method, tc.path, func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
				w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
				w.WriteHeader(tc.status)
				_, _ = io.WriteString(w, tc.body)
			})
			err := tc.call(a)
			e := apWantCode(t, err, tc.code)
			if tc.detail != "" && e.Detail != tc.detail {
				t.Errorf("detail %q, want %q", e.Detail, tc.detail)
			}
			if core.IsDefinite(err) != tc.definite {
				t.Errorf("definite = %v, want %v", core.IsDefinite(err), tc.definite)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAPReadsAreRetriedAndWritesAreNot(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apRaw(t)
	srv.Handle(http.MethodGet, "/accounts/"+apAccount+"/cfd_tunnel", apOK([]any{}))
	srv.Handle(http.MethodPost, "/accounts/"+apAccount+"/cfd_tunnel", apOK(map[string]any{"id": "t1", "name": "n"}))
	srv.Fail(http.MethodGet, "/accounts/"+apAccount+"/cfd_tunnel", cloudfake.Fault{Status: 503})
	srv.Fail(http.MethodPost, "/accounts/"+apAccount+"/cfd_tunnel", cloudfake.Fault{Status: 500})

	if _, err := a.Tunnels(context.Background(), ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a read after one 503: %v", err)
	}
	if n := apCount(srv, http.MethodGet); n != 2 {
		t.Errorf("%d GET requests, want the failed one and its retry", n)
	}
	_, err := a.CreateTunnel(context.Background(), "n")
	_ = apWantCode(t, err, errcode.CloudUncertainOutcome)
	if n := apCount(srv, http.MethodPost); n != 1 {
		t.Errorf("%d POST requests, want exactly one", n)
	}
}

func TestAPAgainstTheFake(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	srv := fake.New(t)
	a, err := cfWith(srv).newAPI(fake.AccountID, []byte(fake.Token), apClock)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := a.VerifyToken(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("verify: %v", err)
	}
	zid := srv.AddZone("example.com")
	zones, err := a.Zones(ctx)
	if err != nil || len(zones) != 1 || zones[0].ID != zid || zones[0].Name != "example.com" {
		t.Fatalf("zones %+v (%v), want example.com", zones, err)
	}

	tun, err := a.CreateTunnel(ctx, "darkpanel-c1")
	if err != nil || tun.ID == "" || tun.Name != "darkpanel-c1" {
		t.Fatalf("create tunnel %+v (%v)", tun, err)
	}
	srv.AddTunnel("other")
	if raw, _ := json.Marshal(srv.Tunnels()); !strings.Contains(string(raw), `"darkpanel-c1"`) {
		t.Errorf("the fake's tunnels %s lack the created one", raw)
	}
	named, err := a.Tunnels(ctx, "darkpanel-c1")
	if err != nil || len(named) != 1 || named[0].ID != tun.ID {
		t.Errorf("tunnels by name %+v (%v), want the created one only", named, err)
	}
	if all, err := a.Tunnels(ctx, ""); err != nil || len(all) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("all tunnels %+v (%v), want two", all, err)
	}

	srv.SetConnections(tun.ID, 2)
	got, err := a.Tunnel(ctx, tun.ID)
	if err != nil || len(got.Connections) != 2 || got.Status == "" {
		t.Errorf("tunnel with connections %+v (%v), want two connections and a status", got, err)
	}
	if conns, err := a.Connections(ctx, tun.ID); err != nil || len(conns) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("connections %+v (%v), want two", conns, err)
	}
	srv.SetConnections(tun.ID, 0)
	if token, err := a.TunnelToken(ctx, tun.ID); err != nil || token == "" {
		t.Errorf("token %q (%v), want one", token, err)
	}

	cfg := ingress.Config{Ingress: []ingress.Rule{{Hostname: "app.example.com", Service: "http://web:80"}, {Service: ingress.CatchAll}}}
	if err := a.PutConfiguration(ctx, tun.ID, cfg); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if raw := srv.Configuration(tun.ID); !strings.Contains(string(raw), "app.example.com") {
		t.Errorf("the fake's configuration %s lacks the rule", raw)
	}
	read, err := a.Configuration(ctx, tun.ID)
	if err != nil || len(read.Ingress) != 2 || read.Ingress[0].Hostname != "app.example.com" {
		t.Errorf("configuration %+v (%v), want the two rules back", read, err)
	}

	rec, err := a.CreateDNSRecord(ctx, zid, DNSRecord{Type: "CNAME", Name: "app.example.com", Content: tun.ID + ".cfargotunnel.com", Proxied: true, Comment: "darkpanel:c1"})
	if err != nil || rec.ID == "" || len(srv.Records(zid)) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("create record %+v (%v), fake holds %d", rec, err, len(srv.Records(zid)))
	}
	if found, err := a.DNSRecords(ctx, zid, "app.example.com", "darkpanel:c1"); err != nil || len(found) != 1 || found[0] != rec {
		t.Errorf("records by name and comment %+v (%v), want %+v", found, err, rec)
	}
	if other, err := a.DNSRecords(ctx, zid, "", "darkpanel:other"); err != nil || len(other) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("records of another comment %+v (%v), want none", other, err)
	}
	if err := a.DeleteDNSRecord(ctx, zid, rec.ID); err != nil || len(srv.Records(zid)) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("delete record: %v, fake holds %d", err, len(srv.Records(zid)))
	}
	_, err = a.DNSRecord(ctx, zid, rec.ID)
	_ = apWantCode(t, err, errcode.NotFound)

	if err := a.DeleteTunnel(ctx, tun.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("delete tunnel: %v", err)
	}
	_, err = a.Tunnel(ctx, tun.ID)
	_ = apWantCode(t, err, errcode.NotFound)
}

func TestAPAgainstTheFakeWithoutAccess(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	srv := fake.New(t)

	wrong, err := cfWith(srv).newAPI(fake.AccountID, []byte("not-the-token"), apClock)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_, err = wrong.Zones(ctx)
	if c := errcode.From(err).Code; c != errcode.CloudAuthFailed && c != errcode.CloudPermissionMissing {
		t.Errorf("wrong token: %v, want an authentication or permission refusal", err)
	}
	if err := wrong.VerifyToken(ctx); err == nil {
		t.Error("verify accepted a wrong token")
	}

	a, err := cfWith(srv).newAPI(fake.AccountID, []byte(fake.Token), apClock)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	srv.SetPermissions()
	_, err = a.Zones(ctx)
	e := apWantCode(t, err, errcode.CloudPermissionMissing)
	if !strings.HasPrefix(e.Detail, "cloudflare answered 403 (") {
		t.Errorf("detail %q, want the provider's error code after the status", e.Detail)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. **`cloudflare.go`:** `type module struct{ c cf }` and `Module()` returns `module{c: productionCF()}`. `Manifest()` stays as it is, so `TestManifestIsASkeleton` keeps passing.

2. **`wire.go`:** the Go types of Contracts "Cloudflare wire shapes", copied verbatim with a doc comment on each exported identifier. It imports `time` and `internal/controller/cloud`.

3. **`client.go`, construction.** `deps` and `cf` are as Contracts gives them; `productionCF()` returns `cf{d: deps{baseURL: "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4"}}` (nil `http` and `sleep`: the cloud client's defaults). `newAPI` refuses an empty account id or an empty token with a `cloudflare:` error and otherwise builds one `*cloud.Client` with `Provider` `"cloudflare"`, `BaseURL`, `HTTP` and `Sleep` from `deps`, the given `Clock`, an `Auth` callback that sets `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every attempt, and an `ErrorCode` function that returns the decimal text of `errors[0].code` in a Cloudflare error body (`""` when the body has none or is not JSON). The token lives only in that callback: no error, detail or log line carries it.

4. **`client.go`, requests.** Every path starts `/accounts/<account id>/` (account-scoped calls) or `/zones` (zone-scoped), each id escaped with `url.PathEscape`. Every request sends `Accept: application/json`, and a body is JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`. A 2xx answer is Cloudflare's envelope `{"success","errors","messages","result","result_info"}`:
   - a body that is not JSON, or whose `result` cannot be decoded into the wanted type, is `cloud.unavailable` for a GET or DELETE and `cloud.uncertain_outcome` for any other method;
   - `"success": false` in a 2xx answer is the same two codes, with a client-safe detail that never repeats the provider's message;
   - non-2xx answers are mapped by the cloud client (`cloud.auth_failed`, `cloud.permission_missing`, `cloud.rate_limited`, `cloud.conflict`, `cloud.unavailable`, `cloud.uncertain_outcome`, `request.invalid_input`) and keep its details, for example `cloudflare answered 403 (10000)`; do not re-wrap them, so a 4xx on a write stays `core.Definite`.

5. **`client.go`, methods.** Decode only the members the types hold; `Tunnel.CreatedAt` and `Connection.OpenedAt` come from `created_at` and `opened_at` (RFC 3339 with or without fractions).
   - `VerifyToken`: the endpoint spec 7.1 records; nil when Cloudflare answers success.
   - `Tunnels(name)`: `GET .../cfd_tunnel` with the query `is_deleted=false` and, when `name != ""`, `name=<name>`; `Tunnel(id)`: `GET .../cfd_tunnel/<id>`. A tunnel's `connections` array fills `Tunnel.Connections` (`id`, `colo_name`, `origin_ip`, `opened_at`, `client_version`).
   - `CreateTunnel(name)`: `POST .../cfd_tunnel` with exactly `{"name": <name>, "config_src": "cloudflare"}`. `DeleteTunnel(id)`: `DELETE .../cfd_tunnel/<id>`. `TunnelToken(id)`: `GET .../cfd_tunnel/<id>/token`, whose `result` is a JSON string.
   - `Connections(id)`: `GET .../cfd_tunnel/<id>/connections`, accepting both shapes the endpoint is documented with: an array of connectors, each with `version` and a `conns` array (every element of `conns` becomes one `Connection`, its `ClientVersion` the connector's `version`), and a flat array of connections that carry `client_version` themselves.
   - `Configuration(id)`: `GET .../cfd_tunnel/<id>/configurations`; the `result.config` object decodes into `ingress.Config`, and a `null` or absent `config` (a tunnel never configured) is an empty `ingress.Config`, not an error. `PutConfiguration(id, c)`: `PUT` the same path with the body `{"config": <c>}`, `c` marshaled by `ingress.Config.MarshalJSON` so members the ingress package keeps are sent back unchanged.
   - `Zones()`: `GET /zones`. `DNSRecords(zoneID, name, comment)`: `GET /zones/<zone>/dns_records` with `name=<name>` and `comment.exact=<comment>`, each only when not `""`. `DNSRecord(zoneID, id)`: `GET /zones/<zone>/dns_records/<id>`. `CreateDNSRecord(zoneID, r)`: `POST` with `{"type","name","content","proxied","comment","ttl":1}`; the answer's record, with its id, is returned. `DeleteDNSRecord(zoneID, id)`: `DELETE` the record.
   - The list methods (`Tunnels`, `Zones`, `DNSRecords`) add `page` and `per_page=100`, and read the next page while the answer's `result_info` exists and its `page` is below `total_pages`; an answer without `result_info` ends the list.
   - A 404 from any call that names one object (`Tunnel`, `DeleteTunnel`, `TunnelToken`, `Connections`, `Configuration`, `PutConfiguration`, `DNSRecord`, `DeleteDNSRecord`) is returned as an `*errcode.Error` with code `not_found` and the client-safe detail `cloudflare <object kind> <id> was not found`, wrapping the cloud client's error so `cloud.Status(err) == 404` still holds and `core.IsDefinite` is unchanged. Later tasks use either test to treat an already-absent object as removed.

6. **`zoneFor(zones, hostname)`:** lower-case both sides and ignore one trailing dot of the hostname; a zone matches when the hostname equals the zone name or ends with `"."+name` (so `notexample.com` does not match `example.com`); the longest matching zone name wins; none gives `Zone{}, false`.

7. **`cfWith`** (in `client_test.go`, as written above) is the only construction of `cf` that tests use for the fake.

import { screen, within } from "@testing-library/react"

import { ContainersTab } from "./containers-tab"
import { dkContainer } from "./fixtures"
import type { DockerContainer } from "./types"

const CT_LIST = "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/resources/docker/containers"
const CT_ACTIONS = ["docker.container.start", "docker.container.stop", "docker.container.restart", "docker.container.remove"]

function ctPlan(call: FetchCall): StubResponse {
  const action = call.path.split("/")[6] ?? ""
  const confirmation = action === "docker.container.remove" ? "web" : null
  return { body: { planId: "p1", hostId: "h1", action, version: 1, inputHash: "h", diff: [{ op: "+", text: action }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z", confirmation } }
}

function ctRender(containers: DockerContainer[], routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}) {
  const calls = stubFetch({
    [CT_LIST]: { body: { containers } },
    "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/modules/docker/availability": { body: { module: "docker", available: true, reason: null, actions: [] } },

    ...routes,

  return { calls, ...result }
}

function ctPlanCall(calls: FetchCall[]): { path: string; body: unknown } {

}

```tsx
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import type { Change, Plan } from "@/api/types"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { tnPolicy } from "./fixtures"
import { PolicyPage } from "./policy-page"

const GET = "POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.policy.get/v1/read"
const PLAN = "POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.policy.set/v1/plan"
const APPLY = "POST /api/v1/actions/tailnet.policy.set/v1/apply"

const ppText = '{\n  // Everyone reaches everything.\n  "acls": [{"action": "accept", "src": ["*"], "dst": ["*:*"]}],\n}\n'
const ppEdited = ppText.replace('"*:*"', '"tag:web:443"')

const ppPlan: Plan = {
  planId: "p1", hostId: null, action: "tailnet.policy.set", version: 1, inputHash: "h",
  diff: [
    { op: " ", text: '  "acls": [{"action": "accept", "src": ["*"],' },
    { op: "-", text: '"dst": ["*:*"]}],' },
    { op: "+", text: '"dst": ["tag:web:443"]}],' },
  ],
  guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z", confirmation: null,
}

const ppChange: Change = {
  id: "c1", hostId: null, action: "tailnet.policy.set", version: 1, class: "compensable", state: "completed", actor: "user:u1",
  createdAt: "2026-10-30T08:00:00Z", updatedAt: "2026-10-30T08:00:00Z", revertDeadline: null, output: { etag: "etag-2" }, error: null,
  compensatedBy: null, parentChangeId: null, owner: null, repairedBy: null, repairOutcome: null, override: null,
}

function ppRender(routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}) {
  const calls = stubFetch({ [GET]: { body: { output: tnPolicy({ text: ppText, etag: "etag-1" }) } }, [PLAN]: { body: ppPlan }, ...routes })
  const result = renderWithProviders(<PolicyPage />)
  return { calls, ...result }
}

async function ppEditor(): Promise<HTMLTextAreaElement> {
  return (await screen.findByLabelText("Policy file (HuJSON)")) as HTMLTextAreaElement
}

// ppEdit replaces the whole text; paste keeps the braces literal, which user.type would read as key names.
async function ppEdit(user: ReturnType<typeof userEvent.setup>, box: HTMLElement, text: string) {
  await user.clear(box)
  await user.click(box)
  await user.paste(text)
}

test("shows the policy file as the provider stores it, with its version", async () => {
  ppRender()
  const box = await ppEditor()
  expect(box.value).toBe(ppText)
  expect(screen.getByText("Version etag-1").textContent).toBe("Version etag-1")
  expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Review changes" }).hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(true)
  expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Discard edits" }).hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(true)
})

test("plans the edited text and shows the line diff", async () => {
  const { calls } = ppRender()
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  await ppEdit(user, await ppEditor(), ppEdited)
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Review changes" }))
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Apply the policy file" })
  const diff = await within(dialog).findByLabelText("Planned changes")
  expect(diff.textContent).toContain('- "dst": ["*:*"]}],')
  expect(diff.textContent).toContain('+ "dst": ["tag:web:443"]}],')
  const plan = calls.find((c) => c.path === "/api/v1/actions/tailnet.policy.set/v1/plan")
  expect(plan?.body).toEqual({ input: { text: ppEdited } })
})

test("a policy the provider rejects is reported and cannot be applied", async () => {
  ppRender({
    [PLAN]: { status: 422, body: { type: "about:blank", title: "Invalid", status: 422, detail: "line 3: unknown field \"acl\"", code: "tailnet.policy_invalid" } },
  })
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  await ppEdit(user, await ppEditor(), ppEdited)
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Review changes" }))
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Apply the policy file" })
  expect((await within(dialog).findByRole("alert")).textContent).toBe('line 3: unknown field "acl"')
  expect(within(dialog).getByRole("button", { name: "Apply" }).hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(true)
})

test("applying reads the policy again and shows the stored text", async () => {
  let stored = tnPolicy({ text: ppText, etag: "etag-1" })
  const { calls } = ppRender({
    [GET]: () => ({ body: { output: stored } }),
    [APPLY]: () => {
      stored = tnPolicy({ text: ppEdited, etag: "etag-2" })
      return { body: ppChange }
    },
  })
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  await ppEdit(user, await ppEditor(), ppEdited)
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Review changes" }))
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Apply the policy file" })
  await within(dialog).findByLabelText("Planned changes")
  await user.click(within(dialog).getByRole("button", { name: "Apply" }))
  await within(dialog).findByText("completed")
  // The dialog's corner button has the same name; the footer's is the last.
  await user.click(within(dialog).getAllByRole("button", { name: "Close" }).slice(-1)[0] as HTMLElement)
  await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByText("Version etag-2").textContent).toBe("Version etag-2"))
  expect(((await ppEditor()).value)).toBe(ppEdited)
  expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Review changes" }).hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(true)
  expect(calls.filter((c) => c.path.endsWith("tailnet.policy.get/v1/read"))).toHaveLength(2)
})

test("discarding the edits restores the stored text", async () => {
  ppRender()
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  const box = await ppEditor()
  await ppEdit(user, box, ppEdited)
  expect(box.value).toBe(ppEdited)
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Discard edits" }))
  expect(box.value).toBe(ppText)
  expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Review changes" }).hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(true)
})

test("a policy that changes on the provider replaces an edit made on the old version", async () => {
  let stored = tnPolicy({ text: ppText, etag: "etag-1" })
  const { client } = ppRender({ [GET]: () => ({ body: { output: stored } }) })
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  await ppEdit(user, await ppEditor(), ppEdited)
  stored = tnPolicy({ text: '{"acls": []}\n', etag: "etag-9" })
  await client.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["tailnet"] })
  await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByText("Version etag-9").textContent).toBe("Version etag-9"))
  expect((await ppEditor()).value).toBe('{"acls": []}\n')
})

test("a tailnet with no account shows the reason instead of an editor", async () => {
  ppRender({ [GET]: { status: 409, body: { type: "about:blank", title: "Not connected", status: 409, detail: "no tailnet account is connected", code: "cloud.not_connected" } } })
  expect((await screen.findByRole("alert")).textContent).toBe("no tailnet account is connected")
  expect(screen.queryByLabelText("Policy file (HuJSON)")).toBeNull()
})

test("has no accessibility violations", async () => {
  const { container } = ppRender()
  await ppEditor()
  expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations()
})

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `policy-page.tsx`, named export `PolicyPage()`. Read the policy with `useQuery` under `tailnetKey("policy")`, calling `readAction<TailnetPolicy>("tailnet.policy.get", TAILNET_ACTION_VERSION)` (no input, no host id: the action is controller-side). While pending show `Spinner` with `aria-label="Loading the policy"`. On error show a destructive `Alert` with `role="alert"` holding `errorMessage(error)` and nothing else (no editor): a controller with no tailnet account answers `cloud.not_connected`, and its message is the whole explanation.
2. Loaded state: one `Card` titled "Policy file" whose description says the text is HuJSON, comments are kept, and that Review checks the text with Tailscale and shows what changes. Inside it a `form` with `aria-label="Policy file"`: a `Label` "Policy file (HuJSON)" bound to a `Textarea` with `id="pp-text"`, `rows={24}`, `spellCheck={false}` and class `font-mono`; a caption `Version <etag>` under it; two buttons: "Review changes" (`type="submit"`) and "Discard edits" (`type="button"`, `variant="outline"`), both `disabled` while the shown text equals the stored text exactly (no trimming anywhere).
3. Draft state: keep `{etag, text}` in `useState`. The shown text is the draft's text only when the draft's `etag` equals the loaded `etag`, otherwise the stored text. This is how a policy that changed on the provider, or was just applied (the change dialog invalidates `["tailnet"]` on close, which reads the policy again), replaces an edit made on the old version, as `DockerSources` in `web/src/modules/firewall/docker-sources.tsx` does with its base text. "Discard edits" sets the draft to `null`.
4. Submitting the form (`preventDefault`) stores the shown text as the pending change. Render `TailnetChange` only while a change is pending, with `action="tailnet.policy.set"`, `title="Apply the policy file"`, `input={{ text }}` (exactly the text shown) and an `onClose` that clears the pending change. The page itself never calls `planAction` or `applyPlan`.
5. `global.tsx`: replace the skeleton with `export default function TailnetGlobal()` (the only export). Render, in order: `PageHeader` from `darkraise-ui/layout` titled "Tailnet" with a one-sentence description; a `nav` with `aria-label="Tailnet pages"` holding four `NavLink`s with the **absolute** targets and labels `/tailnet` "Account" (`end`), `/tailnet/devices` "Devices", `/tailnet/keys` "Auth keys", `/tailnet/policy` "Policy" (active: `font-medium underline underline-offset-4`; otherwise `text-muted-foreground underline-offset-4 hover:underline`); then `Routes` with `index` → `AccountPanel`, `devices` → `DevicesPage`, `keys` → `KeysPage`, `policy` → `PolicyPage` and `*` → `EmptyState` titled "Page not found". The targets are absolute because React Router 8 resolves a relative link inside a splat route (`/tailnet/*`) against the open page, which would give `/tailnet/keys/devices`; the registry (frozen) mounts this page at `/tailnet/*`.
6. TypeScript here targets ES2020: no `Array.prototype.at` and no `String.prototype.replaceAll`. Use `darkraise-ui` components as the neighbouring pages do; add no dependency.

import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import type { Change, Plan } from "@/api/types"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { cfTunnel } from "./fixtures"
import { TunnelsPage } from "./tunnels-page"
import type { TunnelView } from "./types"

const LIST = "POST /api/v1/actions/cloudflare.tunnel.list/v1/read"

function tpConnection(colo: string, id: string) {
  return { id, colo, originIp: "203.0.113.5", openedAt: "2026-10-30T08:05:00Z", version: "2026.10.0" }
}

function tpTunnels(): TunnelView[] {
  return [
    cfTunnel({ id: "t1", name: "darkpanel-c1", status: "healthy", connections: [tpConnection("ams01", "k1"), tpConnection("fra02", "k2")], hostnames: 2 }),
    cfTunnel({ id: "t2", name: "darkpanel-c2", status: "inactive", drift: true }),
    cfTunnel({ id: "t3", name: "darkpanel-c3", status: "unknown" }),
  ]
}

function tpPlan(action: string, confirmation: string | null = null): Plan {
  return {
    planId: "p1", hostId: null, action, version: 1, inputHash: "h", diff: [{ op: "~", text: "tunnel" }], guards: [],
    expiresAt: "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z", confirmation,
  }
}

const tpChange: Change = {
  id: "c9", hostId: null, action: "cloudflare.tunnel.create", version: 1, class: "compensable", state: "completed", actor: "user:u1",
  createdAt: "2026-10-30T08:00:00Z", updatedAt: "2026-10-30T08:00:00Z", revertDeadline: null, output: { id: "t4", name: "darkpanel-c9" }, error: null,
  compensatedBy: null, parentChangeId: null, owner: null, repairedBy: null, repairOutcome: null, override: null,
}

function tpRender(routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}) {
  const calls = stubFetch({ [LIST]: { body: { output: { tunnels: tpTunnels() } } }, ...routes })
  const result = renderWithProviders(<TunnelsPage />)
  return { calls, ...result }
}

async function tpTable() {
  return screen.findByRole("table", { name: "Tunnels" })
}

function tpPlanCall(calls: { path: string; body: unknown }[], action: string) {
  return calls.find((c) => c.path === `/api/v1/actions/${action}/v1/plan`)
}

Loaded: a `Card` titled "Tunnels" whose header holds a "Create tunnel" button; with no tunnels the body is an `EmptyState` titled "No tunnels yet", otherwise a `Table` with `aria-label="Tunnels"`, rows in the server's order, columns Name, Status (a `Badge`, `default` variant only for `healthy`, `secondary` otherwise, text = the status as served), Connections (`0`, or `<n> (<colo>, <colo>)` from `connections[].colo`), Hostnames (the count), Configuration (`Changed outside Darkpanel` when `drift`, else `In sync`), Created (`formatTime`), and an actions cell with a visually hidden header "Actions".
2. Actions are `setPending({action, title, input})` on one `useState`; render `CloudflareChange` only while one is pending, with `onClose` clearing it. "Create tunnel": `cloudflare.tunnel.create`, title "Create a tunnel", input `{}`. Per row "Delete" (`aria-label` `Delete tunnel <name>`): `cloudflare.tunnel.delete`, title `Delete tunnel <name>`, input `{tunnel: <name>}`. Per drifted row only, "Accept configuration" (`aria-label` `Accept the current configuration of <name>`): `cloudflare.tunnel.adopt`, title `Accept the configuration of <name>`, input `{tunnel: <id>}`. The tunnel token is never shown (`cloudflare.tunnel.token` is internal).
3. `hostnames-page.tsx`, named export `HostnamesPage()`. Two queries: tunnels as above and hostnames under `cloudflareKey("hostnames")` with `readAction<{ hostnames: HostnameView[] }>("cloudflare.hostname.list", CLOUDFLARE_ACTION_VERSION)`. A failure of either shows one destructive `Alert` `role="alert"` (hostnames' error first) and nothing else; while either has no data show `Spinner` `aria-label="Loading the hostnames"`. Loaded: a `Card` "Hostnames" holding an `EmptyState` titled "No hostnames yet" when the list is empty, otherwise a `Table` with `aria-label="Hostnames"` in the server's order, columns Hostname, Tunnel (the tunnel's name from the tunnels query, else the raw tunnel id), Service (monospace), State (`Badge`: `default` for phase `active`, else `secondary`; text = the phase with `_` replaced by a space, written `replace(/_/g, " ")`), Health (`Badge`: `default` for `ok`, `secondary` for `unknown`, else `destructive`; same text rule), Checked (`formatTime(checkedAt ?? null)`) and an actions cell with a "Remove" button (`aria-label` `Remove hostname <hostname>`) that plans `cloudflare.hostname.remove`, title `Remove <hostname>`, input `{hostname}`.
4. Below it a second `Card` "Add a hostname". With no tunnels it holds only a `Link` to `/cloudflare/tunnels` with the text "Create a tunnel first". Otherwise a `form` with `aria-label="Add hostname"`: a `RadioGroup` (`aria-label="Tunnel"`, inside a `fieldset` with legend "Tunnel") with one `RadioGroupItem` per tunnel labelled with its name and valued with its id; `Label` "Hostname" bound to an `Input`; `Label` "Service" bound to an `Input` with a help line naming the accepted forms (http:// or https:// with host and port, tcp://, ssh://, http_status:404); a `Checkbox` labelled "Do not verify the origin's TLS certificate"; the submit button "Add hostname". The chosen tunnel is the clicked one, else the only tunnel when exactly one exists, else none. On submit (`preventDefault`): when no tunnel is chosen or the trimmed hostname or service is empty, show a destructive `Alert` `role="alert"` inside the form with exactly "Choose a tunnel and enter the hostname and the service." and plan nothing; otherwise clear that message and plan `cloudflare.hostname.add`, title `Add <hostname>`, input `{tunnel: <id>, hostname: <trimmed>, service: <trimmed>}` plus `noTLSVerify: true` only when the box is ticked (the key is absent otherwise). One `CloudflareChange` for the page, rendered only while a change is pending.
5. `global.tsx`: replace the skeleton with `export default function CloudflareGlobal()` (the only export). Render `PageHeader` (`darkraise-ui/layout`) titled "Cloudflare", a `nav` with `aria-label="Cloudflare pages"` holding `NavLink`s with the **absolute** targets and labels `/cloudflare` "Account" (`end`), `/cloudflare/tunnels` "Tunnels", `/cloudflare/hostnames` "Hostnames" (same active styling as the tailnet page), then `Routes`: `index` → `AccountPanel`, `tunnels` → `TunnelsPage`, `hostnames` → `HostnamesPage`, `*` → `EmptyState` titled "Page not found". The targets are absolute because React Router 8 resolves a relative link inside a splat route (`/cloudflare/*`) against the open page; the registry (frozen) mounts this page at `/cloudflare/*`. `container-actions.tsx` is not touched.
6. TypeScript here targets ES2020: no `Array.prototype.at` and no `String.prototype.replaceAll`; narrow `query.data` before use (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is on, so index a one-element array through a checked value). Use `darkraise-ui` components as `web/src/modules/firewall/docker-sources.tsx` and `exposure-page.tsx` do; add no dependency.

func rdOwned(c *dockerapi.ContainerJSON) { c.Config.Labels["darkpanel.module"] = "npm" }

// rdRead runs a read action's handler with a raw JSON input.
func rdRead(t *testing.T, def core.ActionDef, h *dkHost, input string) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	t.Helper()
	return def.Handler.Read(context.Background(), h.env(""), json.RawMessage(input))
}

// rdSame compares two JSON documents without regard to member order.
func rdSame(t *testing.T, got json.RawMessage, want string) {
	t.Helper()
	var g, w any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(got, &g); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("answer is not JSON: %v\n%s", err, got)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(want), &w); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expectation is not JSON: %v", err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(g, w) {
		t.Errorf("answer\n%s\nwant\n%s", got, want)
	}
}

func rdCode(err error) errcode.Code { return errcode.From(err).Code }

const rdWebDetail = `{

func rdExpectedDetail(owner string) string {
	s := strings.NewReplacer("%ID%", dkID("web"), "%APP%", dkID("app"), "%BRIDGE%", dkID("bridge")).Replace(rdWebDetail)
	if owner != "" {
		s = strings.Replace(s, `"service": "web"`, `"service": "web", "owner": "`+owner+`"`, 1)
		s = strings.Replace(s, `"tier": "front"`, `"tier": "front", "darkpanel.module": "`+owner+`"`, 1)
	}
	return s
}

func TestRdInspectReportsTheContainer(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name  string
		opts  []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON)
		owner string
	}{
		{"unlabelled", nil, ""},
		{"owned by a module", []func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON){rdOwned}, "npm"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			h.docker.put(rdWeb(tc.opts...))
			for _, ref := range []string{"web", dkID("web")} {
				raw, err := rdRead(t, h.dk().containerInspect(), h, `{"container":"`+ref+`"}`)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("inspect %q: %v", ref, err)
				}
				rdSame(t, raw, rdExpectedDetail(tc.owner))
				for _, secret := range rdSecretValues {
					if strings.Contains(string(raw), secret) {
						t.Errorf("inspect %q leaks the environment value %q:\n%s", ref, secret, raw)
					}
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestRdInspectRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name  string
		input string
		prep  func(h *dkHost)
		code  errcode.Code
		path  string
	}{
		{"an empty container", `{"container":""}`, nil, errcode.InvalidInput, "/container"},
		{"an absent container", `{"container":"ghost"}`, nil, errcode.NotFound, ""},
		{"an unreachable daemon", `{"container":"web"}`, func(h *dkHost) { h.docker.fail("InspectContainer", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable) }, errcode.DockerEngineUnavailable, ""},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			h.docker.put(rdWeb())
			if tc.prep != nil {
				tc.prep(h)
			}
			_, err := rdRead(t, h.dk().containerInspect(), h, tc.input)
			if rdCode(err) != tc.code {
				t.Fatalf("code %q (%v), want %q", rdCode(err), err, tc.code)
			}
			if tc.path != "" {
				if f := errcode.From(err).Fields; len(f) != 1 || f[0].Path != tc.path {
					t.Errorf("fields %+v, want one at %s", f, tc.path)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}
