`internal/modules/docker/logs_read_test.go`:

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

// rdStream replays frames and then ends with end (io.EOF when nil).
type rdStream struct {
	frames []dockerapi.LogFrame
	end    error
	closed bool
}

func (s *rdStream) Next() (dockerapi.LogFrame, error) {
	if len(s.frames) == 0 {
		if s.end != nil {
			return dockerapi.LogFrame{}, s.end
		}
		return dockerapi.LogFrame{}, io.EOF
	}
	f := s.frames[0]
	s.frames = s.frames[1:]
	return f, nil
}

func (s *rdStream) Close() error { s.closed = true; return nil }

// rdDocker answers Logs with a scripted stream and records how it was asked; everything else is the fake's.
type rdDocker struct {
	*fakeDocker
	stream *rdStream
	ids    []string
	opts   []dockerapi.LogsOptions
}

func (d *rdDocker) Logs(_ context.Context, id string, o dockerapi.LogsOptions) (logStream, error) {
	d.ids = append(d.ids, id)
	d.opts = append(d.opts, o)
	return d.stream, nil
}

func rdOut(s string) dockerapi.LogFrame { return dockerapi.LogFrame{Stream: "stdout", Data: []byte(s)} }
func rdErr(s string) dockerapi.LogFrame { return dockerapi.LogFrame{Stream: "stderr", Data: []byte(s)} }

// rdLogsHost puts the containers web (unlabelled) and proxy (owned by npm) on a host that holds secrets for
// its modules and whose Logs answers frames.
func rdLogsHost(t *testing.T, secrets [][]byte, end error, frames ...dockerapi.LogFrame) (*dkHost, dk, *rdDocker) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	h.secrets = secrets
	h.docker.put(rdWeb())
	h.docker.put(rdWeb(rdOwned, func(c *dockerapi.ContainerJSON) { c.ID, c.Name = dkID("proxy"), "/proxy" }))
	d := &rdDocker{fakeDocker: h.docker, stream: &rdStream{frames: frames, end: end}}
	k := h.dk()
	k.d.docker = d
	return h, k, d
}

func TestRdLogsSplitsFramesIntoLinesPerStream(t *testing.T) {
	h, k, d := rdLogsHost(t, nil, nil, rdOut("one\ntw"), rdErr("oops\n"), rdOut("o\nthr"), rdOut("ee"))
	raw, err := rdRead(t, k.containerLogs(), h, `{"container":"web"}`)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	rdSame(t, raw, `{"lines":[
	  {"stream":"stdout","text":"one"},{"stream":"stderr","text":"oops"},{"stream":"stdout","text":"two"},{"stream":"stdout","text":"three"}]}`)
	want := dockerapi.LogsOptions{Tail: "200", Stdout: true, Stderr: true}
	if len(d.opts) != 1 || d.opts[0] != want || d.ids[0] != dkID("web") {
		t.Errorf("Logs asked %v for %v, want one request for %s with %+v", d.opts, d.ids, dkID("web"), want)
	}
	if !d.stream.closed {
		t.Error("the log stream was left open")
	}
}

func TestRdLogsPassesTheOptionsOn(t *testing.T) {
	h, k, d := rdLogsHost(t, nil, nil)
	raw, err := rdRead(t, k.containerLogs(), h, `{"container":"web","tail":5000,"since":"2026-10-01T10:00:00+02:00","timestamps":true}`)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	rdSame(t, raw, `{"lines":[]}`)
	if len(d.opts) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("Logs asked %d times", len(d.opts))
	}
	o := d.opts[0]
	if o.Tail != "5000" || !o.Timestamps || !o.Since.Equal(time.Date(2026, 10, 1, 8, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)) || o.Follow || !o.Stdout || !o.Stderr {
		t.Errorf("options %+v", o)
	}
}

func TestRdLogsRefusesBadInputBeforeAskingTheEngine(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct{ name, input, path string }{
		{"an empty container", `{"container":""}`, "/container"},
		{"a negative tail", `{"container":"web","tail":-1}`, "/tail"},
		{"a tail above 5000", `{"container":"web","tail":5001}`, "/tail"},
		{"a since that is not RFC 3339", `{"container":"web","since":"yesterday"}`, "/since"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, k, d := rdLogsHost(t, nil, nil)
			_, err := rdRead(t, k.containerLogs(), h, tc.input)
			f := errcode.From(err).Fields
			if rdCode(err) != errcode.InvalidInput || len(f) != 1 || f[0].Path != tc.path {
				t.Fatalf("error %v (fields %+v), want request.invalid_input at %s", err, f, tc.path)
			}
			if len(d.opts) != 0 {
				t.Error("the engine was asked for logs")
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestRdLogsMapsEngineAnswers(t *testing.T) {
	h, k, _ := rdLogsHost(t, nil, nil)
	if _, err := rdRead(t, k.containerLogs(), h, `{"container":"ghost"}`); rdCode(err) != errcode.NotFound {
		t.Errorf("an absent container: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestRdLogsMasksTheSecretsOfAnOwnedContainerAcrossFrames(t *testing.T) {
	h, k, _ := rdLogsHost(t, [][]byte{[]byte("hunter2")}, nil, rdOut("token=hun"), rdErr("hunter2\n"), rdOut("ter2 end\nlast hun"), rdOut("t"))
	raw, err := rdRead(t, k.containerLogs(), h, `{"container":"proxy"}`)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	rdSame(t, raw, `{"lines":[
	  {"stream":"stderr","text":"[redacted]"},{"stream":"stdout","text":"token=[redacted] end"},{"stream":"stdout","text":"last hunt"}]}`)
}

func TestRdLogsLeavesAnUnownedContainerUnfiltered(t *testing.T) {
	h, k, _ := rdLogsHost(t, [][]byte{[]byte("hunter2")}, nil, rdOut("hunter2\n"))
	raw, err := rdRead(t, k.containerLogs(), h, `{"container":"web"}`)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	rdSame(t, raw, `{"lines":[{"stream":"stdout","text":"hunter2"}]}`)
}

func TestRdLogsFailsClosedWhenTheSecretsCannotBeRead(t *testing.T) {
	h, k, d := rdLogsHost(t, nil, nil, rdOut("hunter2\n"))
	k.d.secrets = func(context.Context, core.Env, string) ([][]byte, error) { return nil, errors.New("registry down") }
	raw, err := rdRead(t, k.containerLogs(), h, `{"container":"proxy"}`)
	if err == nil || len(raw) != 0 || len(d.opts) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("answer %s, error %v, %d Logs requests: want an error before any request", raw, err, len(d.opts))
	}
}

func TestRdLogsReturnsAStreamFailureAndClosesTheStream(t *testing.T) {
	boom := errors.New("connection reset")
	h, k, d := rdLogsHost(t, nil, boom, rdOut("partial\n"))
	raw, err := rdRead(t, k.containerLogs(), h, `{"container":"web"}`)
	if !errors.Is(err, boom) || len(raw) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("answer %s, error %v, want the stream's failure", raw, err)
	}
	if !d.stream.closed {
		t.Error("the log stream was left open")
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. Constructors, methods of `dk`. `containerInspect` is `core.DefineRead[ContainerInput, ContainerDetail]` with `core.ActionSpec{Name: "docker.container.inspect", Summary: <one sentence>, Version: 1, Side: core.SideAgent}`; `containerLogs` is `core.DefineRead[LogsInput, LogsOutput]` named `docker.container.logs`; the handler of each is an unexported struct holding the `dk` with a `Read(ctx, env, in)` method (`core.Reader`). `containerRevealEnv` is `core.DefineReveal[ContainerInput, RevealedEnv]` named `docker.container.reveal-env` with `MinScope: core.ScopeAdmin`. No spec sets `LockKeys`, `Class`, `Reveal` or `Internal` by hand (the `Define*` functions set what they need). A parameter a method does not use is named `_` (the linter rejects an unused one).
2. Input errors come from one small helper of this task, `inspectInvalid(path, message string) error`, returning `*errcode.Error` with code `request.invalid_input`, the message as `Detail` and one `errcode.FieldError{Path: path, Message: message}`. An empty `container` (inspect, reveal-env, logs) is refused with path `/container` **before** the Engine is asked.
3. Engine failures of `InspectContainer` and `Logs` go through `engineError("container", <the input's container>, err)` (Contracts "Docker internals"): an absent container is `not_found`, an unreachable daemon `docker.engine_unavailable`.
4. Inspect rendering, a function `containerDetailOf(c dockerapi.ContainerJSON) (ContainerDetail, error)`: `ID` = `c.ID`; `Name` = `c.Name` without the leading `/`; `Image` = `c.Config.Image`; `ImageID` = `c.Image`; `Created` = `c.Created` parsed with `time.RFC3339Nano` and converted `.UTC()` (a parse error is returned as `docker: container <id>: created: %w`); `State` = `c.State.Status`; `Running`; `ExitCode`; `StartedAt` and `FinishedAt` through `dstate.Instant` (so Docker's zero time and `""` give `""`, and `omitempty` drops them); `RestartPolicy` = `c.HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name`; `Cmd`, `Entrypoint`, `WorkingDir`, `User` and `Labels` from `c.Config`; `Project` and `Service` from the labels `com.docker.compose.project` and `com.docker.compose.service` (string literals; declare no constant); `Owner` = `ownerOf(c.Config.Labels)`.
5. `Env`: one `EnvVar` per `c.Config.Env` entry, in the Engine's order, split at the **first** `=` (an entry without `=` is a name with an empty value). A helper `envVars(entries []string, redact bool) []EnvVar` serves both inspect and reveal-env: inspect passes `redact` true and every value becomes `logfilter.Mask`, for every container, owned or not, including the empty value; reveal-env passes false.
6. `Ports`: from `c.NetworkSettings.Ports` (keys `<port>/<proto>`): one `Port` per binding whose `HostPort` is a number, with `IP` = the binding's `HostIP` as given (empty stays empty), `PrivatePort`, `PublicPort`, `Proto`. A key or host port that does not parse, a key with no binding and a binding with an empty `HostPort` (exposed but not published) produce nothing. Sort by `PrivatePort`, then `Proto`, then `PublicPort`, then `IP`. `Mounts`: one `Mount` per `c.Mounts` entry, in the Engine's order, copying `Type`, `Name`, `Source`, `Destination`, `RW`. `Networks`: one `EndpointView` per `c.NetworkSettings.Networks` entry, `Network` = the map key, `NetworkID`, `EndpointID` and `Aliases` from the endpoint (Engine order), `Container` = the container's name, `IPv4` = `IPAddress.String()` and `IPv6` = `GlobalIPv6Address.String()` only when the address is valid, sorted by `Network`. `Env`, `Ports`, `Mounts` and `Networks` are empty slices, never `nil`, so the JSON has `[]`.
7. `containerRevealEnv`: after the empty check, inspect the container, then `refuseOwned("container", <name without />, c.Config.Labels)` and return its error as is (`docker.owned` with `core.Definite`, before any value is read into the answer). Otherwise return `core.Revealed[RevealedEnv]` with `Identity` = `environment of container <name>, host <env.HostID>` and `Value.Env` = `envVars(c.Config.Env, false)`.
8. `containerLogs` (`logs_read.go`): validate in this order before the Engine is asked: empty container (`/container`); `Tail` 0 means 200, below 1 or above 5000 is refused with path `/tail`; a non-empty `Since` must parse with `time.RFC3339`, otherwise refuse with path `/since`. Then inspect the container (for its id and labels), build the filter with `k.logFilter(ctx, env, c)` and return its error as is (so an owned container whose secrets cannot be read is never shown unfiltered, and `Logs` is not called), then open `Logs(ctx, c.ID, dockerapi.LogsOptions{Tail: strconv.Itoa(tail), Since: <parsed or zero>, Timestamps: in.Timestamps, Stdout: true, Stderr: true})` (`Follow` false) and always close the stream (`defer`). Read frames until `io.EOF`; any other error from `Next` is returned through `engineError` and nothing is answered.
9. Line assembly (a function `readLogLines(s logStream, f *logfilter.Filter) (LogsOutput, error)` or equivalent): for each frame push `f.Push(frame.Stream, frame.Data)` and append the returned bytes to that stream's pending buffer; every `\n` ends a line `LogLine{Stream, Text}` whose text excludes the newline, emitted in the order the lines complete across streams; a partial line stays pending per stream. At the end, for `stdout` then `stderr`, append `f.Flush(stream)` to the pending bytes and emit what is left as a final line when non-empty. `Lines` is an empty slice, never `nil`, when there is nothing. The filter for an unlabelled container is `logfilter.New(nil)` (Task 25's `logFilter` does this), so the same code serves both.
10. Declare no package-level identifier other than the three constructors, the two handler types, `inspectInvalid`, `envVars`, `containerDetailOf` and `readLogLines`; add no constant, no wire type and no filter helper. Do not touch `Manifest()` or any schema snapshot (Task 44).

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
)

func plClock() *coretest.FakeClock {
	return coretest.NewFakeClock(time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))
}

func plEvent(n int) PullEvent { return PullEvent{Status: fmt.Sprintf("e%d", n)} }

func plStatuses(events []PullEvent) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(events))
	for i, e := range events {
		out[i] = e.Status
	}
	return out
}

// plRecv takes one event from ch and fails the test when none arrives.
func plRecv(t *testing.T, ch <-chan PullEvent) PullEvent {
	t.Helper()
	select {
	case e, ok := <-ch:
		if !ok {
			t.Fatal("channel closed, want an event")
		}
		return e
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("no event within 5 seconds")
	}
	return PullEvent{}
}

// plDrain reads ch until it closes and fails the test when it stays open.
func plDrain(t *testing.T, ch <-chan PullEvent) []PullEvent {
	t.Helper()
	var got []PullEvent
	timeout := time.After(5 * time.Second)
	for {
		select {
		case e, ok := <-ch:
			if !ok {
				return got
			}
			got = append(got, e)
		case <-timeout:
			t.Fatalf("channel still open after %d events", len(got))
		}
	}
}

func plSame(t *testing.T, got []PullEvent, want ...string) {
	t.Helper()
	g := plStatuses(got)
	if len(g) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("statuses %v, want %v", g, want)
	}
	for i := range want {
		if g[i] != want[i] {
			t.Fatalf("statuses %v, want %v", g, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestPLHubReplaysTheBacklogOfAFinishedChange(t *testing.T) {
	h := newPullHub(plClock())
	for i := 1; i <= 3; i++ {
		h.publish("c1", plEvent(i))
	}
	h.publish("c2", plEvent(99))
	h.finish("c1")
	h.publish("c1", plEvent(4))

	ch, stop := h.subscribe(context.Background(), "c1")
	defer stop()
	plSame(t, plDrain(t, ch), "e1", "e2", "e3")
}

func TestPLHubDeliversLiveEventsToAnEarlySubscriber(t *testing.T) {
	h := newPullHub(plClock())
	ch, stop := h.subscribe(context.Background(), "c1")
	defer stop()
	go func() {
		for i := 1; i <= 200; i++ {
			h.publish("c1", plEvent(i))
		}
		h.finish("c1")
	}()
	got := plDrain(t, ch)
	if len(got) != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("%d events, want 200", len(got))
	}
	for i, e := range got {
		if e.Status != fmt.Sprintf("e%d", i+1) {
			t.Fatalf("event %d is %s, want e%d", i, e.Status, i+1)
		}
	}
}

func TestPLHubBacklogHoldsTheLast256ThenGoesLive(t *testing.T) {
	h := newPullHub(plClock())
	for i := 1; i <= 300; i++ {
		h.publish("c1", plEvent(i))
	}
	ch, stop := h.subscribe(context.Background(), "c1")
	defer stop()
	for i := 45; i <= 300; i++ {
		if got := plRecv(t, ch).Status; got != fmt.Sprintf("e%d", i) {
			t.Fatalf("backlog event is %s, want e%d", got, i)
		}
	}
	h.publish("c1", plEvent(301))
	h.finish("c1")
	plSame(t, plDrain(t, ch), "e301")
}

func TestPLHubDropsAFinishedBacklogAfterTenMinutes(t *testing.T) {
	clock := plClock()
	h := newPullHub(clock)
	h.publish("c1", plEvent(1))
	h.finish("c1")

	clock.Advance(10*time.Minute - time.Second)
	ch, stop := h.subscribe(context.Background(), "c1")
	plSame(t, plDrain(t, ch), "e1")
	stop()

	clock.Advance(time.Second)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	late, stopLate := h.subscribe(ctx, "c1")
	defer stopLate()
	cancel()
	if got := plDrain(t, late); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("a dropped backlog replayed %v", plStatuses(got))
	}
}

func TestPLHubKeepsChangesApart(t *testing.T) {
	h := newPullHub(plClock())
	h.publish("c1", plEvent(1))
	h.publish("c2", plEvent(2))
	h.finish("c1")
	h.finish("c2")
	ch, stop := h.subscribe(context.Background(), "c2")
	defer stop()
	plSame(t, plDrain(t, ch), "e2")
}

func TestPLHubNeverBlocksOnASubscriberThatDoesNotRead(t *testing.T) {
	h := newPullHub(plClock())
	slow, stop := h.subscribe(context.Background(), "c1")
	defer stop()
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		for i := 0; i < 5000; i++ {
			h.publish("c1", plEvent(i))
		}
		h.finish("c1")
	}()
	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("publish blocked on a subscriber that does not read")
	}

	got := plDrain(t, slow)
	if len(got) == 0 || len(got) >= 5000 {
		t.Fatalf("the slow subscriber kept %d of 5000 events, want some but not all", len(got))
	}
	for i, e := range got {
		if e.Status != fmt.Sprintf("e%d", i) {
			t.Fatalf("kept event %d is %s, want e%d", i, e.Status, i)
		}
	}

	late, stopLate := h.subscribe(context.Background(), "c1")
	defer stopLate()
	replay := plStatuses(plDrain(t, late))
	if len(replay) != 256 || replay[0] != "e4744" || replay[255] != "e4999" {
		t.Errorf("a late subscriber got %d events %v, want the last 256, e4744 to e4999", len(replay), replay)
	}
}

func TestPLHubStopAndContextEndCloseTheChannel(t *testing.T) {
	h := newPullHub(plClock())

	ch, stop := h.subscribe(context.Background(), "c1")
	stop()
	if got := plDrain(t, ch); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("a stopped subscription delivered %v", plStatuses(got))
	}
	h.publish("c1", plEvent(1))
	stop()

	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	byCtx, stopCtx := h.subscribe(ctx, "c2")
	defer stopCtx()
	cancel()
	if got := plDrain(t, byCtx); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("a subscription whose context ended delivered %v", plStatuses(got))
	}
}
```

```go
package docker

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

const plRef = "busybox:1.37"

// plImage is a local image whose tag is ref, with one repository digest.
func plImage(ref string) dockerapi.ImageSummary {
	img := dkImage(ref, 4096)
	img.RepoDigests = []string{"busybox@sha256:" + strings.Repeat("a", 64)}
	return img
}

func plShort(id string) string {
	id = strings.TrimPrefix(id, "sha256:")
	return id[:min(12, len(id))]
}

func plInput(image string) json.RawMessage {
	b, err := json.Marshal(ImagePullInput{Image: image})
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	return b
}

func plCode(t *testing.T, err error) errcode.Code {
	t.Helper()
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("no error")
	}
	return errcode.From(err).Code
}

// plStep is one read of a scripted pull stream.
type plStep struct {
	msg dockerapi.PullMessage
	err error
}

type plStream struct {
	steps  []plStep
	closed *bool
}

func (s *plStream) Next() (dockerapi.PullMessage, error) {
	if len(s.steps) == 0 {
		return dockerapi.PullMessage{}, io.EOF
	}
	st := s.steps[0]
	s.steps = s.steps[1:]
	return st.msg, st.err
}

func (s *plStream) Close() error {
	*s.closed = true
	return nil
}

// plDocker is the fake engine with a scripted pull stream.
type plDocker struct {
	*fakeDocker
	steps  []plStep
	closed bool
}

func (d *plDocker) PullImage(context.Context, string) (pullStream, error) {
	return &plStream{steps: d.steps, closed: &d.closed}, nil
}

func TestPLPullSpec(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	def := h.dk().imagePull(newPullHub(h.clock))
	s := def.Spec
	if s.Name != "docker.image.pull" || s.Version != 1 || s.Class != core.ClassCompensable || s.Side != core.SideAgent {
		t.Errorf("spec %+v, want docker.image.pull v1, compensable, agent-side", s)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(s.LockKeys, []string{"docker"}) || !s.LongRunning || s.ApplyTimeout != 30*time.Minute {
		t.Errorf("spec %+v, want lock key docker, long-running, a 30 minute ApplyTimeout", s)
	}
	if s.CompensatedBy != "" || s.ForwardOnly {
		t.Errorf("spec %+v: the undo handler is the only compensation", s)
	}
	if def.Handler.Plan == nil || def.Handler.Apply == nil || def.Handler.Verify == nil || def.Handler.Observe == nil || def.Handler.Inverse == nil {
		t.Errorf("handler %+v lacks Plan, Apply, Verify, Observe or Inverse", def.Handler)
	}
	if def.InputType != reflect.TypeFor[ImagePullInput]() || def.OutputType != reflect.TypeFor[PulledImage]() {
		t.Errorf("types %v -> %v, want ImagePullInput -> PulledImage", def.InputType, def.OutputType)
	}
}

func TestPLPlanDescribesThePullAndHashesTheLocalImage(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	def := h.dk().imagePull(newPullHub(h.clock))
	ctx := context.Background()

	absent, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), plInput(plRef))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	wantAbsent := []core.DiffLine{
		{Op: "+", Text: "pull image busybox:1.37 from its registry"},
		{Op: " ", Text: "image busybox:1.37 is not present locally"},
		{Op: " ", Text: "undo changes nothing: a pulled or re-pointed tag is not reverted"},
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(absent.Diff, wantAbsent) {
		t.Errorf("diff\n got %+v\nwant %+v", absent.Diff, wantAbsent)
	}
	if absent.Confirmation != "" || absent.StateHash == "" {
		t.Errorf("plan %+v, want no confirmation and a state hash", absent)
	}
	again, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), plInput(plRef))
	if err != nil || again.StateHash != absent.StateHash {
		t.Errorf("a second plan of the same state hashed %q, %v; want %q", again.StateHash, err, absent.StateHash)
	}

	img := plImage(plRef)
	h.docker.putImage(img)
	present, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), plInput(plRef))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	wantPresent := []core.DiffLine{
		{Op: "+", Text: "pull image busybox:1.37 from its registry"},
		{Op: " ", Text: "image busybox:1.37 is local as " + plShort(img.ID) + "; a moved tag is re-pointed to the pulled image"},
		{Op: " ", Text: "undo changes nothing: a pulled or re-pointed tag is not reverted"},
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(present.Diff, wantPresent) {
		t.Errorf("diff\n got %+v\nwant %+v", present.Diff, wantPresent)
	}
	if present.StateHash == absent.StateHash {
		t.Error("the state hash does not change when the local image appears")
	}
}

func TestPLPlanRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	for _, ref := range []string{"", " busybox", "bad ref", "busybox:", "a..b", "x?y", "x#y", "x%y", "a\tb"} {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		def := h.dk().imagePull(newPullHub(h.clock))
		_, err := def.Handler.Plan(context.Background(), h.env(""), plInput(ref))
		if got := plCode(t, err); got != errcode.InvalidInput {
			t.Errorf("reference %q: code %s, want %s", ref, got, errcode.InvalidInput)
		}
		if calls := h.docker.calls(); len(calls) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("reference %q reached the engine: %v", ref, calls)
		}
	}

	h := newDKHost(t)
	def := h.dk().imagePull(newPullHub(h.clock))
	h.docker.fail("InspectImage", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable)
	_, err := def.Handler.Plan(context.Background(), h.env(""), plInput(plRef))
	if got := plCode(t, err); got != errcode.DockerEngineUnavailable {
		t.Errorf("unreachable engine: code %s, want %s", got, errcode.DockerEngineUnavailable)
	}
}

func TestPLApplyPullsPublishesProgressAndReportsTheImage(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	hub := newPullHub(h.clock)
	def := h.dk().imagePull(hub)
	img := plImage(plRef)
	h.docker.putImage(img)
	h.docker.pulls = map[string][]dockerapi.PullMessage{plRef: {
		{Status: "Pulling from library/busybox", ID: "1.37"},
		{Status: "Downloading", ID: "abc", Progress: "[=>]", ProgressDetail: &dockerapi.ProgressDetail{Current: 10, Total: 100}},
		{Status: "Status: Downloaded newer image for busybox:1.37"},
	}}

	raw, err := def.Handler.Apply(context.Background(), h.env("chg1"), plInput(plRef))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var out PulledImage
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if want := (PulledImage{Image: plRef, ID: img.ID, Digests: img.RepoDigests}); !reflect.DeepEqual(out, want) {
		t.Errorf("output %+v, want %+v", out, want)
	}
	if got := h.docker.calls(); !slices.Equal(got, []string{"PullImage", "InspectImage"}) {
		t.Errorf("engine calls %v, want PullImage then InspectImage", got)
	}
	if effects := h.journal.effects(); len(effects) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("a pull journaled %d effects, want none", len(effects))
	}

	ch, stop := hub.subscribe(context.Background(), "chg1")
	defer stop()
	want := []PullEvent{
		{Status: "Pulling from library/busybox", ID: "1.37"},
		{Status: "Downloading", ID: "abc", Progress: "[=>]", Current: 10, Total: 100},
		{Status: "Status: Downloaded newer image for busybox:1.37"},
	}
	if got := plDrain(t, ch); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("events\n got %+v\nwant %+v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestPLApplyRefusalsFinishTheChange(t *testing.T) {
	for name, c := range map[string]struct {
		err  error
		want errcode.Code
	}{

			hub := newPullHub(h.clock)

	}
}

	if got := plDrain(t, ch); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {

}

func TestPLStreamEndsWithTheReader(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	hub := newPullHub(h.clock)
	def := h.dk().pullStreamDef(hub)

	gone := errors.New("reader gone")
	hub.publish("c1", PullEvent{Status: "a"})
	err := def.Run(context.Background(), h.env(""), json.RawMessage(`{"changeId":"c1"}`), func(any) error { return gone })
	if !errors.Is(err, gone) {
		t.Errorf("Run = %v, want the emit error", err)
	}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		done <- def.Run(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(`{"changeId":"c2"}`), func(any) error { return nil })
	}()
	cancel()
	select {
	case err := <-done:
		if !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
			t.Errorf("Run = %v, want context.Canceled", err)
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("Run did not return after its context ended")
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `pull.go`, the hub (`newPullHub(clock core.Clock) *pullHub`). One mutex guards a map from change id to a feed. A feed holds the last 256 events of its change (older ones are discarded as new ones arrive), a set of subscribers and a finished flag. A subscriber is a channel with capacity 1024 (a named constant `pullBuffer`).
   - `publish(changeID, e)`: creates the feed when absent; does nothing once the feed is finished; appends `e` to the backlog, trims it to 256, and sends `e` to every subscriber without blocking. A subscriber whose channel is full is closed and removed (it missed events and reconnects for the backlog), so publishing never waits for a reader.
   - `finish(changeID)`: creates the feed when absent (so a change that fails before its first event still ends its subscribers), does nothing when already finished, marks it finished, closes every subscriber channel, and arms `clock.AfterFunc(10*time.Minute, …)` that deletes that feed (only if the map still holds the same feed value).
   - `subscribe(ctx, changeID) (<-chan PullEvent, func())`: creates the feed when absent, puts a copy of the backlog into a new channel, and closes the channel at once when the feed is finished, else registers it for live events. A change nobody has published yet therefore waits for its first event. The returned stop function is idempotent and safe after the hub already closed the channel (never a double close): it removes the subscriber, closes the channel, and deletes the feed when it is unfinished with no events and no subscribers, so ids a client invents do not accumulate. `context.AfterFunc(ctx, stop)` ends the subscription when `ctx` ends; the stop function also stops that registration.
   - Everything is safe for concurrent use; no goroutine is started.
2. `image_pull.go`, a handler type holding the `dk` and the hub, defined with `core.DefineMutating[ImagePullInput, PulledImage]`. The spec sets `Name` `docker.image.pull`, `Version` 1, `Class` `core.ClassCompensable`, `Side` `core.SideAgent`, `LockKeys` `[]string{lockKey}`, `LongRunning` true and `ApplyTimeout` 30 minutes; it sets no `CompensatedBy` or `ForwardOnly` because the handler's `Inverse` is the compensation. A one-sentence `Summary` states that it pulls an image.
   - Reference rule (shared by `Plan`): `Image` is refused with `request.invalid_input`, wrapped `core.Definite`, before any Engine call when it is empty, contains a Unicode space or control character, any of `?`, `#`, `%`, contains `..`, or ends with `:` (the rules of `dockerapi`'s own check, which a pull must not reach).
   - `Plan`: apply the reference rule; `InspectImage(ref)`; a 404 (`dockerapi.IsNotFound`) means not present, any other error goes through `engineError("image", ref, err)`. The diff is exactly the three lines the test asserts, in that order: `+ pull image <ref> from its registry`; then a context line (op `" "`) that is `image <ref> is local as <short id>; a moved tag is re-pointed to the pulled image` when the image is local (the short id is its first 12 characters after removing a leading `sha256:`) and `image <ref> is not present locally` otherwise; then the context line `undo changes nothing: a pulled or re-pointed tag is not reverted`. `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 of the reference, a NUL byte and the local image id (empty when absent). No `Confirmation` (the action is compensable).
   - `Apply`: requires `env.ChangeID` (a plain error otherwise) and always runs `hub.finish(env.ChangeID)` on return, so subscribers end on every path. Call `PullImage(ctx, in.Image)` with the apply context (its deadline is the 30 minute `ApplyTimeout`); an error goes through `engineError("image", ref, err)`. `defer` the stream's `Close`. Read `Next()` until `io.EOF`: map each message to a `PullEvent` (`Status`, `ID`, `Progress`, and `Current` and `Total` from `ProgressDetail` when it is set) and `publish` it. Any other error ends the read: publish `PullEvent{Status: <the message's status>, ID: <its id>, Error: err.Error()}` and return `fmt.Errorf("docker: pull %s: %w", ref, err)`. After EOF, `InspectImage(ref)` (error through `engineError`) and return `PulledImage{Image: ref, ID: <inspect ID>, Digests: <a non-nil copy of RepoDigests>}`. No effect is journaled and no log line, event or error carries more than the registry's own message.
   - `Verify`: `InspectImage(in.Image)` must succeed (error through `engineError`); `out` is not consulted, because recovery calls it with a zero output.
   - `Observe` delegates to `k.observe` (the engine never calls it for this action, which journals nothing); `Inverse` returns `core.InverseResult{}` and a nil error without calling the Engine.
3. `func (k dk) pullStreamDef(h *pullHub) core.StreamDef` is `core.DefineStream[PullParams, PullEvent]("pull", …)`: an empty `ChangeID` is `request.invalid_input`; otherwise it subscribes with the stream's context, defers the stop function, emits each event in order, returns the `emit` error as soon as one occurs, returns nil when the channel closes because the change finished, and returns `ctx.Err()` when the channel closed because `ctx` ended.
4. Doc comments on every exported identifier of the contract; comments only for non-obvious reasons (why publish drops a slow subscriber, why `finish` creates a feed).

```go
package docker

)

const (
	ccDirMode  = fs.ModeDir | 0o755
	ccSimple   = `{"name":"shop","networks":{"default":{"name":"shop_default","ipam":{}}},"services":{"web":{"image":"nginx:1.27","networks":{"default":null}}}}`
	ccProvider = `{"name":"shop","services":{"web":{"provider":{"type":"model"}}}}`

// ccDiscover records a project through the labels its containers carry.
func ccDiscover(t *testing.T, h *dkHost, name, dir string, files, envFiles []string) projectRow {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	var tables int
	if err := h.db.Read().QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'docker_projects'`).Scan(&tables); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if tables == 0 {
		// The host database of newDKHost holds only the core tables.
		h.db = pjDB(t)
	}
	sum := dockerapi.ContainerSummary{
		ID: dkID(name + "-seed"), Names: []string{"/" + name + "-web-1"},
		Labels: map[string]string{
			"com.docker.compose.project":                  name,
			"com.docker.compose.project.working_dir":      dir,
			"com.docker.compose.project.config_files":     strings.Join(files, ","),
			"com.docker.compose.project.environment_file": strings.Join(envFiles, ","),
		},
	}
	if err := discoverProjects(ctx, h.db, h.clock.Now(), []dockerapi.ContainerSummary{sum}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	row, ok, err := loadProject(ctx, h.db, name)
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadProject(%s) = %v, %v", name, ok, err)
	}
	return row
}

// ccProject puts a valid project, the system plugin directory and the Compose
// plugin into the host's files, records the project, and returns its row. The
// project's directory is /srv/<name> with one Compose file and one env file,
// all owned by root.
func ccProject(t *testing.T, h *dkHost, name string) projectRow {
	t.Helper()
	dir := "/srv/" + name
	h.files["/srv"] = dkFile{Mode: ccDirMode}
	h.files[dir] = dkFile{Mode: ccDirMode}
	h.files[dir+"/compose.yaml"] = dkFile{Mode: 0o644, Data: []byte("services:\n  web:\n    image: nginx:1.27\n")}
	h.files[dir+"/.env"] = dkFile{Mode: 0o600, Data: []byte("TAG=1.27\n")}
	h.files[pluginDir] = dkFile{Mode: ccDirMode}
	h.files[pluginDir+"/docker-compose"] = dkFile{Mode: 0o755, Data: []byte("plugin")}
	return ccDiscover(t, h, name, dir, []string{dir + "/compose.yaml"}, []string{dir + "/.env"})
}

// ccConfig scripts the output of `config --format json` for a project.
func ccConfig(h *dkHost, p projectRow, profiles []string, stdout string) {
	h.results[strings.Join(composeArgs(p, profiles, "config", "--format", "json"), " ")] = core.CmdResult{Stdout: []byte(stdout)}
}

func ccRefused(t *testing.T, err error, code errcode.Code, detail ...string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("no error, want %s", code)
	}
	e := errcode.From(err)
	if e.Code != code {
		t.Fatalf("code %s (%s), want %s", e.Code, e.Detail, code)
	}
	for _, d := range detail {
		if !strings.Contains(e.Detail, d) {
			t.Errorf("detail %q does not contain %q", e.Detail, d)
		}
	}
	if !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Errorf("a refusal that committed nothing must be definite: %v", err)
	}
}

func ccPrepare(h *dkHost, name string, profiles *[]string) (composeRun, error) {
	return h.dk().prepareCompose(context.Background(), h.env(""), ComposeInput{Project: name, Profiles: profiles})
}

	h := newDKHost(t)

	ccConfig(h, p, []string{"debug"}, ccSimple)

	run, err := ccPrepare(h, "shop", &[]string{"debug"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(run.Profiles, []string{"debug"}) {
		t.Errorf("run.Profiles = %v, want [debug]", run.Profiles)
	}
	want := composeArgs(p, []string{"debug"}, "config", "--format", "json")
	if len(h.cmds) != 1 || !reflect.DeepEqual(h.cmds[0].Args, want) {
		t.Errorf("commands %+v, want one with %q", h.cmds, want)
	}
}

func TestCCPrepareUsesTheStoredProfilesAndShowsAChangedHash(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	ccProject(t, h, "shop")

		return setProjectRun(context.Background(), tx, "shop", []string{"web"}, "oldhash", h.clock.Now().Add(-time.Hour))
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	p, ok, err := loadProject(context.Background(), h.db, "shop")
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadProject = %v, %v", ok, err)
	}
	ccConfig(h, p, []string{"web"}, ccSimple)

	run, err := ccPrepare(h, "shop", nil)

		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(run.Profiles, []string{"web"}) || run.Project.RunHash != "oldhash" || run.Hash == "oldhash" {
		t.Errorf("run = %+v, want the stored profiles, the stored run hash and a new hash", run)
	}
}

func TestCCPrepareRefusesMalformedInput(t *testing.T) {
	bad := func(p ...string) *[]string { return &p }
	tests := []struct {
		name     string
		project  string
		profiles *[]string
	}{
		{"empty project", "", nil},
		{"project with a space", "my shop", nil},
		{"project that looks like a flag", "-x", nil},
		{"empty profile", "shop", bad("")},
		{"profile that looks like a flag", "shop", bad("-x")},
		{"profile with a space", "shop", bad("a b")},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		h := newDKHost(t)
		ccProject(t, h, "shop")
		_, err := ccPrepare(h, tc.project, tc.profiles)

			t.Errorf("%s: code %s, want %s", tc.name, got, errcode.InvalidInput)
		}

			t.Errorf("%s ran %v", tc.name, h.cmds)
		}
	}
}

func ccCode(err error) errcode.Code {
	if err == nil {
		return ""
	}
	return errcode.From(err).Code
}

func TestCCPrepareRefusesUnsafePaths(t *testing.T) {
	const dir = "/srv/shop"
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		mutate func(h *dkHost)
		detail []string // empty: accepted
	}{
		{"valid", func(h *dkHost) {}, nil},
		{"directory is a symlink", func(h *dkHost) { h.files[dir] = dkFile{Symlink: true, Mode: 0o777} }, []string{dir, "symlink"}},
		{"parent is a symlink", func(h *dkHost) { h.files["/srv"] = dkFile{Symlink: true, Mode: 0o777} }, []string{"/srv", "symlink"}},
		{"compose file is a symlink", func(h *dkHost) { h.files[dir+"/compose.yaml"] = dkFile{Symlink: true, Mode: 0o777} }, []string{dir + "/compose.yaml", "symlink"}},
		{"compose file is missing", func(h *dkHost) { delete(h.files, dir+"/compose.yaml") }, []string{dir + "/compose.yaml", "does not exist"}},
		{"env file is missing", func(h *dkHost) { delete(h.files, dir+"/.env") }, []string{dir + "/.env", "does not exist"}},
		{"compose file is a directory", func(h *dkHost) { h.files[dir+"/compose.yaml"] = dkFile{Mode: ccDirMode} }, []string{dir + "/compose.yaml", "not a regular file"}},
		{"directory is a file", func(h *dkHost) { h.files[dir] = dkFile{Mode: 0o644} }, []string{dir, "not a directory"}},
		{"file owned by a stranger", func(h *dkHost) {
			h.files[dir+"/compose.yaml"] = dkFile{Mode: 0o644, UID: 1001, Data: []byte("services: {}\n")}
		}, []string{dir + "/compose.yaml", "owned by"}},
		{"files owned by the directory's owner", func(h *dkHost) {
			h.files[dir] = dkFile{Mode: ccDirMode, UID: 1000}
			h.files[dir+"/compose.yaml"] = dkFile{Mode: 0o644, UID: 1000, Data: []byte("services: {}\n")}
			h.files[dir+"/.env"] = dkFile{Mode: 0o600, UID: 1000, Data: []byte("A=1\n")}
		}, nil},
		{"file owned by neither root nor the directory's owner", func(h *dkHost) {
			h.files[dir] = dkFile{Mode: ccDirMode, UID: 1000}
			h.files[dir+"/compose.yaml"] = dkFile{Mode: 0o644, UID: 1001, Data: []byte("services: {}\n")}
		}, []string{dir + "/compose.yaml", "owned by"}},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			p := ccProject(t, h, "shop")
			tc.mutate(h)
			ccConfig(h, p, nil, ccSimple)
			_, err := ccPrepare(h, "shop", nil)
			if tc.detail == nil {
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("prepareCompose = %v, want success", err)
				}
				return
			}
			ccRefused(t, err, errcode.DockerComposeUnavailable, tc.detail...)
			if len(h.cmds) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("an unsafe project ran %v", h.cmds)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCCPrepareReportsAFailedConfigWithoutLeakingOutput(t *testing.T) {
	long := strings.Repeat("Z", 500)
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		res    core.CmdResult
		detail []string
		absent []string
	}{
		{"non-zero exit", core.CmdResult{ExitCode: 1, Stderr: []byte("warning: first line\nservice \"web\" refers to undefined network front\n\n")},
			[]string{"exit status 1", `service "web" refers to undefined network front`}, []string{"first line"}},
		{"long stderr line", core.CmdResult{ExitCode: 15, Stderr: []byte(long + "\n")}, []string{"exit status 15", "ZZZZ"}, nil},
		{"unreadable output", core.CmdResult{Stdout: []byte(`{"name":"shop","services":"SECRET_TOKEN_VALUE"}`)},
			[]string{"resolved configuration"}, []string{"SECRET_TOKEN_VALUE"}},
		{"not JSON", core.CmdResult{Stdout: []byte("SECRET_TOKEN_VALUE")}, []string{"resolved configuration"}, []string{"SECRET_TOKEN_VALUE"}},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			p := ccProject(t, h, "shop")
			h.results[strings.Join(composeArgs(p, nil, "config", "--format", "json"), " ")] = tc.res
			_, err := ccPrepare(h, "shop", nil)
			ccRefused(t, err, errcode.DockerComposeUnavailable, tc.detail...)
			d := errcode.From(err).Detail
			for _, a := range tc.absent {
				if strings.Contains(d, a) {
					t.Errorf("detail %q contains %q", d, a)
				}
			}
			if n := strings.Count(d, "Z"); n > 300 {
				t.Errorf("detail carries %d bytes of stderr, want at most 300", n)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCCPrepareAppliesTheConfigurationRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {

		detail []string
	}{

		{"build without a local image", ccBuild, nil, errcode.DockerComposeUnavailable, []string{"web", "build"}},

		{"external owned network", ccOwnedNet, func(h *dkHost) {
			h.docker.putNetwork(dkNetwork("npm_net", func(n *dockerapi.Network) { n.Labels = map[string]string{core.LabelModule: "npm"} }))
		}, errcode.DockerOwned, []string{"npm_net", "npm"}},
		{"external network of nobody", ccOwnedNet, func(h *dkHost) { h.docker.putNetwork(dkNetwork("npm_net")) }, "", nil},
		{"engine down while the owners are read", ccOwnedNet, func(h *dkHost) { h.docker.fail("ListNetworks", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable) }, errcode.DockerEngineUnavailable, nil},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			p := ccProject(t, h, "shop")
			ccConfig(h, p, nil, tc.config)

				tc.setup(h)
			}
			_, err := ccPrepare(h, "shop", nil)
			if tc.code == "" {
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("prepareCompose = %v, want success", err)
				}
				return
			}
			if tc.code == errcode.DockerEngineUnavailable {
				if got := ccCode(err); got != tc.code {
					t.Errorf("code %s, want %s", got, tc.code)
				}
				return
			}
			ccRefused(t, err, tc.code, tc.detail...)
		})
	}
}

func TestCCPlanComposeRendersWhatTheRunDoes(t *testing.T) {
	old, now := strings.Repeat("a", 64), strings.Repeat("b", 64)
	project := projectRow{Name: "shop", Directory: "/srv/shop", Files: []string{"/srv/shop/a.yaml", "/srv/shop/b.yaml"}, EnvFiles: []string{"/srv/shop/.env"}, RunHash: old}
	head := []core.DiffLine{
		{Op: " ", Text: "runs the project's Compose file as root"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "docker compose up for project shop"},
		{Op: " ", Text: "directory /srv/shop"},
		{Op: " ", Text: "file /srv/shop/a.yaml"},
		{Op: " ", Text: "file /srv/shop/b.yaml"},
		{Op: " ", Text: "env file /srv/shop/.env"},
	}
	withProfile := append(ccClone(head), core.DiffLine{Op: " ", Text: "profile debug"})
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		run  composeRun
		want []core.DiffLine
	}{
		{"hash unchanged", composeRun{Project: project, Hash: old}, head},
		{"never run before", composeRun{Project: func() projectRow { p := project; p.RunHash = ""; return p }(), Hash: now}, head},
		{"profiles", composeRun{Project: project, Hash: old, Profiles: []string{"debug"}}, withProfile},
		{"hash changed", composeRun{Project: project, Hash: now}, append(ccClone(head),
			core.DiffLine{Op: "-", Text: "config hash aaaaaaaaaaaa"}, core.DiffLine{Op: "+", Text: "config hash bbbbbbbbbbbb"})},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		if got := planCompose(tc.run, "up"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tc.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s\n got %+v\nwant %+v", tc.name, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func ccClone(l []core.DiffLine) []core.DiffLine { return append([]core.DiffLine(nil), l...) }
```

`ccProject` records the project through `discoverProjects` from the compose labels of a container summary (so the row's format is Task 26's), and places in `h.files` the entries `/srv`, `/srv/<name>`, its `compose.yaml` and `.env`, the plugin directory and the `docker-compose` plugin, all root-owned. Task 41's tests call it to get a project that passes every check.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the tests to verify they fail**

Run: `mkdir -p /root/.cache/w3-tmp/38 && export TMPDIR=/root/.cache/w3-tmp/38 GOTOOLCHAIN=local && timeout 300 go test -count=1 -run 'TestCC' ./internal/modules/docker/`
Expected: FAIL to build, `undefined: dockerConfigDir` (and `pluginDir`, `ownedPaths`, `composeRun`, `prepareCompose`, `composeArgs`, `planCompose`).

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. Constants and `ownedPaths()` as Contracts gives them: `dockerConfigDir` `/var/lib/darkpanel/agent/docker-config`, `pluginDir` `/usr/libexec/docker/cli-plugins`, and `ownedPaths()` returning one `core.OwnedPath{Path: dockerConfigDir, Kind: core.OwnedManagedDir, Pattern: `^config\.json$`}`.
2. `composeArgs(p, profiles, verb...)` returns `compose`, `--project-directory`, `p.Directory`, `-p`, `p.Name`, then `-f <file>` for each of `p.Files`, `--env-file <file>` for each of `p.EnvFiles`, `--profile <name>` for each of `profiles`, then the verb arguments, in exactly that order (the exec allowlist accepts no other order).
3. A small helper `refuse(code, format, args...)` returns `core.Definite(errcode.New(code, …))`. Every refusal below is `docker.compose_unavailable` unless it says otherwise, and no detail contains file contents, environment values or `config` output. All filesystem reads go through `k.d.lstat` and `k.d.readFile`; the owner of a path is `info.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t).Uid`, and a `Sys()` of any other type is refused with `<path> has no readable owner`.
4. `prepareCompose(ctx, env, in)` runs these steps in order, stopping at the first refusal, and runs no program until step 8:
   1. Syntax: `in.Project` must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` and each given profile `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$`, else `request.invalid_input` (wrapped `core.Definite`) naming the field (`project` or `profiles/<index>`).
   2. A project name starting with `darkpanel` is refused with `docker.owned`, detail `project <name> is reserved for Darkpanel`.
   3. `loadProject(ctx, env.DB, in.Project)`; absent is refused with `project <name> is not known on this host; start it once so that discovery records it`.
   4. Paths (the directory, every compose file and every env file). A path that is not absolute is refused with `<path> is not absolute`; one that differs from `filepath.Clean(path)` with `<path> is not a clean path`. Then each prefix of the path below `/` is `lstat`ed in turn: missing is `<prefix> does not exist` (`fs.ErrNotExist`; any other `lstat` error is returned wrapped), a symlink is `<prefix> is a symlink`. The directory must be a directory (`<path> is not a directory`), each file a regular file (`<path> is not a regular file`), and each file must be owned by uid 0 or by the directory's owner (`<path> is owned by uid <n>, not root or the directory's owner`). Then `hash := k.configHash(row)`; an empty hash is refused with `the files of project <name> cannot be read`.
   5. `docker-config`: `lstat(dockerConfigDir)`; absent is accepted (Task 41 creates it). Otherwise it must not be a symlink (`<dir> is a symlink`), must be a directory, and must be owned by uid 0 (`<dir> is owned by uid <n>, not root`); `lstat(dockerConfigDir + "/cli-plugins")` must be absent (`<dir>/cli-plugins must not exist`); `config.json` read through `k.d.readFile` when present (a read error other than not-exist is refused) must be a JSON object (`<path> is not a JSON object`) without the members `credsStore`, `credHelpers` and `cliPluginsExtraDirs` (`<path> must not set <member>`).
   6. Plugins: `pluginDir` and `pluginDir + "/docker-compose"` must exist (`<path> does not exist`; for the plugin add `; install the Docker Compose plugin`), must not be symlinks, must be owned by uid 0 (`<path> is owned by uid <n>, not root`), and must not have the group or other write bit (`<path> is writable by its group or others`); the directory must be a directory and the plugin a regular file.
   7. Containers: `ListContainers` with `All` true and the filter `label=com.docker.compose.project=<name>`, then keep only summaries whose `com.docker.compose.project` label equals the project (the daemon's filter is not relied on; test fakes may ignore it). A kept summary with a `core.LabelModule` label is refused with `refuseOwned("container", <name without "/">, labels)`. A list error goes through `engineError`.
   8. Run `env.Exec.Run(ctx, core.Cmd{Path: "/usr/bin/docker", Args: composeArgs(row, profiles, "config", "--format", "json")})` where `profiles` is `*in.Profiles` when given, else the stored list (an empty non-nil slice when none). A `Run` error is returned wrapped as `docker: run compose config: %w`. A non-zero exit is refused with `docker compose config failed with exit status <n>: <last non-empty line of stderr, cut to at most 300 bytes>` (just `…exit status <n>` when stderr is empty). Stdout is never put in a detail.
   9. `compose.Parse(stdout)`; a parse error is refused with the fixed text `the resolved configuration of project <name> could not be read`, the cause kept as the error's hidden cause only.
   10. `compose.Validate(in.Project, cfg, compose.Facts{…})` with `ImagePresent` true when `InspectImage(ref)` succeeds, and `Owner(kind, name)` answering the object's `core.LabelModule` label (`ownerOf`): kind `container` from `ListContainers` (All) by an exact match of `"/"+name` in `Names`; `network` from `ListNetworks` filtered by `name` with an exact `Name` match on the result; `volume` from `InspectVolume(name)`. A not-found answer means absent (`""`/false). Any other Engine error is remembered (the first one) and answered as absent; after `Validate` returns, a remembered Engine error is returned through `engineError` in preference to `Validate`'s own result, so an Engine outage never passes or fails a project for the wrong reason. Otherwise return `Validate`'s error unchanged.
   11. Return `composeRun{Project: row, Profiles: profiles, Hash: hash, Config: cfg}`.

`internal/modules/tailnet/client_test.go`:

```go
package tailnet

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/cloud/cloudfake"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/tailnet/fake"
)

// tnWith points a tn at the fake server, with a sleep that returns at once so
// that retries do not wait.
func tnWith(srv *fake.Server) tn {
	return tn{
		d: deps{
			baseURL: srv.URL(),
			http:    srv.Client(),
			sleep:   func(context.Context, time.Duration) error { return nil },
		},
		tokens: newTokenCache(),
	}
}

func apClock() *coretest.FakeClock {
	return coretest.NewFakeClock(time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))
}

// apAPI builds an api for the fake's tailnet with the given client secret.
func apAPI(t *testing.T, tnv tn, secret string, clock core.Clock) *api {
	t.Helper()
	a, err := tnv.newAPI(account{ID: "acc1", Tailnet: fake.Tailnet, ClientID: fake.ClientID}, []byte(secret), clock)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("newAPI: %v", err)
	}
	return a
}

// apFake returns a fake server and an api for it.
func apFake(t *testing.T) (*fake.Server, *api) {
	t.Helper()
	srv := fake.New(t)
	return srv, apAPI(t, tnWith(srv), fake.ClientSecret, apClock())
}

func apTailnet(p string) string { return "/api/v2/tailnet/" + fake.Tailnet + p }

func apCode(t *testing.T, err error) errcode.Code {
	t.Helper()
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("no error")
	}
	return errcode.From(err).Code
}

func apRequests(srv *fake.Server, method, path string) []cloudfake.Request {
	var out []cloudfake.Request
	for _, r := range srv.Cloud().Requests() {
		if r.Method == method && r.Path == path {
			out = append(out, r)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// apAnswer queues one answer in place of the fake's handler.
func apAnswer(srv *fake.Server, method, path string, status int, body string) {
	srv.Cloud().Fail(method, path, cloudfake.Fault{Status: status, Body: body})
}

func apSameJSON(t *testing.T, got []byte, want string) {
	t.Helper()
	var g, w any
	if len(got) == 0 {
		g = nil
	} else if err := json.Unmarshal(got, &g); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("request body %q is not JSON: %v", got, err)
	}
	if want != "" {
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(want), &w); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(g, w) {
		t.Errorf("request body %s, want %s", got, want)
	}
}

func TestAPIdAddressedCalls(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	calls := []struct {
		name        string
		call        func(a *api, id string) error
		method      string
		path        string // for id "n1"
		body        string
		definite404 bool
	}{
		{"authorize", func(a *api, id string) error { return a.Authorize(ctx, id, true) }, http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/device/n1/authorized", `{"authorized":true}`, true},
		{"deauthorize", func(a *api, id string) error { return a.Authorize(ctx, id, false) }, http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/device/n1/authorized", `{"authorized":false}`, true},
		{"expire", func(a *api, id string) error { return a.Expire(ctx, id) }, http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/device/n1/expire", "", true},
		{"delete device", func(a *api, id string) error { return a.DeleteDevice(ctx, id) }, http.MethodDelete, "/api/v2/device/n1", "", false},
		{"delete key", func(a *api, id string) error { return a.DeleteKey(ctx, id) }, http.MethodDelete, apTailnet("/keys/n1"), "", false},
	}
	for _, c := range calls {
		t.Run(c.name+" sends", func(t *testing.T) {
			srv, a := apFake(t)
			apAnswer(srv, c.method, c.path, 200, "")
			if err := c.call(a, "n1"); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			reqs := apRequests(srv, c.method, c.path)
			if len(reqs) != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("%d requests to %s %s, want 1", len(reqs), c.method, c.path)
			}
			apSameJSON(t, reqs[0].Body, c.body)
		})
		t.Run(c.name+" maps 404 to not_found", func(t *testing.T) {
			srv, a := apFake(t)
			apAnswer(srv, c.method, c.path, 404, `{"message":"not found"}`)
			err := c.call(a, "n1")
			if got := apCode(t, err); got != errcode.NotFound {
				t.Errorf("code %s, want %s", got, errcode.NotFound)
			}
			if core.IsDefinite(err) != c.definite404 {
				t.Errorf("IsDefinite = %v, want %v", core.IsDefinite(err), c.definite404)
			}
		})
		t.Run(c.name+" refuses an empty id", func(t *testing.T) {
			srv, a := apFake(t)
			err := c.call(a, "")
			if got := apCode(t, err); got != errcode.InvalidInput || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
				t.Errorf("code %s definite %v, want request.invalid_input and definite", got, core.IsDefinite(err))
			}
			for _, r := range srv.Cloud().Requests() {
				if r.Path != "/api/v2/oauth/token" {
					t.Errorf("request %s %s sent for an empty id", r.Method, r.Path)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAPCreateKeySendsTheRequestAndTheProviderStoresIt(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apFake(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	const desc = "darkpanel-01J00000000000000000000001"
	created, err := a.CreateKey(ctx, KeyRequest{Description: desc, Tags: []string{"tag:server"}, Reusable: true, Preauthorized: true, ExpirySeconds: 3600})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if created.ID == "" || created.Key == "" || created.Description != desc {
		t.Errorf("CreatedKey = %+v, want an id, a secret and the description %s", created, desc)
	}
	if got := len(srv.Keys()); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the provider holds %d keys, want 1", got)
	}
	info, err := a.Key(ctx, created.ID)
	if err != nil || info.Description != desc {
		t.Errorf("Key(%s) = %+v, %v; want the description %s", created.ID, info, err, desc)
	}
	list, err := a.Keys(ctx)
	if err != nil || len(list) != 1 || list[0].ID != created.ID {
		t.Errorf("Keys = %+v, %v; want the created key", list, err)
	}

	if _, err := a.CreateKey(ctx, KeyRequest{Description: desc + "2", Tags: []string{"tag:server"}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	posts := apRequests(srv, http.MethodPost, apTailnet("/keys"))
	if len(posts) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("%d key creations, want 2", len(posts))
	}
	apSameJSON(t, posts[0].Body, `{"capabilities":{"devices":{"create":{"reusable":true,"ephemeral":false,"preauthorized":true,"tags":["tag:server"]}}},
	 "expirySeconds":3600,"description":"`+desc+`"}`)
	apSameJSON(t, posts[1].Body, `{"capabilities":{"devices":{"create":{"reusable":false,"ephemeral":false,"preauthorized":false,"tags":["tag:server"]}}},
	 "description":"`+desc+`2"}`)

	if err := a.DeleteKey(ctx, created.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := len(srv.Keys()); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("the provider holds %d keys after the delete, want 1", got)
	}
}

func TestAPPolicyRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apFake(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	first := "// owners\n{\n\t\"acls\": [],\n}\n"
	etag := srv.SetPolicy(first)
	text, gotETag, err := a.Policy(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if string(text) != first || gotETag != etag {
		t.Errorf("Policy = %q, %q; want %q, %q", text, gotETag, first, etag)
	}
	if reqs := apRequests(srv, http.MethodGet, apTailnet("/acl")); len(reqs) != 1 || reqs[0].Header.Get("Accept") != "application/hujson" {
		t.Errorf("policy read requests %+v, want one with Accept application/hujson", reqs)
	}

	next := "{\n\t// changed\n\t\"acls\": [],\n}\n"
	newETag, err := a.SetPolicy(ctx, []byte(next), etag)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if newETag == "" || newETag == etag {
		t.Errorf("new ETag %q, want one different from %q", newETag, etag)
	}
	if stored, storedETag := srv.Policy(); stored != next || storedETag != newETag {
		t.Errorf("provider policy %q (%q), want %q (%q)", stored, storedETag, next, newETag)
	}
	posts := apRequests(srv, http.MethodPost, apTailnet("/acl"))
	if len(posts) != 1 || posts[0].Header.Get("If-Match") != etag ||
		posts[0].Header.Get("Content-Type") != "application/hujson" || string(posts[0].Body) != next {
		t.Errorf("policy write requests %+v, want one with If-Match %q, hujson content and the new text", posts, etag)
	}
}

func TestAPSetPolicyWithAStaleETagIsADefiniteConflict(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apFake(t)
	stale := srv.SetPolicy("{}")
	srv.SetPolicy("{\"acls\": []}")
	_, err := a.SetPolicy(context.Background(), []byte("{\"groups\": {}}"), stale)
	if got := apCode(t, err); got != errcode.TailnetPolicyConflict {
		t.Errorf("code %s, want %s", got, errcode.TailnetPolicyConflict)
	}
	if !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Error("a 412 refusal committed nothing and must be definite")
	}
	if text, _ := srv.Policy(); text != "{\"acls\": []}" {
		t.Errorf("provider policy %q changed by a refused write", text)
	}
}

func TestAPPolicyAnswersWithoutAnETag(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apFake(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	apAnswer(srv, http.MethodGet, apTailnet("/acl"), 200, "{}")
	_, _, err := a.Policy(ctx)
	if got := apCode(t, err); got != errcode.CloudUnavailable {
		t.Errorf("Policy without an ETag: code %s, want %s", got, errcode.CloudUnavailable)
	}

	apAnswer(srv, http.MethodPost, apTailnet("/acl"), 200, "{}")
	_, err = a.SetPolicy(ctx, []byte("{}"), `"e1"`)
	if got := apCode(t, err); got != errcode.CloudUncertainOutcome {
		t.Errorf("SetPolicy without an ETag: code %s, want %s", got, errcode.CloudUncertainOutcome)
	}
	if core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Error("a write the provider accepted is not definite")
	}
}

func TestAPSetPolicyRequiresIfMatch(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apFake(t)
	_, err := a.SetPolicy(context.Background(), []byte("{}"), "")
	if got := apCode(t, err); got != errcode.InvalidInput || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Errorf("code %s definite %v, want request.invalid_input and definite", got, core.IsDefinite(err))
	}
	if n := len(apRequests(srv, http.MethodPost, apTailnet("/acl"))); n != 0 {
		t.Errorf("%d policy writes sent without an ETag", n)
	}
}

func TestAPValidatePolicy(t *testing.T) {
	const bad = `{"message":"unknown tag tag:nope","data":[{"user":"a","errors":["x"]}]}`
	path := apTailnet("/acl/validate")
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		status int // 0: the fake answers
		body   string
		want   errcode.Code // "" is valid
		detail string
	}{
		{"the fake accepts a valid policy", 0, "", "", ""},
		{"an empty 200 is valid", 200, "", "", ""},
		{"a 200 with an empty object is valid", 200, "{}", "", ""},
		{"a 200 with a message is invalid", 200, bad, errcode.TailnetPolicyInvalid, "unknown tag tag:nope"},
		{"a 400 with a message is invalid", 400, bad, errcode.TailnetPolicyInvalid, "unknown tag tag:nope"},
		{"a 400 without a message is invalid", 400, "not json", errcode.TailnetPolicyInvalid, "rejected"},
		{"a 403 is a missing permission", 403, `{"message":"forbidden"}`, errcode.CloudPermissionMissing, ""},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			srv, a := apFake(t)
			if tc.status != 0 {
				apAnswer(srv, http.MethodPost, path, tc.status, tc.body)
			}
			text := "// c\n{\"acls\": []}\n"
			err := a.ValidatePolicy(context.Background(), []byte(text))
			if tc.want == "" {
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("ValidatePolicy = %v, want nil", err)
				}
			} else {
				if got := apCode(t, err); got != tc.want {
					t.Fatalf("code %s, want %s", got, tc.want)
				}
				if d := errcode.From(err).Detail; !strings.Contains(d, tc.detail) {
					t.Errorf("detail %q does not contain %q", d, tc.detail)
				}
				if tc.want == errcode.TailnetPolicyInvalid && !core.IsDefinite(err) {
					t.Error("an invalid policy committed nothing and must be definite")
				}
			}
			posts := apRequests(srv, http.MethodPost, path)
			if len(posts) != 1 || string(posts[0].Body) != text || posts[0].Header.Get("Content-Type") != "application/hujson" {
				t.Errorf("validate requests %+v, want one with the text as hujson", posts)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAPScopesLimitWhatTheClientMayCall(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apFake(t)

	if _, err := a.Devices(context.Background()); err != nil {

}

func TestAPReadsAreRetriedAndWritesAreNot(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apFake(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	srv.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodGet, apTailnet("/devices"), cloudfake.Fault{Status: 503})
	if _, err := a.Devices(ctx); err != nil {

	if got := apCode(t, err); got != errcode.CloudUncertainOutcome {
		t.Errorf("SetRoutes after a 503: code %s, want %s", got, errcode.CloudUncertainOutcome)
	}
	if n := len(apRequests(srv, http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/device/n1/routes")); n != 1 {
		t.Errorf("%d route writes, want 1", n)
	}
}
```

```go
package tailnet

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/cloud/cloudfake"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/tailnet/fake"
)

// apFetcher is a token source that counts its calls.
type apFetcher struct {
	calls atomic.Int32
	ttl   time.Duration
	err   error
}

func (f *apFetcher) fetch(context.Context) (string, time.Duration, error) {
	n := f.calls.Add(1)
	if f.err != nil {
		return "", 0, f.err
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("tok%d", n), f.ttl, nil
}

func TestAPTokenCacheRenewsAtFiftyMinutes(t *testing.T) {
	base := time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		ttl     time.Duration
		elapsed time.Duration
		want    string
	}{
		{"just under 50 minutes", time.Hour, 49*time.Minute + 59*time.Second, "tok1"},
		{"at 50 minutes", time.Hour, 50 * time.Minute, "tok2"},
		{"a token that lives 10 minutes is renewed at 10", 10 * time.Minute, 10 * time.Minute, "tok2"},
		{"a token that lives 10 minutes is kept at 9", 10 * time.Minute, 9 * time.Minute, "tok1"},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			c, f := newTokenCache(), &apFetcher{ttl: tc.ttl}
			if got, err := c.token(context.Background(), "client", f.fetch, base); err != nil || got != "tok1" {
				t.Fatalf("first token = %q, %v; want tok1", got, err)
			}
			got, err := c.token(context.Background(), "client", f.fetch, base.Add(tc.elapsed))
			if err != nil || got != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("token after %s = %q, %v; want %s", tc.elapsed, got, err, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAPTokenCacheKeepsKeysApart(t *testing.T) {
	now := time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	c, f := newTokenCache(), &apFetcher{ttl: time.Hour}
	a, _ := c.token(context.Background(), "a", f.fetch, now)
	b, _ := c.token(context.Background(), "b", f.fetch, now)
	a2, _ := c.token(context.Background(), "a", f.fetch, now)
	if a == b || a != a2 || f.calls.Load() != 2 {
		t.Errorf("tokens a=%q b=%q a again=%q after %d fetches, want two fetches and a reused", a, b, a2, f.calls.Load())
	}
}

func TestAPTokenCacheDoesNotKeepFailures(t *testing.T) {
	now := time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	c, f := newTokenCache(), &apFetcher{ttl: time.Hour, err: errors.New("down")}
	if _, err := c.token(context.Background(), "a", f.fetch, now); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("token succeeded while the fetch failed")
	}
	f.err = nil
	if got, err := c.token(context.Background(), "a", f.fetch, now); err != nil || got != "tok2" {
		t.Errorf("token after the failure = %q, %v; want a new fetch, tok2", got, err)
	}
}

func TestAPTokenCacheFetchesOnceForConcurrentCallers(t *testing.T) {
	now := time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	c, f := newTokenCache(), &apFetcher{ttl: time.Hour}
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	got := make([]string, 8)
	for i := range got {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			got[i], _ = c.token(context.Background(), "a", f.fetch, now)
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	if f.calls.Load() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("%d fetches, want 1", f.calls.Load())
	}
	for _, g := range got {
		if g != "tok1" {
			t.Errorf("a caller got %q, want tok1", g)
		}
	}
}

func TestAPTokenRequestShapeAndRenewal(t *testing.T) {
	srv := fake.New(t)
	clock := apClock()
	a := apAPI(t, tnWith(srv), fake.ClientSecret, clock)
	ctx := context.Background()
	if devices, err := a.Devices(ctx); err != nil || len(devices) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Devices = %v, %v; want none", devices, err)
	}

	tokenReqs := apRequests(srv, http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/oauth/token")
	if len(tokenReqs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d token requests, want 1", len(tokenReqs))
	}
	tr := tokenReqs[0]
	form, err := url.ParseQuery(string(tr.Body))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	wantForm := url.Values{"client_id": {fake.ClientID}, "client_secret": {fake.ClientSecret}, "grant_type": {"client_credentials"}}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(form, wantForm) {
		t.Errorf("token form %v, want %v", form, wantForm)
	}
	if ct := tr.Header.Get("Content-Type"); ct != "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" {
		t.Errorf("token Content-Type %q, want application/x-www-form-urlencoded", ct)
	}
	if tr.Header.Get("Authorization") != "" {
		t.Error("the token request carries an Authorization header")
	}
	dev := apRequests(srv, http.MethodGet, apTailnet("/devices"))
	if len(dev) != 1 || !strings.HasPrefix(dev[0].Header.Get("Authorization"), "Bearer ") || len(dev[0].Header.Get("Authorization")) <= len("Bearer ") {
		t.Errorf("device requests %+v, want one with a bearer token", dev)
	}

	if _, err := a.Devices(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if n := srv.Tokens(); n != 1 {
		t.Errorf("%d tokens issued after two calls, want 1", n)
	}
	clock.Advance(50 * time.Minute)
	if _, err := a.Devices(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if n := srv.Tokens(); n != 2 {
		t.Errorf("%d tokens issued after 50 minutes, want 2", n)
	}
}

func TestAPTokenIsKeyedByTheSecretToo(t *testing.T) {
	const wrong = "wrong-secret-value"
	srv := fake.New(t)
	shared := tnWith(srv)
	clock := apClock()
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, err := apAPI(t, shared, fake.ClientSecret, clock).Devices(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	srv.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/oauth/token", cloudfake.Fault{Status: http.StatusUnauthorized, Body: `{"error":"invalid_client"}`})
	_, err := apAPI(t, shared, wrong, clock).Devices(ctx)
	if got := apCode(t, err); got != errcode.CloudAuthFailed {
		t.Fatalf("code %s, want %s: a changed secret must not reuse the cached token", got, errcode.CloudAuthFailed)
	}
	if strings.Contains(err.Error(), wrong) || strings.Contains(errcode.From(err).Detail, wrong) {
		t.Errorf("the error %q carries the client secret", err)
	}
	if n := len(apRequests(srv, http.MethodGet, apTailnet("/devices"))); n != 1 {
		t.Errorf("%d device reads, want only the first call's", n)
	}
}

func TestAPTokenEndpointFailureIsUnavailableAndDefinite(t *testing.T) {
	srv, a := apFake(t)
	srv.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/oauth/token", cloudfake.Fault{Status: http.StatusInternalServerError})
	_, err := a.Devices(context.Background())
	if got := apCode(t, err); got != errcode.CloudUnavailable {
		t.Errorf("code %s, want %s", got, errcode.CloudUnavailable)
	}
	if !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Error("a call that never reached the API is definite")
	}
	if n := len(apRequests(srv, http.MethodGet, apTailnet("/devices"))); n != 0 {
		t.Errorf("%d device reads sent without a token", n)
	}
}
```

```go
package tailnet

import (

func TestAPWireShapesKeepTheirJSONMembers(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		v    any
		want string
	}{
		{"connect input", ConnectInput{Tailnet: "example.com", ClientID: "c", ClientSecret: "s", TagsAllowed: []string{"tag:a"}},
			`{"tailnet":"example.com","clientId":"c","clientSecret":"s","tagsAllowed":["tag:a"]}`},
		{"account view", AccountView{Tailnet: "example.com", ClientID: "c", TagsAllowed: []string{"tag:a"},
			Capabilities: []cloud.Capability{{Name: "devices", State: "ok"}}, ConnectedAt: time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)},
			`{"tailnet":"example.com","clientId":"c","tagsAllowed":["tag:a"],"capabilities":[{"name":"devices","state":"ok"}],"connectedAt":"2026-10-30T12:00:00Z"}`},
		{"disconnect input", DisconnectInput{AbandonCleanup: true}, `{"abandonCleanup":true}`},
		{"disconnect input default", DisconnectInput{}, `{}`},
		{"disconnected", Disconnected{Abandoned: []string{"k1"}}, `{"abandoned":["k1"]}`},
		{"account status", AccountStatus{}, `{"connected":false}`},
		{"device", Device{}, `{"id":"","name":"","hostname":"","os":"","user":"","addresses":null,"tags":null,"authorized":false,` +
			`"keyExpiryDisabled":false,"advertisedRoutes":null,"enabledRoutes":null,"exitNode":false,"exitNodeEnabled":false}`},
		{"device routes", DeviceRoutes{Advertised: []string{"a"}, Enabled: []string{}}, `{"advertisedRoutes":["a"],"enabledRoutes":[]}`},
		{"set routes input", SetRoutesInput{Device: "n1", Routes: []string{"a"}}, `{"device":"n1","routes":["a"]}`},
		{"device ref", DeviceRef{ID: "n1", Name: "web"}, `{"id":"n1","name":"web"}`},
		{"auth key input", AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:a"}}, `{"tags":["tag:a"]}`},
		{"auth key input full", AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:a"}, Reusable: true, Ephemeral: true, Preauthorized: true, ExpirySeconds: 60},
			`{"tags":["tag:a"],"reusable":true,"ephemeral":true,"preauthorized":true,"expirySeconds":60}`},
		{"created key", CreatedKey{ID: "k", Key: "s", Expires: time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 13, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC), Description: "d"},
			`{"id":"k","key":"s","expires":"2026-10-30T13:00:00Z","description":"d"}`},
		{"auth key row", AuthKeyRow{Description: "d", Kind: "change", OwnerID: "o", State: "live"},
			`{"description":"d","kind":"change","ownerId":"o","state":"live","requestedAt":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z","expires":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`},
		{"policy", Policy{Text: "t", ETag: "e"}, `{"text":"t","etag":"e"}`},
		{"policy set input", PolicySetInput{Text: "t"}, `{"text":"t"}`},
		{"policy patch input", PolicyPatchInput{Edits: []policy.Edit{{Op: "set", Path: "/a", Value: json.RawMessage("1")}}},
			`{"edits":[{"op":"set","path":"/a","value":1}]}`},
		{"policy written", PolicyWritten{ETag: "e"}, `{"etag":"e"}`},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got, err := json.Marshal(tc.v)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if string(got) != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("JSON\n got %s\nwant %s", got, tc.want)
			}
			back := reflect.New(reflect.TypeOf(tc.v))
			if err := json.Unmarshal(got, back.Interface()); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("unmarshal: %v", err)
			}
			if again, _ := json.Marshal(back.Elem().Interface()); string(again) != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("round trip\n got %s\nwant %s", again, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAPSecretFieldsAreTagged(t *testing.T) {
	for _, f := range []struct {
		typ   reflect.Type
		field string
	}{
		{reflect.TypeFor[ConnectInput](), "ClientSecret"},
		{reflect.TypeFor[CreatedKey](), "Key"},
	} {
		sf, ok := f.typ.FieldByName(f.field)
		if !ok || sf.Tag.Get("secret") != "true" {
			t.Errorf("%s.%s lacks the secret:\"true\" tag", f.typ, f.field)
		}
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the tests to verify they fail**

Run: `mkdir -p /root/.cache/w3-tmp/39 && export TMPDIR=/root/.cache/w3-tmp/39 GOTOOLCHAIN=local && timeout 300 go test -count=1 -run 'TestAP' ./internal/modules/tailnet/`
Expected: FAIL to build, `undefined: deps` (and `productionTN`, `Device`, `KeyRequest`, and the other new identifiers).

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `wire.go`: declare every type of Contracts "Tailnet wire shapes" with the members, tags and comments given there (`PolicyPatchInput` uses `policy.Edit`; `AccountView` and `capabilities` use `cloud.Capability`), plus `KeyRequest` and `KeyInfo` as Contracts "Tailnet internals" gives them. `CreatedKey.Key` and `ConnectInput.ClientSecret` keep their `secret:"true"` tags. Doc comment on each exported type.
2. `tailnet.go`: `type module struct{ t tn }` and `Module()` returning `module{t: productionTN()}`; the manifest stays as it is, so the existing skeleton test keeps passing.
3. `client.go`:
   - `deps`, `tn` and `productionTN()` as Contracts gives them (`baseURL` `https://api.tailscale.com`, a fresh `newTokenCache()`).
   - `func (t tn) newAPI(a account, secret []byte, clock core.Clock) (*api, error)` refuses an empty `a.Tailnet`, `a.ClientID` or `secret` with a plain error (programming errors, nothing client-visible). It builds two `cloud.Client`s with `Provider` `tailscale`, `BaseURL` `t.d.baseURL`, `HTTP` `t.d.http`, `Sleep` `t.d.sleep` and `Clock` `clock`: one with no `Auth`, used only to fetch tokens, and the main one whose `Auth` sets `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from `t.tokens.token(r.Context(), key, fetch, clock.Now())`. `key` is `<client id>/<hex SHA-256 of the secret>`: `token` receives no secret, so the secret's hash travels in its first argument and a changed secret never reuses a token minted from the old one. `fetch` posts `POST /api/v2/oauth/token` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and the form `client_id`, `client_secret`, `grant_type=client_credentials`, and reads `access_token` and `expires_in` seconds (a missing `expires_in` is 3600; an empty token is `cloud.unavailable`). A token request that fails with `cloud.uncertain_outcome` is re-coded `cloud.unavailable` (nothing was written). The `api` keeps the escaped tailnet name and its client config; no error or log line carries the secret, the token or the form.
   - Every `api` method builds its path from `url.PathEscape` of the tailnet or id, returns `request.invalid_input` wrapped `core.Definite` for an empty id before any request, and uses `cloud.Client.Do` (the client's `JSON` helper takes no query string, and `fields=all` is one). A body that cannot be decoded is `cloud.unavailable`. A `cloud.Status(err) == 404` on an id-addressed call (`Device`, `Authorize`, `Routes`, `SetRoutes`, `Expire`, `DeleteDevice`, `Key`, `DeleteKey`) is re-coded `not_found` naming the kind and id, keeping `core.Definite` when the original error had it.
   - `Devices`: `GET /api/v2/tailnet/{t}/devices?fields=all`, answer `{"devices":[…]}`. `Device`: `GET /api/v2/device/{id}?fields=all`. Both map a provider device to `Device`: `ID` from `nodeId`; `Name`, `Hostname`, `OS`, `User`, `Addresses`, `Tags`, `Authorized`, `KeyExpiryDisabled`, `AdvertisedRoutes`, `EnabledRoutes` from the members of the same names; `LastSeen` and `Expires` as the provider's strings, except that the zero instant `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` becomes `""`; every list is a non-nil slice (an absent or null member is `[]`); `ExitNode` is true when `AdvertisedRoutes` holds `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`; `ExitNodeEnabled` is true when `EnabledRoutes` holds both.
   - `Authorize`: `POST /api/v2/device/{id}/authorized`, body `{"authorized":<bool>}`. `Routes`: `GET /api/v2/device/{id}/routes`; `SetRoutes`: `POST` the same path with `{"routes":[…]}` (a nil list sends `[]`, which removes every approval); both answer a `DeviceRoutes` with non-nil lists. `Expire`: `POST /api/v2/device/{id}/expire` with no body. `DeleteDevice`: `DELETE /api/v2/device/{id}`.
   - `CreateKey`: `POST /api/v2/tailnet/{t}/keys` with `{"capabilities":{"devices":{"create":{"reusable":…,"ephemeral":…,"preauthorized":…,"tags":[…]}}},"expirySeconds":N,"description":"…"}`; `expirySeconds` is sent only when `ExpirySeconds > 0`, the three booleans always. The answer's `id`, `key`, `expires` and `description` fill `CreatedKey`. `Keys`: `GET …/keys`, answer `{"keys":[{"id":…, optional description, created, expires, revoked}]}`; `Key`: `GET …/keys/{id}`; both fill `KeyInfo` (`Description` is `""` when the list omits it; times are RFC 3339 and zero when absent; `Revoked` is true when the provider's `revoked` member is a non-empty string). `DeleteKey`: `DELETE …/keys/{id}`.
   - `Policy`: `GET …/acl` with `Accept: application/hujson`; returns the body bytes untouched and the `ETag` header as sent (quotes included); an answer without an `ETag` is `cloud.unavailable`. `SetPolicy`: refuses an empty `ifMatch` with `request.invalid_input` (definite) before any request; `POST …/acl` with `Content-Type: application/hujson`, the text as the body and `If-Match: <ifMatch>`; returns the answer's `ETag`; a 412 (`cloud.Status == 412`) is `tailnet.policy_conflict` wrapped `core.Definite`; a 2xx answer without an `ETag` is `cloud.uncertain_outcome` (not definite: the write may have committed). `ValidatePolicy`: `POST …/acl/validate` with the text and `Content-Type: application/hujson`. A 2xx answer whose body is empty, or a JSON object with neither a non-empty `message` nor a non-empty `data`, means valid (nil). A 2xx body that does carry one, and a 400, is `tailnet.policy_invalid` wrapped `core.Definite` whose detail is the provider's `message` (the fixed text `tailscale rejected the policy` when there is none or the body is not JSON). The `cloud` client never exposes a response body, so `ValidatePolicy` sends its request through a `cloud.Client` built for the call whose `Config.ErrorCode` stores the 4xx body's `message` in a local variable and returns `""`; no other status is re-coded (403 stays `cloud.permission_missing`).
4. `oauth.go`: `tokenCache` guards a map from key to `{token, expiry}` with one mutex held across the fetch, so concurrent callers produce one fetch. `token` returns the cached token while `now` is before `fetchedAt + min(ttl, 50 minutes)` and otherwise calls `fetch`, stores the result with `now` as its time, and returns it; a failed fetch stores nothing.
5. Doc comments on every exported identifier; comments only for a non-obvious why (the secret hash in the cache key, the per-call client of `ValidatePolicy`).
