```tsx
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { Route, Routes } from "react-router"
import { expect, test, vi } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import type { Host, ModuleState } from "@/api/types"
import type { ExposureRow, ExposureView } from "@/modules/firewall/types"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type FetchCall, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { dkDetail } from "./fixtures"
import DockerRoutes from "./routes"
import type { ContainerDetail } from "./types"

// The registry is replaced by three entries so the page's slot logic is
// tested without the real modules: alpha is enabled on the host, beta is
// listed but disabled, gamma is not listed at all.
vi.mock("@/modules/registry", async () => {
  const { lazy } = await import("react")
  const { Server } = await import("lucide-react")
  const entry = (id: string) => ({
    id,
    label: id.toUpperCase(),
    icon: Server,
    containerActions: [
      {
        id: `${id}.probe`,
        label: `${id} probe`,
        render: lazy(async () => ({
          default: ({ container, onDone }: { container: unknown; onDone: () => void }) => (
            <div>
              <output aria-label={`${id} container`}>{JSON.stringify(container)}</output>
              <button type="button" onClick={onDone}>{`${id} done`}</button>
            </div>
          ),
        })),
      },
    ],
  })
  return { moduleRegistry: [entry("alpha"), entry("beta"), entry("gamma")] }
})
vi.mock("./logs-panel", () => ({
  LogsPanel: ({ hostId, containerId }: { hostId: string; containerId: string }) => <p>{`logs of ${containerId} on ${hostId}`}</p>,
}))
vi.mock("./stats-panel", () => ({
  StatsPanel: ({ hostId, containerId }: { hostId: string; containerId: string }) => <p>{`stats of ${containerId} on ${hostId}`}</p>,
}))

const CP_HOSTS = "POST /api/v1/actions/core.host.list/v1/read"
const CP_INSPECT = "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.container.inspect/v1/read"
const CP_EXPOSURE = "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/resources/firewall/exposure"

function cpState(id: string, enabled: boolean, available = true, reason: string | null = null): ModuleState {
  return { id, version: 1, enabled, available, reason, checkedAt: null }
}

const cpFirewallOk = cpState("firewall", true)

function cpHost(firewall: ModuleState | null = cpFirewallOk): Host {
  const modules = [cpState("docker", true), cpState("alpha", true), cpState("beta", false)]
  if (firewall !== null) modules.push(firewall)
  return { id: "h1", name: "web-1", isLocal: true, online: true, modules, ingestion: null }
}

function cpRow(over: Partial<ExposureRow> & { name: string; port: number }): ExposureRow {
  const { name, port, ...rest } = over
  return {
    proto: "tcp",
    addr: "0.0.0.0",
    port,
    family: "v4",
    container: { name, binding: { selector: name, hostPort: port, proto: "tcp" }, containerPort: 80, proxied: false },
    classes: [{ class: "internet", verdict: "open" }],
    ...rest,
  }
}

const cpDetail = (over: Partial<ContainerDetail> = {}) =>
  dkDetail({
    id: "c1",
    name: "/web",
    image: "nginx:1.27",
    state: "running",
    running: true,
    exitCode: 0,
    env: [{ name: "API_KEY", value: "[redacted]" }],
    mounts: [{ type: "bind", source: "/srv/web", destination: "/usr/share/nginx/html", rw: false }],
    networks: [{ network: "bridge", networkId: "n1", container: "web", ipv4: "172.17.0.2" }],
    ports: [
      { ip: "0.0.0.0", privatePort: 80, publicPort: 8080, proto: "tcp" },
      { ip: "::", privatePort: 80, publicPort: 8080, proto: "tcp" },
    ],
    ...over,
  })

function cpRender(opts: { detail?: StubHandler; host?: Host; exposure?: StubHandler; id?: string } = {}) {
  const calls = stubFetch({
    [CP_HOSTS]: { body: { output: { hosts: [opts.host ?? cpHost()] } } },
    [CP_INSPECT]: opts.detail ?? { body: { output: cpDetail() } },
    [CP_EXPOSURE]: opts.exposure ?? { body: { rows: [] } satisfies ExposureView },
  })
  const result = renderWithProviders(
    <Routes>
      <Route path="/hosts/:hostId/docker/*" element={<DockerRoutes hostId="h1" />} />
    </Routes>,
    { path: `/hosts/h1/docker/containers/${opts.id ?? "web"}` },
  )
  return { calls, ...result }
}

const cpCalls = (calls: FetchCall[], key: string) => calls.filter((c) => `${c.method} ${c.path.split("?")[0]}` === key)

test("the page inspects the container named in the address and shows its definition", async () => {
  const { calls } = cpRender()
  expect(await screen.findByRole("heading", { name: "web" })).toBeTruthy()
  expect(cpCalls(calls, CP_INSPECT)[0]?.body).toEqual({ input: { container: "web" } })
  const inspect = screen.getByRole("region", { name: "Inspect" })
  expect(within(inspect).getByText("nginx:1.27")).toBeTruthy()
  expect(within(inspect).getByText("API_KEY=[redacted]")).toBeTruthy()
  expect(within(inspect).getByText("/srv/web → /usr/share/nginx/html (read-only)")).toBeTruthy()
  expect(within(inspect).getByText("bridge 172.17.0.2")).toBeTruthy()
})
```

3. States of the page. Pending container query: `<Spinner aria-label="Loading the container" />`. Failed container query: the back link and `<Alert variant="destructive" role="alert">` whose only text is `errorMessage(error)`. The back link is a `Link` with text `Back to Docker`, `to="../.."` and `relative="path"` (it ends at `/hosts/<id>/docker`).
4. A success shows, top to bottom:
   - An `h2` with the container name without Docker's leading `/`, and a `Badge` reading `running` when `running` is true, else the `state`.
   - A card titled `Inspect` whose body is `<section aria-label="Inspect">`: a definition list with `ID`, `Image`, `State` (`running`, or `<state> (exit code <n>)`), and `Restart policy`, `Compose project`, `Compose service`, `Owner` only when non-empty. Then three sections with `aria-label` and an `h3` of `Environment`, `Mounts` and `Networks`. Environment: one `li` per variable whose text is exactly `<name>=<value>` (the value is what the API returned, `[redacted]`), or `No environment variables.`. Mounts: one `li` per mount with text `<source> → <destination>`, followed by ` (read-only)` when `rw` is false, or `No mounts.`. Networks: one `li` per endpoint with text `<network>` followed by ` <ipv4>` when it has one, or `Not attached to any network.`. Each of these texts is one text node, so the test's `getByText` matches it.
   - A card titled `Logs` holding `<LogsPanel hostId={hostId} containerId={detail.id} />` and a card titled `Statistics` holding `<StatsPanel hostId={hostId} containerId={detail.id} />`. Both receive the container's id from the answer, never the address segment.
   - A card titled `Exposure` (below).
   - When at least one action applies, a card titled `Actions` (below).
5. The `ContainerRef` passed to the slot is built from the answer: `hostId`, `containerId` = `detail.id`, `name` without the leading `/`, `composeService` = `detail.service` only when non-empty (the key is absent otherwise), and `ports` from `detail.ports`. A port without a `publicPort` is not published and is skipped. The rest are grouped by `(privatePort, protocol)` in order of first appearance, `protocol` being `udp` when `proto` is `udp` and `tcp` otherwise; each group's `bindings` keep the order of `detail.ports` and are `{ hostIp, hostPort }` with `hostIp` = `ip`, or `0.0.0.0` when `ip` is absent or empty.
6. Exposure. A child component calls the firewall's exposure resource with `useQuery` (`exposureQueryKey(hostId)`, `readResource<ExposureView>(hostId, FIREWALL_MODULE, "exposure")`) and sets `enabled` to true only when the firewall module state exists, is enabled and available, and the ref has at least one port, so nothing is requested otherwise. While the host list is pending the card shows `<Spinner aria-label="Loading the modules" />`. Then, in this order:
   - no firewall state or not enabled: the paragraph `The firewall module is not enabled on this host.`;
   - enabled but not available: `The firewall module is unavailable: <reason>.` with `<reason>` the state's `reason`, or `no reason was given` when null;
   - the ref has no ports: `This container publishes no ports.`;
   - the query pending: `<Spinner aria-label="Loading the exposure" />`; failed: the destructive alert with `errorMessage(error)`;
   - the rows kept are those with `row.container?.name === ref.name` and, for some port of the ref, `port.protocol === row.proto` and some binding with `hostPort === row.port` (the listening address is not compared, so the IPv4 and IPv6 rows of one binding both show); none kept: `The firewall reports no listening port for this container.`;
   - otherwise `<ul aria-label="Published ports">` with one `li` per kept row: a `span` (monospace) with `<proto> <addr>:<port>`, a single space, then one outline `Badge` per entry of `classes` with the text `<class>: <verdict>`.
7. The action slot. From `moduleRegistry`, take in registry order the `containerActions` of every entry for which `modules.some(s => s.id === entry.id && s.enabled)` holds (computed in the page: `registry.ts` is frozen and `enabledModules` skips entries without host routes). Render each as `<section aria-label={action.label}>` containing `<Suspense fallback={<Spinner aria-label={"Loading " + action.label} />}>` around `<action.render container={ref} onDone={onDone} />`. `onDone` calls `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["resource", hostId] })`, which refetches the container and the exposure rows.
8. Match the firewall pages' style: named imports from `darkraise-ui/components/*`, `@/` aliases, no comments except a one-line doc comment on `ContainerPage`. Do not edit `registry.ts`, `types.ts` or any firewall file.

Compose runs the project's files as root, so the four actions are admin scope and long-running. Task 38 owns every check of the project (`prepareCompose`) and the vector (`composeArgs`); this task adds what happens after the checks pass: the plan's extra lines and hash, the run itself, the error shape of a failed run, the record of the run, the result read back from the Engine API, and the undo of `pull` and `restart`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

The tests call each action's handlers directly (`def.Handler.Plan`, `Apply`, `Verify`, `Observe`, `Inverse`) over `dkHost`: the Compose program is the host's recording `Runner`, the daemon is the fake, and the project is Task 38's `ccProject`. `cuProject` adds what Task 38's checks need besides the project (the system plugin files, which are root-owned and not writable by others) and the answer of the project's `config --format json`, a real Compose v5.1.4 output captured on this host. `cuExec` wraps the host's runner to look at the host's state at the moment a command runs. One test registers the four actions in a private module so the registry's own rules (exactly one compensation mechanism, `LongRunning` with a timeout above 45 s) check the declarations.

```go
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/docker/dstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

// cuConfigJSON is `docker compose config --format json` of a project named
// shop whose Compose file has one service, web, running nginx:1.27 (Compose
// v5.1.4).
const cuConfigJSON = `{
  "name": "shop",
  "networks": {"default": {"name": "shop_default", "ipam": {}}},
  "services": {
    "web": {"command": null, "entrypoint": null, "image": "nginx:1.27", "networks": {"default": null},
      "ports": [{"mode": "ingress", "target": 80, "published": "8080", "protocol": "tcp"}]}
  }
}`

// cuModule registers the four Compose actions the way the module's
// manifest will, so the registry's own rules check their declarations.
type cuModule struct{ k dk }

func (m cuModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: ID, Version: 1, Actions: []core.ActionDef{
		m.k.composeUp(), m.k.composeDown(), m.k.composePull(), m.k.composeRestart(),
	}}
}

// cuExec runs a hook before the host's runner answers a command.
type cuExec struct {
	core.Runner
	before func(cmd core.Cmd)
}

func (e cuExec) Run(ctx context.Context, cmd core.Cmd) (core.CmdResult, error) {
	if e.before != nil {
		e.before(cmd)
	}
	return e.Runner.Run(ctx, cmd)
}

func cuKey(args []string) string { return strings.Join(args, " ") }

// cuConfig makes `config --format json` of p answer cuConfigJSON for profiles.
func cuConfig(h *dkHost, p projectRow, profiles []string) {
	h.results[cuKey(composeArgs(p, profiles, "config", "--format", "json"))] = core.CmdResult{Stdout: []byte(cuConfigJSON)}
}

// cuProject puts the valid project shop, the system plugin files and the
// answer of its config command into h.
func cuProject(t *testing.T, h *dkHost) projectRow {
	t.Helper()
	p := ccProject(t, h, "shop")
	h.files[pluginDir] = dkFile{Mode: fs.ModeDir | 0o755}
	h.files[pluginDir+"/docker-compose"] = dkFile{Mode: 0o755}
	cuConfig(h, p, p.Profiles)
	return p
}

// cuContainers puts the containers of project shop into the fake daemon: web
// and cache running, db stopped, and a running container of another project.
func cuContainers(h *dkHost) {
	label := func(project string) func(*dockerapi.ContainerJSON) {
		return dkLabels(map[string]string{"com.docker.compose.project": project})
	}
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("shop-web-1", dkRunning, label("shop")))
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("shop-cache-1", dkRunning, label("shop")))
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("shop-db-1", label("shop")))
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("other-web-1", dkRunning, label("other")))
}

const cuInput = `{"project":"shop"}`

func cuApply(t *testing.T, h *dkHost, def core.ActionDef, input string) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	t.Helper()
	return def.Handler.Apply(context.Background(), h.env("chg1"), json.RawMessage(input))
}

func cuPlan(t *testing.T, h *dkHost, def core.ActionDef, input string) (core.PlanOutcome, error) {
	t.Helper()
	return def.Handler.Plan(context.Background(), h.env(""), json.RawMessage(input))
}

func cuRow(t *testing.T, h *dkHost) projectRow {
	t.Helper()
	row, ok, err := loadProject(context.Background(), h.db, "shop")
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadProject = %v, %v, want the shop row", ok, err)
	}
	return row
}

func cuHasLine(diff []core.DiffLine, op, text string) bool {
	return slices.Contains(diff, core.DiffLine{Op: op, Text: text})
}

func cuLastCmd(t *testing.T, h *dkHost) core.Cmd {
	t.Helper()
	if len(h.cmds) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no command ran")
	}
	return h.cmds[len(h.cmds)-1]
}

func TestCUActionSpecs(t *testing.T) {
	k := newDKHost(t).dk()
	tests := []struct {
		def     core.ActionDef
		name    string
		class   core.Class
		timeout time.Duration
		undo    bool
	}{
		{k.composeUp(), "docker.compose.up", core.ClassIrreversible, 15 * time.Minute, false},
		{k.composeDown(), "docker.compose.down", core.ClassIrreversible, 10 * time.Minute, false},
		{k.composePull(), "docker.compose.pull", core.ClassCompensable, 30 * time.Minute, true},
		{k.composeRestart(), "docker.compose.restart", core.ClassCompensable, 10 * time.Minute, true},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		s := tc.def.Spec
		if s.Name != tc.name || s.Version != 1 || s.Class != tc.class || s.Side != core.SideAgent {
			t.Errorf("%s: spec %+v, want version 1, class %s on the agent", tc.name, s, tc.class)
		}
		if !slices.Equal(s.LockKeys, []string{"docker"}) || s.MinScope != core.ScopeAdmin || !s.LongRunning || s.ApplyTimeout != tc.timeout {
			t.Errorf("%s: spec %+v, want lock docker, admin scope, long-running, timeout %s", tc.name, s, tc.timeout)
		}
		if (tc.def.Handler.Inverse != nil) != tc.undo || (tc.undo && tc.def.Handler.Observe == nil) {
			t.Errorf("%s: undo handler %v, want %v with an observer", tc.name, tc.def.Handler.Inverse != nil, tc.undo)
		}
	}
	if _, err := core.NewRegistry(cuModule{k}); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("NewRegistry: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestCUPlans(t *testing.T) {
	const root = "runs the project's Compose file as root"
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		def     func(dk) core.ActionDef
		confirm string
		lines   []core.DiffLine
		absent  []core.DiffLine
	}{
		{"up", dk.composeUp, "shop", []core.DiffLine{
			{Op: " ", Text: "containers are created or recreated; a recreated container loses its writable layer"},
		}, nil},
		{"down", dk.composeDown, "shop", []core.DiffLine{
			{Op: "-", Text: "remove container shop-web-1 and its writable layer"},
			{Op: "-", Text: "remove container shop-cache-1 and its writable layer"},
			{Op: "-", Text: "remove container shop-db-1 and its writable layer"},
		}, []core.DiffLine{{Op: "-", Text: "remove container other-web-1 and its writable layer"}}},
		{"pull", dk.composePull, "", []core.DiffLine{
			{Op: " ", Text: "images are pulled; a tag that moved is not reverted by an undo"},
		}, nil},
		{"restart", dk.composeRestart, "", []core.DiffLine{
			{Op: " ", Text: "restart container shop-web-1"},
			{Op: " ", Text: "restart container shop-cache-1"},
		}, []core.DiffLine{
			{Op: " ", Text: "restart container shop-db-1"},
			{Op: " ", Text: "restart container other-web-1"},
		}},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			cuProject(t, h)
			cuContainers(h)
			out, err := cuPlan(t, h, tc.def(h.dk()), cuInput)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("Plan: %v", err)
			}
			if out.Confirmation != tc.confirm {
				t.Errorf("confirmation %q, want %q", out.Confirmation, tc.confirm)
			}
			if !slices.ContainsFunc(out.Diff, func(l core.DiffLine) bool { return strings.Contains(l.Text, root) }) {
				t.Errorf("diff %+v lacks a line saying it %s", out.Diff, root)
			}
			for _, l := range tc.lines {
				if !cuHasLine(out.Diff, l.Op, l.Text) {
					t.Errorf("diff %+v lacks %+v", out.Diff, l)
				}
			}
			for _, l := range tc.absent {
				if cuHasLine(out.Diff, l.Op, l.Text) {
					t.Errorf("diff %+v has %+v", out.Diff, l)
				}
			}
			if out.StateHash == "" {
				t.Error("state hash is empty")
			}
			for _, c := range h.cmds {
				if c.Args[len(c.Args)-1] != "json" {
					t.Errorf("plan ran %q, want only the config command", cuKey(c.Args))
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCUPlanRestartWithNothingRunning(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	cuProject(t, h)
	h.docker.put(dkContainer("shop-db-1", dkLabels(map[string]string{"com.docker.compose.project": "shop"})))
	out, err := cuPlan(t, h, h.dk().composeRestart(), cuInput)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Plan: %v", err)
	}
	if !cuHasLine(out.Diff, " ", "no container of the project is running") {
		t.Errorf("diff %+v lacks the line saying nothing is running", out.Diff)
	}
}

func TestCUPlanOfAnUnknownProjectRunsNothing(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	cuProject(t, h)
	_, err := cuPlan(t, h, h.dk().composeUp(), `{"project":"nope"}`)
	var coded *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &coded) {
		t.Fatalf("Plan = %v, want an *errcode.Error", err)
	}
	if len(h.cmds) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ran %d commands for an unknown project, want none", len(h.cmds))
	}
}

func TestCUStateHashFollowsWhatTheRunActsOn(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	p := cuProject(t, h)
	cuContainers(h)
	def := h.dk().composeRestart()
	hash := func(input string) string {
		t.Helper()
		out, err := cuPlan(t, h, def, input)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Plan %s: %v", input, err)
		}
		return out.StateHash
	}
	base := hash(cuInput)
	if again := hash(cuInput); again != base {
		t.Errorf("hash %q then %q for the same state, want equal", base, again)
	}

	if _, err := h.docker.StopContainer(ctx, dkID("shop-web-1"), time.Second); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	stopped := hash(cuInput)
	if stopped == base {
		t.Error("hash is unchanged after a container of the project stopped")
	}
	if _, err := h.docker.StartContainer(ctx, dkID("shop-web-1")); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if restored := hash(cuInput); restored != base {
		t.Errorf("hash %q after the container started again, want %q", restored, base)
	}

	file := h.files[p.Files[0]]
	file.Data = append(slices.Clone(file.Data), []byte("\n# edited\n")...)
	h.files[p.Files[0]] = file
	if edited := hash(cuInput); edited == base {
		t.Error("hash is unchanged after the Compose file changed")
	}
	file.Data = file.Data[:len(file.Data)-len("\n# edited\n")]
	h.files[p.Files[0]] = file

	cuConfig(h, p, []string{"debug"})
	if withProfile := hash(`{"project":"shop","profiles":["debug"]}`); withProfile == base {
		t.Error("hash is unchanged after the profile list changed")
	}
}

func TestCUUpWritesTheDockerConfigThenRuns(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	p := cuProject(t, h)
	cuContainers(h)
	upKey := cuKey(composeArgs(p, p.Profiles, "up", "-d", "--no-build"))
	var ran bool
	var config string
	env := h.env("chg1")
	env.Exec = cuExec{Runner: h, before: func(c core.Cmd) {
		if cuKey(c.Args) == upKey {
			ran = true
			config = string(h.managed[dockerConfigDir+"/config.json"])
		}
	}}
	raw, err := h.dk().composeUp().Handler.Apply(context.Background(), env, json.RawMessage(cuInput))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
	}
	if !ran || config != "{}\n" {
		t.Errorf("up ran %v with docker-config/config.json %q, want it written as \"{}\\n\" before the run", ran, config)
	}
	last := cuLastCmd(t, h)
	if last.Path != "/usr/bin/docker" || cuKey(last.Args) != upKey {
		t.Errorf("last command %s %q, want /usr/bin/docker %q", last.Path, cuKey(last.Args), upKey)
	}
	keys := make([]string, len(h.cmds))
	for i, c := range h.cmds {
		keys[i] = cuKey(c.Args)
	}
	cfg := slices.Index(keys, cuKey(composeArgs(p, p.Profiles, "config", "--format", "json")))
	if cfg < 0 || cfg > slices.Index(keys, upKey) {
		t.Errorf("commands %q, want the config check before up", keys)
	}

	var out ComposeResult
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := []ContainerState{
		{ID: dkID("shop-cache-1"), Name: "shop-cache-1", Running: true},
		{ID: dkID("shop-db-1"), Name: "shop-db-1", Running: false},
		{ID: dkID("shop-web-1"), Name: "shop-web-1", Running: true},
	}
	if out.Project != "shop" || !slices.Equal(out.Containers, want) {
		t.Errorf("result %+v, want project shop with %+v", out, want)
	}
	row := cuRow(t, h)
	if row.RunHash == "" || row.RunHash != h.dk().configHash(p) || !row.LastRun.Equal(h.clock.Now()) {
		t.Errorf("run recorded as hash %q at %s, want the config hash %q at %s", row.RunHash, row.LastRun, h.dk().configHash(p), h.clock.Now())
	}
}

func TestCUOtherVerbsRunTheirVectorAndRecordTheRun(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		def  func(dk) core.ActionDef
		verb []string
	}{
		{"down", dk.composeDown, []string{"down"}},
		{"pull", dk.composePull, []string{"pull"}},
		{"restart", dk.composeRestart, []string{"restart"}},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			p := cuProject(t, h)
			cuContainers(h)
			if _, err := cuApply(t, h, tc.def(h.dk()), cuInput); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
			}
			last := cuLastCmd(t, h)
			if last.Path != "/usr/bin/docker" || cuKey(last.Args) != cuKey(composeArgs(p, p.Profiles, tc.verb...)) {
				t.Errorf("last command %s %q, want the %s vector", last.Path, cuKey(last.Args), tc.verb[0])
			}
			if got := h.managed[dockerConfigDir+"/config.json"]; string(got) != "{}\n" {
				t.Errorf("docker-config/config.json = %q, want \"{}\\n\"", got)
			}
			if row := cuRow(t, h); row.RunHash != h.dk().configHash(p) {
				t.Errorf("run hash %q, want %q", row.RunHash, h.dk().configHash(p))
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCUProfilesInputReplacesTheStoredList(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	p := cuProject(t, h)
	cuConfig(h, p, []string{"debug", "dev"})
	def := h.dk().composeUp()
	if _, err := cuApply(t, h, def, `{"project":"shop","profiles":["debug","dev"]}`); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Apply with profiles: %v", err)
	}
	want := cuKey(composeArgs(p, []string{"debug", "dev"}, "up", "-d", "--no-build"))
	if got := cuKey(cuLastCmd(t, h).Args); got != want || !strings.Contains(got, "--profile debug --profile dev") {
		t.Errorf("up ran %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
	if row := cuRow(t, h); !slices.Equal(row.Profiles, []string{"debug", "dev"}) {
		t.Errorf("stored profiles %q, want [debug dev]", row.Profiles)
	}
	if _, err := cuApply(t, h, def, cuInput); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Apply without profiles: %v", err)
	}
	if got := cuKey(cuLastCmd(t, h).Args); got != want {
		t.Errorf("up ran %q after the list was stored, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestCUFailedRunNamesTheVerbTheStatusAndTheLastStderrLine(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		stderr string
		code   int
		want   string
	}{
		{"last non-empty line", "pull access denied\nservice web failed to start\n\n", 1, "compose up exited with status 1: service web failed to start"},
		{"no stderr", "", 2, "compose up exited with status 2"},
		{"capped on a rune boundary", "a" + strings.Repeat("é", 200) + "\n", 1, "compose up exited with status 1: a" + strings.Repeat("é", 149)},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			p := cuProject(t, h)
			before := cuRow(t, h)
			h.results[cuKey(composeArgs(p, p.Profiles, "up", "-d", "--no-build"))] = core.CmdResult{ExitCode: tc.code, Stderr: []byte(tc.stderr)}
			_, err := cuApply(t, h, h.dk().composeUp(), cuInput)
			var coded *errcode.Error
			if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != errcode.DockerComposeUnavailable || coded.Detail != tc.want {
				t.Fatalf("Apply = %v, want docker.compose_unavailable %q", err, tc.want)
			}
			if !utf8.ValidString(coded.Detail) {
				t.Errorf("detail %q is not valid UTF-8", coded.Detail)
			}
			if core.IsDefinite(err) {
				t.Error("a failed run is marked definite, but the run may have changed containers")
			}
			if after := cuRow(t, h); after.RunHash != before.RunHash || !after.LastRun.Equal(before.LastRun) {
				t.Errorf("run recorded after a failure: %+v, was %+v", after, before)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCURestartJournalsEveryRunningContainerBeforeTheRun(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	p := cuProject(t, h)
	cuContainers(h)
	restartKey := cuKey(composeArgs(p, p.Profiles, "restart"))
	intended := -1
	env := h.env("chg1")
	env.Exec = cuExec{Runner: h, before: func(c core.Cmd) {
		if cuKey(c.Args) == restartKey {
			intended = len(h.journal.effects())
		}
	}}
	def := h.dk().composeRestart()
	if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(cuInput)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
	}
	if intended != 2 {
		t.Errorf("%d effects were journaled when restart ran, want 2", intended)
	}
	effs := h.journal.effects()
	if len(effs) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("%d effects, want one for each of the two running containers", len(effs))
	}
	for i, name := range []string{"shop-cache-1", "shop-web-1"} {
		e := effs[i]
		c, ok := h.docker.container(dkID(name))
		if !ok {
			t.Fatalf("container %s is gone", name)
		}
		wantBefore, err := dstate.ContainerRunning(dkID(name), c.Created, true)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		wantPost, err := dstate.ContainerRun(c, dstate.Recorded)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if e.Kind != core.EffectModify || e.Resource != containerResource(dkID(name)) || e.Local || e.CommitWait != 2*time.Minute {
			t.Errorf("effect %d = %+v, want a non-local modify of %s with a 2 minute commit wait", i, e, containerResource(dkID(name)))
		}
		if string(e.Before.State) != string(wantBefore) {
			t.Errorf("effect %d before %s, want %s", i, e.Before.State, wantBefore)
		}
		if e.Post == nil || string(e.Post.State) != string(wantPost) {
			t.Errorf("effect %d post %+v, want %s", i, e.Post, wantPost)
		}
		obs, err := def.Handler.Observe(ctx, env, e)
		if err != nil || string(obs.Current.State) != string(wantPost) {
			t.Errorf("Observe of effect %d = %s (%v), want %s", i, obs.Current.State, err, wantPost)
		}
	}
}

func TestCURestartThatFailsLeavesItsEffectsUnmade(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	p := cuProject(t, h)
	cuContainers(h)
	h.results[cuKey(composeArgs(p, p.Profiles, "restart"))] = core.CmdResult{ExitCode: 1, Stderr: []byte("daemon went away\n")}
	_, err := cuApply(t, h, h.dk().composeRestart(), cuInput)
	if err == nil || core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Fatalf("Apply = %v, want an indefinite error", err)
	}
	effs := h.journal.effects()
	if len(effs) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("%d effects, want the two intended before the run", len(effs))
	}
	for i, e := range effs {
		if e.Post != nil {
			t.Errorf("effect %d has a post-state %+v, but the run failed", i, e.Post)
		}
	}
}

func TestCURestartInverseStartsWhatIsStopped(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	cuProject(t, h)
	cuContainers(h)
	def := h.dk().composeRestart()
	env := h.env("chg1")
	if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(cuInput)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
	}
	effs := h.journal.effects()
	if _, err := h.docker.StopContainer(ctx, dkID("shop-web-1"), time.Second); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, e := range effs {
		res, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, env, e)
		if err != nil || res.Resource != "" {
			t.Errorf("Inverse of %s = %+v, %v, want an empty result", e.Resource, res, err)
		}
	}
	for _, name := range []string{"shop-web-1", "shop-cache-1"} {
		if c, _ := h.docker.container(dkID(name)); !c.State.Running {
			t.Errorf("%s is stopped after the undo, want it running as before", name)
		}
	}
	if c, _ := h.docker.container(dkID("shop-db-1")); c.State.Running {
		t.Error("shop-db-1 was started by the undo, but it was stopped before the restart")
	}
}

func TestCURestartInverseFailures(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name     string
		err      error
		definite bool
	}{
		{"a refusal of the daemon", &dockerapi.APIError{StatusCode: 409, Message: "container is paused"}, true},
		{"a failure to reach the daemon", errors.New("connection reset"), false},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			ctx := context.Background()
			h := newDKHost(t)
			cuProject(t, h)
			cuContainers(h)
			def := h.dk().composeRestart()
			env := h.env("chg1")
			if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(cuInput)); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
			}
			e := h.journal.effects()[1]
			if _, err := h.docker.StopContainer(ctx, dkID("shop-web-1"), time.Second); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			h.docker.fail("StartContainer", tc.err)
			_, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, env, e)
			if err == nil || core.IsDefinite(err) != tc.definite {
				t.Errorf("Inverse = %v (definite %v), want an error with definite %v", err, core.IsDefinite(err), tc.definite)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCUPullUndoChangesNothing(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newDKHost(t)
	cuProject(t, h)
	cuContainers(h)
	def := h.dk().composePull()
	env := h.env("chg1")
	if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(cuInput)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
	}
	if n := len(h.journal.effects()); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("pull journaled %d effects, want none", n)
	}
	calls, cmds := len(h.docker.calls()), len(h.cmds)
	res, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, env, core.Effect{ChangeID: "chg1"})
	if err != nil || res.Resource != "" {
		t.Errorf("Inverse = %+v, %v, want an empty result", res, err)
	}
	if len(h.docker.calls()) != calls || len(h.cmds) != cmds {
		t.Error("the undo of a pull called the daemon or ran a command")
	}
}

func TestCUVerifyChecksTheContainersThatShouldExist(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	empty := json.RawMessage("{}")
	input := json.RawMessage(cuInput)
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		def     func(dk) core.ActionDef
		present bool
		wantErr bool
	}{
		{"up with containers", dk.composeUp, true, false},
		{"up without containers", dk.composeUp, false, true},
		{"down with containers left", dk.composeDown, true, true},
		{"down without containers", dk.composeDown, false, false},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newDKHost(t)
			cuProject(t, h)
			if tc.present {
				cuContainers(h)
			} else {
				h.docker.put(dkContainer("other-web-1", dkRunning, dkLabels(map[string]string{"com.docker.compose.project": "other"})))
			}
			err := tc.def(h.dk()).Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("chg1"), input, empty)
			if (err != nil) != tc.wantErr {
				t.Errorf("Verify = %v, want error %v", err, tc.wantErr)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `compose_run.go`, the four constructors and two handler types.

1. Constructors. Each returns `core.DefineMutating(spec, handler)` with `Version: 1`, `Side: core.SideAgent`, `LockKeys: []string{lockKey}`, `MinScope: core.ScopeAdmin`, `LongRunning: true` and a one-line `Summary`:

   | Constructor | Name | Class | ApplyTimeout | Handler | Verb passed to `composeArgs` |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | `composeUp` | `docker.compose.up` | irreversible | 15 min | `composeVerb` | `up`, `-d`, `--no-build` |
   | `composeDown` | `docker.compose.down` | irreversible | 10 min | `composeVerb` | `down` |
   | `composePull` | `docker.compose.pull` | compensable | 30 min | `composeVerbUndo` | `pull` |
   | `composeRestart` | `docker.compose.restart` | compensable | 10 min | `composeVerbUndo` | `restart` |

   The irreversible actions use `composeVerb`, which has no `Observe` or `Inverse` method (the registry would otherwise find an undo handler on an irreversible action). `composeVerbUndo` embeds `composeVerb` and adds `Observe` (delegating to `k.observe`) and `Inverse`; as the compensable ones' only compensation mechanism it must be the sole one: no `CompensatedBy`, no `ForwardOnly`.

2. `composeVerb` holds the `dk`, the verb arguments and the verb's word (`up`, `down`, `pull`, `restart`). Its `Plan`:
   - runs `k.prepareCompose(ctx, env, in)` and returns its error unchanged;
   - lists the project's containers with `composeContainersOf`;
   - the diff is `planCompose(r, <the verb arguments joined by spaces>)` followed by the verb's own lines, in this order, sorted by container name: `up`: one ` ` line `containers are created or recreated; a recreated container loses its writable layer`; `down`: one `-` line `remove container <name> and its writable layer` per container, running or not; `pull`: one ` ` line `images are pulled; a tag that moved is not reverted by an undo`; `restart`: one ` ` line `restart container <name>` per running container, or the single ` ` line `no container of the project is running` when none runs;
   - `Confirmation` is the project name for `up` and `down` and `""` for the others;
   - `StateHash` is `composeStateHash`: the hex SHA-256 of the lines `project=<name>`, `hash=<r.Hash>`, `profiles=<r.Profiles joined by ",">` and, for each container sorted by name, `container=<id>:<true|false for running>`, joined by newlines. A container starting or stopping, an edited Compose file, or another profile list therefore changes it, and nothing else does (not timestamps).

3. `composeContainersOf(ctx, name)` lists containers with `ListContainers(All: true, Filters{"label": {"com.docker.compose.project=" + name}})`, inspects each, keeps those whose `Config.Labels["com.docker.compose.project"]` equals `name` (so the result is right even if a daemon ignores the filter), sorts by name without the leading `/`, and maps daemon errors with `engineError("container", ...)`.

4. `Apply`, in this order:
   1. `prepareCompose` again (the project may have changed since the plan).
   2. `env.Files.WriteManaged(ctx, "docker", dockerConfigDir, "config.json", []byte("{}\n"), 0o600, 0, 0)`.
   3. `restart` only: `composeContainersOf`, and for each running container (sorted by name) build `dockerEffect(core.EffectModify, containerResource(id), before)` with `before` = `dstate.ContainerRunning(id, created, true)` (the state an undo restores: running), and `env.Effects.Intend` it. Every effect is therefore journaled before the program runs.
   4. Run `env.Exec.Run(ctx, core.Cmd{Path: "/usr/bin/docker", Args: composeArgs(r.Project, r.Profiles, verb...)})` with the apply context as it is (its deadline is the action's `ApplyTimeout`). A runner error is returned as `docker: compose <word>: %w`. A non-zero exit returns `composeFailure`: `*errcode.Error` `docker.compose_unavailable` with the detail `compose <word> exited with status <n>`, followed by `: <line>` when `lastStderrLine` is not empty. It is not wrapped in `core.Definite`: the program may have changed containers before it failed. On a failed `restart` the effects stay intended, so the engine settles them as uncertain.
   5. `restart` only: for each effect, inspect the container and call `env.Effects.Made(ctx, seq, containerResource(id), core.StateDoc{State: <dstate.ContainerRun(container, dstate.Recorded)>})`.
   6. Record the run: `env.DB.Write` with `setProjectRun(ctx, tx, name, r.Profiles, r.Hash, env.Clock.Now())`. `r.Profiles` is the input's list when given, so a given list replaces the stored one here, and the stored one otherwise.
   7. Return `ComposeResult{Project: name, Containers: ...}` with one `ContainerState{ID, Name, Running}` per container of `composeContainersOf`, name without the leading `/`, sorted by name; `Containers` is never nil.

5. `lastStderrLine(stderr []byte) string` splits on newlines, takes the last line that is not empty after `strings.TrimSpace`, and cuts it to at most 300 bytes without splitting a UTF-8 sequence (back up to the previous rune start). The line is only shown as the error detail; nothing else of stderr or stdout is kept.

6. `Verify` is read-only and ignores the output (recovery passes an empty one): `up` fails when the project has no container; `down` fails when it still has one; `pull` and `restart` return nil. Errors are plain `docker: project <name> ...` errors.

7. `composeVerbUndo.Inverse(ctx, env, e)`: for `pull`, return `core.InverseResult{}` and a nil error without calling the daemon (a pull is documented as not reversed). For `restart`, the container id is `e.Resource` without the prefix `docker.container:`: inspect it; if it is running, return nil; otherwise `StartContainer`. A daemon answer in the 4xx range (a `*dockerapi.APIError` with `StatusCode` 400–499, including not found) is returned as `core.Definite(engineError("container", id, err))`; any other error is returned as `engineError(...)` unwrapped, so the engine treats the call as uncertain. The result is always an empty `core.InverseResult`. It touches only that container, and the other effects' containers are handled by their own `Inverse` calls.

8. Comments only where the why is not obvious: the "not Definite after a non-zero exit" rule is one.

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 2 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 8
**Lenses:** security

Connecting stores one OAuth client for the controller: the client id, the client secret sealed at rest, and the tags the client may assign. Connect proves the credentials by fetching a token and probing the read endpoints (spec 1.9, "Capability probes"); it never writes to Tailscale. The stored row is the action's one effect, a local create that the undo reverses once no provider cleanup is pending (spec 4.2, 1.9 "Accounts"). Disconnect is irreversible, typed with the tailnet name, and deletes the row unless cleanup is pending.

Capability names, fixed here because the web account panel shows them verbatim. Probed with a harmless read, in this order: `devices:core:read` (`Devices`), `auth_keys:read` (`Keys`), `policy_file:read` (`Policy`). Reported `unverified` until a write succeeds, in this order: `devices:core`, `devices:routes`, `auth_keys`, `policy_file`.

The tests run each action's handlers directly (`def.Handler.Plan`, `Apply`, `Verify`, `Observe`, `Inverse`, `Read`) against `tnWith(fake.New(t))` and a `tnHost`, and three of them run a real controller `lifecycle.Engine` over the host's database (`acEngine`) with a private module `acModule` that lists the three actions the way Task 57's manifest will. The engine tests settle what no production module has yet shown: a controller-side action with an undo handler plans, applies and undoes, and an undo refused with `cloud.cleanup_pending` ends in `needs_repair` with the row and the effect kept. The scope names used with `SetScopes` (`devices:core`, `devices:routes`, `auth_keys`) are the OAuth scopes of spec 4.2a; leaving out `policy_file` makes the fake answer 403 on the policy endpoint.

```go
package tailnet

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/cloud"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/lifecycle"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/tailnet/fake"
)

// acModule registers the three account actions the way the module's
// manifest will, so the registry's own rules check their declarations and
// a controller engine can run them.
type acModule struct{ t tn }

func (m acModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: ID, Version: 1, Actions: []core.ActionDef{
		m.t.accountConnect(), m.t.accountDisconnect(), m.t.accountGet(),
	}}
}

// acConnect inserts a connected account whose secret is the fake's client
// secret, sealed as the connect action seals it.
func acConnect(t *testing.T, h *tnHost, _ *fake.Server) account {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	ct, err := cloud.SealCredential(coretest.Sealer{}, "tailnet_accounts", "client_secret_ct", "ACCT1", []byte(fake.ClientSecret))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	a := account{
		ID: "ACCT1", Tailnet: fake.Tailnet, ClientID: fake.ClientID, SecretCT: ct, TagsAllowed: []string{"tag:server"},
		Capabilities: []cloud.Capability{{Name: "devices:core:read", State: cloud.CapabilityOK}}, ConnectedAt: h.clock.Now(),
	}
	if err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertAccount(ctx, tx, a) }); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return a
}

// acInput is a valid connect input for the fake's client; the tags are
// out of order and repeated on purpose.
func acInput(over func(*ConnectInput)) json.RawMessage {
	in := ConnectInput{
		Tailnet: fake.Tailnet, ClientID: fake.ClientID, ClientSecret: fake.ClientSecret,
		TagsAllowed: []string{"tag:web", "tag:server", "tag:web"},
	}
	if over != nil {
		over(&in)
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(in)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	return b
}

func acPending(t *testing.T, h *tnHost, description, state string) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	k := keyRow{
		Description: description, Kind: "change", OwnerID: "CHG", State: state, RequestedAt: h.clock.Now(), UpdatedAt: h.clock.Now(),
		ExpirySeconds: 3600, Tags: []string{"tag:server"},
	}
	if err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertKey(ctx, tx, k) }); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func acCode(t *testing.T, err error) *errcode.Error {
	t.Helper()
	var coded *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &coded) {
		t.Fatalf("error %v is not an *errcode.Error", err)
	}
	return coded
}

func acCapabilities(caps []cloud.Capability) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(caps))
	for i, c := range caps {
		out[i] = c.Name + "=" + c.State
	}
	return out
}

func TestACActionSpecs(t *testing.T) {
	m := acModule{t: tnWith(fake.New(t))}
	tests := []struct {
		def     core.ActionDef
		name    string
		class   core.Class
		locks   []string
		undo    bool
		minimum core.Scope
	}{
		{m.t.accountConnect(), "tailnet.account.connect", core.ClassCompensable, []string{"tailnet"}, true, core.ScopeAdmin},
		{m.t.accountDisconnect(), "tailnet.account.disconnect", core.ClassIrreversible, []string{"tailnet"}, false, core.ScopeAdmin},
		{m.t.accountGet(), "tailnet.account.get", core.ClassRead, nil, false, core.ScopeRead},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		s := tc.def.Spec
		if s.Name != tc.name || s.Version != 1 || s.Class != tc.class || s.Side != core.SideController || !slices.Equal(s.LockKeys, tc.locks) {
			t.Errorf("%s: spec %+v, want version 1, class %s on the controller with locks %q", tc.name, s, tc.class, tc.locks)
		}
		if (tc.def.Handler.Inverse != nil) != tc.undo || (tc.undo && tc.def.Handler.Observe == nil) || s.CompensatedBy != "" {
			t.Errorf("%s: undo handler %v, want %v with an observer and no compensating action", tc.name, tc.def.Handler.Inverse != nil, tc.undo)
		}
		if got := core.RequiredScope(s); got != tc.minimum {
			t.Errorf("%s: scope %s, want %s", tc.name, got, tc.minimum)
		}
	}
	if _, err := core.NewRegistry(m); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("NewRegistry: %v", err)
	}
}

		{Op: "+", Text: "tags the client may assign: tag:server, tag:web"},

	}

func TestACPlanRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		over  func(*ConnectInput)
		code  errcode.Code
		field string
	}{
		{"empty tailnet", func(in *ConnectInput) { in.Tailnet = "" }, errcode.InvalidInput, "/tailnet"},
		{"tailnet with a slash", func(in *ConnectInput) { in.Tailnet = "a/b" }, errcode.InvalidInput, "/tailnet"},
		{"empty client id", func(in *ConnectInput) { in.ClientID = "" }, errcode.InvalidInput, "/clientId"},
		{"empty client secret", func(in *ConnectInput) { in.ClientSecret = "" }, errcode.InvalidInput, "/clientSecret"},
		{"no tags", func(in *ConnectInput) { in.TagsAllowed = nil }, errcode.InvalidInput, "/tagsAllowed"},
		{"tag without the prefix", func(in *ConnectInput) { in.TagsAllowed = []string{"tag:ok", "server"} }, errcode.InvalidInput, "/tagsAllowed/1"},
		{"tag with a space", func(in *ConnectInput) { in.TagsAllowed = []string{"tag:a b"} }, errcode.InvalidInput, "/tagsAllowed/0"},
		{"the provider refuses the client", func(in *ConnectInput) { in.ClientSecret = "wrong" }, errcode.CloudAuthFailed, ""},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newTNHost(t)
			_, err := tnWith(fake.New(t)).accountConnect().Handler.Plan(context.Background(), h.env(""), acInput(tc.over))
			coded := acCode(t, err)
			if coded.Code != tc.code || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
				t.Fatalf("Plan = %v (definite %v), want %s as a definite refusal", err, core.IsDefinite(err), tc.code)
			}
			if tc.field != "" && !slices.ContainsFunc(coded.Fields, func(f errcode.FieldError) bool { return f.Path == tc.field }) {
				t.Errorf("fields %+v, want one at %s", coded.Fields, tc.field)
			}
			if strings.Contains(coded.Detail, "wrong") {
				t.Errorf("detail %q carries the secret", coded.Detail)
			}
		})
	}
}

	if strings.Contains(string(raw), fake.ClientSecret) {
		t.Errorf("the output %s carries the client secret", raw)
	}

	a, ok, err := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read())
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadAccount = %v, %v, want the row", ok, err)
	}
	if a.ID != "CHG1" || a.Tailnet != fake.Tailnet || a.ClientID != fake.ClientID || !slices.Equal(acCapabilities(a.Capabilities), wantCaps) {
		t.Errorf("stored account %+v", a)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(a.SecretCT), fake.ClientSecret) {
		t.Error("the stored secret is not sealed")
	}
	secret, err := cloud.OpenCredential(coretest.Sealer{}, "tailnet_accounts", "client_secret_ct", "CHG1", a.SecretCT)
	if err != nil || string(secret) != fake.ClientSecret {
		t.Errorf("the sealed secret opens to %q (%v), want the client secret", secret, err)
	}

	effs := h.journal.effects()
	if len(effs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d effects, want one", len(effs))
	}
	e := effs[0]
	if e.Kind != core.EffectCreate || e.Resource != "tailnet.account:CHG1" || !e.Local || !e.InverseLocal ||
		e.Recovery == nil || e.Recovery.Kind != "name" || e.Recovery.Value != "CHG1" {
		t.Errorf("effect %+v, want a local create of tailnet.account:CHG1 recovered by name CHG1", e)
	}
	if string(e.Before.State) != "null" || e.Post == nil {
		t.Errorf("effect before %s and post %+v, want null before and a post-state", e.Before.State, e.Post)
	}
	var post struct {
		ID          string   `json:"id"`
		Tailnet     string   `json:"tailnet"`
		ClientID    string   `json:"clientId"`
		TagsAllowed []string `json:"tagsAllowed"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Post.State, &post); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if post.ID != "CHG1" || post.Tailnet != fake.Tailnet || post.ClientID != fake.ClientID || !slices.Equal(post.TagsAllowed, []string{"tag:server", "tag:web"}) {
		t.Errorf("post-state %s", e.Post.State)
	}
	if b, _ := json.Marshal(effs); strings.Contains(string(b), fake.ClientSecret) {
		t.Errorf("the journal %s carries the client secret", b)
	}

	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, env, acInput(nil), json.RawMessage("{}")); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("Verify after Apply: %v", err)
	}
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("OTHER"), acInput(nil), json.RawMessage("{}")); err == nil {
		t.Error("Verify passed for a change that stored no account")
	}
}

func TestACApplyRefusalsJournalNothing(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	t.Run("provider refuses the client", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newTNHost(t)
		_, err := tnWith(fake.New(t)).accountConnect().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("CHG1"),
			acInput(func(in *ConnectInput) { in.ClientSecret = "wrong" }))
		if coded := acCode(t, err); coded.Code != errcode.CloudAuthFailed || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Errorf("Apply = %v, want a definite cloud.auth_failed", err)
		}
		acNothingStored(t, h)
	})
	t.Run("an account exists", func(t *testing.T) {
		srv := fake.New(t)
		h := newTNHost(t)
		acConnect(t, h, srv)
		_, err := tnWith(srv).accountConnect().Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("CHG1"), acInput(nil))
		if coded := acCode(t, err); coded.Code != errcode.CloudConflict || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Errorf("Apply = %v, want a definite cloud.conflict", err)
		}
		if len(h.journal.effects()) != 0 {
			t.Error("an effect was journaled for a refused connect")
		}
	})
}

func TestACObserveFindsTheRowByTheChangeId(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newTNHost(t)
	def := tnWith(fake.New(t)).accountConnect()
	env := h.env("CHG1")
	unnamed := core.Effect{
		ChangeID: "CHG1", Seq: 1, Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: "tailnet.account:?CHG1",
		Recovery: &core.RecoveryID{Kind: "name", Value: "CHG1"}, Local: true, InverseLocal: true,
	}
	obs, err := def.Handler.Observe(ctx, env, unnamed)
	if err != nil || obs.Matches != 0 || string(obs.Current.State) != "null" {
		t.Errorf("Observe before Apply = %+v, %v, want no match and a null state", obs, err)
	}
	if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, env, acInput(nil)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
	}
	obs, err = def.Handler.Observe(ctx, env, unnamed)
	if err != nil || obs.Matches != 1 || obs.Resource != "tailnet.account:CHG1" || !obs.Exclusive {
		t.Fatalf("Observe of the unnamed creation after Apply = %+v, %v, want one exclusive match", obs, err)
	}
	made := h.journal.effects()[0]
	obs, err = def.Handler.Observe(ctx, env, made)
	if err != nil || string(obs.Current.State) != string(made.Post.State) {
		t.Errorf("Observe of the made effect = %s (%v), want its post-state %s", obs.Current.State, err, made.Post.State)
	}
}

func TestACInverseDeletesTheRowUnlessCleanupIsPending(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newTNHost(t)
	def := tnWith(fake.New(t)).accountConnect()
	env := h.env("CHG1")
	if _, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, env, acInput(nil)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
	}
	e := h.journal.effects()[0]
	acPending(t, h, "darkpanel-CHG0", "uncertain")

	_, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, env, e)
	if coded := acCode(t, err); coded.Code != errcode.CloudCleanupPending || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Fatalf("Inverse = %v, want a definite cloud.cleanup_pending", err)
	}
	if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read()); !ok {
		t.Fatal("the account was deleted although cleanup is pending")
	}

	err = h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return setKeyState(ctx, tx, "darkpanel-CHG0", "deleted", "", h.clock.Now()) })
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	res, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, env, e)
	if err != nil || res.Resource != "" {
		t.Fatalf("Inverse after cleanup = %+v, %v, want success", res, err)
	}
	if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read()); ok {
		t.Error("the account is still stored after the inverse")
	}
	if _, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, env, e); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("a second Inverse = %v, want success: the row is already gone", err)
	}
}

func TestACDisconnectPlans(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	srv := fake.New(t)
	h := newTNHost(t)
	def := tnWith(srv).accountDisconnect()

	_, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage("{}"))
	if coded := acCode(t, err); coded.Code != errcode.CloudNotConnected {
		t.Errorf("Plan without an account = %v, want cloud.not_connected", err)
	}

	acConnect(t, h, srv)
	out, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage("{}"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Plan: %v", err)
	}
	if out.Confirmation != fake.Tailnet {
		t.Errorf("confirmation %q, want the tailnet name %q", out.Confirmation, fake.Tailnet)
	}
	wantLine := core.DiffLine{Op: "-", Text: "disconnect tailnet " + fake.Tailnet + " (OAuth client " + fake.ClientID + "): the stored credentials are deleted"}
	if !slices.Contains(out.Diff, wantLine) || !slices.Contains(out.Diff, core.DiffLine{Op: " ", Text: "keys and devices in the tailnet stay as they are"}) {
		t.Errorf("diff %+v, want %+v and the line saying the tailnet is untouched", out.Diff, wantLine)
	}

	acPending(t, h, "darkpanel-CHG0", "retired")
	_, err = def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage("{}"))
	coded := acCode(t, err)
	if coded.Code != errcode.CloudCleanupPending || !core.IsDefinite(err) || !strings.Contains(coded.Detail, "darkpanel-CHG0") {
		t.Errorf("Plan with cleanup pending = %v, want a definite cloud.cleanup_pending naming the key", err)
	}

	out, err = def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(`{"abandonCleanup":true}`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Plan with abandonCleanup: %v", err)
	}
	if !slices.ContainsFunc(out.Diff, func(l core.DiffLine) bool {
		return l.Op == "-" && strings.HasPrefix(l.Text, "abandons pending cleanup: ") && strings.Contains(l.Text, "darkpanel-CHG0")
	}) {
		t.Errorf("diff %+v lacks the abandoned item", out.Diff)
	}
}

func TestACDisconnectApply(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	t.Run("nothing pending", func(t *testing.T) {
		srv := fake.New(t)
		h := newTNHost(t)
		acConnect(t, h, srv)
		def := tnWith(srv).accountDisconnect()
		raw, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("CHG2"), json.RawMessage("{}"))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
		}
		if string(raw) != `{"abandoned":[]}` {
			t.Errorf("output %s, want {\"abandoned\":[]}", raw)
		}
		if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read()); ok {
			t.Error("the account is still stored")
		}
		if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("CHG2"), json.RawMessage("{}"), raw); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("Verify after Apply: %v", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("cleanup pending", func(t *testing.T) {
		srv := fake.New(t)
		h := newTNHost(t)
		acConnect(t, h, srv)
		acPending(t, h, "darkpanel-CHG0", "uncertain")
		def := tnWith(srv).accountDisconnect()
		_, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("CHG2"), json.RawMessage("{}"))
		if coded := acCode(t, err); coded.Code != errcode.CloudCleanupPending {
			t.Fatalf("Apply = %v, want cloud.cleanup_pending", err)
		}
		if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read()); !ok {
			t.Fatal("the account was deleted although cleanup is pending")
		}
		if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env("CHG2"), json.RawMessage("{}"), json.RawMessage("{}")); err == nil {
			t.Error("Verify passed with the account still stored")
		}

		var pending []string
		if err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) (err error) { pending, err = cleanupPending(ctx, tx); return err }); err != nil || len(pending) == 0 {
			t.Fatalf("cleanupPending = %v, %v, want the key", pending, err)
		}
		raw, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env("CHG3"), json.RawMessage(`{"abandonCleanup":true}`))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Apply with abandonCleanup: %v", err)
		}
		var out Disconnected
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &out); err != nil || !slices.Equal(out.Abandoned, pending) {
			t.Errorf("abandoned %q (%v), want %q", out.Abandoned, err, pending)
		}
		if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read()); ok {
			t.Error("the account is still stored after abandoning the cleanup")
		}
		if _, ok, err := loadKey(ctx, h.db.Read(), "darkpanel-CHG0"); err != nil || !ok {
			t.Errorf("the key row is gone (%v, %v): disconnect must leave it for a later reconnect", ok, err)
		}
	})
}

// acEngine is a controller engine over the host's database serving the
// account actions.
func acEngine(t *testing.T, h *tnHost, srv *fake.Server) *lifecycle.Engine {
	t.Helper()
	reg, err := core.NewRegistry(acModule{t: tnWith(srv)})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	eng, err := lifecycle.New(lifecycle.Config{
		Side: core.SideController, Registry: reg, Validator: schema.NewValidator(), Journal: &coretest.MemJournal{}, Redact: schema.Redact,
		Base: core.Env{DB: h.db, Sealer: coretest.Sealer{}, Clock: h.clock, Log: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil))},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(eng.Close)
	return eng
}

var acAdmin = core.Principal{Actor: "user:u1", UserID: "u1", Scope: core.ScopeAdmin, Source: "203.0.113.7"}

func acWait(t *testing.T, eng *lifecycle.Engine, id string) core.ChangeView {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for {
		v, err := eng.Change(context.Background(), id)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if v.State != core.StateUndoing {
			return v
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("change %s is still undoing", id)
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

func acConnectThroughTheEngine(t *testing.T, eng *lifecycle.Engine) core.ChangeView {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	pv, err := eng.Plan(ctx, acAdmin, core.ActionRef{Name: "tailnet.account.connect", Version: 1}, acInput(nil), core.PlanOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Plan: %v", err)
	}
	cv, err := eng.Apply(ctx, acAdmin, pv.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
	if err != nil || cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("Apply = %+v, %v, want a completed change", cv, err)
	}
	return cv
}

func TestACEngineConnectsAndUndoes(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	srv := fake.New(t)
	h := newTNHost(t)
	eng := acEngine(t, h, srv)
	cv := acConnectThroughTheEngine(t, eng)
	if strings.Contains(string(cv.Output), fake.ClientSecret) {
		t.Errorf("the change output %s carries the client secret", cv.Output)
	}
	if a, ok, err := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read()); err != nil || !ok || a.ID != cv.ID {
		t.Fatalf("loadAccount = %+v, %v, %v, want the row of change %s", a, ok, err, cv.ID)
	}

	if _, err := eng.Undo(ctx, acAdmin, cv.ID, nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Undo: %v", err)
	}
	if v := acWait(t, eng, cv.ID); v.State != core.StateReverted {
		t.Fatalf("change is %s after the undo, want reverted", v.State)
	}
	if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read()); ok {
		t.Error("the account is still stored after the undo")
	}
	effs, err := eng.Effects(ctx, cv.ID)
	if err != nil || len(effs) != 1 || effs[0].State != core.EffectUndone {
		t.Errorf("effects %+v (%v), want one undone effect", effs, err)
	}
}

func TestACEngineUndoWithCleanupPendingNeedsRepair(t *testing.T) {
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the test to verify it fails**

Run: `mkdir -p /root/.cache/w3-tmp/42 && TMPDIR=/root/.cache/w3-tmp/42 GOTOOLCHAIN=local timeout 300 go test -count=1 -run 'TestAC' ./internal/modules/tailnet/`
Expected: FAIL to build, the first error `m.t.accountConnect undefined (type tn has no field or method accountConnect)` (and the same for `accountDisconnect`, `accountGet`, `connected`, `cloudEffect`).

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

`account.go` holds the helpers; `account_actions.go` the three constructors and their handlers (`accountConnectHandler`, `accountDisconnectHandler`, `accountGetHandler`, all private, each holding the `tn`).

1. `connected(ctx, db, s, clock)`: `loadAccount(ctx, db.Read())`; none: `errcode.New(errcode.CloudNotConnected, "no tailnet is connected")`. Otherwise open the secret with `cloud.OpenCredential(s, "tailnet_accounts", "client_secret_ct", a.ID, a.SecretCT)`, build the client with `t.newAPI(a, secret, clock)` and return it with the account. Wrap other errors as `tailnet: ...: %w`.
2. `cloudEffect(kind, resource, before)`: `core.Effect{Kind: kind, Resource: resource, Local: false, InverseLocal: false, CommitWait: cloud.CommitWait, Before: core.StateDoc{State: before}}` (`before` nil becomes `null`). Task 45 and later use it for provider writes; connect does not.
3. State document of the account row: the JSON object `{"id", "tailnet", "clientId", "tagsAllowed"}` (tags sorted). It holds no secret and no capability (capabilities can change between plan and undo and would make the engine see a conflict). The effect's `After` and `Post` and `Observe` all use it.
4. Input checks, shared by `Plan` and `Apply`, return `errcode.InvalidInput` wrapped in `core.Definite`, with a `FieldError` per problem: `tailnet` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9._@-]{1,253}$` (field `/tailnet`); `clientId` and `clientSecret` non-empty (`/clientId`, `/clientSecret`); `tagsAllowed` non-empty (`/tagsAllowed`) and each tag matching `^tag:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*$` (field `/tagsAllowed/<index>`, the index in the input). Tags are then de-duplicated and sorted. No detail or message quotes an input value.
5. Probing: build `Probe`s for the three reads above from the `api` methods (discarding the results) and call `cloud.ProbeReads(ctx, probes, writes)` with the four write names. When any probed read failed with detail `cloud.auth_failed`, return `core.Definite(errcode.New(errcode.CloudAuthFailed, "the OAuth client id or secret was refused"))`. Every other probe failure stays a `missing` capability. The temporary `account` value given to `newAPI` before the row exists carries the input's tailnet and client id and the change id (empty at plan).
6. `accountConnect()`: `core.DefineMutating` with `Name: "tailnet.account.connect"`, `Version: 1`, `Class: core.ClassCompensable`, `Side: core.SideController`, `LockKeys: []string{"tailnet"}`, no `CompensatedBy`, no `ForwardOnly` (the handler's `Inverse` is its one compensation mechanism).
   - `Plan`: validate; when `loadAccount` finds a row, `core.Definite(errcode.New(errcode.CloudConflict, "a tailnet is already connected: disconnect it first"))`; build the client with `[]byte(in.ClientSecret)`, probe. The diff is exactly: `+ connect tailnet <tailnet> with OAuth client <client id>`; `+ tags the client may assign: <tags joined by ", ">`; one ` ` line per capability in probe order, `capability <name>: <state>` plus ` (<detail>)` when the detail is not empty; and the final ` ` line `undo deletes the stored credentials once no provider cleanup is pending`. `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 of the lines `tailnet.account`, the tailnet, the client id, the sorted tags joined by `,` and `absent` (not the capabilities, which a second probe could change). No confirmation. The plan carries no secret.
   - `Apply`: validate; refuse an existing row as the plan does; build the client and probe (a refused client returns the `cloud.auth_failed` error above before anything is journaled); seal the secret with `cloud.SealCredential(env.Sealer, "tailnet_accounts", "client_secret_ct", env.ChangeID, secret)`; `env.Effects.Intend` a `core.EffectCreate` with `Resource: "tailnet.account:?" + env.ChangeID`, `Recovery: &core.RecoveryID{Kind: "name", Value: env.ChangeID}`, `Local: true`, `InverseLocal: true`, `Before: {State: null}`, `After` the state document; `env.DB.Write` that re-checks no row exists (`core.Definite` `cloud.conflict`) and `insertAccount` with `ID: env.ChangeID`, `ConnectedAt: env.Clock.Now()` and the probed capabilities; then `Made(ctx, seq, "tailnet.account:"+env.ChangeID, {State: the state document})`. Return `AccountView` from the stored values. The secret appears in no effect, output, error or log line.
   - `Verify`: `loadAccount` must find a row whose `ID` is `env.ChangeID`, else a plain `tailnet: change <id> stored no account` error.
   - `Observe(ctx, env, e)`: the row id is `e.Recovery.Value` while the resource still carries `?`, else the resource without the prefix `tailnet.account:`. Load the account: when its id matches, `Current` is the state document, `Matches` 1 and `Resource` `tailnet.account:<id>`; otherwise `Current` is `{State: null}` and `Matches` 0. `Exclusive` is true. The same code serves an effect that is undoing or undone.
   - `Inverse(ctx, env, e)`: one `env.DB.Write` transaction; when `cleanupPending(ctx, tx)` returns anything, return `core.Definite(errcode.New(errcode.CloudCleanupPending, <"cleanup is pending: " plus the lines joined by "; ">))` without writing, so the effect stays made and the undo settles in `needs_repair`. Otherwise `deleteAccount` for the id (a row already gone is success). Result: empty `core.InverseResult`.
7. `accountDisconnect()`: `Name: "tailnet.account.disconnect"`, `Class: core.ClassIrreversible`, controller side, `LockKeys: []string{"tailnet"}`.
   - `Plan`: no row: `core.Definite` `cloud.not_connected`. Read `cleanupPending` inside a read transaction (`env.DB.Read().BeginTx(ctx, nil)`, rolled back). Pending and not `abandonCleanup`: `core.Definite(errcode.New(errcode.CloudCleanupPending, ...))` whose detail names every pending line and says to wait or pass `abandonCleanup`. Diff: `- disconnect tailnet <tailnet> (OAuth client <client id>): the stored credentials are deleted`, ` ` `keys and devices in the tailnet stay as they are`, and with `abandonCleanup` one `-` line `abandons pending cleanup: <line>` per pending line. `Confirmation` is the tailnet name. `StateHash` covers the account id, the flag and the pending lines.
   - `Apply`: one `env.DB.Write`: `loadAccount` (none: `cloud.not_connected`), `cleanupPending`; pending without the flag: `core.Definite` `cloud.cleanup_pending`; `deleteAccount`. Output `Disconnected{Abandoned: <the pending lines when the flag is set, else an empty non-nil slice>}`. It deletes nothing else: the `tailnet_keys` rows stay for a later reconnect.
   - `Verify`: no row remains.
8. `accountGet()`: `core.DefineRead`, `Name: "tailnet.account.get"`, controller side, no lock keys. It reads `loadAccount(ctx, env.DB.Read())` and answers `AccountStatus{Connected: false}` or `{Connected: true, Account: &AccountView{...}}`; it calls no provider and carries no secret.

```go
package cloudflare

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/cloud"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/lifecycle"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/cloudflare/fake"
)

const acAccountChange = "01J00000000000000000000001"

var acAdmin = core.Principal{Actor: "user:u1", UserID: "u1", Scope: core.ScopeAdmin, Source: "203.0.113.7"}

// acConnect inserts the connected account the fake server accepts.
func acConnect(t *testing.T, h *cfHost, _ *fake.Server) account {
	t.Helper()
	ct, err := cloud.SealCredential(coretest.Sealer{}, "cloudflare_accounts", "token_ct", acAccountChange, []byte(fake.Token))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	a := account{
		ID: acAccountChange, AccountID: fake.AccountID, TokenCT: ct, ConnectedAt: h.clock.Now(),
		Capabilities: []cloud.Capability{{Name: "tunnels.read", State: cloud.CapabilityOK}},
	}
	ctx := context.Background()
	if err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertAccount(ctx, tx, a) }); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return a
}

type acModule struct{ actions []core.ActionDef }

func (m acModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: ID, Version: 1, Actions: m.actions}
}

func acEngine(t *testing.T, h *cfHost, c cf) *lifecycle.Engine {
	t.Helper()
	reg, err := core.NewRegistry(acModule{[]core.ActionDef{c.accountConnect(), c.accountDisconnect(), c.accountGet()}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	eng, err := lifecycle.New(lifecycle.Config{
		Side: core.SideController, Registry: reg, Validator: schema.NewValidator(), Journal: &coretest.MemJournal{}, Redact: schema.Redact,
		Base: core.Env{DB: h.db, Sealer: coretest.Sealer{}, Clock: h.clock, Log: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil))},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(eng.Close)
	return eng
}

// acRun plans action and applies the plan with the plan's confirmation phrase.
func acRun(t *testing.T, eng *lifecycle.Engine, action, input string) (core.PlanView, core.ChangeView, error) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	pv, err := eng.Plan(ctx, acAdmin, core.ActionRef{Name: action, Version: 1}, json.RawMessage(input), core.PlanOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		return pv, core.ChangeView{}, err
	}
	cv, err := eng.Apply(ctx, acAdmin, pv.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{Confirmation: pv.Confirmation})
	return pv, cv, err
}

// acUndo undoes a change and waits until the undo has settled.
func acUndo(t *testing.T, eng *lifecycle.Engine, changeID string) core.ChangeView {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, err := eng.Undo(ctx, acAdmin, changeID, nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for {
		v, err := eng.Change(ctx, changeID)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if v.State != core.StateUndoing || time.Now().After(deadline) {
			return v
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

func acEffects(t *testing.T, h *cfHost, changeID string) []string {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := h.db.Read().QueryContext(context.Background(),
		`SELECT kind, resource, state, local FROM core_effects WHERE change_id = ? ORDER BY seq`, changeID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
	var out []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var kind, resource, state string
		var local int
		if err := rows.Scan(&kind, &resource, &state, &local); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%s %s %s local=%d", kind, resource, state, local))
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return out
}

// acPending inserts a hostname row that is not active, which blocks deleting the account.
func acPending(t *testing.T, h *cfHost) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	now := h.clock.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
	err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO cloudflare_tunnels (id, name, change_id, created_at) VALUES ('t1', 'darkpanel-x', 'c1', ?)`, now); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		_, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO cloudflare_hostnames (hostname, tunnel_id, service, phase, change_id, updated_at)
			VALUES ('app.example.com', 't1', 'http://10.0.0.5:80', 'adding_rule', 'c1', ?)`, now)
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func acActivate(t *testing.T, h *cfHost) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		_, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `UPDATE cloudflare_hostnames SET phase = 'active' WHERE hostname = 'app.example.com'`)
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func acConnectInput(token string) string {
	return `{"accountId":"` + fake.AccountID + `","apiToken":"` + token + `"}`
}

func acDiff(pv core.PlanView) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, l := range pv.Diff {
		b.WriteString(l.Op + " " + l.Text + "\n")
	}
	return b.String()
}

func TestAcConnectStoresTheAccount(t *testing.T) {
	srv := fake.New(t)
	h := newCFHost(t)
	eng := acEngine(t, h, cfWith(srv))

	pv, cv, err := acRun(t, eng, "cloudflare.account.connect", acConnectInput(fake.Token))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("change is %s (%+v), want completed", cv.State, cv.Error)
	}
	diff := acDiff(pv)
	for _, want := range []string{
		"cloudflare account " + fake.AccountID,
		"capability tunnels.read: ok", "capability zones.read: ok",
		"capability tunnels.write: unverified", "capability dns.write: unverified",
	} {
		if !strings.Contains(diff, want) {
			t.Errorf("plan diff lacks %q:\n%s", want, diff)
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(diff, fake.Token) {
		t.Error("the plan diff carries the API token")
	}

	ctx := context.Background()
	acct, ok, err := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read())
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("loadAccount = %v, %v; want the connected account", ok, err)
	}
	wantCaps := []cloud.Capability{
		{Name: "tunnels.read", State: cloud.CapabilityOK}, {Name: "zones.read", State: cloud.CapabilityOK},
		{Name: "tunnels.write", State: cloud.CapabilityUnverified}, {Name: "dns.write", State: cloud.CapabilityUnverified},
	}
	if acct.ID != cv.ID || acct.AccountID != fake.AccountID || !slices.Equal(acct.Capabilities, wantCaps) {
		t.Errorf("stored account %+v, want id %s, account %s and capabilities %+v", acct, cv.ID, fake.AccountID, wantCaps)
	}
	token, err := cloud.OpenCredential(coretest.Sealer{}, "cloudflare_accounts", "token_ct", acct.ID, acct.TokenCT)
	if err != nil || string(token) != fake.Token {
		t.Errorf("sealed token opens to %q (%v), want the connected token", token, err)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(cv.Output), fake.Token) {
		t.Errorf("change output %s carries the API token", cv.Output)
	}
	var view AccountView
	if err := json.Unmarshal(cv.Output, &view); err != nil || view.AccountID != fake.AccountID || !slices.Equal(view.Capabilities, wantCaps) {
		t.Errorf("output %s (%v), want the account view", cv.Output, err)
	}
	if got, want := acEffects(t, h, cv.ID), []string{"create cloudflare.account:" + cv.ID + " made local=1"}; !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("effects %q, want %q", got, want)
	}

	var tunnelsRead, zonesRead bool
	for _, r := range srv.Cloud().Requests() {
		if r.Method != http.MethodGet {
			t.Errorf("connect sent %s %s; it may only read from Cloudflare", r.Method, r.Path)
		}
		if got := r.Header.Get("Authorization"); got != "Bearer "+fake.Token {
			t.Errorf("%s %s sent Authorization %q", r.Method, r.Path, got)
		}
		tunnelsRead = tunnelsRead || strings.HasSuffix(r.Path, "/cfd_tunnel")
		zonesRead = zonesRead || strings.HasSuffix(r.Path, "/zones")
	}
	if !tunnelsRead || !zonesRead {
		t.Errorf("tunnels listed %v, zones listed %v; connect probes both", tunnelsRead, zonesRead)
	}
}

func TestAcConnectReportsAMissingPermission(t *testing.T) {
	srv := fake.New(t)
	srv.SetPermissions(fake.PermTunnelWrite, fake.PermDNSWrite)
	h := newCFHost(t)
	eng := acEngine(t, h, cfWith(srv))

	pv, cv, err := acRun(t, eng, "cloudflare.account.connect", acConnectInput(fake.Token))
	if err != nil || cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("connect = %v, %v (%+v); a missing read permission is reported, not refused", cv.State, err, cv.Error)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(acDiff(pv), "capability zones.read: missing (cloud.permission_missing)") {
		t.Errorf("plan diff does not report the missing Zone Read permission:\n%s", acDiff(pv))
	}
	acct, _, err := loadAccount(context.Background(), h.db.Read())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := acct.Capabilities[:2]; !slices.Equal(got, []cloud.Capability{
		{Name: "tunnels.read", State: cloud.CapabilityOK},
		{Name: "zones.read", State: cloud.CapabilityMissing, Detail: "cloud.permission_missing"},
	}) {
		t.Errorf("stored read capabilities %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestAcConnectRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name      string
		input     string
		connected bool
		code      errcode.Code
		field     string
	}{
		{"account id of the wrong shape", `{"accountId":"nope","apiToken":"` + fake.Token + `"}`, false, errcode.InvalidInput, "/accountId"},
		{"blank token", acConnectInput("  "), false, errcode.InvalidInput, "/apiToken"},
		{"token with a space", acConnectInput("fake token"), false, errcode.InvalidInput, "/apiToken"},
		{"token the provider rejects", acConnectInput("other-token"), false, errcode.CloudAuthFailed, ""},
		{"an account is already connected", acConnectInput(fake.Token), true, errcode.InvalidInput, ""},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			srv := fake.New(t)
			h := newCFHost(t)
			if tt.connected {
				acConnect(t, h, srv)
			}
			_, _, err := acRun(t, acEngine(t, h, cfWith(srv)), "cloudflare.account.connect", tt.input)
			e := errcode.From(err)
			if e.Code != tt.code {
				t.Fatalf("error %v, want code %s", err, tt.code)
			}
			if tt.field != "" && !slices.ContainsFunc(e.Fields, func(f errcode.FieldError) bool { return f.Path == tt.field }) {
				t.Errorf("error fields %+v, want one naming %s", e.Fields, tt.field)
			}
			if strings.Contains(e.Detail, "other-token") || strings.Contains(e.Detail, fake.Token) {
				t.Errorf("detail %q carries the token", e.Detail)
			}
			if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(context.Background(), h.db.Read()); ok != tt.connected {
				t.Errorf("an account is stored = %v after the refusal, want %v", ok, tt.connected)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAcConnectUndo(t *testing.T) {
	srv := fake.New(t)
	h := newCFHost(t)
	eng := acEngine(t, h, cfWith(srv))
	_, cv, err := acRun(t, eng, "cloudflare.account.connect", acConnectInput(fake.Token))
	if err != nil || cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("connect = %v, %v", cv.State, err)
	}
	acPending(t, h)

	v := acUndo(t, eng, cv.ID)
	if v.State != core.StateNeedsRepair {
		t.Fatalf("undo with a hostname mid-phase left the change %s, want needs_repair", v.State)
	}
	if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(context.Background(), h.db.Read()); !ok {
		t.Error("the undo deleted the account while cleanup was pending")
	}
	if got, want := acEffects(t, h, cv.ID), []string{"create cloudflare.account:" + cv.ID + " made local=1"}; !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("effects %q after the refused undo, want %q", got, want)
	}

	acActivate(t, h)
	v = acUndo(t, eng, cv.ID)
	if v.State != core.StateReverted {
		t.Fatalf("undo once cleanup finished left the change %s, want reverted", v.State)
	}
	if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(context.Background(), h.db.Read()); ok {
		t.Error("the account row is still there after the undo")
	}
	if got, want := acEffects(t, h, cv.ID), []string{"create cloudflare.account:" + cv.ID + " undone local=1"}; !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("effects %q after the undo, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestAcDisconnect(t *testing.T) {
	srv := fake.New(t)
	h := newCFHost(t)
	acConnect(t, h, srv)
	eng := acEngine(t, h, cfWith(srv))
	ctx := context.Background()
	ref := core.ActionRef{Name: "cloudflare.account.disconnect", Version: 1}

	pv, err := eng.Plan(ctx, acAdmin, ref, json.RawMessage(`{}`), core.PlanOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if pv.Confirmation != fake.AccountID {
		t.Errorf("confirmation %q, want the account id %s", pv.Confirmation, fake.AccountID)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(acDiff(pv), "- cloudflare account "+fake.AccountID) {
		t.Errorf("plan diff:\n%s", acDiff(pv))
	}
	_, err = eng.Apply(ctx, acAdmin, pv.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
	if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.PlanConfirmationNeeded {
		t.Fatalf("apply without the confirmation = %v, want %s", err, errcode.PlanConfirmationNeeded)
	}
	cv, err := eng.Apply(ctx, acAdmin, pv.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{Confirmation: pv.Confirmation})
	if err != nil || cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("apply = %v, %v (%+v)", cv.State, err, cv.Error)
	}
	if string(cv.Output) != `{"abandoned":[]}` {
		t.Errorf("output %s, want an empty abandoned list", cv.Output)
	}
	if _, ok, _ := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read()); ok {
		t.Error("the account row is still there")
	}
	_, err = eng.Plan(ctx, acAdmin, ref, json.RawMessage(`{}`), core.PlanOptions{})
	if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.CloudNotConnected {
		t.Errorf("plan with no account = %v, want %s", err, errcode.CloudNotConnected)
	}
}

func TestAcDisconnectWithCleanupPending(t *testing.T) {
```
