func TestAcGet(t *testing.T) {

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

`account.go`:

1. Doc comments on every exported identifier; error strings that are not `*errcode.Error` start `cloudflare:`. Constants for the capability names `tunnels.read`, `zones.read` (the read probes) and `tunnels.write`, `dns.write` (the write capabilities, always reported `unverified`).
2. `connected(ctx, db, s, clock)`: `loadAccount(ctx, db.Read())`; no row is `errcode.New(errcode.CloudNotConnected, ...)`; otherwise `cloud.OpenCredential(s, "cloudflare_accounts", "token_ct", acct.ID, acct.TokenCT)` and `c.newAPI(acct.AccountID, token, clock)`. It returns the api and the stored account. A failure to open the secret is returned wrapped, never as `cloud.not_connected`.
3. `cloudEffect(kind, resource, before)`: a `core.Effect` with `Kind`, `Resource`, `Local` false, `InverseLocal` false, `CommitWait` `cloud.CommitWait` and `Before.State` set to `before`, or to the JSON `null` when `before` is empty. It sets no `Recovery` and no `After`: the caller adds them (a creation sets its own `Recovery`).
4. `accountView(a account) AccountView` (capabilities never nil) and `accountState(accountID string) json.RawMessage`, the effect's state document `{"accountId":"<id>"}`.
5. `probeCapabilities(ctx, a *api) []cloud.Capability`: `cloud.ProbeReads` with a probe `tunnels.read` that calls `a.Tunnels(ctx, "")` and a probe `zones.read` that calls `a.Zones(ctx)`, and the writes `tunnels.write`, `dns.write`. The result order is exactly `tunnels.read`, `zones.read`, `tunnels.write`, `dns.write`.
6. `accountGet()`: `core.DefineRead` of `cloudflare.account.get`, version 1, `Side: core.SideController`, no lock keys, handler reading `loadAccount(ctx, env.DB.Read())`: `AccountStatus{Connected: false}` when there is no row, else `Connected: true` with `accountView`. It never returns the sealed token.

`account_connect.go`: `accountConnect()` is `core.DefineMutating` of `cloudflare.account.connect`, version 1, `Class: core.ClassCompensable`, `Side: core.SideController`, `LockKeys: []string{"cloudflare"}`, with a handler that implements `Plan`, `Apply`, `Verify`, `Observe` and `Inverse` (so `findHandlers` registers the undo).

- Input check (used by Plan and Apply): `accountId` must match `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`; `apiToken` must be non-empty after trimming, at most 512 bytes, with no space or control character. A failure is `core.Definite` of an `*errcode.Error` with code `request.invalid_input` and a `FieldError` at path `/accountId` or `/apiToken`; no detail contains the token.
- `Plan`: check the input; an existing row is `core.Definite` of `request.invalid_input` with the detail "a Cloudflare account is already connected"; build the api with `c.newAPI(in.AccountID, []byte(in.APIToken), env.Clock)`, call `VerifyToken` (its error is returned as is: `cloud.auth_failed` for a rejected token) and `probeCapabilities`. The diff is one `+` line `cloudflare account <accountId>` followed by one `+` line per capability, `capability <name>: <state>` with ` (<detail>)` appended when the capability has a detail. `StateHash` is the constant `no account`. A missing read permission is reported in the diff, never refused.
- `Apply`: repeat the input check, `VerifyToken` and the probe. Seal the token with `cloud.SealCredential(env.Sealer, "cloudflare_accounts", "token_ct", env.ChangeID, token)`. Journal one effect before the write: `Kind` create, `Resource` `cloudflare.account:?<change id>`, `Recovery` `{Kind: "name", Value: <change id>}`, `Local` true, `InverseLocal` true, `Before.State` `null`, `After` `accountState`. Then, in one `env.DB.Write` transaction, refuse with `core.Definite` `request.invalid_input` when a row exists and `insertAccount` the row (`ID` the change id, `ConnectedAt` `env.Clock.Now()`). When that transaction fails, call `env.Effects.Skipped` before returning the error; on success call `env.Effects.Made` with resource `cloudflare.account:<change id>` and the same state document. Return `accountView`. Nothing is sent to Cloudflare except reads.
- `Verify`: the stored row exists and its `AccountID` equals `in.AccountID`; it must not use `out`.
- `Observe`: the identity of `e.Resource` after the colon, without a leading `?`, is the account id; `loadAccount(ctx, env.DB.Read())`; a row with that id observes `{"accountId":"<id>"}` with `Matches` 1 and `Resource` `cloudflare.account:<id>`, anything else observes JSON `null` with `Matches` 0; `Exclusive` true.
- `Inverse`: one `env.DB.Write` transaction that calls `cleanupPending(ctx, tx)`; a non-empty list returns `core.Definite(errcode.New(errcode.CloudCleanupPending, "cleanup is pending: " + items joined by "; "))` without writing (the engine then leaves the effect `made` and the undo `needs_repair`); otherwise `deleteAccount(ctx, tx, <identity>)`.

`account_disconnect.go`: `accountDisconnect()` is `core.DefineMutating` of `cloudflare.account.disconnect`, version 1, `Class: core.ClassIrreversible`, controller side, lock key `cloudflare`, with `Plan`, `Apply` and `Verify` only (no effect is journaled).

- `Plan`: no row is `core.Definite` `cloud.not_connected`. Read the pending list with `cleanupPending` inside `env.DB.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {...})` that writes nothing (Plan has no transaction of its own). With items pending and `abandonCleanup` false, fail with `core.Definite` `cloud.cleanup_pending` whose detail is `cleanup is pending: ` plus the items joined by `; `. `Confirmation` is the account's `AccountID`. The diff is the `-` line `cloudflare account <accountId>` and, when abandoning, one `-` line `abandon: <item>` per pending item. `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 of the account id and the pending items, so a pending list that changes between plan and apply forces a new plan.
- `Apply`: in one `env.DB.Write` transaction load the account (none: `core.Definite` `cloud.not_connected`), call `cleanupPending` again, refuse with the same `cloud.cleanup_pending` error unless `abandonCleanup` is set, and `deleteAccount`. The output `Disconnected.Abandoned` lists the items when abandoning and is an empty, non-nil slice otherwise, so it encodes as `[]`. Tunnel and hostname rows are left as they are.
- `Verify`: no account row remains.

)

type regAction struct {
	name   string
	class  core.Class
	scope  core.Scope // MinScope; "" keeps the class default
	long   bool
	apply  time.Duration // 0 keeps the 30 s default
	undoer bool
}

var regActions = []regAction{
	{"docker.container.start", core.ClassCompensable, "", false, 0, true},
	{"docker.container.stop", core.ClassCompensable, "", false, 0, true},
	{"docker.container.restart", core.ClassCompensable, "", false, 0, true},
	{"docker.container.remove", core.ClassIrreversible, "", false, 0, false},
	{"docker.container.inspect", core.ClassRead, "", false, 0, false},
	{"docker.container.logs", core.ClassRead, "", false, 0, false},
	{"docker.container.reveal-env", core.ClassRead, core.ScopeAdmin, false, 0, false},
	{"docker.image.pull", core.ClassCompensable, "", true, 30 * time.Minute, true},
	{"docker.image.remove", core.ClassIrreversible, "", false, 0, false},
	{"docker.image.prune", core.ClassIrreversible, "", false, 0, false},
	{"docker.network.create", core.ClassCompensable, "", false, 0, true},
	{"docker.network.remove", core.ClassIrreversible, "", false, 0, false},
	{"docker.network.connect", core.ClassCompensable, "", false, 0, true},
	{"docker.network.disconnect", core.ClassCompensable, "", false, 0, true},

	{"docker.compose.down", core.ClassIrreversible, core.ScopeAdmin, true, 10 * time.Minute, false},
	{"docker.compose.pull", core.ClassCompensable, core.ScopeAdmin, true, 30 * time.Minute, true},
	{"docker.compose.restart", core.ClassCompensable, core.ScopeAdmin, true, 10 * time.Minute, true},
}

func regModule(t *testing.T) module {
	t.Helper()
	return newModule(newDKHost(t).dk(), coretest.NewFakeClock(time.Date(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)))
}

func TestRegManifestDeclaresTheActions(t *testing.T) {
	man := regModule(t).Manifest()
	if man.ID != ID || man.Version != 1 || !man.DefaultEnabled {
		t.Errorf("manifest %q v%d default-enabled %v, want docker v1 enabled by default", man.ID, man.Version, man.DefaultEnabled)
	}
	got := map[string]core.ActionDef{}
	for _, a := range man.Actions {
		if _, dup := got[a.Spec.Name]; dup {
			t.Errorf("%s is declared twice", a.Spec.Name)
		}
		got[a.Spec.Name] = a
	}
	for _, want := range regActions {
		a, ok := got[want.name]
		if !ok {
			t.Errorf("%s is not declared", want.name)
			continue
		}
		delete(got, want.name)
		s := a.Spec
		timeout := s.ApplyTimeout
		if timeout == 0 {
			timeout = 30 * time.Second
		}
		wantTimeout := want.apply
		if wantTimeout == 0 {
			wantTimeout = 30 * time.Second
		}
		wantLocks := []string{"docker"}
		if want.class == core.ClassRead {
			wantLocks = nil
		}
		if s.Version != 1 || s.Class != want.class || s.Side != core.SideAgent || !slices.Equal(s.LockKeys, wantLocks) ||
			s.MinScope != want.scope || s.LongRunning != want.long || timeout != wantTimeout || s.Internal ||
			s.Reveal != (want.name == "docker.container.reveal-env") {
			t.Errorf("%s: spec %+v; want class %s on the agent, locks %v, min scope %q, long-running %v, timeout %s",
				want.name, s, want.class, wantLocks, want.scope, want.long, wantTimeout)
		}
		if (a.Handler.Inverse != nil) != want.undoer {
			t.Errorf("%s: undo handler %v, want %v", want.name, a.Handler.Inverse != nil, want.undoer)
		}
		if want.class != core.ClassRead && a.Handler.Observe == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s has no Observe", want.name)
		}
	}
	for name := range got {
		t.Errorf("%s is declared but is not in the action table", name)
	}
}

func TestRegProductionModuleHoldsAPullHub(t *testing.T) {

var errRegEnough = errors.New("enough events")

// TestRegPullHubIsShared: the hub the module creates is the one docker.image.pull
// publishes to and the docker.pull stream reads from.
func TestRegPullHubIsShared(t *testing.T) {
	h := newDKHost(t)
	const ref = "alpine:3.20"
	h.docker.putImage(dkImage(ref, 1000))
	if h.docker.pulls == nil {
		h.docker.pulls = map[string][]dockerapi.PullMessage{}
	}
	h.docker.pulls[ref] = []dockerapi.PullMessage{{Status: "Pulling from library/alpine"}, {Status: "Pull complete", ID: "abc123"}}
	m := newModule(h.dk(), h.clock)

	var pull core.ActionDef
	for _, a := range m.Manifest().Actions {
		if a.Spec.Name == "docker.image.pull" {
			pull = a
		}
	}
	const changeID = "01J00000000000000000000001"
	if _, err := pull.Handler.Apply(context.Background(), h.env(changeID), json.RawMessage(`{"image":"`+ref+`"}`)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	var stream core.StreamDef
	for _, s := range m.Streams() {
		if s.Name == "pull" {
			stream = s
		}
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	var statuses []string
	_ = stream.Run(ctx, h.env(""), json.RawMessage(`{"changeId":"`+changeID+`"}`), func(event any) error {
		ev, ok := event.(PullEvent)
		if !ok {
			t.Errorf("stream emitted %T, want PullEvent", event)
			return errRegEnough
		}
		statuses = append(statuses, ev.Status)
		if slices.Contains(statuses, "Pull complete") {
			return errRegEnough
		}
		return nil
	})
	if want := []string{"Pulling from library/alpine", "Pull complete"}; !slices.Equal(statuses[:min(len(statuses), len(want))], want) {
		t.Errorf("pull stream replayed %q, want it to begin with %q", statuses, want)
	}
}

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `docker.go`:

1. `module` becomes `struct{ k dk; pulls *pullHub }`. `newModule(k dk, clock core.Clock) module` returns `module{k: k, pulls: newPullHub(clock)}`; `Module()` returns `newModule(productionDK(), core.SystemClock{})`. Neither opens a connection to the Engine: registration builds every `core.ActionDef`, `core.ResourceDef` and `core.StreamDef` without a call to the daemon, because `registry.Build()` runs on hosts without Docker and in the schema generator.
2. `Manifest()` returns `ID`, `Version: 1`, `DefaultEnabled: true`, `Actions: m.actions()`, `Resources: m.resources()`, `Preflight: m.k.preflight()`, `OwnedPaths: ownedPaths()` and `Migrations: map[core.Side]fs.FS{core.SideAgent: agentMigrations()}`. ```go
package tailnet

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/cloud"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/cloud/cloudfake"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/lifecycle"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/tailnet/fake"
)

var dvAdmin = core.Principal{Actor: "user:u1", UserID: "u1", Scope: core.ScopeAdmin, Source: "203.0.113.7"}

type dvModule struct{ actions []core.ActionDef }

func (m dvModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: ID, Version: 1, Actions: m.actions}
}

type dvFixture struct {
	t   *testing.T
	srv *fake.Server
	h   *tnHost
	tn  tn
	eng *lifecycle.Engine
}

// dvNew builds a controller engine serving the three device actions over the
// fake Tailscale API, with the account connected when connect is set.
func dvNew(t *testing.T, connect bool) *dvFixture {
	t.Helper()
	srv := fake.New(t)
	h := newTNHost(t)
	if connect {
		acConnect(t, h, srv)
	}
	n := tnWith(srv)
	reg, err := core.NewRegistry(dvModule{[]core.ActionDef{n.deviceList(), n.deviceAuthorize(), n.deviceSetRoutes()}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	eng, err := lifecycle.New(lifecycle.Config{
		Side: core.SideController, Registry: reg, Validator: schema.NewValidator(), Journal: &coretest.MemJournal{}, Redact: schema.Redact,
		Base: core.Env{DB: h.db, Sealer: coretest.Sealer{}, Clock: h.clock, Log: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil))},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(eng.Close)
	return &dvFixture{t: t, srv: srv, h: h, tn: n, eng: eng}
}

func (f *dvFixture) plan(action, input string) (core.PlanView, error) {
	f.t.Helper()
	return f.eng.Plan(context.Background(), dvAdmin, core.ActionRef{Name: action, Version: 1}, json.RawMessage(input), core.PlanOptions{})
}

// do plans action and applies the plan.
func (f *dvFixture) do(action, input string) (core.PlanView, core.ChangeView, error) {
	f.t.Helper()
	pv, err := f.plan(action, input)
	if err != nil {
		return pv, core.ChangeView{}, err
	}
	cv, err := f.eng.Apply(context.Background(), dvAdmin, pv.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
	return pv, cv, err
}

// undo undoes a change and waits until the undo has settled.
func (f *dvFixture) undo(changeID string) core.ChangeView {
	f.t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, err := f.eng.Undo(ctx, dvAdmin, changeID, nil); err != nil {
		f.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for {
		v, err := f.eng.Change(ctx, changeID)
		if err != nil {
			f.t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if v.State != core.StateUndoing || time.Now().After(deadline) {
			return v
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

func (f *dvFixture) effects(changeID string) []string {
	f.t.Helper()
	rows, err := f.h.db.Read().QueryContext(context.Background(),
		`SELECT kind, resource, state, reason, local, commit_wait_ns FROM core_effects WHERE change_id = ? ORDER BY seq`, changeID)
	if err != nil {
		f.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
	var out []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var kind, resource, state, reason string
		var local int
		var wait int64
		if err := rows.Scan(&kind, &resource, &state, &reason, &local, &wait); err != nil {
			f.t.Fatal(err)
		}
		out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%s %s %s %s local=%d wait=%d", kind, resource, state, reason, local, wait))
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		f.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return out
}

// posts counts the POST requests the fake received on a path ending in suffix.
func (f *dvFixture) posts(suffix string) int {
	n := 0
	for _, r := range f.srv.Cloud().Requests() {
		if r.Method == http.MethodPost && strings.HasSuffix(r.Path, suffix) {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

	}
	return v
}

func TestDvListSortsAndNormalizesDevices(t *testing.T) {
	f := dvNew(t, true)
	web := f.srv.AddDevice(fake.Device{Name: "web-1.example.ts.net", Hostname: "web-1", OS: "linux", User: "a@example.com",
		Addresses: []string{"100.64.0.1"}, Tags: []string{"tag:server"}, Authorized: true})
	gw := f.srv.AddDevice(fake.Device{Name: "gw.example.ts.net", Hostname: "gw", OS: "linux", User: "a@example.com",
		Addresses: []string{"100.64.0.2"}, Authorized: true,
		AdvertisedRoutes: []string{"::/0", "10.0.0.0/24", "0.0.0.0/0"}, EnabledRoutes: []string{"10.0.0.0/24"}})
	bare := f.srv.AddDevice(fake.Device{Name: "bare.example.ts.net", Hostname: "bare"})

	raw, err := f.eng.Read(context.Background(), dvAdmin, core.ActionRef{Name: "tailnet.device.list", Version: 1}, json.RawMessage(`{}`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(raw), "null") {
		t.Errorf("the list carries a null member: %s", raw)
	}
	var got DeviceList
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &got); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var ids []string
	for _, d := range got.Devices {
		ids = append(ids, d.ID)
	}
	if want := []string{bare, gw, web}; !slices.Equal(ids, want) {
		t.Fatalf("devices %v, want %v (sorted by name)", ids, want)
	}
	b, g, w := got.Devices[0], got.Devices[1], got.Devices[2]
	if b.Authorized || b.Addresses == nil || b.Tags == nil || b.AdvertisedRoutes == nil || b.EnabledRoutes == nil || b.ExitNode {
		t.Errorf("bare device %+v, want empty lists, unauthorized, not an exit node", b)
	}
	if want := []string{"0.0.0.0/0", "10.0.0.0/24", "::/0"}; !slices.Equal(g.AdvertisedRoutes, want) || !slices.Equal(g.EnabledRoutes, []string{"10.0.0.0/24"}) {
		t.Errorf("gateway routes %v / %v, want the advertised routes sorted and one enabled", g.AdvertisedRoutes, g.EnabledRoutes)
	}
	if !g.ExitNode || g.ExitNodeEnabled {
		t.Errorf("gateway exit node %v enabled %v, want an exit node that is not approved", g.ExitNode, g.ExitNodeEnabled)
	}
	if w.Hostname != "web-1" || w.OS != "linux" || w.User != "a@example.com" || !w.Authorized ||
		!slices.Equal(w.Addresses, []string{"100.64.0.1"}) || !slices.Equal(w.Tags, []string{"tag:server"}) {
		t.Errorf("web device %+v", w)
	}
}

func TestDvAuthorizeAndUndo(t *testing.T) {
	f := dvNew(t, true)
	id := f.srv.AddDevice(fake.Device{Name: "web-1.example.ts.net", Hostname: "web-1"})

	pv, cv, err := f.do("tailnet.device.authorize", `{"device":"`+id+`"}`)
	if err != nil || cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("authorize = %v, %v (%+v)", cv.State, err, cv.Error)
	}
	wantDiff := []core.DiffLine{
		{Op: " ", Text: "device web-1.example.ts.net (" + id + ")"},
		{Op: "-", Text: "authorized: false"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "authorized: true"},
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(pv.Diff, wantDiff) {
		t.Errorf("plan diff %+v, want %+v", pv.Diff, wantDiff)
	}
	if d, ok := f.srv.Device(id); !ok || !d.Authorized {
		t.Errorf("the fake's device %+v (%v), want it authorized", d, ok)
	}
	var out Device
	if err := json.Unmarshal(cv.Output, &out); err != nil || out.ID != id || !out.Authorized {
		t.Errorf("output %s (%v), want the authorized device", cv.Output, err)
	}
	want := fmt.Sprintf("modify tailnet.device:%s made  local=0 wait=%d", id, int64(cloud.CommitWait))
	if got := f.effects(cv.ID); !slices.Equal(got, []string{want}) {
		t.Errorf("effects %q, want %q", got, want)
	}

	if v := f.undo(cv.ID); v.State != core.StateReverted {
		t.Fatalf("undo left the change %s (%+v), want reverted", v.State, v.Error)
	}
	if d, _ := f.srv.Device(id); d.Authorized {
		t.Error("the device is still authorized after the undo")
	}
	if got := f.effects(cv.ID); len(got) != 1 || !strings.Contains(got[0], " undone ") {
		t.Errorf("effects %q after the undo, want the one effect undone", got)
	}
}

func TestDvAuthorizeConvergesWhenAlreadyAuthorized(t *testing.T) {
	f := dvNew(t, true)
	id := f.srv.AddDevice(fake.Device{Name: "web-1.example.ts.net", Hostname: "web-1", Authorized: true})

	pv, cv, err := f.do("tailnet.device.authorize", `{"device":"`+id+`"}`)
	if err != nil || cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("authorize = %v, %v (%+v)", cv.State, err, cv.Error)
	}
	if len(pv.Diff) != 0 || len(f.effects(cv.ID)) != 0 || f.posts("/authorized") != 0 {
		t.Errorf("diff %+v, effects %q, authorize calls %d; want an empty plan that writes nothing", pv.Diff, f.effects(cv.ID), f.posts("/authorized"))
	}
	if v := f.undo(cv.ID); v.State != core.StateReverted {
		t.Errorf("undo of an empty change left it %s, want reverted", v.State)
	}
	if d, _ := f.srv.Device(id); !d.Authorized {
		t.Error("undoing a change that authorized nothing de-authorized the device")
	}
}

func TestDvAuthorizeRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	f := dvNew(t, true)
	tests := []struct {
		name, input string
		code        errcode.Code
		field       string
	}{
		{"unknown device", `{"device":"nope"}`, errcode.NotFound, ""},
		{"empty device", `{"device":""}`, errcode.InvalidInput, "/device"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		_, err := f.plan("tailnet.device.authorize", tt.input)
		e := errcode.From(err)
		if e.Code != tt.code {
			t.Errorf("%s: plan = %v, want %s", tt.name, err, tt.code)
		}
		if tt.field != "" && !slices.ContainsFunc(e.Fields, func(fe errcode.FieldError) bool { return fe.Path == tt.field }) {
			t.Errorf("%s: fields %+v, want one naming %s", tt.name, e.Fields, tt.field)
		}
	}
}

func TestDvAuthorizeWriteFailures(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name       string
		status     int
		state      string
		effect     string
		changeCode string
	}{
		{"refused by the provider", http.StatusForbidden, core.StateFailed, " skipped ", string(errcode.CloudPermissionMissing)},
		{"outcome unknown", http.StatusInternalServerError, core.StateNeedsRepair, " unresolved uncertain ", string(errcode.NeedsRepair)},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := dvNew(t, true)
			id := f.srv.AddDevice(fake.Device{Name: "web-1.example.ts.net", Hostname: "web-1"})
			f.srv.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodPost, "/api/v2/device/"+id+"/authorized", cloudfake.Fault{Status: tt.status})

			_, cv, err := f.do("tailnet.device.authorize", `{"device":"`+id+`"}`)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if cv.State != tt.state || cv.Error == nil || cv.Error.Code != tt.changeCode {
				t.Errorf("change %s with error %+v, want %s with code %s", cv.State, cv.Error, tt.state, tt.changeCode)
			}
			if got := f.effects(cv.ID); len(got) != 1 || !strings.Contains(got[0], tt.effect) {
				t.Errorf("effects %q, want one containing %q", got, tt.effect)
			}
			if d, _ := f.srv.Device(id); d.Authorized {
				t.Error("the device was authorized although the call failed")
			}
		})
	}
}

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

All actions are controller-side (`Side: core.SideController`), version 1. Every read of the provider goes through `t.connected(ctx, env.DB, env.Sealer, env.Clock)`; its error (`cloud.not_connected`) is returned as is by a read or plan, and wrapped in `core.Definite` by an `Inverse`, because nothing was sent. Every device state is read with `a.Device(ctx, id)` (its 404 is `not_found`), never with `a.Routes`. Doc comments on exported identifiers; error strings that are not `*errcode.Error` start `tailnet:`.

`devices.go`:

1. `deviceView(d Device) Device` returns a copy with `Addresses`, `Tags`, `AdvertisedRoutes` and `EnabledRoutes` never nil, both route lists sorted ascending and de-duplicated, `ExitNode` true when the advertised routes contain `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`, and `ExitNodeEnabled` true when the enabled routes contain both. Every device this module returns passes through it.
2. `deviceList()`: `core.DefineRead` of `tailnet.device.list`, no lock keys; the handler returns `DeviceList` of `deviceView` over `a.Devices(ctx)`, sorted by `Name` then `ID`, with a non-nil `Devices` slice.

`devices_authorize.go`: `deviceAuthorize()` is `core.DefineMutating` of `tailnet.device.authorize`, `Class: core.ClassCompensable`, `LockKeys: []string{"tailnet"}`, with a handler implementing `Plan`, `Apply`, `Verify`, `Observe` and `Inverse` (the undo; no `CompensatedBy`, no `ForwardOnly`).

- `Plan`: an empty `device` is `core.Definite` `request.invalid_input` with a `FieldError` at `/device`. Read the device. When it is already authorized the diff is the empty, non-nil slice. Otherwise the diff is the context line `device <name> (<id>)` (Op `" "`), then `-` `authorized: false` and `+` `authorized: true`. `StateHash` is `<id> authorized=<true|false>` of the device as read.
- `Apply`: read the device again; when it is already authorized return `deviceView(d)` without an effect. Otherwise journal one effect before the call, built with `cloudEffect(core.EffectModify, "tailnet.device:<id>", {"authorized":false})` and `After` `{"authorized":true}`, call `a.Authorize(ctx, id, true)`, and on an error that satisfies `core.IsDefinite` call `env.Effects.Skipped` before returning it; any other error is returned with the effect left intended (the engine then settles it unresolved, `uncertain`). On success call `env.Effects.Made` with the same resource and the after state, and return `deviceView` of the device read with `Authorized` true.
- `Verify`: read the device; it must be authorized, else an error naming the id.
- `Observe`: the identity after the colon of `e.Resource` is the node id; a device that is `not_found` observes JSON `null`; otherwise `{"authorized":<bool>}`; `Matches` 1, `Exclusive` true, `Resource` the effect's resource.
- `Inverse`: decode `e.UndoTo.State` and call `a.Authorize(ctx, id, <its authorized value>)`; a nil `UndoTo` is an error.

`devices_routes.go`: `deviceSetRoutes()` is `core.DefineMutating` of `tailnet.device.set-routes`, compensable, lock key `tailnet`, same handler shape.

- `parseRoutes(in []string) ([]string, error)`: each element through `netip.ParsePrefix`, rendered with `String()`, sorted ascending and de-duplicated, never nil; a parse failure is an error naming the element.
- `Plan`: empty `device` as above; `routes` through `parseRoutes` (failure: `core.Definite` `request.invalid_input` at `/routes`); read the device; every wanted route must be in the device's advertised routes, else `request.invalid_input` at `/routes` naming the route. The diff is empty when the wanted list equals the enabled list; otherwise the context line `device <name> (<id>)`, then one `-` line `route <prefix>` per enabled route not wanted, then one `+` line `route <prefix>` per wanted route not enabled, each group sorted. `StateHash` is `<id> enabled=<enabled routes joined by ,>`.
- `Apply`: read the device; when its enabled routes already equal the wanted list return `DeviceRoutes` without an effect. Otherwise journal `cloudEffect(core.EffectModify, "tailnet.routes:<id>", {"enabledRoutes":<current>})` with `After` `{"enabledRoutes":<wanted>}`, call `a.SetRoutes(ctx, id, wanted)` with the same Skipped-or-leave-intended rule as authorize, record `Made` with the after state, and return the provider's `DeviceRoutes` with both lists sorted and non-nil.
- `Verify`: the device's enabled routes equal `parseRoutes(in.Routes)`.
- `Observe`: `not_found` observes `null`, otherwise `{"enabledRoutes":<sorted enabled routes>}`.
- `Inverse`: decode `e.UndoTo.State` and call `a.SetRoutes(ctx, id, <its enabledRoutes>)`.

	dxExpiry = "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"

// dxRig is a connected account, a fake tailnet holding one device, and the module under test.

	srv *fake.Server
	t   tn
}

func dxNew(t *testing.T) dxRig {
	t.Helper()
	h := newTNHost(t)
	srv := fake.New(t)
	acConnect(t, h, srv)
	srv.AddDevice(fake.Device{
		ID: dxID, Name: dxName, Hostname: "laptop", Addresses: []string{"100.64.0.7"}, Authorized: true, Expires: dxExpiry,

func dxInput(device string) json.RawMessage {
	return json.RawMessage(fmt.Sprintf(`{"device":%q}`, device))
}

func (r dxRig) plan(def core.ActionDef, device string) (core.PlanOutcome, error) {
	return def.Handler.Plan(context.Background(), r.h.env(""), dxInput(device))
}

func (r dxRig) apply(def core.ActionDef, changeID, device string) (DeviceRef, error) {
	raw, err := def.Handler.Apply(context.Background(), r.h.env(changeID), dxInput(device))
	var ref DeviceRef
	if err == nil {
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &ref); err != nil {
			return DeviceRef{}, err
		}
	}
	return ref, err
}

	t.Helper()
	var g, w any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(got, &g); err != nil {

	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(want), &w); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(g, w) {
		t.Errorf("%s = %s, want %s", what, got, want)
	}

			if tc.kind == core.EffectDelete {
				def = r.t.deviceDelete()
			}
			obs, err := def.Handler.Observe(context.Background(), r.h.env("chg-o"),
				core.Effect{ChangeID: "chg-o", Kind: tc.kind, Resource: "tailnet.device:" + tc.id})
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			dxSameJSON(t, "state", obs.Current.State, tc.want)
		})
	}
	_, err := r.t.deviceExpire().Handler.Observe(context.Background(), newTNHost(t).env("chg-o"),
		core.Effect{ChangeID: "chg-o", Kind: core.EffectModify, Resource: "tailnet.device:" + dxID})
	if dxCode(err) != errcode.CloudNotConnected {
		t.Errorf("without an account: error %v, want cloud.not_connected", err)
	}
}

func TestDxVerify(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		remove bool
	}{{"expire", false}, {"delete", true}} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			r := dxNew(t)
			def := r.t.deviceExpire()
			if tc.remove {
				def = r.t.deviceDelete()
			}
			ctx := context.Background()
			if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, r.h.env("chg-v"), dxInput(dxID), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err == nil {
				t.Error("verify passed with no recorded call")
			}
			if _, err := r.apply(def, "chg-v", dxID); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, r.h.env("chg-v"), dxInput(dxID), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err != nil {
				t.Errorf("verify after the call: %v", err)
			}
		})
		t.Run(tc.name+" unchanged", func(t *testing.T) {
			r := dxNew(t)
			def, kind := r.t.deviceExpire(), core.EffectModify
			before := fmt.Sprintf(`{"expires":%q}`, dxExpiry)
			if tc.remove {
				def, kind = r.t.deviceDelete(), core.EffectDelete
				before = fmt.Sprintf(`{"id":%q,"name":%q}`, dxID, dxName)
			}
			ctx, env := context.Background(), r.h.env("chg-v")
			seq, err := env.Effects.Intend(ctx, cloudEffect(kind, "tailnet.device:"+dxID, json.RawMessage(before)), nil)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if err := env.Effects.Made(ctx, seq, "tailnet.device:"+dxID, core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(`null`)}); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, env, dxInput(dxID), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err == nil {
				t.Error("verify passed although the provider still reports the recorded before-state")
			}
		})
	}
}

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `device_expire_delete.go` (package `tailnet`, a doc comment on every identifier, errors starting `tailnet:`):

1. `type deviceEnd struct{ t tn; remove bool }` is the handler of both actions. It implements `core.Mutator[DeviceInput, DeviceRef]` (`Plan`, `Apply`, `Verify`) and `core.Observer` (`Observe`), and has no `Inverse` method: the registry refuses an undo handler on an irreversible action. `func (t tn) deviceExpire() core.ActionDef` and `func (t tn) deviceDelete() core.ActionDef` call `core.DefineMutating[DeviceInput, DeviceRef]` with `ActionSpec{Name: "tailnet.device.expire"` or `"tailnet.device.delete", Version: 1, Summary, Class: core.ClassIrreversible, Side: core.SideController, LockKeys: []string{ID}}` (`ID` is the module id `tailnet`, the lock key of Global Constraints), and `deviceEnd{t: t}` or `deviceEnd{t: t, remove: true}`.
2. A shared method reads the target for Plan and Apply. An empty `Device` is `core.Definite` of an `*errcode.Error` with code `request.invalid_input` and the field error path `/device`. Otherwise it calls `t.connected(ctx, env.DB, env.Sealer, env.Clock)` (its `cloud.not_connected` is returned as is) and `api.Device(ctx, in.Device)` (its `not_found` is returned as is). `DeviceInput.Device` is the provider's device id, as the device list shows it; a name is not resolved.
3. `Plan` returns `Confirmation` = the device's `Name`, and `StateHash` = the hex SHA-256 of the JSON array `[ID, Name, Expires, Authorized, KeyExpiryDisabled]` (not `LastSeen`, which changes on every read). The diff of expire is two lines: `-` "node key of <name> (<id>) expires <Expires>" (`never` when `Expires` is empty or `KeyExpiryDisabled`) and `+` "node key of <name> (<id>) expires now; the device must authenticate again to rejoin <tailnet>". The diff of delete is one `-` line: "device <name> (<id>) with addresses <comma-separated addresses> leaves tailnet <tailnet>". `<tailnet>` is the account's tailnet name. Every line names both the device name and its id.
4. `Apply` reads the target as in 2, then journals one effect through `cloudEffect(kind, "tailnet.device:"+id, before)` with `endResourcePrefix = "tailnet.device:"`. Expire: kind `core.EffectModify`, `before` = `endState` = `{"expires": <the device's Expires>}`, `After` left nil because the provider chooses the new value. Delete: kind `core.EffectDelete`, `before` = `{"id": <id>, "name": <name>}`, `After` = `{"state": null}`. `Intend` comes before the provider call. Then it calls `api.Expire` or `api.DeleteDevice` and settles the effect:
   - A refusal is `endRefused(err)`: `core.IsDefinite(err)` or `cloud.Status(err)` between 400 and 499. The effect is `Skipped` and the error returned wrapped in `core.Definite`. The cloud client marks only non-GET, non-DELETE 4xx answers Definite, so the DELETE case needs the status check.
   - Delete only: `cloud.Status(err) == 404` counts as success. The cloud client resends a DELETE whose response was lost, and the resend finds the device gone.
   - Any other error is returned as it is and the effect stays `intended`, so the engine settles it as unresolved (`cloud.uncertain_outcome` for a lost POST).
   - On success: delete records `Made(ctx, seq, resource, {state: null})`; expire re-reads the device with `api.Device` and records `Made` with `endState` of the re-read device (a failed re-read is returned and leaves the effect intended). The output is `DeviceRef{ID, Name}` of the device read before the call.
5. `Observe(ctx, env, e)` connects (an error is returned), reads `api.Device(ctx, strings.TrimPrefix(e.Resource, endResourcePrefix))`, and answers a `core.Observation` with `Matches` 1, `Exclusive` true, `Resource` `e.Resource` and `Current.State` null when the error is `not_found`; any other error is returned. A present device renders as the delete form `{"id","name"}` when `e.Kind == core.EffectDelete` and as the expire form `{"expires"}` otherwise. These forms are exactly the `Before` forms of step 4, so the engine's reconcile finds "not made" when the provider still shows the before-state.
6. `Verify(ctx, env, in, _)` lists `env.Effects`, takes the made effect whose resource is `endResourcePrefix+in.Device`, observes it, and fails when there is none or when the observed state equals the effect's `Before.State` (compared with `endSameJSON`, a JSON-value comparison ignoring key order). It reads only the provider and the journal, so startup recovery can call it.
7. No diff line, effect, state document or error carries a token or secret; the account's secret stays inside `connected`.

func tuSameJSON(t *testing.T, what string, got json.RawMessage, want string) {
	t.Helper()
	var g, w any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(got, &g); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %q is not JSON: %v", what, got, err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(want), &w); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(g, w) {
		t.Errorf("%s = %s, want %s", what, got, want)
	}

func tuCode(err error) errcode.Code {

		return ""
	}
	return errcode.From(err).Code
}

func tuDoc(id, name string) string { return fmt.Sprintf(`{"id":%q,"name":%q}`, id, name) }

// tuUndo runs the engine's undo protocol on one made effect: the observation must equal the recorded post-state
// before the inverse and the undo target after it.
func tuUndo(t *testing.T, r tuRig, def core.ActionDef, e core.Effect) error {
	t.Helper()
	ctx, env := context.Background(), r.h.env("chg-undo")
	obs, err := def.Handler.Observe(ctx, env, e)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	tuSameJSON(t, "state before the inverse", obs.Current.State, string(e.Post.State))
	e.State = core.EffectUndoing
	if _, err := def.Handler.Inverse(ctx, env, e); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	obs, err = def.Handler.Observe(ctx, env, e)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	tuSameJSON(t, "state after the inverse", obs.Current.State, "null")
	return nil
}

	}

	}

	r.srv.SetConnections(ref.ID, 1)
	if err := inverse(effs[0]); tuCode(err) != errcode.CloudConflict || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Errorf("tunnel undo with a connector: error %v, want a definite cloud.conflict", err)
	}
	if len(r.srv.Tunnels()) != 1 {
		t.Error("a refused undo deleted the tunnel")
	}
	r.srv.SetConnections(ref.ID, 0)
	if err := inverse(effs[0]); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("tunnel undo: %v", err)
	}
	if len(r.srv.Tunnels()) != 0 {
		t.Error("the tunnel survived its undo")
	}
}

func TestTuDeleteRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	r := tuNew(t)
	row := tuTunnel(t, r.h, r.srv)
	def := r.c.tunnelDelete()
	plan := func(env core.Env, tunnel string) error {
		_, err := def.Handler.Plan(context.Background(), env, tuInput(tunnel))
		return err
	}
	if err := plan(r.h.env(""), ""); tuCode(err) != errcode.InvalidInput {
		t.Errorf("empty tunnel: error %v, want request.invalid_input", err)
	}
	if err := plan(r.h.env(""), "darkpanel-other"); tuCode(err) != errcode.NotFound || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Errorf("unmanaged tunnel: error %v, want a definite not_found", err)
	}
	if err := plan(newCFHost(t).env(""), row.ID); tuCode(err) != errcode.CloudNotConnected {
		t.Errorf("no account: error %v, want cloud.not_connected", err)
	}
	tuAddHostname(t, r.h, row.ID, "app.example.com")
	if err := plan(r.h.env(""), row.ID); tuCode(err) != errcode.CloudConflict || !core.IsDefinite(err) ||
		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "1 hostnames") {
		t.Errorf("tunnel with a hostname: error %v, want a definite cloud.conflict naming the count", err)
	}
	tuRemoveHostname(t, r.h, "app.example.com")
	r.srv.SetConnections(row.ID, 2)
	if err := plan(r.h.env(""), row.ID); tuCode(err) != errcode.CloudConflict || !core.IsDefinite(err) ||
		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "2 connectors") {
		t.Errorf("tunnel with connectors: error %v, want a definite cloud.conflict naming the count", err)
	}
	if _, err := r.apply(def, "chg-del", tuInput(row.ID)); tuCode(err) != errcode.CloudConflict {
		t.Errorf("apply with connectors: error %v, want cloud.conflict", err)
	}
	if len(r.srv.Tunnels()) != 1 || len(r.h.journal.effects()) != 0 {
		t.Error("a refused delete changed the provider or journaled an effect")
	}
}

func TestTuDelete(t *testing.T) {
	r := tuNew(t)
	row := tuTunnel(t, r.h, r.srv)
	def := r.c.tunnelDelete()
	ref, err := r.apply(def, "chg-del", tuInput(row.Name))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if ref != (TunnelRef{ID: row.ID, Name: row.Name}) {
		t.Errorf("output %+v", ref)
	}
	if n := len(r.srv.Tunnels()); n != 0 {
		t.Errorf("%d provider tunnels, want none", n)
	}
	if _, found, _ := loadTunnel(context.Background(), r.h.db.Read(), row.ID); found {
		t.Error("the row survived")
	}
	effs := r.h.journal.effects()
	if len(effs) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("%d effects, want 2", len(effs))
	}
	remote, local := effs[0], effs[1]
	if remote.Kind != core.EffectDelete || remote.Resource != "cloudflare.tunnel:"+row.ID || remote.State != core.EffectMade ||
		remote.Local || remote.CommitWait != cloud.CommitWait {
		t.Errorf("provider effect %+v", remote)
	}
	if local.Kind != core.EffectDelete || local.Resource != "cloudflare.tunnelrow:"+row.ID || local.State != core.EffectMade || !local.Local {
		t.Errorf("row effect %+v", local)
	}
	for _, e := range effs {
		tuSameJSON(t, e.Resource+" before", e.Before.State, tuDoc(row.ID, row.Name))
		if e.After == nil || e.Post == nil {
			t.Fatalf("effect %s: after %v, post %v", e.Resource, e.After, e.Post)
		}
		tuSameJSON(t, e.Resource+" after", e.After.State, "null")
		tuSameJSON(t, e.Resource+" post", e.Post.State, "null")
	}
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(context.Background(), r.h.env("chg-del"), tuInput(row.Name), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("verify: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestTuDeleteRefusedAndLost(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("refused", func(t *testing.T) {
		r := tuNew(t)
		row := tuTunnel(t, r.h, r.srv)
		r.srv.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodDelete, tuCollection(t, r)+"/"+row.ID, cloudfake.Fault{Status: http.StatusForbidden})
		_, err := r.apply(r.c.tunnelDelete(), "chg-del", tuInput(row.ID))
		if tuCode(err) != errcode.CloudPermissionMissing || !core.IsDefinite(err) {
			t.Fatalf("error %v, want a definite cloud.permission_missing", err)
		}
		if effs := r.h.journal.effects(); len(effs) != 1 || effs[0].State != core.EffectSkipped {
			t.Errorf("effects %+v, want one skipped effect", effs)
		}
		if _, found, _ := loadTunnel(context.Background(), r.h.db.Read(), row.ID); !found || len(r.srv.Tunnels()) != 1 {
			t.Error("a refused delete removed the row or the tunnel")
		}
	})
	t.Run("lost response converges", func(t *testing.T) {
		r := tuNew(t)
		row := tuTunnel(t, r.h, r.srv)
		r.srv.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodDelete, tuCollection(t, r)+"/"+row.ID, cloudfake.Fault{LoseResponse: true})
		if _, err := r.apply(r.c.tunnelDelete(), "chg-del", tuInput(row.ID)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("the retry that finds the tunnel gone must count as done: %v", err)
		}
		if _, found, _ := loadTunnel(context.Background(), r.h.db.Read(), row.ID); found {
			t.Error("the row survived")
		}
	})
}

func TestTuObserve(t *testing.T) {
	r := tuNew(t)
	row := tuTunnel(t, r.h, r.srv)
	remote := core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectDelete, Before: core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(tuDoc(row.ID, row.Name))}}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name     string
		resource string
		want     string
	}{
		{"tunnel present", "cloudflare.tunnel:" + row.ID, tuDoc(row.ID, row.Name)},
		{"tunnel absent", "cloudflare.tunnel:tun-gone", "null"},
		{"row present", "cloudflare.tunnelrow:" + row.ID, tuDoc(row.ID, row.Name)},
		{"row absent", "cloudflare.tunnelrow:tun-gone", "null"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			e := remote
			e.Resource = tc.resource
			if strings.HasSuffix(tc.resource, "tun-gone") {
				e.Before = core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(tuDoc("tun-gone", "darkpanel-gone"))}
			}
			obs, err := r.c.tunnelDelete().Handler.Observe(context.Background(), r.h.env("chg-o"), e)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			tuSameJSON(t, "state", obs.Current.State, tc.want)
		})
	}
	e := remote
	e.Resource = "cloudflare.tunnel:" + row.ID
	if _, err := r.c.tunnelDelete().Handler.Observe(context.Background(), newCFHost(t).env("chg-o"), e); tuCode(err) != errcode.CloudNotConnected {
		t.Errorf("without an account: error %v, want cloud.not_connected", err)
	}
}

func TestTuVerifyNeedsTheCallMade(t *testing.T) {
	r := tuNew(t)
	row := tuTunnel(t, r.h, r.srv)
	def := r.c.tunnelDelete()
	ctx, env := context.Background(), r.h.env("chg-v")
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, env, tuInput(row.ID), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err == nil {
		t.Error("verify passed with no recorded call")
	}
	e := core.Effect{
		Kind: core.EffectDelete, Resource: "cloudflare.tunnelrow:" + row.ID, Local: true,
		Before: core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(tuDoc(row.ID, row.Name))},
	}
	seq, err := env.Effects.Intend(ctx, e, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := env.Effects.Made(ctx, seq, e.Resource, core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(`null`)}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, env, tuInput(row.ID), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err == nil {
		t.Error("verify passed although the row still exists")
	}
}

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `tunnel_lifecycle.go` (package `cloudflare`, a doc comment on every identifier, errors starting `cloudflare:`):

1. Constants `tunnelNoun = "cloudflare.tunnel:"` and `tunnelRowNoun = "cloudflare.tunnelrow:"`. `tunnelDoc(id, name)` renders the state document `{"id": id, "name": name}`. `tunnelRefused(err)` is `core.IsDefinite(err)` or `cloud.Status(err)` between 400 and 499 (the cloud client marks only non-GET, non-DELETE 4xx answers Definite, and a DELETE is among the 4xx cases a refusal must catch). `tunnelStateHash(parts ...any)` is the hex SHA-256 of the JSON array of its parts. `tunnelSameJSON(a, b json.RawMessage) bool` compares two JSON values by content, ignoring key order. `tunnelDeleteAtProvider(ctx, a, id)` calls `api.DeleteTunnel` and answers nil on success or `cloud.Status == 404` (the cloud client resends a DELETE whose response was lost, and the resend finds the tunnel gone), `core.Definite(err)` when `tunnelRefused`, otherwise the error unchanged.
2. `type tunnelObserver struct{ c cf }` implements `core.Observer`; `tunnelCreator` and `tunnelDeleter` each embed it. `Observe(ctx, env, e)`:
   - A resource under `tunnelRowNoun` is read from the database alone, without connecting: the row id is the part after the prefix, or `e.Recovery.Value` when the resource is a creation (`...:?<id>`). The state is `tunnelDoc` of the row, or null when `loadTunnel` finds none; `Matches` 1 or 0, `Exclusive` true, `Resource` `tunnelRowNoun+id` when found.
   - A resource under `tunnelNoun` connects (an error is returned) and lists `api.Tunnels(ctx, name)` with `tunnelNameOf(e)` (`e.Recovery.Value` when set, else the `name` member of `e.Post.State` when `e.Post` is set, else of `e.Before.State`), keeping the entries whose `Name` equals that name and, for an id resource, whose `ID` equals the id. It lists rather than reads one tunnel because Cloudflare keeps answering a deleted tunnel by id. For a creation resource (`...:?<name>`) `Matches` is the number kept; for any other resource it is 1. One kept tunnel: `Current.State` is its `tunnelDoc`, `Resource` is `tunnelNoun+id`. None: `Current.State` null and `Resource` empty. Several (a creation only): `Current.State` null and `Candidates` holds each as `{Resource, State}`. `Exclusive` is true.
   - A shared method `busy(ctx, env, a, row, provider bool)` refuses a tunnel in use: `core.Definite` of `errcode.CloudConflict` "tunnel <name> still has <n> hostnames; remove them first" when `listHostnames` holds rows (any phase) for `row.ID`; when `provider` is true and `a.Connections(ctx, row.ID)` is not empty, `core.Definite` of `errcode.CloudConflict` "tunnel <name> still has <n> connectors; stop them first". A `Connections` error is returned as it is. A shared method `verify(ctx, env, want int)` lists `env.Effects`, observes every made effect, fails when an observed state differs from the effect's `Post.State` (`tunnelSameJSON`), and fails when fewer than `want` effects are made.
3. `tunnelCreate`: `core.DefineMutating[TunnelCreateInput, TunnelRef]` with `ActionSpec{Name: "cloudflare.tunnel.create", Version: 1, Summary, Class: core.ClassCompensable, Side: core.SideController, LockKeys: []string{ID}}` and `tunnelCreator{tunnelObserver{c}}`; the registry requires an `Inverse` method on it and no `CompensatedBy`.
   - `Plan` connects (its error is returned) and returns one `+` diff line "tunnel darkpanel-<change id>, remotely managed, in Cloudflare account <account id>" (the literal text `<change id>`: a plan has no change yet) and `StateHash` = `tunnelStateHash("tunnel.create", account id)`.
   - `Apply` fails with `cloudflare: tunnel.create needs a change id` when `env.ChangeID` is empty. Name = `"darkpanel-" + env.ChangeID`. Effect 1: `cloudEffect(core.EffectCreate, "cloudflare.tunnel:?"+name, null)` with `Recovery` `{Kind: "name", Value: name}`; `Intend` first, then `api.CreateTunnel(ctx, name)`. A `tunnelRefused` error: `Skipped`, return `core.Definite(err)`; any other error: return it unchanged and leave the effect intended. On success `Made(ctx, seq, "cloudflare.tunnel:"+id, {state: tunnelDoc(id, name)})`. Effect 2: a `core.Effect` with `Kind` create, `Resource` `cloudflare.tunnelrow:?<id>`, `Recovery` `{Kind: "name", Value: id}`, `Local` true, `InverseLocal` true, `Before` `{state: null}`, `After` `{state: tunnelDoc}`; `Intend`, then `env.DB.Write` with `insertTunnel` (`ChangeID` = `env.ChangeID`, `CreatedAt` = `env.Clock.Now()`), then `Made(ctx, seq, "cloudflare.tunnelrow:"+id, after)`. Journal calls and the database write are separate calls, never nested: the database has one writer connection. The output is `TunnelRef{ID, Name}`.
   - `Verify` is `verify(ctx, env, 2)`.
   - `Inverse(ctx, env, e)` dispatches on the resource. Row effect: `loadTunnel`; a missing row is a no-op; otherwise `busy(..., provider=false)` (a hostname refuses, `core.Definite`), then `env.DB.Write` with `deleteTunnel`. Tunnel effect: `connected` (an error is wrapped in `core.Definite`: nothing was sent), then `busy(..., provider=true)` (a refusal is `core.Definite`), then `tunnelDeleteAtProvider`. It returns `core.InverseResult{}`. The engine undoes the row (newest effect) before the tunnel.
4. `tunnelDelete`: `core.DefineMutating[TunnelInput, TunnelRef]` with `Name: "cloudflare.tunnel.delete"`, `Class: core.ClassIrreversible`, `Side: core.SideController`, `LockKeys: []string{ID}`, and `tunnelDeleter{tunnelObserver{c}}` (no `Inverse` method). A shared method `inspect(ctx, env, in)` returns a `tunnelDeletion{a, acct, row, present}`: an empty `Tunnel` is `core.Definite` of `request.invalid_input` with the field path `/tunnel`; then `connected`; then `loadTunnel(ctx, env.DB.Read(), in.Tunnel)` (id or name), none is `core.Definite` of `not_found` "no managed tunnel <input>"; then `present` = the tunnel appears in `api.Tunnels(ctx, row.Name)`; then `busy(..., provider = present)`, whose refusal is returned.
   - `Plan` returns `Confirmation` = `row.Name`, `StateHash` = `tunnelStateHash("tunnel.delete", id, name, present)` and one `-` line naming both name and id: "tunnel <name> (<id>) deleted from Cloudflare account <account id> and from Darkpanel", or, when not present, "tunnel <name> (<id>) is already gone from Cloudflare; only Darkpanel's record is removed".
   - `Apply` runs `inspect` again. When `present`: effect `cloudEffect(core.EffectDelete, "cloudflare.tunnel:"+id, tunnelDoc(id, name))` with `After` `{state: null}`; `Intend`, `tunnelDeleteAtProvider`, a Definite error means `Skipped` and the error is returned, any other error leaves the effect intended, success is `Made` with post `{state: null}`. Then, always, the row effect: kind delete, resource `cloudflare.tunnelrow:<id>`, `Local` true, `InverseLocal` true, `Before` `tunnelDoc`, `After` null; `Intend`, `env.DB.Write` with `deleteTunnel`, `Made` with post null. The provider call comes first: if the process stops between the two, a second delete finds the tunnel absent and removes only the row. The output is `TunnelRef{ID, Name}`.
   - `Verify` is `verify(ctx, env, 1)`.
5. No diff line, effect, state document or error carries a token. The tunnel's connector token is never read here.

	c   cf
}

// trTunnel creates a tunnel in the fake and records its row, as tunnel.create leaves them.
func trTunnel(t *testing.T, h *cfHost, srv *fake.Server, name string) tunnelRow {

	row := tunnelRow{ID: srv.AddTunnel(name), Name: name, ChangeID: "tr-seed", CreatedAt: h.clock.Now()}

	return row
}

func trInsertRow(t *testing.T, h *cfHost, row tunnelRow) {

	err := h.db.Write(context.Background(), func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertTunnel(context.Background(), tx, row) })
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func trWrite(t *testing.T, h *cfHost, fn func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	if err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return fn(ctx, tx) }); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func trInput(tunnel string) json.RawMessage {
	return json.RawMessage(fmt.Sprintf(`{"tunnel":%q}`, tunnel))
}

func trCode(err error) errcode.Code {
	if err == nil {
		return ""
	}
	return errcode.From(err).Code
}

func trSameJSON(t *testing.T, what string, got json.RawMessage, want string) {
	t.Helper()
	var g, w any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(got, &g); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %q is not JSON: %v", what, got, err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(want), &w); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(g, w) {
		t.Errorf("%s = %s, want %s", what, got, want)
	}
}

		t.Errorf("tunnel b: %+v", vb)

	if vc.ID != gone.ID || vc.Status != "unknown" || len(vc.Connections) != 0 || vc.Hostnames != 0 {

	if !va.CreatedAt.Equal(a.CreatedAt) {

	if err != nil || strings.Count(string(enc), `"connections":[]`) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("encoded list %s (err %v), want an empty array for each tunnel without connections", enc, err)
	}
}

		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("plan %q: %v", ref, err)
		}
		return out
	}

	out := plan(row.Name)
	if len(out.Diff) != 1 || out.Diff[0].Op != "+" || !strings.Contains(out.Diff[0].Text, want) || out.StateHash == "" {
		t.Errorf("first adoption: %+v, want one + line holding %s", out, want)
	}
	if got := trRow(t, r, row.ID); got.ConfigHash != "" {
		t.Errorf("planning stored hash %q", got.ConfigHash)
	}

	out = plan(row.ID)
	if len(out.Diff) != 2 || out.Diff[0].Op != "-" || !strings.Contains(out.Diff[0].Text, "stale-hash") ||
		out.Diff[1].Op != "+" || !strings.Contains(out.Diff[1].Text, want) {

	trWrite(t, r.h, func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) error { return setTunnelHash(ctx, tx, row.ID, want) })
	out = plan(row.ID)
	if len(out.Diff) != 1 || out.Diff[0].Op != " " || !strings.Contains(out.Diff[0].Text, "already matches") {
		t.Errorf("matching hash: %+v, want one context line saying it already matches", out.Diff)
	}
	if out.StateHash == changed {
		t.Error("the state hash must change with the stored hash")
	}

	r.srv.SetConfiguration(row.ID, json.RawMessage(`{"ingress":[{"service":"http_status:404"}]}`))

		t.Error("the state hash must change with the tunnel's configuration")
	}

		Before: core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(trAdoptDoc("", false))},

	seq, err := env.Effects.Intend(ctx, e, nil)

		t.Fatal(err)

	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, env, trInput(row.ID), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err == nil {

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `tunnel_read.go` (package `cloudflare`, a doc comment on every identifier, errors starting `cloudflare:`):

1. `type tunnelReader struct{ c cf }` implements `core.Reader[TunnelListInput, TunnelList]`. `func (c cf) tunnelList() core.ActionDef` calls `core.DefineRead` with `ActionSpec{Name: "cloudflare.tunnel.list", Version: 1, Summary, Side: core.SideController}` (no lock key: read actions take none). `Read` builds the list from the stored rows, so a tunnel Cloudflare no longer has still appears:
   - `listTunnels` and `listHostnames` supply the rows; `Hostnames` counts the hostname rows (any phase) whose `TunnelID` is the tunnel's id; `Drift` and `CreatedAt` come from the row. The result is never a nil slice (an empty database answers `{"tunnels":[]}`) and each view's `Connections` is never nil (it encodes as `[]`). Views are sorted by name.
   - Provider status: `connected` is called once. A `cloud.not_connected` error leaves every view with `Status` `"unknown"` and no connections; any other error from `connected` is returned. With an api, each tunnel's `Status` is `api.Tunnel(ctx, id).Status` and its connections are `api.Connections(ctx, id)` mapped to `ConnectionView{ID, Colo: ColoName, OriginIP, OpenedAt, Version: ClientVersion}`. Each read fails on its own: a failed `Tunnel` read leaves `Status` `"unknown"`, a failed `Connections` read leaves the connections empty, and neither fails the list.
2. `func (c cf) tunnelToken() core.ActionDef` calls `core.DefineInternalRead[TunnelInput, TunnelToken]` with `ActionSpec{Name: "cloudflare.tunnel.token", Version: 1, Summary, Side: core.SideController}` and the method `func (c cf) readTunnelToken(ctx, env, in TunnelInput) (core.Revealed[TunnelToken], error)`. An empty `Tunnel` is `core.Definite` of `request.invalid_input` with the field path `/tunnel`; `loadTunnel(ctx, env.DB.Read(), in.Tunnel)` (id or name) finding none is `core.Definite` of `not_found` "no managed tunnel <input>"; then `connected` and `api.TunnelToken(ctx, row.ID)`. The result is `Revealed{Identity: "Cloudflare tunnel token of <tunnel name>", Value: TunnelToken{Token}}`. The identity names the tunnel and never contains the token; the token is not logged or put in an error.

In `tunnel_adopt.go`:

3. `const adoptNoun = "cloudflare.tunnelhash:"`. `adoptDoc(hash string, drift bool) json.RawMessage` renders the state document `{"hash": hash, "drift": drift}`; every comparison in this file is of documents it rendered itself. `type tunnelAdopter struct{ c cf }` implements `core.Mutator[TunnelInput, TunnelRef]`, `core.Observer` and `core.Undoer`. `func (c cf) tunnelAdopt() core.ActionDef` calls `core.DefineMutating[TunnelInput, TunnelRef]` with `ActionSpec{Name: "cloudflare.tunnel.adopt", Version: 1, Summary, Class: core.ClassCompensable, Side: core.SideController, LockKeys: []string{ID}}`; the `Inverse` method is its one compensation mechanism.
4. A shared method reads the tunnel and the provider's configuration for Plan and Apply: an empty `Tunnel` is `core.Definite` of `request.invalid_input` with the field path `/tunnel`; `loadTunnel` finding none is `core.Definite` of `not_found` "no managed tunnel <input>"; then `connected` (its `cloud.not_connected` returned as is) and `api.Configuration(ctx, row.ID)`; the new hash is `ingress.Hash` of the configuration.
5. `Plan` returns `StateHash` = `<new hash>:<stored hash>` and the diff: stored hash differs and is not empty: a `-` line and a `+` line, "tunnel <name>: stored configuration hash <hash>" with the old and the new hash; stored hash empty: the `+` line only; stored hash equal: one context line (`Op` `" "`) "tunnel <name>: stored configuration hash <hash> already matches Cloudflare". Plan writes nothing.
6. `Apply` repeats the read of step 4, then journals one effect: `Kind` modify, `Resource` `cloudflare.tunnelhash:<id>`, `Local` true, `InverseLocal` true, `Before` `{state: adoptDoc(stored hash, stored drift)}`, `After` `{state: adoptDoc(new hash, false)}`. `Intend` first; then one `env.DB.Write` that calls `setTunnelHash` with the new hash and `setTunnelCheck(ctx, tx, id, false, env.Clock.Now())` (the stored configuration now matches, so the drift mark clears); then `Made` with the `After` document as post-state. A database error is returned and leaves the effect intended (a Local effect, so the engine settles it by observation). The output is `TunnelRef{ID, Name}`. Cloudflare is only read.
7. `Observe(ctx, env, e)` loads the row named by the resource's id: the state is `adoptDoc(row.ConfigHash, row.Drift)`, or null when the row is gone; `Matches` 1, `Exclusive` true, `Resource` `e.Resource`. `Inverse(ctx, env, e)` decodes `e.Before.State`, answers `core.Definite` of `not_found` "no managed tunnel <id>" when the row is gone (without writing), and otherwise restores the previous hash and drift in one `env.DB.Write` with `setTunnelHash` and `setTunnelCheck(ctx, tx, id, previous drift, env.Clock.Now())`; it returns `core.InverseResult{}`. `Verify(ctx, env, in, _)` lists `env.Effects`, takes the first made effect, observes it and fails when the observed state differs from the effect's `Post.State`, or when no effect is made.

func akSame(t *testing.T, got, want json.RawMessage) {
	t.Helper()
	var g, w any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(got, &g); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decode %s: %v", got, err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(want, &w); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decode %s: %v", want, err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(g, w) {
		t.Errorf("got %s, want %s", got, want)
	}
}

// akUncertain applies a create whose answer is lost: committed says whether the
// provider kept the key.
func akUncertain(t *testing.T, committed bool) (akEnv, core.Effect) {
	t.Helper()
	e := akSetup(t)
	fault := cloudfake.Fault{Status: http.StatusInternalServerError}
	if committed {
		fault = cloudfake.Fault{LoseResponse: true}
	}
	e.srv.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodPost, akKeysPath, fault)
	_, err := akApply(t, e, akChange, AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:ci"}})
	if got := akCode(t, err); got != errcode.CloudUncertainOutcome || core.IsDefinite(err) {
		t.Fatalf("apply error %v (definite %v), want an uncertain outcome", err, core.IsDefinite(err))
	}
	return e, akOnly(t, e)
}

func TestAkPlan(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name      string
		in        AuthKeyInput
		noAccount bool
		code      errcode.Code
		field     string
		diff      string
	}{
		{name: "default expiry", in: AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:ci"}, Preauthorized: true}, diff: "24h0m0s"},
		{name: "given expiry", in: AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:ci", "tag:web"}, ExpirySeconds: 3600}, diff: "1h0m0s"},
		{name: "no tags", in: AuthKeyInput{}, code: errcode.InvalidInput, field: "/tags"},
		{name: "tag outside tagsAllowed", in: AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:db"}}, code: errcode.InvalidInput, field: "/tags"},
		{name: "malformed tag", in: AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"ci"}}, code: errcode.InvalidInput, field: "/tags"},
		{name: "expiry above 90 days", in: AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:ci"}, ExpirySeconds: 7776001}, code: errcode.InvalidInput, field: "/expirySeconds"},
		{name: "negative expiry", in: AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:ci"}, ExpirySeconds: -1}, code: errcode.InvalidInput, field: "/expirySeconds"},
		{name: "no account", in: AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:ci"}}, noAccount: true, code: errcode.CloudNotConnected},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			e := akSetup(t)
			if tc.noAccount {
				e = akEnv{h: newTNHost(t), srv: e.srv, t: e.t}
			}
			out, err := e.t.authkeyCreate().Handler.Plan(context.Background(), e.h.env(""), akJSON(t, tc.in))
			if tc.code != "" {
				if got := akCode(t, err); got != tc.code {
					t.Fatalf("code %s, want %s (%v)", got, tc.code, err)
				}
				fields := errcode.From(err).Fields
				if tc.field != "" && !slices.ContainsFunc(fields, func(f errcode.FieldError) bool { return f.Path == tc.field }) {
					t.Errorf("fields %v lack %s", fields, tc.field)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if out.StateHash == "" {
				t.Error("empty state hash")
			}
			if !slices.ContainsFunc(out.Diff, func(l core.DiffLine) bool { return l.Op == "+" && strings.Contains(l.Text, tc.diff) }) {
				t.Errorf("no added line mentions %s: %v", tc.diff, out.Diff)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAkApplyCreatesAndJournals(t *testing.T) {
	e := akSetup(t)
	ck, err := akApply(t, e, akChange, AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:web", "tag:ci"}, Reusable: true})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := "darkpanel-" + akChange
	if ck.ID == "" || ck.Key == "" || ck.Description != want {
		t.Fatalf("created key %+v, want an id, a key and description %s", ck, want)
	}
	if n := len(e.srv.Keys()); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("provider holds %d keys, want 1", n)
	}

	row := akRow(t, e, want)
	if row.State != "live" || row.KeyID != ck.ID || row.Kind != "change" || row.OwnerID != akChange || row.ExpirySeconds != 86400 ||
		!reflect.DeepEqual(row.Tags, []string{"tag:ci", "tag:web"}) || !row.RequestedAt.Equal(e.h.clock.Now()) {
		t.Errorf("row %+v", row)
	}

	eff := akOnly(t, e)
	if eff.Kind != core.EffectCreate || eff.State != core.EffectMade || eff.Resource != "tailnet.key:"+ck.ID ||
		eff.Local || eff.CommitWait != cloud.CommitWait {
		t.Errorf("effect %+v", eff)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(eff.Recovery, &core.RecoveryID{Kind: "marker", Value: want}) {
		t.Errorf("recovery %+v", eff.Recovery)
	}
	akSame(t, eff.Before.State, json.RawMessage(`null`))
	if eff.Post == nil {
		t.Fatal("no post state")
	}
	akSame(t, eff.Post.State, akJSON(t, map[string]string{"id": ck.ID, "description": want}))
	if blob, _ := json.Marshal(eff); strings.Contains(string(blob), ck.Key) {
		t.Error("the journal holds the key secret")
	}

	var sent string
	for _, r := range e.srv.Cloud().Requests() {
		if r.Method == http.MethodPost && r.Path == akKeysPath {
			sent = string(r.Body)
		}
	}
	for _, part := range []string{want, "tag:ci", "tag:web", "86400"} {
		if !strings.Contains(sent, part) {
			t.Errorf("create request %q lacks %s", sent, part)
		}
	}
}

	ctx := context.Background()
	desc := "darkpanel-" + akChange

	t.Run("made key", func(t *testing.T) {

		ck, err := akApply(t, e, akChange, AuthKeyInput{Tags: []string{"tag:ci"}})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		eff := akOnly(t, e)
		obs, err := e.t.authkeyCreate().Handler.Observe(ctx, e.h.env(akChange), eff)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if obs.Matches != 1 || obs.Resource != "tailnet.key:"+ck.ID {
			t.Errorf("observation %+v", obs)
		}
		akSame(t, obs.Current.State, eff.Post.State)
	})

	t.Run("committed but unanswered create", func(t *testing.T) {
		e, eff := akUncertain(t, true)
		a, _, err := e.t.connected(ctx, e.h.db, coretest.Sealer{}, e.h.clock)

		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)

func TestAkResolved(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name       string
		committed  bool
		resolution string
		want       string
		withID     bool
	}{
		{"accept an observed key", true, core.ResolutionAccept, "live", true},
		{"reconcile an observed key", true, core.ResolutionReconcile, "live", true},
		{"accept no key", false, core.ResolutionAccept, "retired", false},
		{"reconcile no key", false, core.ResolutionReconcile, "retired", false},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			ctx := context.Background()
			e, eff := akUncertain(t, tc.committed)
			def := e.t.authkeyCreate()
			obs, err := def.Handler.Observe(ctx, e.h.env(akChange), eff)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			e.h.clock.Advance(time.Hour)
			res := eff
			res.ResolvedAt = e.h.clock.Now()
			switch {
			case tc.resolution == core.ResolutionAccept:
				cur := obs.Current
				res.State, res.Current = core.EffectAccepted, &cur
			case obs.Matches == 0:
				res.State = core.EffectSkipped
			default:
				post := obs.Current
				res.State, res.Resource, res.Post = core.EffectMade, obs.Resource, &post
			}
			err = e.h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return def.Handler.Resolved(ctx, tx, res, tc.resolution) })
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			row := akRow(t, e, "darkpanel-"+akChange)
			if row.State != tc.want || !row.UpdatedAt.Equal(res.ResolvedAt) {
				t.Errorf("row %+v, want state %s updated at %v", row, tc.want, res.ResolvedAt)
			}
			if tc.withID != (row.KeyID != "" && row.KeyID == strings.TrimPrefix(obs.Resource, "tailnet.key:")) {
				t.Errorf("key id %q, observed resource %q", row.KeyID, obs.Resource)
			}
		})
	}
}

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `authkey.go`:

1. `func (t tn) authkeyCreate() core.ActionDef` returns `core.DefineMutating[AuthKeyInput, CreatedKey]` with `ActionSpec{Name: "tailnet.authkey.create", Version: 1, Class: core.ClassCompensable, Side: core.SideController, LockKeys: []string{ID}, Summary: <one sentence>}`; no `CompensatedBy`, `ForwardOnly` or `ApplyTimeout` (the undo handler is the one compensation mechanism, and the 30 s default applies). The handler is `type authkeyHandler struct{ t tn }`; its `Plan`, `Apply` and `Verify` are in this file, its `Observe`, `Inverse` and `Resolved` in `authkey_resolve.go`. `func (t tn) authkeyList() core.ActionDef` returns `core.DefineRead[AuthKeyListInput, AuthKeyList]` named `tailnet.authkey.list`, no lock key, handler `type authkeyLister struct{}`.
2. `normalizeAuthKey(in AuthKeyInput, allowed []string) (AuthKeyInput, error)` is the one input check, used by Plan and by Apply. Tags: at least one, each matching `^tag:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*$` and present in `allowed` (the account's `TagsAllowed`); the result is sorted and de-duplicated. `ExpirySeconds`: 0 becomes 86400; below 0 or above 7776000 is refused. A refusal is an `*errcode.Error` with code `errcode.InvalidInput` and a `FieldError` at `/tags` or `/expirySeconds` whose message names the offending value; Apply wraps it in `core.Definite`.
3. `Plan`: load the account with `t.connected(ctx, env.DB, env.Sealer, env.Clock)` (`cloud.not_connected` passes through; it makes no provider request), normalize, and return `core.PlanOutcome` whose `Diff` holds added (`+`) lines saying: an auth key with the tags, `reusable`, `ephemeral` and `preauthorized` values and the expiry as a `time.Duration` string (86400 s prints `24h0m0s`); its description is `darkpanel-<change id>` (written literally, the id is not known at plan); the key is shown once in the change's output; the row is recorded in `tailnet_keys` before the request. `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 over the account id and the normalized input, so it does not depend on the order of tags and does not change between two plans of the same input.
4. `Apply`, in this order:
   a. Load the account and normalize against its tags (a refusal is `core.Definite`). The description is `"darkpanel-" + env.ChangeID`.
   b. Insert the `tailnet_keys` row with `insertKey` in one `env.DB.Write`: kind `change`, owner the change id, `RequestedAt` and `UpdatedAt` `env.Clock.Now().UTC()`, the normalized expiry and tags, state `requested`, empty key id.
   c. `Intend` the effect built with `cloudEffect(core.EffectCreate, "tailnet.key:?"+description, <null>)`, then set `Recovery` to `&core.RecoveryID{Kind: "marker", Value: description}` and `Before` to `core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage("null")}`. If `Intend` fails, set the row `deleted` (nothing was sent) and return the error.
   d. Call `a.CreateKey` with a `KeyRequest` carrying the description, tags, the three booleans and the expiry.
   e. On success: set the row `live` with the key id (`setKeyState`), then `env.Effects.Made(ctx, seq, "tailnet.key:"+id, core.StateDoc{State: {"id","description"}})`, and return `CreatedKey` with the id, the key, `Expires` and the description. Writing the row before `Made` is deliberate: if either write fails the effect stays `intended`, the engine settles it `unresolved`, and the operator's resolution (`Resolved`) repairs the row.
   f. On an error for which `core.IsDefinite` is true (the provider refused: 4xx): `Skipped(seq)`, set the row `deleted`, return the error unchanged. On any other error (5xx, transport failure, a 2xx answer that cannot be read: the key may exist): set the row `uncertain`, do not call `Made` or `Skipped`, return the error unchanged so the engine leaves the effect `unresolved` (`uncertain`) with cause `cloud.uncertain_outcome`. Every journal and row write after the provider call uses `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`, so a deadline that ended mid-call still records the outcome.
5. `Verify`: when `out.ID` is empty return nil; otherwise `a.Key(ctx, out.ID)` must find a key that is not revoked, else an error.
6. `authkeyLister.Read`: `listKeys(ctx, env.DB.Read())` mapped to `AuthKeyRow` in that order, with `Expires = RequestedAt + ExpirySeconds`; no provider request and no account is needed, and an empty table answers an empty (not null) `keys` array.

In `authkey_resolve.go`:

7. `describedKeys(ctx, a *api) ([]KeyInfo, error)`: `a.Keys`, then `a.Key(ctx, id)` for each entry whose `Description` is empty (the list may carry ids only, spec 4.2a); revoked keys are dropped. The state document of a key is built by one function from its id and description.
8. `Observe(ctx, env, e)`: load the api with `connected`. If `e.Resource` holds `?` (a creation not yet named), match `describedKeys` against `e.Recovery.Value`: `Matches` is the count, `Resource` the single match's `tailnet.key:<id>`, `Candidates` every match when there is more than one, `Exclusive` true, `Current` the match's state or `{"state": null}` when none. Otherwise read `a.Key` for the id in `e.Resource` (for every effect state, including undoing and undone: the key id is the identity, `UndoResource` is empty); a not-found answer (error code `errcode.NotFound` or `cloud.Status(err) == 404`) or a revoked key is `{"state": null}`; `Matches` is 1 and `Resource` is `e.Resource`.
9. `Inverse(ctx, env, e)`: refuse a resource that still holds `?` with a `core.Definite` error; `a.DeleteKey(ctx, id)`; an error with a 4xx `cloud.Status` is wrapped in `core.Definite`, any other error is returned as it is. After a successful delete set the row `deleted` (keeping the key id) in `env.DB.Write`; a failure of that write is logged on `env.Log` and not returned (the row stays `live`, which no sweep touches). Return an empty `core.InverseResult`.
10. `Resolved(ctx, tx, e, resolution)` moves the row named by `e.Recovery.Value` in the resolution's transaction, with `setKeyState(ctx, tx, description, state, keyID, e.ResolvedAt)`: effect `accepted` whose `Current.State` is not null: `live` with the `id` member of that state; `accepted` with a null state: `retired`; `made` (reconcile): `live` with the id after `tailnet.key:` in `e.Resource`; `skipped`: `retired`. Any other effect state is an error.

Spec 1.9's table row "Tailscale auth key create" governs this task. A sweep is cleanup of keys Darkpanel owns: it never settles an effect and never creates a key. `orphans` is false for the five-minute pass and true for the daily pass. A key is in Darkpanel's namespace when its description matches `^darkpanel-[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$` (a change id) or `^darkpanel-enroll-[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$` (a host id); a key outside both is never read as ours and never deleted. The window of a row is its `RequestedAt` plus `ExpirySeconds` plus 24 hours.

// swChange returns a 26-character change id that differs by n.
func swChange(n int) string { return fmt.Sprintf("01J9X4K8Q2M5N7P0R3S6T8V%03d", n) }

func swSetup(t *testing.T) swFix {

	h := newTNHost(t)
	srv := fake.New(t)
	acConnect(t, h, srv)
	tnn := tnWith(srv)
	a, _, err := tnn.connected(context.Background(), h.db, coretest.Sealer{}, h.clock)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	audit := &coretest.MemAudit{}
	return swFix{h: h, srv: srv, t: tnn, api: a, audit: audit, deps: ext.Deps{
		DB: h.db, Sealer: coretest.Sealer{}, Clock: h.clock, Audit: audit,
		Log: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil)),
	}}
}

// key creates a provider key with the description and returns its id.
func (f swFix) key(t *testing.T, description string) string {
	t.Helper()
	ck, err := f.api.CreateKey(context.Background(), KeyRequest{Description: description, Tags: []string{"tag:ci"}, ExpirySeconds: 3600})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return ck.ID
}

func (f swFix) alive(id string) bool {
	k, err := f.api.Key(context.Background(), id)
	return err == nil && !k.Revoked
}

// row records a tailnet_keys row requested age ago with a one hour expiry.
func (f swFix) row(t *testing.T, description, state, keyID string, age time.Duration) {
	t.Helper()
	now := f.h.clock.Now()
	err := f.h.db.Write(context.Background(), func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		return insertKey(context.Background(), tx, keyRow{
			Description: description, Kind: "change", OwnerID: swChange(900), KeyID: keyID, State: state,
			RequestedAt: now.Add(-age), UpdatedAt: now.Add(-age), ExpirySeconds: 3600, Tags: []string{"tag:ci"},
		})
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func (f swFix) state(t *testing.T, description string) string {
	t.Helper()
	r, ok, err := loadKey(context.Background(), f.h.db.Read(), description)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	return r.State
}

func swEventually(t *testing.T, what string, cond func() bool) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
	for !cond() {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

func TestSwSweepRules(t *testing.T) {
	change := "darkpanel-" + swChange(1)
	enroll := "darkpanel-enroll-" + swHost
	const (
		inWindow   = time.Hour      // request time + 1 h expiry + 24 h is still ahead
		pastWindow = 48 * time.Hour // it is not
	)
	cases := []struct {
		name        string
		desc        string
		state       string // "" records no row
		age         time.Duration
		orphans     bool
		wantDeleted bool
		wantState   string
	}{
		{"uncertain in window, five-minute pass", change, "uncertain", inWindow, false, true, "uncertain"},
		{"retired in window, five-minute pass", change, "retired", inWindow, false, true, "deleted"},
		{"retired past window, five-minute pass", change, "retired", pastWindow, false, false, "retired"},
		{"retired past window, daily pass", change, "retired", pastWindow, true, true, "deleted"},
		{"uncertain past window, five-minute pass", change, "uncertain", pastWindow, false, false, "uncertain"},
		{"uncertain past window, daily pass", change, "uncertain", pastWindow, true, true, "uncertain"},
		{"live row is never swept", change, "live", pastWindow, true, false, "live"},
		{"used row is never swept", enroll, "used", pastWindow, true, false, "used"},
		{"orphan, five-minute pass", change, "", 0, false, false, ""},
		{"orphan, daily pass", change, "", 0, true, true, ""},
		{"enroll orphan, daily pass", enroll, "", 0, true, true, ""},
		{"deleted row, five-minute pass", change, "deleted", pastWindow, false, false, "deleted"},
		{"deleted row, daily pass", change, "deleted", pastWindow, true, true, "deleted"},
		{"young requested row is skipped", change, "requested", 2 * time.Minute, true, false, "requested"},
		{"old requested row becomes uncertain and is swept", change, "requested", 10 * time.Minute, true, true, "uncertain"},
		{"old requested row, five-minute pass", change, "requested", 10 * time.Minute, false, false, "requested"},
		{"foreign description", "ci-runner", "", 0, true, false, ""},
		{"change namespace with a short id", "darkpanel-" + swChange(1)[1:], "", 0, true, false, ""},
		{"enroll namespace with a short id", "darkpanel-enroll-short", "", 0, true, false, ""},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := swSetup(t)
			id := f.key(t, tc.desc)
			if tc.state != "" {
				f.row(t, tc.desc, tc.state, "", tc.age)
			}
			if err := f.t.sweep(context.Background(), f.deps, f.h.clock.Now(), tc.orphans); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if got := !f.alive(id); got != tc.wantDeleted {
				t.Errorf("key deleted %v, want %v", got, tc.wantDeleted)
			}
			if got := f.state(t, tc.desc); got != tc.wantState {
				t.Errorf("row %q, want %q", got, tc.wantState)
			}
			entries, _, err := f.audit.List(context.Background(), core.AuditQuery{Actor: "system:tailnet.keysweep"})
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !tc.wantDeleted {
				if len(entries) != 0 {
					t.Errorf("%d audit entries for a pass that deleted nothing", len(entries))
				}
				return
			}
			if len(entries) != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("%d audit entries, want 1", len(entries))
			}
			e := entries[0]
			var in map[string]string
			if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Input, &in); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if e.Action != "tailnet.keysweep" || e.Phase != "delete" || e.Result != "ok" ||
				in["keyId"] != id || in["description"] != tc.desc || len(in) != 2 {
				t.Errorf("audit entry %+v input %s", e, e.Input)
			}
		})
	}
}
