```go
func TestSwProviderFailureDoesNotStopThePass(t *testing.T) {
	f := swSetup(t)
	d1, d2 := "darkpanel-"+swChange(3), "darkpanel-"+swChange(4)
	k1, k2 := f.key(t, d1), f.key(t, d2)
	f.row(t, d1, "uncertain", k1, time.Hour)
	f.row(t, d2, "uncertain", k2, time.Hour)
	f.srv.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodDelete, swKeysPath+"/"+k1, cloudfake.Fault{Status: http.StatusInternalServerError, Times: 4})
	if err := f.t.sweep(context.Background(), f.deps, f.h.clock.Now(), false); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("the pass hid a failed delete")
	}
	if !f.alive(k1) || f.alive(k2) {
		t.Errorf("first key alive %v, second alive %v; want true, false", f.alive(k1), f.alive(k2))
	}
	entries, _, _ := f.audit.List(context.Background(), core.AuditQuery{Actor: "system:tailnet.keysweep"})
	if len(entries) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("%d audit entries, want 1 (only the delete that happened)", len(entries))
	}
}

func TestSwServiceSchedule(t *testing.T) {
	f := swSetup(t)
	_, services, err := module{t: f.t}.Controller(f.deps)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	orphanAtStart := f.key(t, "darkpanel-"+swChange(5))

	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { done <- services[0].Run(ctx) }()
	defer func() {
		cancel()
		select {
		case err := <-done:
			if err != nil {
				t.Errorf("Run returned %v after its context ended", err)
			}
		case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
			t.Error("Run did not return after its context ended")
		}
	}()

	swEventually(t, "the pass at start to delete an orphan", func() bool { return !f.alive(orphanAtStart) })
	swEventually(t, "both timers to be armed", func() bool { return f.h.clock.Pending() == 2 })

	owned := "darkpanel-" + swChange(6)
	ownedID := f.key(t, owned)
	f.row(t, owned, "uncertain", ownedID, time.Minute)
	orphan := f.key(t, "darkpanel-"+swChange(7))

	f.h.clock.Advance(5 * time.Minute)
	swEventually(t, "the five-minute pass", func() bool { return !f.alive(ownedID) && f.h.clock.Pending() == 2 })
	if !f.alive(orphan) {
		t.Fatal("a five-minute pass deleted an orphan")
	}

	f.h.clock.Advance(24 * time.Hour)
	swEventually(t, "the daily pass to delete the orphan", func() bool { return !f.alive(orphan) })
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `keysweep.go`:

1. `func (m module) Controller(deps ext.Deps) ([]ext.Route, []ext.Service, error)` returns no routes and one `ext.Service` named `tailnet.keysweep` whose `Run` calls `m.t.runKeySweep(ctx, deps)`.
2. `func (t tn) sweep(ctx, deps, now, orphans) error` is one pass:
   a. `t.connected(ctx, deps.DB, deps.Sealer, deps.Clock)`; an error with code `errcode.CloudNotConnected` ends the pass with nil and no provider request (the sweeps run only while the account is connected); any other error is returned.
   b. Read the rows with `listKeys(ctx, deps.DB.Read())`, keyed by description.
   c. Only when `orphans`: every row in `requested` whose `RequestedAt` is older than 15 s + 5 min before `now` is first set to `uncertain` (`setKeyState`, key id kept, `UpdatedAt` `now`) and treated as `uncertain` from here on; a younger one is left alone, so a key whose create may still be answered is never deleted. The five-minute pass leaves `requested` rows alone.
   d. List the provider's keys with descriptions through Task 49's `describedKeys(ctx, a)` (it drops revoked keys); drop keys outside the namespace. Declare no listing helper of your own.
   e. For each such key decide by its row (none, or a state): no row: delete only when `orphans`; `live` or `used`: never; `requested`: never; `uncertain` or `retired`: delete when `orphans`, or when `now` is not after the row's window; `deleted`: delete only when `orphans`.
   f. A delete is `a.DeleteKey`; after it succeeds record one audit entry with `deps.Audit.Record(ctx, core.AuditEntry{Actor: "system:tailnet.keysweep", Action: "tailnet.keysweep", Phase: "delete", Result: "ok", At: now, Input: {"keyId","description"}})` and, when the row is `retired`, set it `deleted` with the key id. A failed delete or audit write is collected and the pass goes on with the next key; the pass returns the collected errors joined with `errors.Join`, so one provider failure does not hide the others.
   g. After the keys, in either pass: every `retired` row whose description matched no listed key and whose window is over (`now` after it) is set `deleted`: its key can no longer exist, and a `retired` row would otherwise block disconnecting the account (`cleanupPending`) for ever. Skip this step when the listing in (d) failed.
3. `func (t tn) runKeySweep(ctx context.Context, deps ext.Deps) error` is the service body: run `sweep(…, deps.Clock.Now(), true)` once at start (a controller restarted often must still reach a daily pass), then arm two timers on `deps.Clock.AfterFunc`, five minutes (pass with `orphans` false) and 24 hours (`orphans` true); a timer's callback sends its kind on a channel of capacity 2 without blocking, and the loop re-arms that timer only after its pass has finished, so passes never overlap and `Pending()` on a fake clock returns to 2 after each. A pass error is logged on `deps.Log` (the error text carries the provider and the status, never a credential) and does not end the service. When `ctx` ends, stop both timers and return nil.
4. `Controller` must not touch `deps` outside the service's `Run`: the server calls it with whatever `ext.Deps` it has, including a test server's. In `internal/controller/server/extensions_test.go`, `TestContributionsCollectInOrder`, make the two collecting loops keep only the test contributors' own contributions, so compiled-in modules (this task's `tailnet.keysweep`, later `cloudflare.hostnames`) do not change what the test compares; change no other line of the file (`strings` is already imported):

```go
func TestPoSetPlan(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name      string
		text      string
		fault     *cloudfake.Fault // on the validate request
		noAccount bool
		code      errcode.Code
		validated bool
	}{
		{name: "valid", text: poAfter, validated: true},
		{name: "not HuJSON", text: `{"acls": [`, code: errcode.TailnetPolicyInvalid},
		{name: "empty", text: "  ", code: errcode.TailnetPolicyInvalid},
		{name: "provider validation fails", text: poAfter, fault: &cloudfake.Fault{Status: http.StatusForbidden}, code: errcode.CloudPermissionMissing, validated: true},
		{name: "no account", text: poAfter, noAccount: true, code: errcode.CloudNotConnected},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			e := poSetup(t)
			if tc.noAccount {
				e.h = newTNHost(t)
			}
			if tc.fault != nil {
				e.srv.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodPost, poValidatePath, *tc.fault)
			}
			out, err := e.t.policySet().Handler.Plan(context.Background(), e.h.env(""), poJSON(t, PolicySetInput{Text: tc.text}))
			if validated := len(poRequests(e, http.MethodPost, poValidatePath)) > 0; validated != tc.validated {
				t.Errorf("validate request sent %v, want %v", validated, tc.validated)
			}
			if tc.code != "" {
				if got := poCode(t, err); got != tc.code {
					t.Fatalf("code %s, want %s (%v)", got, tc.code, err)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			var added, removed int
			for _, l := range out.Diff {
				switch {
				case l.Op == "+" && strings.Contains(l.Text, "tagOwners"):
					added++
				case l.Op == "-":
					removed++
				}
			}
			if added != 1 || removed != 0 {
				t.Errorf("diff %v: want one added tagOwners line and no removed line", out.Diff)
			}
			if out.StateHash == "" {
				t.Error("empty state hash")
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestPoSetApply(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	e := poSetup(t)
	w, err := poSet(t, e, poAfter)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	text, etag := e.srv.Policy()
	if text != poAfter || w.ETag != etag || etag == e.etag {
		t.Fatalf("provider holds %q with ETag %s; apply answered %+v (ETag before %s)", text, etag, w, e.etag)
	}
	posts := poRequests(e, http.MethodPost, poACLPath)
	if len(posts) != 1 || posts[0].Header.Get("If-Match") != e.etag {
		t.Fatalf("policy writes %+v, want one with If-Match %s", posts, e.etag)
	}

	eff := poOnly(t, e)
	if eff.Kind != core.EffectModify || eff.State != core.EffectMade || eff.Resource != poResource || eff.Local || eff.CommitWait != cloud.CommitWait {
		t.Errorf("effect %+v", eff)
	}
	poSame(t, eff.Before.State, poCanonState(t, poBefore))
	if string(eff.Before.Version) != strconv.Quote(e.etag) {
		t.Errorf("before version %s, want the ETag read", eff.Before.Version)
	}
	if eff.Post == nil {
		t.Fatal("no post state")
	}
	poSame(t, eff.Post.State, poCanonState(t, poAfter))
	if string(eff.Post.Version) != strconv.Quote(w.ETag) {
		t.Errorf("post version %s, want the ETag written", eff.Post.Version)
	}
	secret, err := e.h.journal.Secret(ctx, eff.Seq)
	if err != nil || string(secret) != poBefore {
		t.Errorf("sealed before-text %q (%v), want the policy with its comments", secret, err)
	}

	in := poJSON(t, PolicySetInput{Text: poAfter})
	if err := e.t.policySet().Handler.Verify(ctx, e.h.env(poChange), in, poJSON(t, w)); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("verify after the write: %v", err)
	}
	e.srv.SetPolicy(`{"acls": []}`)
	if err := e.t.policySet().Handler.Verify(ctx, e.h.env(poChange), in, poJSON(t, w)); err == nil {
		t.Error("verify accepted a policy that is not the one written")
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `policy.go`:

1. `func (t tn) policyGet() core.ActionDef` returns `core.DefineRead[PolicyGetInput, Policy]` named `tailnet.policy.get`, no lock key. Its handler loads the api with `t.connected`, calls `a.Policy(ctx)` and answers the text exactly as the provider sent it (comments kept) with its ETag.
2. `func (t tn) policySet() core.ActionDef` returns `core.DefineMutating[PolicySetInput, PolicyWritten]` named `tailnet.policy.set`, Version 1, `ClassCompensable`, `SideController`, `LockKeys: []string{ID}`, default `ApplyTimeout`, no `CompensatedBy` or `ForwardOnly`. Its handler is `type policySetHandler struct{ policyHandler }`; the embedded type supplies `Observe` and `Inverse`, so `core.DefineMutating` finds the undo handler by type assertion.
3. A shared check of the input text: empty or whitespace-only text, or text for which `policy.Canonical` fails, is `errcode.TailnetPolicyInvalid` with the parse message as detail (Apply wraps it in `core.Definite`); it runs before any provider request.
4. `Plan`: the text check; `t.connected`; `before, etag := a.Policy(ctx)`; `a.ValidatePolicy(ctx, text)`, whose error (the provider's `tailnet.policy_invalid`, or `cloud.*`) is returned unchanged; `Diff` is `policy.Diff(before, text)`; `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 over the account id, the ETag and the text, so a policy changed after the plan makes the apply fail with `plan.state_changed` before any write.
5. `Apply`: the text check; `t.connected`; read `before, etag` again; when `bytes.Equal(before, text)` return `PolicyWritten{ETag: etag}` with no effect and no request (nothing to write; texts that differ only in comments or spacing are different texts and are written); otherwise `newETag, err := t.writePolicy(ctx, env, a, acct, before, etag, text)` and return `PolicyWritten{ETag: newETag}`.
6. `Verify`: read the policy; its `policy.Canonical` must equal that of the input text (the written policy is present; the ETag is not compared, so an unrelated later edit of comments does not fail the change), else an error.

In `policy_effects.go`:

7. A state document of a policy: `State` is `{"policy": <policy.Canonical of the text>}`, `Version` the ETag as a JSON string.
8. `writePolicy` journals, posts and records: build the effect with `cloudEffect(core.EffectModify, "tailnet.policy:"+acct.Tailnet, …)` and then assign `Before` to the state document of `before` and `etag`, and `After` to a pointer to the state document of `after` with no `Version`; `env.Effects.Intend(ctx, e, before)` passes the before-text as the sealed secret. Call `a.SetPolicy(ctx, after, etag)` (the api sends `If-Match: etag`). On success `Made(ctx, seq, e.Resource, <state document of after with the returned ETag as Version>)` and return the new ETag. On an error with `core.IsDefinite` true (including `tailnet.policy_conflict` for a 412): `Skipped(seq)` and return the error unchanged. On any other error: write nothing to the journal and return the error unchanged, so the engine leaves the effect `unresolved` (`uncertain`). Journal writes after the provider call use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`.
9. `type policyHandler struct{ t tn }` with `Observe(ctx, env, e)`: `t.connected`, `a.Policy`, `Current` the state document of the text read with its ETag, `Resource` `e.Resource`, `Matches` 1 (the same for an effect that is undoing or undone: the resource is the tailnet's one policy). The engine compares `State` only, so a changed ETag with the same canonical policy is not a conflict.
10. `Inverse(ctx, env, e)`: the before-text is `env.Effects.Secret(ctx, e.Seq)`; an error or an empty secret is a `core.Definite` error (the text is gone, nothing is written). The ETag to send is the `Post.Version` of the effect (a JSON string). Call `a.SetPolicy(ctx, beforeText, thatETag)` and return its error unchanged: a 412 arrives as `tailnet.policy_conflict` wrapped in `core.Definite`, which the engine reports as a failed undo with the effect still `made`; the later edit is never overwritten. Return an empty `core.InverseResult`.

```go
package cloudflare

import (

	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/cloudflare/fake"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/cloudflare/ingress"
)

const (
	haTunnelName = "darkpanel-ha"
	haService    = "http://10.0.0.5:8080"
	haZoneName   = "example.com"
)

var haAdmin = core.Principal{Actor: "user:u1", UserID: "u1", Scope: core.ScopeAdmin, Source: "203.0.113.7"}

// haModule serves the hostname add action under the cloudflare module id, so
// the engine tests do not depend on the module's Manifest.
type haModule struct{ c cf }

func (m haModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: ID, Version: 1, Actions: []core.ActionDef{m.c.hostnameAdd()}}
}

func haInputWith(tunnel, hostname, service string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf(`{"tunnel":%q,"hostname":%q,"service":%q}`, tunnel, hostname, service)
}

func haInput(hostname string) string { return haInputWith(haTunnelName, hostname, haService) }

// haPrepare makes sure the host has a connected account, the zone example.com
// and the tunnel darkpanel-ha, on the fake and in the database, and returns
// what a test needs to reach them. Calling it twice changes nothing.
func haPrepare(t *testing.T, h *cfHost, srv *fake.Server) (c cf, a *api, zoneID, tunnelID string) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	c = cfWith(srv)
	if _, ok, err := loadAccount(ctx, h.db.Read()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	} else if !ok {
		acConnect(t, h, srv)
	}
	a, err := c.newAPI(fake.AccountID, []byte(fake.Token), h.clock)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	zones, err := a.Zones(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, z := range zones {
		if z.Name == haZoneName {
			zoneID = z.ID
		}
	}
	if zoneID == "" {
		zoneID = srv.AddZone(haZoneName)
	}
	row, ok, err := loadTunnel(ctx, h.db.Read(), haTunnelName)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if ok {
		return c, a, zoneID, row.ID
	}
	tunnelID = srv.AddTunnel(haTunnelName)
	err = h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		return insertTunnel(ctx, tx, tunnelRow{ID: tunnelID, Name: haTunnelName, ChangeID: "01HATUNNEL", CreatedAt: h.clock.Now()})
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return c, a, zoneID, tunnelID
}

// haEngine is a controller engine over the host's database serving the
// hostname add action. The caller closes it.
func haEngine(t *testing.T, h *cfHost, c cf) *lifecycle.Engine {
	t.Helper()
	reg, err := core.NewRegistry(haModule{c})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	eng, err := lifecycle.New(lifecycle.Config{
		Side: core.SideController, Registry: reg, Validator: schema.NewValidator(), Journal: &coretest.MemJournal{},
		Redact: schema.Redact,
		Base:   core.Env{DB: h.db, Sealer: coretest.Sealer{}, Clock: h.clock, Log: slog.New(slog.DiscardHandler)},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := eng.Recover(context.Background()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return eng
}

// haApplyPlan plans and applies the hostname add action with input.
func haApplyPlan(t *testing.T, eng *lifecycle.Engine, input string) core.ChangeView {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	pv, err := eng.Plan(ctx, haAdmin, core.ActionRef{Name: "cloudflare.hostname.add", Version: 1}, json.RawMessage(input), core.PlanOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("plan: %v", err)
	}
	cv, err := eng.Apply(ctx, haAdmin, pv.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("apply: %v", err)
	}
	return cv
}

// haAdd adds an active hostname to the tunnel darkpanel-ha through the
// action, preparing the account, zone and tunnel first, and returns its row.
// It builds an engine of its own and closes it before it returns.
func haAdd(t *testing.T, h *cfHost, srv *fake.Server, hostname string) hostnameRow {
	t.Helper()
	c, _, _, _ := haPrepare(t, h, srv)
	eng := haEngine(t, h, c)
	defer eng.Close()
	if cv := haApplyPlan(t, eng, haInput(hostname)); cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("adding %s ended %s: %+v", hostname, cv.State, cv.Error)
	}
	row, ok, err := loadHostname(context.Background(), h.db.Read(), hostname)
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("hostname %s: found %t, error %v", hostname, ok, err)
	}
	return row
}

// settle waits for the change to reach want.
func (f *haFixture) settle(id, want string) core.ChangeView {
	f.t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for {
		cv, err := f.eng.Change(context.Background(), id)
		if err != nil {
			f.t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if cv.State == want {
			return cv
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			f.t.Fatalf("change %s is %s, want %s: %+v", id, cv.State, want, cv.Error)
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

// path is the fake's request path for suffix, found from the path of a
// request the client sent for zones.
func (f *haFixture) path(suffix string) string {
	f.t.Helper()
	if _, err := f.api.Zones(context.Background()); err != nil {
		f.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	reqs := f.srv.Cloud().Requests()
	prefix, ok := strings.CutSuffix(reqs[len(reqs)-1].Path, "/zones")
	if !ok {
		f.t.Fatalf("the zones request went to %q", reqs[len(reqs)-1].Path)
	}
	return prefix + suffix

func haDiffText(diff []core.DiffLine) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, l := range diff {
		b.WriteString(l.Op + " " + l.Text + "\n")
	}
	return b.String()
}

func TestHAAddWritesTheRuleBeforeTheCatchAllAndTheRecord(t *testing.T) {
	f := newHAFixture(t)
	input := haInput("app.example.com")
	pv, err := f.plan(input, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	diff := haDiffText(pv.Diff)
	for _, want := range []string{"app.example.com", haService, f.tunnelID + ".cfargotunnel.com", "not detected"} {
		if !strings.Contains(diff, want) {
			t.Errorf("the plan's diff lacks %q:\n%s", want, diff)
		}
	}
	if w := f.writes(); len(w) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("planning sent the writes %v, want none", w)
	}
	cv, err := f.eng.Apply(context.Background(), haAdmin, pv.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
	if err != nil || cv.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("apply = %+v, %v; want a completed change", cv, err)
	}
	var out HostnameView
	if err := json.Unmarshal(cv.Output, &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	recs := f.records("app.example.com")
	if len(recs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("records for app.example.com = %+v, want exactly one", recs)
	}
	r := recs[0]
	if r.Type != "CNAME" || r.Content != f.tunnelID+".cfargotunnel.com" || !r.Proxied || r.Comment != "darkpanel:"+cv.ID {
		t.Errorf("record = %+v, want a proxied CNAME to the tunnel commented darkpanel:%s", r, cv.ID)
	}
	if out.Hostname != "app.example.com" || out.Tunnel != f.tunnelID || out.Service != haService || out.Phase != "active" ||
		out.Health != "ok" || out.RecordID != r.ID {
		t.Errorf("output = %+v, want the active hostname with record %s", out, r.ID)
	}
	cfg := f.config()
	rule, ok := ingress.Lookup(cfg, "app.example.com")
	if !ok || rule.Service != haService {
		t.Errorf("rule = %+v (found %t), want service %s", rule, ok, haService)
	}
	if last := cfg.Ingress[len(cfg.Ingress)-1]; last.Hostname != "" || last.Service != ingress.CatchAll {
		t.Errorf("the last rule is %+v, want the catch-all %s", last, ingress.CatchAll)
	}
	row, found := f.row("app.example.com")
	if !found || row.Phase != "active" || row.ChangeID != cv.ID || row.RecordID != r.ID || row.ZoneID != f.zoneID || row.Service != haService {
		t.Errorf("row = %+v (found %t), want the active row of change %s", row, found, cv.ID)
	}
	if got := f.tunnel().ConfigHash; got != ingress.Hash(cfg) {
		t.Errorf("stored configuration hash = %q, want the hash of the configuration read back, %q", got, ingress.Hash(cfg))
	}
	effs := f.effects(cv.ID)
	if len(effs) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("effects = %+v, want two", effs)
	}
	if e := effs[0]; e.Resource != "cloudflare.ingress:"+f.tunnelID+"/app.example.com" || e.Kind != core.EffectModify || e.State != core.EffectMade || e.Local {
		t.Errorf("effect 1 = %+v, want the made, non-local ingress modification", e)
	}
	if e := effs[1]; e.Resource != "cloudflare.dnsrecord:"+f.zoneID+"/"+r.ID || e.Kind != core.EffectCreate || e.State != core.EffectMade || e.Local {
		t.Errorf("effect 2 = %+v, want the made, non-local DNS record creation", e)
	}
	if w := strings.Join(f.writes(), " "); w != "PUT POST" {
		t.Errorf("writes = %q, want one PUT of the configuration and one POST of the record", w)
	}
}

func TestHAAddCarriesUnrelatedRulesOver(t *testing.T) {
	f := newHAFixture(t)
	var cfg ingress.Config
	const raw = `{"ingress":[{"hostname":"keep.example.com","service":"http://10.0.0.9:80","originRequest":{"connectTimeout":"30s"}},{"service":"http_status:404"}],"warp-routing":{"enabled":true}}`
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &cfg); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.api.PutConfiguration(context.Background(), f.tunnelID, cfg); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.apply(haInput("app.example.com"))
	got := f.config()
	kept, ok := ingress.Lookup(got, "keep.example.com")
	b, _ := json.Marshal(kept)
	if !ok || kept.Service != "http://10.0.0.9:80" || !strings.Contains(string(b), `"connectTimeout":"30s"`) {
		t.Errorf("rule keep.example.com = %s (found %t), want it unchanged with its origin settings", b, ok)
	}
	all, _ := json.Marshal(got)
	if !strings.Contains(string(all), `"warp-routing":{"enabled":true}`) {
		t.Errorf("configuration %s lost its top-level warp-routing member", all)
	}
	if len(got.Ingress) != 3 {
		t.Errorf("ingress = %+v, want keep, the new rule and the catch-all", got.Ingress)
	}
}

func TestHAAddRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name  string
		setup func(f *haFixture)
		input func(f *haFixture) string
		want  errcode.Code
	}{
		{"unknown tunnel", nil, func(*haFixture) string { return haInputWith("darkpanel-nope", "app.example.com", haService) }, errcode.NotFound},
		{"uppercase hostname", nil, func(*haFixture) string { return haInputWith(haTunnelName, "App.example.com", haService) }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"hostname with one label", nil, func(*haFixture) string { return haInputWith(haTunnelName, "single", haService) }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"wildcard hostname", nil, func(*haFixture) string { return haInputWith(haTunnelName, "*.example.com", haService) }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"leading hyphen", nil, func(*haFixture) string { return haInputWith(haTunnelName, "-a.example.com", haService) }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"unsupported scheme", nil, func(*haFixture) string { return haInputWith(haTunnelName, "app.example.com", "ftp://10.0.0.5:21") }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"service without a port", nil, func(*haFixture) string { return haInputWith(haTunnelName, "app.example.com", "http://10.0.0.5") }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"service with a path", nil, func(*haFixture) string { return haInputWith(haTunnelName, "app.example.com", "http://10.0.0.5:80/x") }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"status out of range", nil, func(*haFixture) string { return haInputWith(haTunnelName, "app.example.com", "http_status:99") }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"hostname outside every zone", nil, func(*haFixture) string { return haInputWith(haTunnelName, "app.example.org", haService) }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"hostname already managed", func(f *haFixture) { f.apply(haInput("dup.example.com")) },
			func(*haFixture) string { return haInput("dup.example.com") }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"dns record exists", func(f *haFixture) {
			_, err := f.api.CreateDNSRecord(context.Background(), f.zoneID, DNSRecord{Type: "CNAME", Name: "taken.example.com", Content: "x.example.net"})
			if err != nil {
				f.t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}, func(*haFixture) string { return haInput("taken.example.com") }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"rule exists", func(f *haFixture) { f.putRule("ruled.example.com", "http://10.0.0.9:80") },
			func(*haFixture) string { return haInput("ruled.example.com") }, errcode.InvalidInput},
		{"configuration drift", func(f *haFixture) {
			err := f.h.db.Write(context.Background(), func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return setTunnelHash(context.Background(), tx, f.tunnelID, "stale") })
			if err != nil {
				f.t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}, func(*haFixture) string { return haInput("app.example.com") }, errcode.CloudConflict},
		{"panel gateway service", nil, func(*haFixture) string {
			return haInputWith(haTunnelName, "app.example.com", "http://172.31.255.1:8080")
		}, errcode.CloudflareReserved},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newHAFixture(t)
			if c.setup != nil {
				c.setup(f)
			}
			before := len(f.writes())
			_, err := f.plan(c.input(f), nil)
			if err == nil || errcode.From(err).Code != c.want {
				t.Errorf("plan error = %v, want code %s", err, c.want)
			}
			if n := len(f.writes()); n != before {
				t.Errorf("the refused plan sent %d writes", n-before)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestHAReservedServiceNeedsTheExposureParent(t *testing.T) {

	for name, call := range map[string]*core.CallContext{
		"no parent":           nil,
		"another parent":      {ParentChangeID: "01HPARENT", ParentAction: "panel.exposure.remove", StepID: "hostname"},
		"an unrelated parent": {ParentChangeID: "01HPARENT", ParentAction: "cloudflare.expose.container", StepID: "hostname"},
	} {
		if _, err := f.plan(input, call); err == nil || errcode.From(err).Code != errcode.CloudflareReserved {

		}
	}
}

func TestHAReserved(t *testing.T) {
	for service, want := range map[string]bool{
		"http://172.31.255.1:8080": true, "tcp://172.31.255.254:22": true, "https://172.31.255.7": true,
		"http://172.31.254.1:80": false, "http://172.31.256.1:80": false, "http://panel.internal:80": false,
		"http_status:404": false, "ssh://[::1]:22": false, "": false,
	} {

			t.Errorf("reserved(%q) = %t, want %t", service, got, want)

	}

func TestHACheckDrift(t *testing.T) {
	f := newHAFixture(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	f.putRule("a.example.com", "http://10.0.0.9:80")
	cfg := f.config()
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name, hash string
		conflict   bool
	}{{"none stored", "", false}, {"matching hash", ingress.Hash(cfg), false}, {"another hash", "stale", true}} {
		got, err := f.c.checkDrift(ctx, f.api, tunnelRow{ID: f.tunnelID, Name: haTunnelName, ConfigHash: c.hash})
		switch {
		case c.conflict && (err == nil || errcode.From(err).Code != errcode.CloudConflict || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), haTunnelName)):
			t.Errorf("%s: error %v, want cloud.conflict naming the tunnel", c.name, err)
		case !c.conflict && (err != nil || ingress.Hash(got) != ingress.Hash(cfg)):
			t.Errorf("%s: %v, hash %q; want the configuration read", c.name, err, ingress.Hash(got))
		}
	}
}

func TestHAPlanStateHashCoversTheConfiguration(t *testing.T) {
	f := newHAFixture(t)
	input := haInput("app.example.com")
	pv, err := f.plan(input, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.putRule("other.example.com", "http://10.0.0.9:80")

		t.Errorf("apply of a plan made before the configuration changed: %v, want %s", err, errcode.PlanStateChanged)
	}
	if w := f.writes(); len(w) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("writes = %v, want only the test's own PUT", w)
	}
}

func TestHAUndoRemovesTheRecordAndTheRule(t *testing.T) {
	f := newHAFixture(t)
	cv := f.apply(haInput("app.example.com"))
	if _, err := f.eng.Undo(context.Background(), haAdmin, cv.ID, nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.settle(cv.ID, core.StateReverted)
	if recs := f.records("app.example.com"); len(recs) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("records after the undo = %+v, want none", recs)
	}
	cfg := f.config()
	if _, ok := ingress.Lookup(cfg, "app.example.com"); ok {
		t.Error("the rule is still in the configuration after the undo")
	}
	if last := cfg.Ingress[len(cfg.Ingress)-1]; last.Service != ingress.CatchAll {
		t.Errorf("the last rule is %+v, want the catch-all", last)
	}
	if _, ok := f.row("app.example.com"); ok {
		t.Error("the hostname row is still stored after the undo")
	}
	if got := f.tunnel().ConfigHash; got != ingress.Hash(cfg) {
		t.Errorf("stored hash = %q, want the hash of the configuration after the undo", got)
	}
	for _, e := range f.effects(cv.ID) {
		if e.State != core.EffectUndone {
			t.Errorf("effect %d is %s, want undone", e.Seq, e.State)
		}
	}
}

func TestHAUncertainRecordCreateNeedsRepair(t *testing.T) {
	f := newHAFixture(t)
	f.srv.Cloud().Fail(http.MethodPost, f.path("/zones/"+f.zoneID+"/dns_records"), cloudfake.Fault{LoseResponse: true})
	cv := f.apply(haInput("app.example.com"))
	cv = f.settle(cv.ID, core.StateNeedsRepair)
	effs := f.effects(cv.ID)
	if len(effs) != 2 || effs[1].State != core.EffectUnresolved || effs[1].Reason != core.ReasonUncertain ||
		!strings.HasPrefix(effs[1].Resource, "cloudflare.dnsrecord:?darkpanel:") {
		t.Fatalf("effects = %+v, want the record creation unresolved as uncertain and still unnamed", effs)
	}
	res, err := f.eng.Observe(context.Background(), haAdmin, cv.ID, 2)
	recs := f.records("app.example.com")
	if err != nil || len(recs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("observe error %v, records %+v; want the committed record found", err, recs)
	}
	if res.Observation.Matches != 1 || res.Observation.Resource != "cloudflare.dnsrecord:"+f.zoneID+"/"+recs[0].ID {
		t.Errorf("observation = %+v, want one match naming record %s", res.Observation, recs[0].ID)
	}
	if row, ok := f.row("app.example.com"); !ok || row.Phase != "adding_record" {
		t.Errorf("row = %+v (found %t), want it left in adding_record", row, ok)
	}
	for _, w := range f.writes() {
		if w == http.MethodDelete {
			t.Error("a DELETE was sent while the effect was unresolved")
		}
	}
}

func TestHARecover(t *testing.T) {
	const host, changeID = "rec.example.com", "01HRECOVER"
	cases := []struct {
		name                        string
		phase                       string // "" stores no row
		rule, record                bool   // present at the provider
		ingressEffect, recordEffect string // "", made or skipped
		want                        string
		wantRow, wantRule, wantRec  bool
		wantWrites                  int
	}{
		{"no row", "", false, false, "", "", core.RecoveryFailed, false, false, false, 0},
		{"rule write refused", "adding_rule", false, false, "skipped", "", core.RecoveryFailed, false, false, false, 0},
		{"rule made, record never tried", "adding_record", true, false, "made", "", core.RecoveryRolledBack, false, false, false, 1},
		{"record refused", "adding_record", true, false, "made", "skipped", core.RecoveryRolledBack, false, false, false, 1},
		{"both made, row behind", "adding_record", true, true, "made", "made", core.RecoveryCompleted, true, true, true, 0},
		{"already active", "active", true, true, "made", "made", core.RecoveryCompleted, true, true, true, 0},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newHAFixture(t)
			ctx := context.Background()
			if c.phase != "" {
				row := hostnameRow{Hostname: host, TunnelID: f.tunnelID, Service: haService, ZoneID: f.zoneID, Phase: c.phase, ChangeID: changeID,
					Health: "unknown", UpdatedAt: f.h.clock.Now()}
				if err := f.h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertHostname(ctx, tx, row) }); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			}
			if c.rule {
				f.putRule(host, haService)
			}
			var rec DNSRecord
			if c.record {
				var err error
				rec, err = f.api.CreateDNSRecord(ctx, f.zoneID, DNSRecord{Type: "CNAME", Name: host, Content: f.tunnelID + ".cfargotunnel.com", Proxied: true, Comment: "darkpanel:" + changeID})
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			}
			env := f.h.env(changeID)
			if c.ingressEffect != "" {
				e := core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectModify, Resource: "cloudflare.ingress:" + f.tunnelID + "/" + host, CommitWait: cloud.CommitWait,
					Before: core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(`{"rule":null}`)}}
				seq, err := env.Effects.Intend(ctx, e, nil)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				if c.ingressEffect == "skipped" {
					err = env.Effects.Skipped(ctx, seq)
				} else {
					rule, _ := ingress.Lookup(f.config(), host)
					b, _ := json.Marshal(rule)
					err = env.Effects.Made(ctx, seq, e.Resource, core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(`{"rule":` + string(b) + `}`)})
				}
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			}
			if c.recordEffect != "" {
				e := core.Effect{Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: "cloudflare.dnsrecord:?darkpanel:" + changeID, CommitWait: cloud.CommitWait,
					Recovery: &core.RecoveryID{Kind: "marker", Value: "darkpanel:" + changeID}, Before: core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(`null`)}}
				seq, err := env.Effects.Intend(ctx, e, nil)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				if c.recordEffect == "skipped" {
					err = env.Effects.Skipped(ctx, seq)
				} else {
					err = env.Effects.Made(ctx, seq, "cloudflare.dnsrecord:"+f.zoneID+"/"+rec.ID, core.StateDoc{State: json.RawMessage(`{"name":"` + host + `"}`)})
				}
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			}
			before := len(f.writes())
			out, err := hostnameHandler{c: f.c}.Recover(ctx, env)
			if err != nil || out.State != c.want {
				t.Fatalf("Recover = %+v, %v; want state %s", out, err, c.want)
			}
			row, found := f.row(host)
			_, hasRule := ingress.Lookup(f.config(), host)
			hasRec := len(f.records(host)) > 0
			if found != c.wantRow || hasRule != c.wantRule || hasRec != c.wantRec {
				t.Errorf("row %t, rule %t, record %t; want %t, %t, %t", found, hasRule, hasRec, c.wantRow, c.wantRule, c.wantRec)
			}
			if n := len(f.writes()) - before; n != c.wantWrites {
				t.Errorf("Recover sent %d writes, want %d", n, c.wantWrites)
			}
			if c.want == core.RecoveryCompleted {
				var view HostnameView
				if err := json.Unmarshal(out.Output, &view); err != nil || view.Phase != "active" || view.RecordID != rec.ID || row.Phase != "active" || row.RecordID != rec.ID {
					t.Errorf("output %s (%v), row %+v; want the active hostname with record %s", out.Output, err, row, rec.ID)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

`hostname.go`:

1. `panelNetwork` is the prefix `172.31.255.0/24`. `reserved(service)` parses the service as a URL and reports whether its host is an IP address inside `panelNetwork`; a service that does not parse, has no host, names a host that is not an IP literal (`http://panel.internal:80`), or is `http_status:<code>`, is not reserved. The port is optional here.
2. `ingressResource(tunnelID, hostname)` is `cloudflare.ingress:<tunnel id>/<hostname>`; `dnsRecordResource(zoneID, recordID)` is `cloudflare.dnsrecord:<zone id>/<record id>` (Contracts "Hostname helpers"). `hostnameViewOf` maps a row to `HostnameView`: `Tunnel` is the tunnel id, and `CheckedAt` is a pointer that stays nil while the row's `CheckedAt` is the zero time.
3. `checkDrift` reads the tunnel's configuration with `a.Configuration` and returns it. When the tunnel row stores a non-empty `ConfigHash` that differs from `ingress.Hash` of the configuration read, it returns an `*errcode.Error` `cloud.conflict` whose detail names the tunnel by name and says to accept the current configuration with `cloudflare.tunnel.adopt`; an empty stored hash is not drift. A read failure is returned unchanged. The error is not wrapped `core.Definite`: callers that have intended an effect decide that.
4. `hostnameHandler` holds the `cf` value as field `c`. Every method below finds the account and the provider client with `c.connected(ctx, env.DB, env.Sealer, env.Clock)`; an absent object at the provider (an error that is `errcode.NotFound` or carries `cloud.Status(err) == 404`) means "absent", never a failure.
   - One function renders a hostname's rule document `{"rule": <ingress.Rule marshalled, or null>}` from a configuration, and one renders a record document `{"name","content","proxied","comment"}` (or `null`) from a `DNSRecord`. The apply code and `Observe` both use them, so what `Made` records is what `Observe` later reads. A document never carries a secret.
   - `Observe(ctx, env, e)` decides by the resource prefix. `cloudflare.ingress:<tunnel>/<hostname>`: read the configuration, return the rule document with `Matches: 1`, `Exclusive: true`, `Resource: e.Resource`. `cloudflare.dnsrecord:<zone>/<id>`: read the record; absent is the `null` document. A creation not yet named (`cloudflare.dnsrecord:?darkpanel:<change id>`): find the hostname row whose `ChangeID` is `e.ChangeID` for the zone and hostname, list `DNSRecords(zone, hostname, e.Recovery.Value)`, keep those whose comment equals the marker; `Matches` is their number, `Current` is the record document of the single match (`null` for none or several), `Resource` is `dnsRecordResource(zone, id)` for exactly one match, `Candidates` lists every match when there are several, `Exclusive` is true. The same code serves an effect that is undoing or undone.
   - `Inverse(ctx, env, e)` makes the inverse of one made effect and touches nothing else. Every refusal that changed nothing is `core.Definite(*errcode.Error cloud.conflict)` naming the object. For a DNS record effect: read the record; absent counts as removed; otherwise require type `CNAME`, a content ending in `.cfargotunnel.com` and the comment `darkpanel:<e.ChangeID>`, else refuse; then `DeleteDNSRecord`, and move the hostname row of this change (found by `ChangeID`) to phase `removing_rule` with an empty record id (`setHostnamePhase`). For an ingress effect: load the tunnel row and the hostname row of the resource, run `checkDrift` (a drift error is refused as above), look the rule up; absent counts as removed; otherwise require its service and `NoTLSVerify` to equal the row's, else refuse; remove it with `ingress.Remove`, `PutConfiguration`, read the configuration back and require `ingress.Hash` of it to equal that of what was sent; then in one `env.DB.Write` store the hash of the configuration read back (`setTunnelHash`) and delete the hostname row (`deleteHostname`). Return `core.InverseResult{}`.
   - `Recover(ctx, env)` settles an add change after a crash or a live failure; the engine has already settled `intended` effects and runs it only when none is unresolved. It reads the hostname row whose `ChangeID` is `env.ChangeID` (`listHostnames`, filtered) and the change's effects (`env.Effects.List`), and decides from them alone: no row, or the ingress effect absent or `skipped`: delete the row if there is one and return `core.RecoveryFailed` with a reason saying the rule was not written; row phase `active`: `core.RecoveryCompleted` with the `HostnameView` as `Output`; ingress effect `made` and record effect `made`: move the row to phase `active` with the record id taken from the made effect's resource (`setHostnamePhase`) and health `ok` (`setHostnameHealth`), return `core.RecoveryCompleted` with the view as `Output`; ingress effect `made` and no `made` record effect: run the ingress inverse on that effect, which removes the rule, stores the new hash and deletes the row, and return `core.RecoveryRolledBack`. An effect in any other state (accepted, abandoned, undoing) is `core.RecoveryNeedsRepair` naming it. A provider error is returned as the error, so the engine records `needs_repair` and repair runs the handler again; every branch is safe to run twice.

`hostname_add.go`:

5. `func (c cf) hostnameAdd() core.ActionDef` is `core.DefineMutating` with `ActionSpec{Name: "cloudflare.hostname.add", Version: 1, Class: core.ClassCompensable, Side: core.SideController, LockKeys: []string{"cloudflare"}}` and a one-sentence summary; it declares neither `CompensatedBy` nor `ForwardOnly` (the handler's `Inverse` is its one compensation mechanism). The handler is `hostnameAddHandler`, which embeds `hostnameHandler` (so `Observe`, `Inverse` and `Recover` come from it) and adds `Plan`, `Apply` and `Verify` over `HostnameAddInput` and `HostnameView`.
6. `Plan` runs these checks in order and returns the first failure as an `*errcode.Error` with the field path in `Fields` where one applies: the hostname must be lower case, have at least two labels of 1 to 63 characters from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-` without a leading or trailing hyphen, and at most 253 characters in all (`request.invalid_input`, `/hostname`; a wildcard is refused); the service must be `http_status:<100 to 599>` or an `http`, `https`, `tcp` or `ssh` URL with a host, a numeric port from 1 to 65535, no user, path, query or fragment (`request.invalid_input`, `/service`); the tunnel must be found by `loadTunnel` by id or name (`not_found` naming it); a reserved service with `env.Call.ParentAction != "panel.exposure.add"` is `core.Definite(cloudflare.reserved)`; the account must be connected (`cloud.not_connected` is returned as is); a stored hostname row for the hostname is `request.invalid_input` (already managed); `zoneFor` over `a.Zones` must find a zone (`request.invalid_input`, `/hostname`, naming the hostname); `checkDrift` must pass; a rule for the hostname already in the configuration, or an error from `ingress.Add`, is `request.invalid_input` (`/hostname`); any DNS record for the hostname in the zone (`DNSRecords(zone, hostname, "")`) is `request.invalid_input`. The outcome's diff is three lines: `+` `ingress rule: <hostname> -> <service>` (with ` (noTLSVerify)` appended when set), `+` `dns record: CNAME <hostname> -> <tunnel id>.cfargotunnel.com (proxied, comment darkpanel:<change id>)`, and a ` ` line `the configuration and the DNS record are written after reading them; a change another client makes in between is not detected`. `StateHash` is the hex SHA-256 of the tunnel id, `ingress.Hash` of the configuration read, the zone id and the zone's record ids for the hostname, joined with `|`, so a configuration changed after the plan fails the apply with `plan.state_changed`. A plan reads and never writes.
7. `Apply` repeats the plan's checks that read the provider (connected, zone, drift, rule, records) and refuses with `core.Definite` as the plan did, then:
   - inserts the hostname row in phase `adding_rule` (`insertHostname`: the zone id, service, `NoTLSVerify`, `ChangeID` `env.ChangeID`, health `unknown`, `UpdatedAt` the clock);
   - journals the rule: `cloudEffect(core.EffectModify, ingressResource(tunnel, hostname), <{"rule":null}>)` with `After` the rule document of the new rule, `env.Effects.Intend`; `PutConfiguration` with `ingress.Add`'s result; on an error, `Skipped` when `core.IsDefinite(err)` and otherwise leave the effect intended (the engine makes it unresolved); on success read the configuration back and require its `ingress.Hash` to equal that of the configuration sent (a mismatch is an error, effect left intended); then `Made` with the rule document read back, and in one `env.DB.Write` store `ingress.Hash` of the configuration read back on the tunnel (`setTunnelHash`) and move the row to `adding_record`;
   - journals the record: `cloudEffect(core.EffectCreate, "cloudflare.dnsrecord:?darkpanel:<change id>", <null>)` with `Recovery: &core.RecoveryID{Kind: "marker", Value: "darkpanel:<change id>"}` and `After` the record document, `Intend`; `CreateDNSRecord` of a proxied `CNAME` for the hostname with content `<tunnel id>.cfargotunnel.com` and comment `darkpanel:<change id>`; `Skipped` on a definite error and the effect left intended otherwise; on success `Made` with `dnsRecordResource(zone, record id)` and the record document read from the answer;
   - in one `env.DB.Write` moves the row to `active` with the record id, health `ok` and `CheckedAt` now, and returns the `HostnameView`.
   Provider writes are never retried by the action. Every error string starts with `cloudflare:`.
8. `Verify` is read-only and must work with a zero output (recovery calls it so): the hostname row of the input is `active` with `ChangeID` `env.ChangeID`, the configuration holds the rule with the requested service and `NoTLSVerify`, and the recorded DNS record exists with the expected content, proxied flag and comment; otherwise an error naming what is missing.
9. Nothing outside the two new files changes: the action is not added to `Manifest()` (Task 58), and no schema snapshot is written.

```go
	mid := hostnameRow{Hostname: "mid.example.com", TunnelID: a.TunnelID, Service: "http://10.0.0.9:80", ZoneID: a.ZoneID,
		Phase: "removing_rule", ChangeID: "01HMID", Health: "unknown", UpdatedAt: h.clock.Now()}
	err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := insertHostname(ctx, tx, mid); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return setHostnameHealth(ctx, tx, "a.example.com", "record_missing", checked)
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got, _ := hsList(t, h, cfWith(srv))
	if len(got.Hostnames) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("hostnames = %+v, want three rows", got.Hostnames)
	}
	names := got.Hostnames[0].Hostname + " " + got.Hostnames[1].Hostname + " " + got.Hostnames[2].Hostname
	if names != "a.example.com b.example.com mid.example.com" {
		t.Errorf("order = %q, want it sorted by hostname", names)
	}
	ga, gb, gm := got.Hostnames[0], got.Hostnames[1], got.Hostnames[2]
	if ga.Tunnel != a.TunnelID || ga.Service != a.Service || ga.RecordID != a.RecordID || ga.RecordID == "" || ga.Phase != "active" {
		t.Errorf("row a = %+v, want the stored tunnel, service, record and the active phase", ga)
	}
	if ga.Health != "record_missing" || ga.CheckedAt == nil || !ga.CheckedAt.Equal(checked) {
		t.Errorf("row a health = %q checked at %v, want record_missing at %v", ga.Health, ga.CheckedAt, checked)
	}
	if gb.RecordID != b.RecordID {
		t.Errorf("row b record = %q, want %q", gb.RecordID, b.RecordID)
	}
	if gm.Phase != "removing_rule" || gm.Health != "unknown" || gm.CheckedAt != nil || gm.RecordID != "" {
		t.Errorf("row mid = %+v, want its phase, unknown health, no check time and no record", gm)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

`hostname_list.go`:

1. `func (c cf) hostnameList() core.ActionDef` is `core.DefineRead` with `ActionSpec{Name: "cloudflare.hostname.list", Version: 1, Side: core.SideController}`, no lock key, and a handler whose `Read(ctx, env, HostnameListInput)` loads every row with `listHostnames(ctx, env.DB.Read())`, sorts them by hostname, maps each with `hostnameViewOf` and returns `HostnameList` whose `Hostnames` is a non-nil slice (an empty table encodes as `"hostnames":[]`). It lists rows in every phase, and needs no connected account.

`hostnames_service.go`:

2. `func (m module) Controller(deps ext.Deps)` returns no routes, one `ext.Service{Name: "cloudflare.hostnames", Run: <closure calling m.c.runHostnames(ctx, deps)>}` and a nil error.
3. `runHostnames` runs `checkHostnames` once at start with `deps.Clock.Now()`, then waits with `deps.Clock.AfterFunc(5*time.Minute, …)` signalling a channel (never `time.Sleep`), runs a pass when it fires and re-arms the timer after the pass; it returns nil when `ctx` ends (stopping a pending timer) and returns a pass's error to the supervisor, which restarts the service.
4. `checkHostnames(ctx, deps, now)` is one pass and writes nothing to Cloudflare (it uses only `Configuration` and `DNSRecord` reads). The account comes from `c.connected(ctx, deps.DB, deps.Sealer, deps.Clock)`; `cloud.not_connected` ends the pass with nil. For each tunnel row from `listTunnels` that has at least one hostname row:
   - when any hostname row of the tunnel is not in phase `active`, an add or remove is in flight: skip the tunnel without a request and without a write;
   - read the configuration; when that fails with anything but a cancelled context, set every hostname row of the tunnel to health `unknown` with `checked_at` now, leave the tunnel's `drift` as stored, and go on to the next tunnel (the pass still returns nil); a cancelled context returns its error;
   - `drift` is true when the tunnel row's `ConfigHash` is not empty and differs from `ingress.Hash` of the configuration; store it with `setTunnelCheck(tx, id, drift, now)`;
   - for each hostname row, health is `rule_missing` when the configuration has no rule for the hostname (no DNS read is made); otherwise the row's record is read with `DNSRecord(row.ZoneID, row.RecordID)` and health is `record_missing` when it is absent (not_found or `cloud.Status` 404), `record_changed` when its content is not `<tunnel id>.cfargotunnel.com`, it is not proxied or its comment is not `darkpanel:<row.ChangeID>`, `unknown` when the read fails otherwise, and `ok` in every other case; store it with `setHostnameHealth(tx, hostname, health, now)` (which also stores `checked_at`);
   - all of one tunnel's writes are one `deps.DB.Write`.
5. Audit: after the write commits, `deps.Audit.Record(ctx, core.AuditEntry{Actor: "system:cloudflare.hostnames", Action: "cloudflare.hostnames", Phase: "check", Result: "ok", At: now, Input: …})` once for each tunnel whose drift changed (input `{"tunnel": <id>, "drift": <new value>}`) and once for each hostname whose health changed (input `{"hostname": …, "from": <old>, "to": <new>}`). A pass that changes nothing records nothing. Input JSON carries no secret.
6. Error strings start with `cloudflare:`; the service takes no lock and never plans a change.

```go
	t.Helper()
	old := pollInterval
	pollInterval = 5 * time.Millisecond
	t.Cleanup(func() { pollInterval = old })
	return NewAPI(srv.URL, (&net.Dialer{}).DialContext)
}

func TestM4xFrames(t *testing.T) {
	const two = "id: 1\nevent: data\ndata: {\"text\":\"a\"}\n\n: keep-alive\n\nevent: data\ndata: {\"text\":\"b\"}\n\nevent: end\ndata: {\"reason\":\"done\"}\n\n"
	got, err := m4xFrames(strings.NewReader(two), 2)
	if err != nil || len(got) != 2 || string(got[0]) != `{"text":"a"}` || string(got[1]) != `{"text":"b"}` {
		t.Fatalf("m4xFrames = %s, %v; want the two data events", got, err)
	}
	bad := []struct{ name, in, want string }{
		{"end first", "event: end\ndata: {\"reason\":\"expired\"}\n\n", "expired"},
		{"end before n", "event: data\ndata: {\"n\":1}\n\nevent: end\ndata: {\"reason\":\"done\"}\n\n", "1 of 3"},
		{"not JSON", "event: data\ndata: {oops\n\n", "not JSON"},
		{"closed early", "event: data\ndata: {\"n\":1}\n\n", "closed after 1 of 3"},
	}
	for _, c := range bad {
		if _, err := m4xFrames(strings.NewReader(c.in), 3); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s: error %v, want one naming %q", c.name, err, c.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestM4xAtLeast(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		have, min string
		want      bool
	}{
		{"1.44", "1.44", true}, {"1.51", "1.44", true}, {"1.9", "1.44", false},
		{"2.0", "1.44", true}, {"1.43", "1.44", false}, {"", "1.44", false}, {"abc", "1.44", false},
	} {
		if got := m4xAtLeast(c.have, c.min); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("m4xAtLeast(%q, %q) = %t, want %t", c.have, c.min, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestM4xUndoSettled(t *testing.T) {
	if err := m4xUndoSettled(Change{ID: "c1", State: core.StateReverted}); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("a reverted change: %v", err)
	}
	err := m4xUndoSettled(Change{ID: "c1", State: core.StateNeedsRepair})
	var ue *m4UndoError
	if !errors.As(err, &ue) || ue.Change.State != core.StateNeedsRepair || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "needs_repair") {
		t.Errorf("a needs_repair change: %v, want an *m4UndoError naming the state", err)
	}
}

func TestM4Plan(t *testing.T) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		switch r.URL.Path {
		case "/api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.compose.up/v1/plan":
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"planId":"p1","confirmation":"web","diff":[{"op":"+","text":"x"}],"guards":[]}`))
		case "/api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.container.stop/v1/plan":
			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusConflict)
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"code":"docker.owned","detail":"container web belongs to module npm"}`))
		default:
			http.NotFound(w, r)
		}
	}))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	api := m4TestAPI(t, srv)
	p, err := m4Plan(context.Background(), api, "h1", "docker.compose.up", map[string]any{"project": "web"})
	if err != nil || p.PlanID != "p1" || p.Confirmation != "web" || len(p.Diff) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("m4Plan = %+v, %v; want plan p1 with confirmation web", p, err)
	}
	_, err = m4Plan(context.Background(), api, "h1", "docker.container.stop", map[string]any{"container": "web"})
	var ae *APIError
	if !errors.As(err, &ae) || ae.Code != "docker.owned" {
		t.Errorf("m4Plan of a refused action = %v, want an *APIError with code docker.owned", err)
	}
}

func TestM4ApplyAsync(t *testing.T) {
	var polls atomic.Int32
	var confirmed atomic.Value
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		switch r.URL.Path {
		case "/api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.compose.up/v1/plan":
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"planId":"p1","confirmation":"web","diff":[],"guards":[]}`))
		case "/api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.compose.up/v1/apply":
			var body struct {
				PlanID       string `json:"planId"`
				Confirmation string `json:"confirmation"`
			}
			_ = json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&body)
			confirmed.Store(body.PlanID + "/" + body.Confirmation)
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"id":"c1","state":"applying"}`))
		case "/api/v1/changes/c1":
			if polls.Add(1) < 3 {
				_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"id":"c1","state":"applying"}`))
				return
			}
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"id":"c1","state":"completed","output":{"project":"web"}}`))
		default:
			http.NotFound(w, r)
		}
	}))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	ch := m4ApplyAsync(context.Background(), t, m4TestAPI(t, srv), "h1", "docker.compose.up", map[string]any{"project": "web"})
	if ch.State != core.StateCompleted || string(ch.Output) != `{"project":"web"}` {
		t.Errorf("change = %+v, want completed with the output", ch)
	}
	if got := confirmed.Load(); got != "p1/web" {
		t.Errorf("apply carried %v, want the plan id and the plan's confirmation p1/web", got)
	}
	if polls.Load() < 3 {
		t.Errorf("polled %d times, want it to wait while the change was applying", polls.Load())
	}
}

func TestM4Undo(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name, final string
		wantErr     bool
	}{{"reverted", "reverted", false}, {"conflict", "needs_repair", true}} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			var polls atomic.Int32
			srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
				switch {
				case r.Method == http.MethodPost && r.URL.Path == "/api/v1/changes/c1/undo":
					_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"id":"c1","state":"undoing"}`))
				case r.URL.Path == "/api/v1/changes/c1":
					state := "undoing"
					if polls.Add(1) >= 2 {
						state = c.final
					}
					_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"id":"c1","state":"` + state + `"}`))
				default:
					http.NotFound(w, r)
				}
			}))
			t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
			err := m4Undo(context.Background(), m4TestAPI(t, srv), "c1")
			var ue *m4UndoError
			switch {
			case c.wantErr && (!errors.As(err, &ue) || ue.Change.State != c.final):
				t.Errorf("m4Undo = %v, want an *m4UndoError in state %s", err, c.final)
			case !c.wantErr && err != nil:
				t.Errorf("m4Undo = %v, want nil", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestM4Stream(t *testing.T) {
	var query atomic.Value
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if r.URL.Path != "/api/v1/hosts/h1/streams/docker/logs" {
			http.NotFound(w, r)
			return
		}
		query.Store(r.URL.RawQuery)
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte("event: data\ndata: {\"stream\":\"stdout\",\"text\":\"hello\"}\n\nevent: end\ndata: {\"reason\":\"done\"}\n\n"))
	}))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	api := m4TestAPI(t, srv)
	got, err := m4Stream(context.Background(), api, "h1", "docker", "logs", url.Values{"container": {"web"}, "tail": {"5"}}, 1)
	if err != nil || len(got) != 1 || !strings.Contains(string(got[0]), `"hello"`) {
		t.Fatalf("m4Stream = %s, %v; want the one logged line", got, err)
	}
	if q, _ := query.Load().(string); q != "container=web&tail=5" {
		t.Errorf("the stream was opened with %q, want container=web&tail=5", q)
	}
	if _, err := m4Stream(context.Background(), api, "h1", "docker", "logs", nil, 2); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "1 of 2") {
		t.Errorf("a stream that ends early: %v, want an error naming 1 of 2", err)
	}
	if _, err := m4Stream(context.Background(), api, "h1", "docker", "stats", nil, 1); err == nil {
		t.Error("a missing stream: no error")
	}
}

func TestM4xContainers(t *testing.T) {
	const list = `{"containers":[{"id":"a1","name":"web","image":"nginx","state":"running","owner":""},{"id":"b2","name":"cf","image":"cloudflared","state":"exited","owner":"cloudflare"}]}`
	cs, err := m4xContainers([]byte(list))
	if err != nil || len(cs) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("m4xContainers = %+v, %v", cs, err)
	}
	if c, ok := m4xFindContainer(cs, "cf"); !ok || c.State != "exited" || c.Owner != "cloudflare" {
		t.Errorf("m4xFindContainer(cf) = %+v, %t", c, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := m4xFindContainer(cs, "absent"); ok {
		t.Error("m4xFindContainer found a container that is not listed")
	}
	if _, err := m4xContainers([]byte(`{"containers":`)); err == nil {
		t.Error("m4xContainers accepted truncated JSON")
	}
}

func TestM4RevealReleaseEffects(t *testing.T) {
	var released atomic.Value
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		switch {
		case r.Method == http.MethodPost && r.URL.Path == "/api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/docker.container.reveal-env/v1/reveal":
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"value":{"env":[{"name":"K","value":"v"}]}}`))
		case r.Method == http.MethodPost && r.URL.Path == "/api/v1/changes/c1/release":
			var b struct{ Reason string }
			_ = json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&b)
			released.Store(b.Reason)
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"change":{"id":"c1","state":"failed"},"abandoned":[]}`))
		case r.URL.Path == "/api/v1/changes/c1/effects":
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"effects":[{"seq":1,"resource":"docker.container:a1","state":"unresolved","reason":"conflict"}]}`))
		default:
			http.NotFound(w, r)
		}
	}))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	api, ctx := m4TestAPI(t, srv), context.Background()
	var env struct {
		Env []struct{ Name, Value string } `json:"env"`
	}
	if err := m4Reveal(ctx, api, "h1", "docker.container.reveal-env", map[string]any{"container": "web"}, &env); err != nil || len(env.Env) != 1 || env.Env[0].Value != "v" {
		t.Errorf("m4Reveal = %+v, %v; want the revealed value", env, err)
	}
	if err := m4Release(ctx, api, "c1", "scenario cleanup"); err != nil || released.Load() != "scenario cleanup" {
		t.Errorf("m4Release = %v, reason %v; want the reason sent", err, released.Load())
	}
	effs, err := m4Effects(ctx, api, "c1")
	if err != nil || len(effs) != 1 || effs[0].State != "unresolved" || effs[0].Reason != "conflict" {
		t.Errorf("m4Effects = %+v, %v; want the one unresolved conflict", effs, err)
	}
}
```

Create `test/harness/m4_test.go` with exactly this content:

```go
//go:build harness

package harness

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

var m4Flag = flag.Bool("m4", false, "run the M4 Docker module scenarios")

// m4Deadline bounds TestM4, a go test run of its own that needs -os, -m2 and -m4.
const m4Deadline = 60 * time.Minute

// m4Step is one scenario of TestM4; a failed gate step ends the run.
type m4Step struct {
	name string
	gate bool // later steps need this one
	run  func(t *testing.T)
}

// TestM4 is the Docker half of M4 (spec, Verification) on the enrolled agent
// of the M2 fleet, whose controller and agent run the harness build of this
// commit. The workflow selects it with -run and -m4.
func TestM4(t *testing.T) {
	if *osFlag == "" || *m2Flag == "" || !*m4Flag {
		t.Skip("no -os, -m2 or -m4 given: the VM tests run in .github/workflows/harness.yml")
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), m4Deadline)
	defer cancel()
	f := bootFleet(ctx, t)
	serveReleases(ctx, t, f)
	steps := []m4Step{
		{"install", true, func(t *testing.T) { scenarioInstall(ctx, t, f) }},
		{"docker-ready", true, func(t *testing.T) { m4dReady(ctx, t, f) }},
		{"resources", false, func(t *testing.T) { m4dResources(ctx, t, f) }},
		{"container-lifecycle", false, func(t *testing.T) { m4dLifecycle(ctx, t, f) }},
		{"undo-conflict", false, func(t *testing.T) { m4dUndoConflict(ctx, t, f) }},
		{"inspect-and-streams", false, func(t *testing.T) { m4dInspect(ctx, t, f) }},
		{"container-remove", false, func(t *testing.T) { m4dRemove(ctx, t, f) }},
		{"images", false, func(t *testing.T) { m4dImages(ctx, t, f) }},
		{"networks-and-volumes", false, func(t *testing.T) { m4dNetworksVolumes(ctx, t, f) }},
		{"owned-refused", false, func(t *testing.T) { m4dOwned(ctx, t, f) }},
	}
	for _, s := range steps {
		if !t.Run(s.name, s.run) && s.gate {
			return
		}
	}
}
```

Create `test/harness/m4_objects_test.go` with exactly this content. These are the VM scenarios; they run only through `TestM4` on a fleet.

```go
//go:build harness

package harness

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"net/url"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

const m4dSecret = "s3cr3t-m4-value"

// m4dReady waits until the agent's docker.engine resource reports a running
// Engine whose API is at least 1.44.
func m4dReady(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet) {
	var eng struct {
		Available  bool   `json:"available"`
		Reason     string `json:"reason"`
		APIVersion string `json:"apiVersion"`
	}
	err := eventually(ctx, 2*time.Minute, func(ctx context.Context) error {
		if err := f.api.Resource(ctx, f.agentID, "docker.engine", &eng); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if !eng.Available {
			return errors.New("the engine is unavailable: " + eng.Reason)
		}
		if !m4xAtLeast(eng.APIVersion, "1.44") {
			return errors.New("the engine's API is " + eng.APIVersion + ", want 1.44 or later")
		}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("docker.engine of host %s: %v", f.agentID, err)
	}
}

// m4dRun starts the pinned pebble image as the container name with extra
// docker run arguments, and removes the container when the test ends.
func m4dRun(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet, name string, extra ...string) {
	t.Helper()
	ref, err := m3dxImage("pebble")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	args := append([]string{"run", "-d", "--name", name}, extra...)
	m4Docker(ctx, t, f.agent, append(args, ref)...)
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Minute)
		defer cancel()
		_, _ = f.agent.Run(ctx, "sudo docker rm -f "+m3dxShell(name))
	})
	m3dWaitRunning(ctx, t, f.agent, name)
}

// m4dRunning reports whether the container name runs, by the Docker CLI on
// the agent VM.
func m4dRunning(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet, name string) bool {
	t.Helper()
	return strings.TrimSpace(m4Docker(ctx, t, f.agent, "inspect", "-f", "{{.State.Running}}", name)) == "true"
}

// m4dStartedAt is the container's State.StartedAt as the Docker CLI reports it.
func m4dStartedAt(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet, name string) string {
	t.Helper()
	return strings.TrimSpace(m4Docker(ctx, t, f.agent, "inspect", "-f", "{{.State.StartedAt}}", name))
}

// m4dAct applies the container action name on container and waits for it.
func m4dAct(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet, action, container string) Change {
	t.Helper()
	return m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, action, map[string]any{"container": container})
}

// m4dRefused requires that planning action with input is refused with code.
func m4dRefused(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet, action string, input any, code errcode.Code) {
	t.Helper()
	_, err := m4Plan(ctx, f.api, f.agentID, action, input)
	var ae *APIError
	if !errors.As(err, &ae) || ae.Code != string(code) {
		t.Errorf("plan %s: %v, want an API error with code %s", action, err, code)
	}
}

// m4dResources: every resource lists the objects the Docker CLI created.
func m4dResources(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet) {
	m4dRun(ctx, t, f, "m4-res")
	err := eventually(ctx, time.Minute, func(ctx context.Context) error {
		var raw json.RawMessage
		if err := f.api.Resource(ctx, f.agentID, "docker.containers", &raw); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		cs, err := m4xContainers(raw)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		c, ok := m4xFindContainer(cs, "m4-res")
		if !ok || c.State != "running" {
			return errors.New("docker.containers does not list m4-res as running")
		}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var images struct {
		Images []struct {
			ID         string   `json:"id"`
			Containers []string `json:"containers"`
		} `json:"images"`
	}
	if err := f.api.Resource(ctx, f.agentID, "docker.images", &images); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	used := false
	for _, im := range images.Images {
		used = used || slices.Contains(im.Containers, "m4-res")
	}
	if !used {
		t.Errorf("docker.images lists no image used by m4-res: %+v", images.Images)
	}
	var networks struct {
		Networks []struct {
			Name string `json:"name"`
		} `json:"networks"`
	}
	if err := f.api.Resource(ctx, f.agentID, "docker.networks", &networks); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(networks.Networks) == 0 || !strings.Contains(m3JSON(networks), `"bridge"`) {
		t.Errorf("docker.networks does not list the bridge network: %+v", networks)
	}
	if err := f.api.Resource(ctx, f.agentID, "docker.volumes", &json.RawMessage{}); err != nil {
		t.Error(err)
	}
}

// m4dLifecycle: start, stop and restart act on the Engine, and the undo of
// the newest change restores what its journal recorded.
func m4dLifecycle(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet) {
	const name = "m4-life"
	m4dRun(ctx, t, f, name)

	stop := m4dAct(ctx, t, f, "docker.container.stop", name)
	if m4dRunning(ctx, t, f, name) {
		t.Fatal("the container still runs after docker.container.stop")
	}
	if err := m4Undo(ctx, f.api, stop.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !m4dRunning(ctx, t, f, name) {
		t.Error("the undo of stop did not start the container that was running before")
	}

	m4dAct(ctx, t, f, "docker.container.stop", name)
	start := m4dAct(ctx, t, f, "docker.container.start", name)
	if !m4dRunning(ctx, t, f, name) {
		t.Fatal("the container does not run after docker.container.start")
	}
	if err := m4Undo(ctx, f.api, start.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if m4dRunning(ctx, t, f, name) {
		t.Error("the undo of start did not stop the container that was stopped before")
	}

	m4dAct(ctx, t, f, "docker.container.start", name)
	before := m4dStartedAt(ctx, t, f, name)
	restart := m4dAct(ctx, t, f, "docker.container.restart", name)
	if after := m4dStartedAt(ctx, t, f, name); after == before {
		t.Errorf("StartedAt is still %s after docker.container.restart", before)
	}
	if err := m4Undo(ctx, f.api, restart.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !m4dRunning(ctx, t, f, name) {
		t.Error("the undo of restart left the container stopped")
	}
}

// m4dUndoConflict: a container restarted by hand after docker.container.start
// is not stopped by the undo, which becomes a conflict for the operator.
func m4dUndoConflict(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet) {
	const name = "m4-conflict"
	m4dRun(ctx, t, f, name)
	m4dAct(ctx, t, f, "docker.container.stop", name)
	start := m4dAct(ctx, t, f, "docker.container.start", name)
	m4Docker(ctx, t, f.agent, "restart", name)

	err := m4Undo(ctx, f.api, start.ID)
	var ue *m4UndoError
	if !errors.As(err, &ue) || ue.Change.State != "needs_repair" {
		t.Fatalf("undo of start after a manual restart: %v, want an undo that ended needs_repair", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Minute)
		defer cancel()
		if err := m4Release(ctx, f.api, start.ID, "M4 scenario cleanup"); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("release %s: %v", start.ID, err)
		}
	})
	effs, err := m4Effects(ctx, f.api, start.ID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	found := false
	for _, e := range effs {
		found = found || (e.State == "unresolved" && e.Reason == "conflict")
	}
	if !found {
		t.Errorf("the effects of %s are %+v, want one unresolved with reason conflict", start.ID, effs)
	}
	if !m4dRunning(ctx, t, f, name) {
		t.Error("the refused undo stopped the container")
	}
}

// m4dInspect: inspect redacts every environment value, reveal-env returns
// them, and the logs and stats streams deliver events.
func m4dInspect(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet) {
	const name = "m4-env"
	m4dRun(ctx, t, f, name, "-e", "M4_SECRET="+m4dSecret, "-e", "M4_PLAIN=1")
	in := map[string]any{"container": name}

	var raw json.RawMessage
	if err := f.api.Read(ctx, f.agentID, "docker.container.inspect/v1", in, &raw); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var detail struct {
		Env []struct{ Name, Value string } `json:"env"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &detail); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(raw), m4dSecret) {
		t.Error("docker.container.inspect returned the secret value")
	}
	redacted := false
	for _, e := range detail.Env {
		redacted = redacted || (e.Name == "M4_SECRET" && e.Value == "[redacted]")
	}
	if !redacted {
		t.Errorf("inspect lists the environment %+v, want M4_SECRET with the value [redacted]", detail.Env)
	}

	var revealed struct {
		Env []struct{ Name, Value string } `json:"env"`
	}
	if err := m4Reveal(ctx, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.container.reveal-env", in, &revealed); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got := ""
	for _, e := range revealed.Env {
		if e.Name == "M4_SECRET" {
			got = e.Value
		}
	}
	if got != m4dSecret {
		t.Errorf("reveal-env returned %q for M4_SECRET, want the value", got)
	}

	err := eventually(ctx, time.Minute, func(ctx context.Context) error {
		out, err := f.agent.Run(ctx, "sudo docker logs "+m3dxShell(name))
		if err == nil && strings.TrimSpace(out) == "" {
			err = errors.New("the container has logged nothing yet")
		}
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	lines, err := m4Stream(ctx, f.api, f.agentID, "docker", "logs", url.Values{"container": {name}, "tail": {"all"}}, 1)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(lines[0]), m4dSecret) {
		t.Error("the logs stream returned the secret value")
	}
	if _, err := m4Stream(ctx, f.api, f.agentID, "docker", "stats", url.Values{"container": {name}}, 2); err != nil {
		t.Error(err)
	}
}

// m4dRemove: removing a container asks for its name, and refuses another.
func m4dRemove(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet) {
	const name = "m4-rm"
	m4dRun(ctx, t, f, name)
	m4Docker(ctx, t, f.agent, "stop", name)
	in := map[string]any{"container": name}

	p, err := m4Plan(ctx, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.container.remove", in)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if p.Confirmation != name {
		t.Errorf("the plan asks for the confirmation %q, want the container name %q", p.Confirmation, name)
	}
	path, _ := actionPath(f.agentID, "docker.container.remove/v1", "apply")
	err = f.api.do(ctx, "POST", path, map[string]any{"planId": p.PlanID, "confirmation": "wrong"}, nil)
	var ae *APIError
	if !errors.As(err, &ae) || ae.Code != string(errcode.PlanConfirmationNeeded) {
		t.Errorf("apply with a wrong confirmation: %v, want code %s", err, errcode.PlanConfirmationNeeded)
	}
	m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.container.remove", in)
	if out := strings.TrimSpace(m4Docker(ctx, t, f.agent, "ps", "-a", "-q", "--filter", "name=^"+name+"$")); out != "" {
		t.Errorf("container %s still exists after docker.container.remove: %s", name, out)
	}
}

// m4dImages: a pull runs as a long change with a progress stream, remove
// asks for the reference, and prune lists before it removes.
func m4dImages(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet) {
	ref, err := m3dxImage("pebble-challtestsrv")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ch := m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.image.pull", map[string]any{"image": ref})
	var pulled struct {
		ID string `json:"id"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(ch.Output, &pulled); err != nil || pulled.ID == "" {
		t.Fatalf("the pull's output is %s (%v), want the image id", ch.Output, err)
	}
	if _, err := m4Stream(ctx, f.api, f.agentID, "docker", "pull", url.Values{"changeId": {ch.ID}}, 1); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("the pull stream of change %s: %v", ch.ID, err)
	}
	m4Docker(ctx, t, f.agent, "image", "inspect", ref)

	m4dRefused(ctx, t, f, "docker.image.remove", map[string]any{"image": ""}, errcode.InvalidInput)
	p, err := m4Plan(ctx, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.image.remove", map[string]any{"image": ref})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if p.Confirmation != ref {
		t.Errorf("remove asks for the confirmation %q, want the reference as given", p.Confirmation)
	}
	m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.image.remove", map[string]any{"image": ref})
	if _, err := f.agent.Run(ctx, "sudo docker image inspect "+m3dxShell(ref)); err == nil {
		t.Error("the image is still present after docker.image.remove")
	}
	prune, err := m4Plan(ctx, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.image.prune", map[string]any{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if prune.Confirmation != "prune" {
		t.Errorf("prune asks for the confirmation %q, want prune", prune.Confirmation)
	}
}

// m4dNetworksVolumes: create and remove for both kinds, the undo of a create,
// connect and disconnect, and the refusal to remove a network in use.
func m4dNetworksVolumes(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet) {
	nw := map[string]any{"name": "m4-net"}
	created := m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.network.create", nw)
	m4Docker(ctx, t, f.agent, "network", "inspect", "m4-net")
	if err := m4Undo(ctx, f.api, created.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := f.agent.Run(ctx, "sudo docker network inspect m4-net"); err == nil {
		t.Error("the undo of network.create left the network")
	}
	m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.network.create", nw)
	t.Cleanup(func() { _, _ = f.agent.Run(context.Background(), "sudo docker network rm m4-net") })

	m4dRun(ctx, t, f, "m4-nc")
	link := map[string]any{"network": "m4-net", "container": "m4-nc"}
	m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.network.connect", link)
	if out := m4Docker(ctx, t, f.agent, "inspect", "-f", "{{json .NetworkSettings.Networks}}", "m4-nc"); !strings.Contains(out, `"m4-net"`) {
		t.Errorf("m4-nc is not attached to m4-net after docker.network.connect: %s", out)
	}
	m4dRefused(ctx, t, f, "docker.network.remove", map[string]any{"network": "m4-net"}, errcode.DockerInUse)
	m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.network.disconnect", link)
	m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.network.remove", map[string]any{"network": "m4-net"})
	if _, err := f.agent.Run(ctx, "sudo docker network inspect m4-net"); err == nil {
		t.Error("the network is still present after docker.network.remove")
	}

	vol := map[string]any{"name": "m4-vol"}
	vc := m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.volume.create", vol)
	m4Docker(ctx, t, f.agent, "volume", "inspect", "m4-vol")
	if err := m4Undo(ctx, f.api, vc.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := f.agent.Run(ctx, "sudo docker volume inspect m4-vol"); err == nil {
		t.Error("the undo of volume.create left the volume")
	}
	m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.volume.create", vol)
	m4ApplyAsync(ctx, t, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.volume.remove", map[string]any{"volume": "m4-vol"})
	if _, err := f.agent.Run(ctx, "sudo docker volume inspect m4-vol"); err == nil {
		t.Error("the volume is still present after docker.volume.remove")
	}
}

// m4dOwned: actions on a container labelled darkpanel.module are refused,
// and its environment is never revealed.
func m4dOwned(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet) {
	const name = "m4-owned"
	m4dRun(ctx, t, f, name, "--label", "darkpanel.module=cloudflare", "-e", "M4_SECRET="+m4dSecret)
	in := map[string]any{"container": name}
	for _, action := range []string{"docker.container.stop", "docker.container.restart"} {
		m4dRefused(ctx, t, f, action, in, errcode.DockerOwned)
	}
	var out json.RawMessage
	err := m4Reveal(ctx, f.api, f.agentID, "docker.container.reveal-env", in, &out)
	var ae *APIError
	if !errors.As(err, &ae) || ae.Code != string(errcode.DockerOwned) {
		t.Errorf("reveal-env of an owned container: %v, want code %s", err, errcode.DockerOwned)
	}
	if !m4dRunning(ctx, t, f, name) {
		t.Error("the owned container stopped")
	}
}
```
